{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.198217+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e1755027b6b72bacceb84a2948a53af4813916207fa89947be3d5506f36530d0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 124 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall the definition \eqref{e:bad.times.J}. 
If $(p^N)'$ converges to $p'$ in the L\'evy--Prohorov metric in the sense of Definition~\ref{d:levy.prohorov.derivs}, then  we have
	\[
	J^N\equiv
	J(p^N,\tep,\lambda)
		\subseteq 
		J\bigg(p,2\tep,\frac{\lambda}{2}\bigg)
	\equiv J
	\] for all $N$ large enough. 

\begin{proof}
The function $(p^N)'$ is nonincreasing, so there exists a nonnegative measure $\nu_N$ on $[q_0,1]$ with
	\[
	\nu_N( (s,t]) = -\Big[(p^N)'(t)-(p^N)'(s)\Big]
	\]
for all $q_0 \le s\le t\le1$, and with $\nu_N(\{0\})=0$. Define analogously the measure $\nu$ corresponding to the limiting function $p$.
The L\'evy--Prohorov convergence assumption implies that for all $N\ge N(\tep)$ we have
	\[
	\nu_N(A) \le \nu(A^{\tep})+\tep
	\]
where $A\subseteq[q_0,1]$ is any Borel set, and $A^{\tep}$ is the $\tep$-fattening of $A$. (The same inequality also holds with $\nu$ and $\nu_N$ exchanged.) It follows that
	\begin{align*}
	&-\Big[(p^N)'(t+\tep)-(p^N)'(t-\tep)\Big]
	= \nu_N([t-\tep,t+\tep])\\
	&\qquad\le \nu([t-2\tep,t+2\tep]) + \tep
	=-\Big[p'(t+2\tep)-p'(t-2\tep)\Big]+ \tep
	\le \frac{\lambda}{2}+\tep\,,
	\end{align*}
where the last bound holds provided $t\notin J$. Since $\tep\ll\lambda$ by Assumption~\ref{a:params}, this shows that if $t\notin J$ then $t\notin J^N$, as claimed.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:45:27.983072+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e19bbdb1de2b9c37f1da247a329630235cc337249e399a62b37c588084ba8d43","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:main-canonical-bridge-limit of arXiv:2607.04264, 'Macroscopic Feynman Cycles and Poisson--Kingman Universality in Bose Condensation'] Assume~(ass:limiting-effective-kernel of the paper),
(ass:limiting-effective-density of the paper),
(ass:effective-marked-trace-convergence of the paper),

(ass:canonical-density-regime of the paper). Fix \(\kappa > 0\) satisfies~(ass:background-density-concentration of the paper).  Let

under \(\mathbb{P}_{L,N_L}^{\mathrm{can}}\),

    \Xi_L
    \Longrightarrow

    \text{in } \mathcal{N}_\ell(\mathsf{E}).
\]

\[

is the marked Poisson--Kingman bridge defined

\]
Thus the background contributes the deterministic density
\(\rho_{\mathrm{bg}}\), while the effective part carries the remaining
density \(\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}\): under
\(\mathbb{P}_{L,N_L}^{\mathrm{can}}\),
\[
    \left(
        \frac{B_L}{V_L},\;
        \frac{G_L}{V_L}
    \right)
    \longrightarrow
    \left(
        \rho_{\mathrm{bg}},\;
        \rho_{\mathrm{eff}}
    \right)
    \qquad
    \text{in probability}.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:13:18.506242+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e1a7d34e91f2f0976f773bd3135152e1bc9d3d8151c236c9717840a98f0ff0a8","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 11 (Parseval-type identity and intrinsic reconstruction) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] Assume that the family $\{\Psi_{j,k}\}_{(j,k)\in\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}^d}\subset L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.148711+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e1ba5cc6782dbe119dc23f6823d03dd94daf10ae75432259117f319071b13319","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 13 of arXiv:2608.29361, 'Convergence of the subcritical $\gamma$-LQG metric to the critical $2$-LQG metric as $\gam'] Let $\mathcal{D}'(\CC)$ denote the space of distributions (generalized functions) on $\CC$, equipped with the standard weak topology.     \begin{enumerate}[(I)]
        \item  
        \textbf{Length space.} A.s., $(\CC,D_h)$ is a length space.

            (e^{\xi f} \cdot D_h)(z,w):=\inf_{P : z \rightarrow w} \left\{\int_0^{\text{len}(P;D_h)} e^{\xi f(P(t))} dt \right\} \quad \text{for all} \quad z,w \in \CC,

        \[

       \]
       for some fixed  $C>0$.

            \\
         &> C  - \frac{1}{(\ell + 1)\log(n)} \sum_{j=0}^{\ell} \frac{2(m+1) \log(n)^{2/3} + (m+1)^2}{K_j}. \notag
    } (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:30:52.739334+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e1ca8aa1be528ba2153f63d929364e550ac9826c0586e2d72ae3caab07654d24","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 10 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] [\textbf{Regularized Kullback-Leibler divergence between Gaussian measures on Hilbert spaces}\cite{Minh:LogDet2016,Minh:2020regularizedDiv}]
			
			Let $\Ncal(m_1,C_1), \Ncal(m_2,C_2) \in \Gauss(\Hcal)$,
			
			
			
			with corresponding mean vectors $m_1,m_2 \in \H$  
			and
			
			covariance operators $C_1, C_2 \in \Sym^{+}(\H) \cap \Tr(\H)$. 
			For any 
			
			fixed $\gamma \in \R$, 
			$\gamma > 0$, 
			the regularized 
			
			KL divergence, denoted by ${\KL}^{\gamma}(\Ncal(m_1, C_1)|| \Ncal(m_2, C_2))$,

{"assumptions":["Lebesgue measure on [0,1] for the counterexample","0 < p < 1"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:36.553704+00:00","domain":"real analysis, Lp spaces","id":"claim_e1f1d09dab661f59168150611995537e63e0f249b26c9ceb645e324eb84a1360","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"For 0 < p < 1 the functional ||f||_p = (int |f|^p)^{1/p} is NOT a norm and the triangle inequality is false. Counterexample: on [0,1] with Lebesgue measure take f = 1_{[0,1/2]} and g = 1_{(1/2,1]}. Then ||f+g||_p = ||1_{[0,1]}||_p = 1, while ||f||_p + ||g||_p = 2 * (1/2)^{1/p} = 2^{1 - 1/p} < 1 for every p < 1 (e.g. 2^{-1} = 0.5 at p = 1/2). What survives: (i) the reverse inequality ||f+g||_p >= ||f||_p + ||g||_p for nonnegative f, g when 0 < p < 1; (ii) the quasi-triangle inequality ||f+g||_p <= 2^{1/p - 1}(||f||_p + ||g||_p); (iii) the p-th power is subadditive, int |f+g|^p <= int |f|^p + int |g|^p, so d(f,g) = ||f - g||_p^p is a complete translation-invariant metric and L^p (0 < p < 1) is a complete metric topological vector space - but it is not locally convex on a nonatomic space, and its dual is {0}. Related trap: the generalized Hölder inequality with 1/r = sum 1/p_i remains valid for r < 1, but the TWO-exponent Hölder inequality with a negative conjugate exponent (0 < p < 1, q = p/(p-1) < 0) points the other way under the appropriate positivity and finiteness hypotheses, so the standard direction may not be quoted when p < 1.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:31:20.864288+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2069d1afb6f67b3701640a860faeb5ff84d4044d1c572cc42e53b268a42a291","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2506.10856, 'The space of multifurcating ranked tree shapes: enumeration, lattice structure, and Markov'] The space $\mathcal{T}_{N,K}$ of ranked tree shapes with $N$ leaves and $K$ internal nodes is in bijection with the space $\mathcal{F}_{N,K}$ of $K\times K$ lower triangular matrices with non-negative integer entries that obey the
following constraints:
\begin{enumerate}[label={F\arabic*.}]
    \item The diagonal elements $F_{i,i}$ are strictly increasing: $F_{1,1}< F_{2,2}<...<F_{K,K}$ with $F_{K,K}=N$. The subdiagonal elements satisfy $F_{i+1,i} = F_{i,i}-1$ for all $i=1,...,K-1$.
    \item The elements $F_{i,1}, i=3,...,K$ in the first column satisfy \[ \max\{0, F_{i-1,1}- 1\} \leq F_{i,1} \leq F_{i-1,1}\] This just implies the column elements are decreasing by at most 1 if $F_{i-1,1}$ is non-zero. 
    \item All other elements $F_{i,j}, i=4,...,K, j=2,...,i-2$ satisfy these three conditions. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label={\alph*.}]
        \item $\max\{0, F_{i,j-1} \} \leq F_{i,j}$: Row-wise non-decreasing. 
        \item $F_{i-1, j}-1 \leq F_{i,j} \leq F_{i-1, j}$: Column-wise change is either 1 or 0.
        \item $0\leq (F_{i-1, j} - F_{i,j}) - (F_{i-1, j-1}- F_{i,j-1}) \leq 1$: in any $2\times 2$ grid, sum of off-diagonal elements minus sum of on-diagonal elements is 1 or 0. 
    \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
The space of such matrices is denoted $\mathcal{F}_{N,K}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:38:13.651647+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2081f0ae91205c715cd1ca304eefcc1ccfbf302567ce8bf25fd2909aa22a6b0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 21 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] Let $\sR=(R,\alpha_R\colon N\to R)$ be as in \eqref{eq;SN} and write $\sR/p=(R/p,N)$. The restriction on the subcategory $\mathrm{lSm}^{\rm Cart}_{\sR/p}$ of affine fine log-smooth algebras of Cartier type of the log-crystalline cohomology functor
      	\[
      	R\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR) \colon \PreLog_{\sR/p} \to \mathcal{D}(R)^\wedge_p
      	\]
      	is the left Kan extension of its restriction to $\mathrm{lPoly}_{\sR/p}$. In particular, derived log crystalline cohomology and underived crystalline cohomology coincide for log smooth algebras of Cartier type.  
         Moreover, the algebra structure of $R\Gamma_{crys}(X/\sR)$ for $X\in \mathrm{lSm}^{\rm Cart}_{\sR/p}$ is left Kan extended from that for polynomial objects. 
     	\begin{proof}This is basically well-known, and follows the same argument of the non-logarithmic counterpart. We give a proof for the convenience of the reader. 
      		Considering the restriction of $R\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$ to  polynomial pre-log algebras and the resulting left Kan extension, (here, we use the fact that $\mathcal{D}(R)^\wedge_p$ admits colimits)
      		we obtain a natural comparison map from derived log crystalline cohomology $dR\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$ to $R\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$. Both functors satisfy étale descent: this is clear for the underived version. As for derived log crystalline cohomology, it is enough to note that, since $dR\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)$ takes value in $p$-complete $\sR$-modules, we can check descent by reduction modulo $p$. Since by construction derived log crystalline cohomology is obtained by Kan extension from polynomials pre-log algebras over $\sR/p$, on any such algebra 
      		$\sP$,  we can choose a polynomial algebra $\widetilde{\sP}$ over $\sR$ as its smooth lift. Then, the derived log crystalline cohomology $R\Gamma_{\text{crys}}(\sP/\sR)$ is exactly computed by the $p$-completion of $\omega_{\widetilde{\sP}/\sR}^{*}$ as \eqref{eq;omegalogcryscomparison}. 
      		Reducing modulo $p$ again, this is precisely $\omega_{\sP/(\sR/p)}^{*}$, thus $dR\Gamma_{crys}(-/\sR)/p$ is $L\omega^*_{-/(\sR/p)}$, which satisfies étale descent. At this point, the claim of the Lemma follows again from the fact that         for log smooth pre-log algebras $\sA$ of Cartier type over $\sR/p$,
      		the comparison map 
      		$L\omega^*_{\sA/(\sR/p)}\to \omega^*_{\sA/(\sR/p)}$ is an equivalence (see for example \cite[Proposition 4.6]{BLPO-HKR}).
            Finally, the last statement follows from Remark \ref{rmk;multiplicativity}).

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:41:29.030242+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2351169168b4c85914f103820c5442ac5097307f07d54331756cd3b5d8a6e39","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2608.26565, 'A Horizon-Free Extrinsic Penrose Inequality'] For every $t\in(0,t_0)$, the following assertions hold.

 \]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:23:05.299975+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e24889e4fd5825bc288daedce508a877706cdda9e02cf792d8e1985c8e632777","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 14 (Aligned anisotropic Gaussian allocation) of arXiv:2608.21709, 'Posterior Information Dynamics of Diffusion Models for Linear Inverse Problems'] Let $X_0\sim\calN(0,\Sigma)$, where
\[
\Sigma=V\diag(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d)V^\top,
\qquad \lambda_i>0.
\]
Let $A\in\R^{d_y\times d}$ have full row rank and suppose the measurement
is aligned with the prior eigenbasis,
\[
A=U\begin{bmatrix}\diag(s_1,\ldots,s_{d_y})&0\end{bmatrix}V^\top,
\qquad
\Gamma=\sigma_y^2\Id_{d_y},
\]
with $s_i=0$ for $i>d_y$.  Define
\begin{equation}

B_{i,t}=a_t^2\lambda_i+\Delta_t,
\qquad
v_{i,t}=\frac{\lambda_i\Delta_t}{B_{i,t}},
\qquad
\tau_i^2=\left(\lambda_i^{-1}+s_i^2/\sigma_y^2\right)^{-1},
\qquad
\widetilde B_{i,t}=a_t^2\tau_i^2+\Delta_t,
\end{equation}
where $\tau_i^2=\lambda_i$ when $s_i=0$.  Under the joint law of $(X_t,R)$,
\begin{equation}

\E|s_{t,i}^{\rm prior}(X_t)|^2=\frac1{B_{i,t}},
\qquad
\E|g_{t,i}(X_t,R)|^2
=
\frac{a_t^2s_i^2\lambda_i^2}
{B_{i,t}^2(s_i^2v_{i,t}+\sigma_y^2)},
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}

\rho_i(t)
=
\frac{a_t^2s_i^2\lambda_i^2}
{B_{i,t}(s_i^2v_{i,t}+\sigma_y^2)}
=
\frac{B_{i,t}}{\widetilde B_{i,t}}-1.
\end{equation}
Consequently:
\begin{enumerate}
\item As $a_t\to0$,
\[
\rho_i(t)=
\frac{a_t^2s_i^2\lambda_i^2}{s_i^2\lambda_i+\sigma_y^2}+O(a_t^4).
\]
\item For $s_i>0$, $\rho_i(t)$ is strictly increasing along the reverse
trajectory, with low-noise limit $s_i^2\lambda_i/\sigma_y^2$, and
\begin{equation}

\rho_i(t)=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\widetilde B_{i,t}=\frac12B_{i,t}.
\end{equation}
Thus, within this aligned linear-Gaussian model, $\rho_i=1$ is a
variance-halving, equal-Fisher-energy reference level.  It is crossed at a
unique interior noise level iff $s_i^2\lambda_i>\sigma_y^2$; when
$s_i^2\lambda_i=\sigma_y^2$, it is attained only at the clean endpoint.
\item Since the exact force is null on unmeasured aligned coordinates,
\begin{equation}

\rho_t^{\rm global}=\omega_t\rho_t^{\rm row},
\qquad
\omega_t=
\frac{\sum_{i:s_i>0}B_{i,t}^{-1}}{\sum_{i=1}^dB_{i,t}^{-1}}.
\end{equation}
For an isotropic prior, $\omega_t=d_y/d$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

In the critical beta-splitting random tree on n leaves, closed into a cycle, take a uniformly random leaf and the leaf r places further round the cycle. Aldous and Janson (The critical beta-splitting random tree II: overview and open problems, arXiv:2303.02529, Section 3.9, Open Problem 1) asked for a proof that the correlation of the two leaf heights tends to 1 - alpha when log r_n / log n tends to alpha in [0, 1]. The paper proves that, uniformly in 1 <= r <= n/2, the covariance of the two heights is sigma^2 log(n/r) + O(sqrt(log n)) and the variance of one height is sigma^2 log n + O(sqrt(log n)), with sigma^2 = 2 zeta(3)/zeta(2)^3, so the correlation equals 1 - log r / log n + O((log n)^(-1/2)). The proof uses a potential of each leaf's position in its clade that decreases at rate zeta(2) up to square-integrable errors, and compares the two martingales it produces up to the cut that separates the two leaves. Exact rational checks, a Monte Carlo simulation and a Lean 4 file accompany the paper. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/beta-splitting-leaf-correlation (commit e337fd88d00f). Not refereed.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:45:01.899018+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e25cf4f546bd223fd5788f3c0c2ce12c7c0495999a782eb032a5b2e26609f170","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2512.19897, 'On the convoy of the ASEP speed process'] Let $X_n$ be a discrete Markov chain on $\mathbb{N}$, with transition probabilities
    \[
    \mathbb{P}_{ij} := \mathbb{P}\left(X_{n+1} = j | X_n = i\right).
    \]
    We say that $X_n$ is a birth-death chain if its transition probabilities $\mathbb{P}_{ij}$ is tridiagonal; that is, 
    \[
    P_{ij} = 0, \text{if} \quad |i-j|>1.
    \]
    In this case, the nonzero entries are given by $P_{i,i} = r_i, P_{i,i+1} = p_i, P_{i,i-1} = q_i$. We also define the m step transition probabilities,
    \[
    \mathbb{P}^{m}_{ij} := \mathbb{P}\left(X_{n+m} = j | X_n = i\right).
    \]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.179516+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2625d957dbeafa21c7d1caca97d4ada8270ebbc0476643f8dc29e54931a3975","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 93 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recalling Definitions \ref{d:SDE.classification.sym}--\ref{d:measure.classes.sym}, we have

\begin{proof}
We repeat the most relevant part of Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification.sym} for the first assertion:

The $\svi$ and $\svii$ classes
 differ only in the constraint on $p$: the $\svi$ class satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.6} (i.e. $p(\epsilon) \ge 1-\epsilon$, among other conditions) while the $\svii$ class satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.7} (i.e. $p\equiv 1$). Consider any
	\[\mu = \mu^\sym(q_*=0,b,\sigma,p,\zeta=\zeta_0)
	 \in \cM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\,,\]
corresponding to controls
	\[(q_*=0,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta=\delta_0,\zeta^\Ising=\delta_0) \in \Adm^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\,.\]
In particular, $p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.6}.
Recall the notation of Definition~\ref{d:X.adm}: 
we have $(b,\sigma) \in \Adm(0;p,f)$
for budget function $f(t) = (\bbE w_t)^2 / \alpha$, so
    \[
        \acute\mu = \mu(q_*=0,b,\sigma,p,\zeta=\zeta_0) \in \cM(0;p,f)\,.
    \]
Note that $\mu = \sym(\acute\mu)$.
Now consider the functions $\tilde p, \hat p \in \incr([0,1];[0,1])$ given by $\tilde p \equiv 1$ and
    \[
        \hat p(t) = \begin{cases}
            p(\epsilon) & t\in [0,\epsilon) \,, \\
            p(t) & t \in [\epsilon,1]\,.
        \end{cases}
    \]
    Since the restrictions of $p$ and $\hat p$ to $[\epsilon,1]$ agree, Proposition~\ref{p:continuity.in.p.near.0} implies
    \beq
        d_\cH\Big(\cM(0;p,f),\cM(0;\hat p,f)\Big) 
        \le \Big(9(1+1/\alpha) \epsilon\Big)^{1/2}\,,

    for $\cM(0;p,f)$ specified in Definition~\ref{d:X.adm}.
    Since $p$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.6}, we have $p(\epsilon) \ge 1-\epsilon$, and so
    \[
        \|\hat p' - \tilde p'\|_1
        =\|\hat p' \|_1 
        = \hat p(1) - \hat p(\epsilon)
        = p(1) - p(\epsilon)
        \le \epsilon\,.
    \]
    Then Proposition~\ref{p:continuity.in.p} implies
    \beq
        d_\cH\Big(\cM(0;\hat p,f),\cM(0;\tilde p,f)\Big) 
        \le \Big(6(1+1/\alpha) \epsilon\Big)^{1/2}\,.
    \eeq
    For some $\tilde\epsilon = \tilde\epsilon(\epsilon)$ tending to $0$ as $\epsilon \rightarrow 0$, \eqref{e:grt.in.spr.hausdorff1} and \eqref{e:grt.in.spr.hausdorff2} imply the existence of $\tilde \mu \in \cM(0;\tilde p,f)$ such that
    (since $\sym$ is a contraction)
    \beq
        \bbW_2\Big(
        \mu=\sym(\acute{\mu}), 
        \sym(\tilde \mu)
        \Big) 
        \le \bbW_2(\acute \mu,\tilde \mu)
        \le \tilde\epsilon\,.
    \eeq
    Let $\tilde\mu$ be attained by controls $(\tilde b,\tilde \sigma) \in \Adm(0;\tilde p,f)$, i.e.,
    \[
        \tilde\mu = \mu(q_*=0,\tilde b,\tilde \sigma,\tilde p,\zeta=\zeta_0)\,.
    \]
Since $\tilde{p}\equiv1$ satisfies condition~\ref{it:3.7}, we have 
    \[
        (q_*=0,\tilde b,\tilde \sigma,w,\tilde p,\zeta=\delta_0,\zeta^\Ising=\delta_0) 
        \in \Adm^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;\epsilon)\,,
    \]
    and therefore $\sym(\tilde\mu) \in \cM^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;\epsilon)$. 
    Since for all $\mu \in \cM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$ we can find such $\sym(\tilde\mu)$ satisfying \eqref{e:great.in.spr.sym.W2}, we conclude
    \[
        \cM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon) 
        \subseteq 
        \cB_{\tilde\epsilon}\Big( \sM^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;\epsilon) \Big)\,.
    \]
Adjusting $\tilde\epsilon$ gives
    \[
        \cB_\epsilon\Big( \cM^{\svi,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon) \Big)
        \subseteq 
        \cB_{\tilde\epsilon}\Big( \sM^{\svii,\sym}(\alpha,0;\tilde\epsilon) \Big)\,.
    \]
Recalling Definition~\ref{d:measure.classes.sym}, 
taking a union over $L$ and an intersection over $\epsilon$ proves the first assertion.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:31:02.817682+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e26e6aa63ec9ac5c4e9e517f98bf9c1567adb7f91529aecc36ee41c1f43814b1","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:factorial-box-divisibility of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Let $d,t\geq0$ be integers, let $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_t$ be positive
integers, put $R=\ell_1\cdots\ell_t$, and, for an indeterminate $x$, set
\[
 \Psi_{\boldsymbol\ell,d}(x)
 =\sum_{0\leq j_i<\ell_i}
   \binom{x-j_1-\cdots-j_t+d}{d}.
\]
Here $\binom{X}{d}=X(X-1)\cdots(X-d+1)/d!$ is the generalized binomial
polynomial (with $\binom{X}{0}=1$).
There is a universal polynomial
\[
 F_{d,t}(X,L_1,\ldots,L_t)
 \in\mathbb Z[X,L_1,\ldots,L_t]
\]
of degree $d$ in $X$ such that, after the specialization
$X=x$ and $L_i=\ell_i$,
\begin{equation}
 (d+t)!\,\Psi_{\boldsymbol\ell,d}(x)
 =R F_{d,t}(x,\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_t).
\end{equation}
Its leading coefficient in $X$ is $(d+t)!/d!$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:59:45.020469+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e28789073f4b71652d0652e82f8dfc31af214119cf8091a74d240e5de06a4557","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:CBess of arXiv:2605.15545, 'Crossover from subcritical to critical decay: \\ random walk, self-avoiding walk, percolat'] Let $d\ge 1$ and $\nu = (d-2)/2$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:37:15.062605+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e290d389ee1d213943133d51282ad804808edce692d39fdb23f6883f94eb7031","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2607.11756, 'Full replica symmetry breaking in the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model'] Suppose that
\[
 0<a<b\le1,
 \qquad
 \alpha(s)=m\in(0,1)
 \quad(a<s<b).
\]
Set
\[
 T=\beta^2(b-a),
 \qquad
 \sigma(t)=a+\frac{t}{\beta^2},
 \qquad
 U(t,x)=u(\sigma(t),x),
 \qquad 0\le t<T.
\]
Let $\widehat X_t=X_{\sigma(t)}$, denote its density by $p(t,\cdot)$,
and define
\begin{equation}
 f(t,x)=p(t,x)\e^{-mU(t,x)},
 \qquad
 V(t,x)=-\log f(t,x).
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 U_t=-\frac12(U_{xx}+mU_x^2),
 \qquad
 f_t=\frac12f_{xx}
\end{equation}
on $(0,T)\times\R$, and
\begin{equation}
 V_x\ge0,
 \qquad V_{xx}\ge0,
 \qquad V_{xxx}\le0
 \qquad\text{on }(0,T)\times(0,\infty).
\end{equation}

For $0\le B<1$, let $x=x(t,B)\ge0$ be the inverse slope coordinate
\[
 B=U_x(t,x),
\]
and set
\[
 C(t,B)=U_{xx}(t,x(t,B)).
\]
Define
\begin{align}
 z&=-\frac12C_B=(m+K)B,
 &J&=K+BK_B,                                      \\
 \Phi&=2z^2-mC,
 &N&=V_x+KB,                                      \\
 R_1&=KBV_x+\frac12(KB)^2,
 &R_V&=\frac12(V_x^2-V_{xx}),                     \\
 R_0&=2CJ-\frac m2C-\frac12z^2,
 &G&=2Cz(3zJ-CJ_B),                               \\
 L&=CJ-z(N+z),                                    \\
 w(t,B)&=2p(t,x(t,B))C(t,B).                      
\end{align}
Every derivative of $V$ appearing in slope coordinates is evaluated at
$(t,x(t,B))$.

Fix a compact interval $I\subset[0,T)$, so that $\max I<T$. There are constants
$c_I,C_I>0$ such that, for every $t\in I$ and $x\in\R$,
\begin{align}
 c_I\e^{-C_Ix^2}
 &\le f(t,x)\le C_I\e^{-c_Ix^2},                 \\
 p(t,x)&\le C_I\e^{-c_Ix^2},                     \\
 |V_x(t,x)|&\le C_I(1+|x|),                      \\
 0\le V_{xx}(t,x)&\le C_I,                       \\
 |V_{xxx}(t,x)|&\le C_I.                         
\end{align}
Consequently, for every $A\ge0$ and integer $k\ge0$, there are
constants $c_{I,A,k},C_{I,A,k}>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{t\in I}\int_R^\infty
 p(t,x)(1+x)^k\e^{Ax}\dd x
 \le C_{I,A,k}\e^{-c_{I,A,k}R^2},
 \qquad R\ge0.
\end{equation}

There are constants $A_I,C_I'<\infty$ such that, for $t\in I$ and
$0\le B<1$,
\begin{align}
 &|N|+|\Phi|+|G|+|R_0|+|(R_0)_B|
 +|R_1|+|(R_1)_B|\notag\\
 &\qquad
 +|R_V|+|(R_V)_B|+|L|+|L_B|
 \le C_I'\e^{A_Ix(t,B)}.                         
\end{align}
If $I\Subset(0,T)$, then, with the time derivative taken at fixed
$B$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\frac{\partial_t(w\Phi)}w\right|
 \le C_I'\e^{A_Ix(t,B)}.
\end{equation}

More generally, suppose $Q$ is continuous on $I\times[0,1)$ and
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 |Q(t,B)|\le C\e^{Ax(t,B)}
\end{equation}
for some $A,C<\infty$. Then
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{t\in I}\int_0^1w(t,B)|Q(t,B)|\dd B<\infty.
\end{equation}
If
\[
 B_I(R)=\sup_{t\in I}U_x(t,R),
\]
then
\[
 B_I(R)<1,
 \qquad
 B_I(R)\uparrow1
 \quad(R\to\infty),
\]
and
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{t\in I}\int_{B_I(R)}^1w(t,B)|Q(t,B)|\dd B
 \le C_{I,Q}\e^{-c_{I,Q}R^2}.
\end{equation}

Define
\begin{equation}
 F(t,B)=\int_B^1w(t,D)\Phi(t,D)\dd D.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 |F(t,B)|\le C_I\e^{-c_Ix(t,B)^2}.
\end{equation}
In particular, if $Q$ satisfies \eqref{eq:admissible-Q}, then
\begin{equation}
 F(t,B)Q(t,B)\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(B\uparrow1),
\end{equation}
uniformly for $t\in I$, and
\begin{equation}
 w(t,B)C(t,B)z(t,B)\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(B\uparrow1)
\end{equation}
uniformly for $t\in I$.

If $I\Subset(0,T)$, the function
\begin{equation}
 H(t)=\int_0^1w(t,B)\Phi(t,B)\dd B
\end{equation}
belongs to $C^1(I)$, with
\begin{equation}
 H'(t)=\int_0^1\partial_t(w\Phi)(t,B)\dd B.
\end{equation}
At any $t\in(0,T)$ for which $H(t)=0$, one has $F(t,0)=0$ and
\begin{equation}
 \int_0^1w\Phi R_0\dd B
 =\int_0^1F(R_0)_B\dd B
 =\int_0^1w\tau(R_0)_B\dd B,
 \qquad \tau=\frac Fw.
\end{equation}
At such a centered time, the function
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H(B)=w(B)C(B)z(B)-F(B)
\end{equation}
extends to an absolutely continuous function on $[0,1]$, satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H_B=wL
 \qquad\text{a.e.\ on }(0,1),
\end{equation}
and has
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H(0)=\mathcal H(1)=0.
\end{equation}
In particular,
\b","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["H is a Hilbert space","a is bounded sesquilinear on H × H","the claimed coercivity constant α > 0 must hold on all of H"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:42.772311+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, elliptic PDE, finite element analysis","id":"claim_e2aa108ac361aa69126eca86591b9d8beaedd4bc7bdd886699f31c317c3ce026","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Load-bearing hypothesis: Re a(u, u) ≥ α‖u‖² for all u in the Hilbert space H, with a fixed α > 0 and the norm of H itself (the trial and test space). What fails: strict positivity a(u, u) > 0 for u ≠ 0, or injectivity of the associated operator, is not enough - the solution operator need not be bounded and the problem need not be solvable. Counterexample 1: H = ℓ², a(u, v) = Σ_{n ≥ 1} n^{-1} u_n conj(v_n). Then a is bounded (C = 1), Hermitian, and a(u, u) > 0 for every u ≠ 0, but the associated operator is the injective compact diagonal operator with entries 1/n, whose range is not closed. For f = (1/n)_n ∈ ℓ², the equation a(u, v) = ⟨f, v⟩ for all v forces u_n = 1 for all n, which is not in ℓ²: no solution exists. Counterexample 2 (the practical one): on a bounded connected Lipschitz domain Ω, a(u, v) = ∫_Ω ∇u·∇v̄ on H = H¹(Ω) is bounded and positive semidefinite but not coercive, since a(1, 1) = 0; the Neumann problem −Δu = f, ∂_ν u = 0 is solvable only under the compatibility condition ∫_Ω f = 0, and is never uniquely solvable in H¹(Ω) (constants can be added). Coercivity is recovered only on the subspace {u ∈ H¹(Ω) : ∫_Ω u = 0} via the Poincaré-Wirtinger inequality; on H_0^1(Ω) it is recovered via the Poincaré inequality, which is why the Dirichlet problem is the easy case. Other silent hypotheses: H must be complete (a coercive bounded form on a dense non-closed subspace gives no existence), and the coercivity constant α must be uniform, not depending on u. Note a is not assumed symmetric - that part is genuinely unnecessary. For non-coercive but well-posed problems (e.g. mixed or saddle point formulations, convection dominated problems, different trial and test spaces), the correct replacement is the Banach-Necas-Babuska inf-sup theorem: an inf-sup condition on a plus injectivity of the adjoint form, of which coercivity is only a sufficient condition.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.095016+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2bdc304174e9fecc0b830e21a47837cec922f95e7efd160273f5cec30664a8e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:paired-resource of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] A safe gate and its $C$-degree are as in
(def:circuit-primitives of the paper); the amplified estimate is proved in
(lem:safe of the paper).

For an active eigenframe of an arbitrary self-adjoint pure-Weyl $C$, put
\[
 (F_Cx)_a=\lambda_aA_a^Tx,
 \qquad
 F_C^*F_C=Q_2:=-\sum_a\lambda_a^2A_a^2,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Tr} Q_2=2\|C\|_2^2.
\tag{2.2.1}
\]
A concrete carrier for these two fronts is obtained as follows.  Let
$E_C=\ell^2(I_C)$ be the active label space,
$J_C:E_C\to\Lambda^2H$ the isometry $J_Ce_a=A_a$, and
\[
 \iota_\wedge A=2^{-1/2}\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}e_i\otimes e_j,
 \qquad
 \mathsf W_C=(\iota_\wedge J_C)\otimes I_H,
\]
and define the one-hole column
\[
 (T_Cx)_{ijk}=\sum_\ell C_{ij,k\ell}x_\ell.
\tag{2.2.2}
\]
With the ordered-pair convention
$C_{ij,k\ell}=\sum_a\lambda_a(A_a)_{ij}(A_a)_{k\ell}$,
one has the exact typed identity
\[
 \mathsf W_CF_C=-2^{-1/2}T_C,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak q_C^{\rm hole}
 :=\mathsf W_CF_CF_C^*\mathsf W_C^*
 =\frac12T_CT_C^*.
\tag{2.2.3}
\]
Thus the open token is a specified three-strand operator, up to the signed
leg permutations recorded by its port state; it is not defined merely by
having a prescribed scalar cap.  Moreover
\[
 T_C^*T_C=2Q_2,
 \qquad
 T_C=P_{[2,1]_0}T_C,
\tag{2.2.4}
\]
where $P_{[2,1]_0}$ is the trace-free hook projection on the first three
indices.

A paired-front atom contains the two correlated Hilbert--Schmidt fronts
of this single $F_C$ pair, equivalently the concrete hole
$\mathfrak q_C^{\rm hole}$ in (eq:2.2.3 of the paper), any safe left and right gates, and
an untouched typed ancillary boundary $E$.  Let $\mathfrak M_C^{\rm alg}(E)$ be
the algebraic span of these atoms.  Its projective norm is the infimum,
over all atomic presentations, of the sum of the products of the two
front Hilbert--Schmidt norms and all safe-gate operator-norm bounds.  The
completion is denoted $\mathfrak M_C(E)$.  Its distinguished token
$\mathfrak q_C$ satisfies
\[
 \|\mathfrak q_C\|_{\mathfrak M_C}\le\operatorname{Tr} Q_2=2\|C\|_2^2.
\tag{2.2.5}
\]
The two fronts form one resource: they may move or fuse but are never
duplicated.  Equality in (eq:2.2.5 of the paper) is not asserted, and the cap identity
does not identify this open pair with a differently typed polar pair.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:16:33.593334+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e2fc1d175bae9a5f00102fd544cb38332daba9209acf4dfe55424ec6326d61de","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Abstract of arXiv:2609.02755, 'The Sharp Rate of Probabilistically Strong Convergence to the KPZ Equation'] One of the most common descriptions of solutions of singular SPDEs is their characterisation as the limit of solutions of renormalised smooth random PDEs. We quantify the speed of this convergence in the case of the KPZ equation. In particular, we show that the na\\\"ive guess that the rate is given by the distance of the noise regularity from the endpoint regularity for well-posedness is not correct. Instead, we obtain convergence at the larger rate $1/2$ and show that this rate is sharp. This is achieved by considering the equation satisfied by the rescaled error, which is critical for variance blowup, and showing that this equation has a limit given by an affine linear singular SPDE driven by a new, independent noise. This result can be alternatively interpreted as identifying the asymptotic size and law of fluctuations of the solutions of the KPZ equation driven by mollified noise around their singular limit.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:52:51.763133+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3223d8c3fad1c6c8b05cff9dce34e7d45416a97ea810ebf9d22dca071224981","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:classicalStochStab of arXiv:2604.28068, 'Mean-square Stability and Bifurcations for Dissipative SDEs'] Suppose that $x^*$ is an equilibrium of the SDE (equation eq:main_d of the paper) and let
$X$ be a global solution with initial data $X_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$. Then $Y=X-x^*$ is a solution of the centered SDE (equation eq:main_YSDE of the paper) with $Y_0=X_0-x^*$. We say that the equilibrium  $x^*$ is
\begin{enumerate}
\item stable in probability for $t\geq 0$ if  for any  $s\geq 0$ and $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
\lim_{Y_0\to 0}\mathbb{P}\left[\sup_{t>s}\|Y(t)\|>\varepsilon\right]=0;
\]
\item asymptotically stable in probability if  it is stable in probability and 
\[
\lim_{Y_0\to 0}\mathbb{P}\left[\lim_{t\to\infty}\|Y(t)\|=0\right]=1;
\]
\item pth-moment stable if for any $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a $\delta> 0$ such that
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[\|Y(t)\|^p\right]<\varepsilon,\quad t\geq 0,
\]
whenever $\|Y_0\|^p<\delta$; if $p=2$, the equilibrium is said to be mean-square stable;
\item globally pth-moment asymptotically stable if  it is pth-moment stable, and for all $Y_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\|Y(t)\|^p\right]=0;
\] 
if $p=2$, the equilibrium is said to be mean-square asymptotically stable;
\item a.s.~stable if  for any $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta> 0$ such that
\[
\|Y(t)\|<\varepsilon,\quad t\geq 0,\quad a.s,
\] 
whenever $\|Y_0\|<\delta$;
\item globally a.s.~asymptotically stable if  for all $Y_0\in\mathbb{R}^d$, 
\[
\lim_{t\to \infty}\|Y(t)\|=0\quad a.s.
\]
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:37:08.315976+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e32440cc41f68abac6ac9d2743f0d73cab20e4d42ceb9a3318db378f5633265b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:partialflow of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(N\) be a compact manifold.
A \emph{semiflow} on \(N\) is a continuous map \(\varphi\) mapping a subset \(U\subset N\times \mathbb{R}\) to \(N\), which satisfies that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item for each \(x\in N\), \(\{t\in \mathbb{R}:(x,t)\in U\}\) is a closed interval of \(\mathbb{R}\) and contains \(0\).

\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

$\bar{D}^{\frozen,\RomII}$) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In addition to Lemma~\ref{l:barD.II.second} we have the quenched second moment bound
	\[\max\bigg\{
	\frac{\bE[\Delta\bar{D}^{\RomII}(q_d)^2]}{p(q_d)}
	: 0\le d\le \dmax-1\bigg\}
	\le \frac{\SMAX_N(\RomII)^2 \BUCKETS \delta}{M}\,,\]
where $\SMAX_N(\RomII)$ is a random variable satisfying the bound
	\[\P\Big(\SMAX_N(\RomII) \ge \log N\Big)
	\le\exp\bigg(-\frac{(\log N)^2}{L^{O(1)}}\bigg)\,.\]
The same bound holds with $\bar{D}^{\frozen,\RomII}$ in place of
$\bar{D}^{\RomII}$.

\begin{proof} Recall that
we can rewrite \eqref{e:drift.error.II} as
	\[
	\frac{\Delta\bar{D}^{\RomII}(q_d)}{(p_d)^{1/2}}
	= 
	\frac{(\delta_d)^{1/2}}{|B|^{1/2}}
	\bigg(\frac{1}{N^{1/2}}\sum_{a\in B}
	\frac{\bar{\bg}^a(q_d)}{|B|^{1/2}},\by(q_{d+1})\bigg)
	\equiv
	\frac{(\delta_d)^{1/2}}{|B|^{1/2}}
	\bigg( \frac{\bar{\bg}^B(q_d)}{N^{1/2}},\by(q_{d+1}) \bigg)\,.
	\]
If we define the random variable
	\[
	\SMAX_N(\RomII)
	\equiv\max
	\bigg\{
	\bigg|
	\bigg( \frac{\bar{\bg}^B(q_d)}{N^{1/2}},\by(q_{d+1}) \bigg)
	\bigg|
	: 
	0\le d\le \dmax-1,
	B\in \mathcal{B}(q_d)
	\bigg\}\,,
	\]
then we have the quenched second moment bound
	\[
	\frac{\bE[\Delta\bar{D}^{\RomII}(q_d)^2]}{p_d}
	= \frac{\delta_d}{M}\sum_{B\in\mathcal{B}(q_d)}
	\bigg( \frac{\bar{\bg}^B(q_d)}{N^{1/2}},\by \bigg)^2
	\le \frac{\SMAX_N(\RomII)^2\BUCKETS\delta}{M}\,,
	\]
Note that for any $B\subseteq[M]$ we have
$\bar{\bg}^B= \bar{\bG}^\st \be_B$, so $\|\bar{\bg}^B\| \le\|\bar{\bG}\|_\textup{op}$. It then follows from Lemma~\ref{l:wishart} that for $C(\alpha)$ large enough, we have 
	\beq
	\P\Big(\|\bar{\bg}^B\|^2 \ge 
	C(\alpha) N \textup{ for any }B\subseteq[M]\Big)
	\le \frac{1}{2^N}\,.
	\eeq
The vectors $(\bar{\bg}^B : B\in\mathcal{B}(q_d))$ are measurable with respect to $\cG(q_d)$, so applying Lemma~\ref{l:y.subgaus} gives
	\begin{align*}
	&\P\Big(\SMAX_N(\RomII) \ge \log N\Big)
	=\P\bigg(
	\bigg|
	\bigg( \frac{\bar{\bg}^B(q_d)}{N^{1/2}},\by(q_{d+1}) \bigg)
	\bigg|
		\ge \log N
	\textup{ for any } 0\le d\le \dmax- 1, B \in \mathcal{B}(q_d)
	\bigg)\\
	&\qquad\le
	\dmax\BUCKETS
	\bigg\{ \frac{1}{2^N}
	+ \exp\bigg(-\frac{(\log N)^2}{L^{O(1)}}\bigg)
	\bigg\}
	\le\exp\bigg(-\frac{(\log N)^2}{L^{O(1)}}\bigg)
	\,,
	\end{align*}
where the $1/2^N$ in the second line comes from \eqref{e:II.union.bound}, and the final simplification uses Assumption~\ref{a:params}. This proves the claim for $\bar{D}^{\RomII}$, and the claim for
$\bar{D}^{\frozen,\RomII}$ follows by using \eqref{e:barD.vs.plus}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:36:49.928517+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e347ff1c8563c534518f837e5edb616a903a413aaa066bbb80a24db7a809b259","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Openproblem op:mather-measures of arXiv:2609.01557, '$L^\infty$ Variational Approximation of the Aubry Set'] Conceptually, (equation eq:AtoM of the paper) shows that the Mather set can, in principle, be recovered from the projected Aubry set $\mathcal A$ together with the limiting function $u_\infty$. However, this characterization is not particularly convenient from a numerical point of view. It is therefore natural to ask whether Evans' variational approximation also provides a more direct way to recover the projected Mather set $\mathcal M$, or equivalently the full Mather set $\widetilde{\mathcal M}$.

Let
\[
\sigma_k(x)
:=
\frac{e^{kH(Du_k(x),x)}}
{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb T^n}
e^{kH(Du_k(y),y)}\,dy}.
\]
The pair \((u_k,\sigma_k)\) is also the logarithmically coupled stationary mean-field game associated with Evans' variational approximation; see [GY20].
Thanks to [Evans03, Evans04], along a subsequence,
\[
\sigma_{k_j}\rightharpoonup \sigma
\qquad\text{weakly in the sense of measures},
\]
where \(\sigma\) is a projected Mather measure. In dimension one, under a
suitable nondegeneracy condition, \(\operatorname{spt}(\sigma)\) coincides
with the whole projected Mather set (i.e., $\operatorname{spt}(\sigma)=\mathcal M$),  whereas degeneracy may lead to further
selection ([GISMY10]). What is the corresponding picture in higher dimensions? In
particular, under what conditions does
\[
\operatorname{spt}(\sigma)=\mathcal M,
\]
and what determines the subset of \(\mathcal M\) selected when this equality
fails? (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:28:53.635755+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e36eb431d095075c6f6163f9ba614c828bc78fb8f503f83a0d1c1374880e9a66","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2605.13512, '2605.13512'] Fix $(x,t)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R_+$ and define
\[
F_{x,t}(q):=v_0(q)-g^q(x-q,t),
\qquad q\in [r_L(x,t),r_U(x,t)],
\]
where $r_L(x,t),r_U(x,t)$ are as in Corollary \ref{cor: restriction to compact interval}. Define the two contact sets
\[
A_0(x,t):=\{q\in [r_L,r_U]: q\le x,\ g^q(x-q,t)=0\},
\]
and
\[
A_1(x,t):=\{q\in [r_L,r_U]: q\ge x,\ g^q(x-q,t)=q-x\}.
\]
Then
\[
\max_{q\in[r_L,r_U]}F_{x,t}(q)
=
\max_{q\in [r_L,r_U]\setminus (\operatorname{int}A_0(x,t)\cup \operatorname{int}A_1(x,t))}F_{x,t}(q).
\]
In particular, there exists a maximiser $q^*$ such that either
\[
g^{q^*}(x-q^*,t)>\max\{0,q^*-x\},
\]
or $q^*$ is an endpoint of a connected component of $A_0(x,t)$ or of $A_1(x,t)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:58:09.065659+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e380bb9ad37ab55f3cadd27be2b8d0e39bc3a8d24d464e6e40f8dbc84dd9e9b6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 (Convergence in path space) of arXiv:2606.27117, 'Occupation-Time Fluctuations of an Age-Dependent Branching System Driven by Poisson Immigr'] Let $F$ be an absolutely continuous lifetime distribution such that
\[
F(0)=0,\quad F(x)<1 \ \textit{\ for \ all } \ x\ge 0,\quad \textit{and}\quad
1-F(t)\sim\frac{1}{t^{\gamma}\Gamma(1-\gamma)}\quad\mbox{with}\quad\gamma<1.
\]

Let $0<\alpha<d<(1+\gamma)\alpha$, and $F_T^2 = T^{3+\gamma-\frac{d}{\alpha}}.$
Then $\X_T$ converges weakly to $\X$ in $C([0,\Upsilon],{\cal S}'(\mathbb{R}^d))$ as $T\to\infty$ for any $\Upsilon>0$, where $\X:=\{\X(t),\ t\ge 0\}$ is a centered Gaussian process with covariance functional given by
$$
\mathrm{Cov}\big(\langle \X(s),\varphi\rangle,\langle \X(t),\psi\rangle\big)
=
\frac{\gamma\Gamma(1/\alpha)\langle\lambda,\varphi\rangle\langle\lambda,\psi\rangle}
{2(\frac{d}{\alpha}-1)(2-\frac{d}{\alpha})(3-\frac{d}{\alpha})
\pi\alpha\Gamma(1+\gamma)} C(s,t),
$$
where
\begin{align}
\nonumber
C(s,t)
&=
\int_0^s w^{\gamma-1}\Bigg[
3(s-w)^{\b} + (t-w)^{\b}

+\frac{\b}{\gamma}w\Big(
(t-w)^{2-\frac{d}{\alpha}} - (s-w)^{2-\frac{d}{\alpha}}
\Big)
-(t+s-2w)^{\b}
\Bigg]\,dw,
\\ 
&\qquad 0\le s\le t,\quad \varphi,\psi\in\E.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["conditioned Galton-Watson (simply generated) tree with n vertices","N_d = number of vertices of outdegree d"],"created_at":"2026-09-24T23:46:59.318625+00:00","domain":"probability/random trees","id":"claim_e3850e9afeb448f99ec9561d012acf69","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Janson's Problem 20.2 (Probability Surveys 2012, Section 20.2) asks whether the outdegree counts N_d of a conditioned Galton-Watson (simply generated) tree are asymptotically normal. (a) nu = 1 with finite variance: yes, jointly with the covariances (Janson, Random Structures Algorithms 48 (2016), Theorem 1.13 with Example 2.2 and Section 8). (b) nu = 1 with infinite variance and (c) nu < 1: yes when the offspring law is regularly varying (Thevenin, Electron. J. Probab. 25 (2020), Theorems 6.2 and 6.7, variance pi_d(1 - pi_d)), but not in general. A subcritical law whose bulk sits on {0, 1}, with two rare atoms at (1 - q - c) n_r +/- A sqrt(n_r), each of probability n_r^{-4}, makes the conditioned tree carry exactly one of the two with probability tending to 1/2 each, so N_1 = n pi_1 -/+ A sqrt(n) up to smaller terms, a near two-point law (Theorem A, full proof); the critical infinite-variance case is the same construction with the pair straddling the missing mass of an absent rarer atom (Theorem B, a sketch that still needs a lattice local moderate-deviation expansion). Thevenin's conjecture that normality holds for every such law is therefore false. The regularly varying case survives because the giant's law is locally flat at scale sqrt(n).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["product measure on a FINITE index set","BK: both events increasing","Reimer: no monotonicity hypothesis"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.542992+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3854fb8e108d83f54f7a2c762956ced396b14b16573131eabefa9f8eab4f84b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let P be a product measure on {0,1}^E with E FINITE. For events A and B define the DISJOINT OCCURRENCE A box B as the set of configurations omega for which there exist DISJOINT sets of coordinates K and L such that every configuration agreeing with omega on K lies in A and every configuration agreeing with omega on L lies in B - informally, A and B occur for disjoint reasons. VAN DEN BERG-KESTEN: if A and B are both INCREASING then P(A box B) <= P(A) P(B). REIMER: the same inequality holds for ARBITRARY events A and B, with no monotonicity hypothesis. The direction is opposite to Harris-FKG, which is the point: increasing events are positively correlated, but requiring them to occur on disjoint witnesses destroys that correlation and more. The finiteness of E is a genuine hypothesis of the standard statements; infinite index sets are handled by approximation, and the definition of disjoint occurrence itself needs care there. Typical use: bounding the probability of two disjoint open crossings, or of a self-avoiding open path of length n, by a product. [van den Berg and Kesten (1985); Reimer (2000), Combin. Probab. Comput. 9; see Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Theorem 2.12]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:43:16.143603+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e39c9e003296cf45dab228636af8df06943a82b31b2ed08c21f86b11bc5848a6","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 2 (Spectral radius) of arXiv:2604.13134, '\bf From Gaussian to Gumbel: extreme eigenvalues of complex Ginibre products with exact ra'] Let \(X_n\), \(\alpha\), \(a_n\), \(v_\alpha\), \(q_1(j,\cdot)\), \(q_2(j,\cdot)\), and

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:09:34.487280+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3be3c9182f994af2806f0d42922ebf649a4ecf9e795918fbcd91230f3fe9f9f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn Coulomb gas correlations for a divisor on the Riemann sphere of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] Let the divisor
$$
\boldsymbol{\sigma}=\sum \sigma_j \cdot z_j,
$$
where $\left\{z_j\right\}_{j=1}^n$ is a finite set of distinct points on $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$.
The Coulomb gas correlation $C_{(b)}[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ is a differential of conformal dimension $\lambda_j$ at $z_j$, given by

\begin{equation}
\lambda_j=\lambda_b\left(\sigma_j\right) \equiv \frac{\sigma_j^2}{2}-\sigma_j b ,
\end{equation}

where $\lambda_b(\sigma)=\frac{\sigma^2}{2}-\sigma b \quad(\sigma \in \mathbb{C})$
whose value is given by

\begin{equation}
C_{(b)}[\boldsymbol{\sigma}] =\prod_{j<k}\left(z_j-z_k\right)^{\sigma_j \sigma_k} ,
\end{equation}
where the product is taken over all finite $z_j$ and $z_k$. 

This defines a holomorphic function of $\boldsymbol{z}$ on the configuration space
\[
\mathbb{C}_{\mathrm{distinct}}^n = \left\{ \boldsymbol{z} = (z_1, \ldots, z_n) \in \mathbb{C}^n \,\middle|\, z_j \neq z_k \text{ for } j \neq k \right\}.
\]
In general, the function is multivalued, and one must choose a single-valued branch for each factor $(z_j-z_k)^{\sigma_j\sigma_k}$, except in special cases where all $\sigma_j$ are integers. If all $\sigma_j$ are even integers, the function becomes single-valued and independent of the ordering of the product. In the special case where $\sigma_j = 1$ for all $j$, the correlation function coincides with the Vandermonde determinant.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:25:39.120731+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3cc1fa1154102f504e898815b49b8cceb927c121b826bbd2318d87db76d9089","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def: boundary connectivity event of arXiv:2606.13147, 'Scaling limits of the single-curve interface and outermost loops in the planar random fiel'] Write
$\Sigma_M^c=\{-1,1\}^{\partial\Lambda_M\cup (\Lambda_N\setminus\Lambda_M)}.$

For any $\xi\in \Sigma_M^c$, let
$
\mathcal P=\{x\in \partial \Lambda_M:\xi_x=1\}.
$
Let $\mathcal P_0,\mathcal P_1\subset \mathcal P$ be two disjoint subsets, and let $\mathcal U$ be a collection of mutually disjoint subsets of $\mathcal P$, each of which is also disjoint from $\mathcal P_0\cup \mathcal P_1$.

Define $\mathcal Y^{-}$ to be the event that $\mathcal P_0$ is not plus-connected to $\mathcal P_1$ inside $\Lambda_M$, and define $\mathcal Y^{+}$ to be the event that, for every $U\in \mathcal U$, the set $U$ is plus-connected to $\mathcal P_0$ inside $\Lambda_M$. We then write
$
\mathcal Y=\mathcal Y^{-}\cap \mathcal Y^{+}.
$

Next, let $\mathcal X^{-}$ be the event that there exists a $*$-minus circuit in the annulus
$
\Lambda_{M/2}\setminus \Lambda_{M/4},
$
and let $\mathcal X^{+}$ be the event that there exists a plus circuit in the same annulus which is plus-connected to $\mathcal P_0$. We define
$
\mathcal X=\mathcal X^{+}\cap \mathcal X^{-}.
$

Finally, set
$
\mathcal R=\mathcal Y\setminus \mathcal X,
\mathcal S=\mathcal X\cap \mathcal Y.
$
For simplicity, we use
$
X,X^{+},X^{-},Y,Y^{+},Y^{-},R,S\in\{0,1\}
$
to denote the indicator functions of the events
$
\mathcal X,\mathcal X^{+},\mathcal X^{-},\mathcal Y,\mathcal Y^{+},\mathcal Y^{-},\mathcal R,\mathcal S,
$
respectively.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:11:44.474714+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3dee286195256974c00320143178eec22488dc4238290cd51aec9f091188a29","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 37 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Suppose that $p$ is odd, $\chi$ is injective, $m$ is even, and the morphism $X\rightarrow X/G$ is an HKG cover. Let $l_1<\cdots<l_s$ be the lower jumps and let $u_1<\cdots<u_s$ be the upper jumps of the wild cyclic subgroup $H=C_{p^s}$ acting on the completion of the local ring of $X$ at the ramified point. For each $j\in\llbracket0,s\rrbracket$ let $H_{s-j}$ and $Y_j$ be as in Corollary \ref{C4} and, if $j\ge 1$, let 
$$\l_j:=l_j-1.$$ Then the following properties hold. 

\medskip
{\bf (1)} We have $\textup{g}_{Y_0}=0$ and for each $i\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket$ we have
\[
\textup{g}_{Y_i}=\frac{p-1}{2}\sum_{j=1}^i \l_jp^{i-j}.
\]

{\bf (2)} For each $i\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket$, $p-1$ divides $\textup{g}_{Y_i}$.

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} Let $\mathcal R_X$ be the $B_0[H]$-module of Proposition \ref{P5}(2). Then we have identities 
$$\frac{\textup{g}_{Y_i}-\textup{g}_{Y_{i-1}}}{p^i-p^{i-1}}=\frac{\l_i+(p-1)\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}\l_jp^{i-1-j}}{2p^{i-1}}=\frac{u_i-1}{2}$$
for each $i\in\llbracket1,s\rrbracket$ and hence a $B_0[H]$-linear isomorphism 
$$\mathcal R_X\cong\oplus_{i=1}^s \frac{\l_i+(p-1)\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}\l_jp^{i-1-j}}{2p^{i-1}}\mathcal B_i= \oplus_{i=1}^s \frac{u_i-1}{2}\mathcal B_i.$$

{\bf (4)} Let $\mathcal X$ be a smooth projective curve over $\Spec R$ whose reduction modulo $\upsilon$ is $X$ and such that there exists a homomorphism $\varrho:G\rightarrow\Aut(\mathcal X)$ that lifts $\rho$. Then the following properties hold.

\medskip\noindent
{\bf (4.a) (de Jong)} For each subgroup $\Delta$ of $G$, the quotient curve $\mathcal X/\Delta$ is smooth projective over $\Spec R$ with geometrically connected fibers.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (4.b)} For each subgroup $\Delta$ of $G$, the special fiber $(\mathcal X/\Delta)_k$ of $\mathcal X/\Delta$ is naturally identified with $X/\Delta$.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (4.c) (Chinburg--Guralnick--Harbater)} The KGB obstruction for the HKG cover $X\rightarrow X/G$ vanishes.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (4.d)} We have $B[H]$-linear isomorphisms
$$H^0(\mathcal X,\Omega_{\mathcal X})\otimes_R B\cong H^1(\mathcal X,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})\otimes_R B\cong\oplus_{i=1}^s \frac{u_i-1}{2}\mathcal B_i.$$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:57:28.221127+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3e9050bed568a5832fc609ed28297c290eb9df777f984c24eb78ffc28b92d99","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.17662, 'On the Strong Law of Large Numbers under Sublinear Expectations'] A \textit{sublinear expectation} $\mathbb{E}$ on $\mathcal{H}$ is a functional $\mathbb{E}\colon \mathcal{H} \to \overline{\mathbb{R}} := [-\infty, +\infty]$ satisfying the following properties for all $X, Y \in \mathcal{H}$:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item[(a)] \textit{Monotonicity.} If $X \geq Y$, then $\mathbb{E}[X] \geq \mathbb{E}[Y]$.
			\item[(b)] \textit{Constant preserving.} $\mathbb{E}[c] = c$, $\forall\, c \in \mathbb{R}$.
			\item[(c)] \textit{Positive homogeneity.} $\mathbb{E}[\lambda X] = \lambda\,\mathbb{E}[X]$, $\forall\, \lambda \geq 0$.
			\item[(d)] \textit{Subadditivity.} $\mathbb{E}[X + Y] \leq \mathbb{E}[X] + \mathbb{E}[Y]$, provided that $\mathbb{E}[X] + \mathbb{E}[Y]$ does not take the form $\infty - \infty$ or $-\infty + \infty$.
		\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:02:28.653269+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e3ed8a2095bd6054c4de10d9c2270c68eb0eb0119e3346760bd88d1b8453c55c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Def 39 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] Let $m < n$ be positive integers and $a_1, \dots, a_n, b_1 \dots b_n$ be integers.
Let $R = \mbC [x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be the polynomial ring endowed with a $\mbZ^2$-grading defined by the $2 \times n$ matrix
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
a_1 & \cdots & a_n \\
b_1 & \cdots & b_n 
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This means that the bi-degree of the variable $x_i$ is $(a_i, b_i) \in \mbZ^2$.
We denote by 
\begin{equation} 
\mbT \begin{pNiceArray}{ccc|ccc}[first-row]
x_1 & \dots & x_m & x_{m+1} & \dots & x_n \\
a_1 & \dots & a_m & a_{m+1} & \dots & a_n \\
b_1 & \dots & b_m & b_{m+1} & \dots & b_n
\end{pNiceArray}
\end{equation}
the toric variety whose Cox ring is $R$ and irrelevant ideal is 
\[
I = (x_1, \dots, x_m) \cap (x_{m+1}, \dots, x_n).
\]
In other words, this toric variety is the geometric quotient
\[
(\mbA^n_{x_1, \dots, x_n} \setminus V (I))/(\mbC^*)^2,
\]
where the $(\mbC^*)^2$-action is defined by
\[
(\lambda, \mu) \cdot (x_1, \dots, x_n) = (\lambda^{a_1} \mu^{b_1} x_1, \dots, \lambda^{a_n} \mu^{b_n} x_n).
\]
For a point $\msp$ of the toric variety \eqref{eq:deftoricT}, which we denote by $\mbT$, we pick a point $\msq = (\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n) \in \mbA^n$ in the preimage of the natural projection $\mbA^n \setminus V (I) \to \mbT$ over $\msp$.
In this case we express $\msp$ as $\msp = (\alpha_1\!:\!\cdots\!:\!\alpha_m;\alpha_{m+1}\!:\!\cdots\!:\!\alpha_n) \in \mbT$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-23T13:15:27.869358+00:00","domain":"probability","id":"claim_e3fe93c1b93e4bf1bae09cdb537c1446b11a7eef12cc45dbf8842efaebdec015","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"FIRES WHEN you are about to prove a convex-order dominance for a Markov-modulated inter-event time by conditioning on the modulating state and calling the result a mixture of exponentials. THE ROUTE: conditionally on the chain's stationary sojourn structure the inter-event time is exponential with a state-dependent rate, and a MIXTURE of exponentials always dominates the matched exponential in the convex order by Jensen applied to t -> E[exp(-lambda t)]. WHERE IT FAILS: only when the chain does NOT move during the inter-event interval. A general MMPP lets it move, and then the law of T is PHASE-TYPE, not a mixture of exponentials, and phase-type laws are not automatically above the exponential in the convex order. MINIMAL WITNESS that the simplest sufficient condition also fails: the source's own four-state example has a NON-MONOTONE hazard rate, so the decreasing-hazard-rate criterion does not apply either. CONDITION OF FAILURE: any modulating transition inside an inter-event interval. The route that worked instead was Palm inversion - see the E0078 result node.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:52:47.271306+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e404df3cb2e235b58e9b1b2e17f50f5e1d2ec0e5026dbe3027870738508b3282","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 7 (Admissible analytic resolution) of arXiv:2609.01116, 'Vector-Carleson, Calder\'on, and Poisson--Atomic Criteria for\\ Generalized Hilbert Operat'] Let
\[
 I_k=\{n\in\mathbb N:2^k\le n<2^{k+1}\},\qquad k\ge0.
\]
A family of scalar sequences
$\sigma=(\sigma_j)_{j\ge0}$ on $\mathbb N$ is called
$(L,M,p)$-admissible if:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
 \item $\sigma_j(n)=0$ for $n\in I_k$ whenever $|j-k|>L$;
 \item $\sum_{j\ge0}\sigma_j(n)=1$ for every $n\ge1$;
 \item for every $|\ell|\le L$, the patched sequence
 \[
  m_\ell(n)=\sigma_{k+\ell}(n)\qquad(n\in I_k),
  \tag{3.8}
 \]
 with $\sigma_j=0$ for $j<0$, is an $H^p$ coefficient multiplier of
 norm at most $M$.
\end{enumerate}
Put
\[
 W_j^\sigma\phi(z)=\sum_{n\ge1}\sigma_j(n)\widehat\phi(n)z^n,
 \qquad
 \mathscr S_{\phi,p}^{\sigma}a
 =a_{-1}\phi(0)+
  \sum_{j\ge0}a_j2^{-j/p'}W_j^\sigma\phi.
 \tag{3.9}
\]
The hard resolution is $\sigma_j=\mathbf1_{I_j}$ and has $L=0$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:19:46.227892+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e40608a37e4de12076c5bc6e9e448876a6b9b555bdd13c5118d52fc6908afd03","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 5 (Large deviations principle) of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] The sequence $(\mu_n)_{n\ge 1}$ obeys the \textbf{large deviations principle} (`\textbf{LDP}') with \textbf{rate function} $I$ if the following hold:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[i.] (Upper bound) If $x \in \X$ and $a < I(x)$, then there is a neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that
		\[\mu_n U \le e^{-an + o(n)}.\]
		\item[ii.] (Lower bound) If $x \in \X$ and $I(x) < a < \infty$, then any neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ satisfies
		\[\mu_n U \ge e^{-a n - o(n)}.\]
		\item[iii.] (Exponential tightness) For every $a > 0$ there is a compact subset $K$ of $\X$ such that
		\[\mu_n (\X\setminus K) \le e^{-an + o(n)}.\]
	\end{itemize}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:07:56.656860+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e40d3f350c8d318f0c66cccca44dc7c116ccf56efaf13103a6135068d8412d5b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:drift of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] An $\mathcal F$-predictable process $\overline{\delta}:{\mathbb R}\to{\mathbb R}$ is called a drift function if there exists a deterministic vector $(\delta_i)_{1\le i\le n} \in {\mathbb R}^n$ and $\mathcal F$-stopping times $-\infty=\tilde{t}_1<\tilde{t}_2<\ldots<\tilde{t}_{n+1}=\infty$ such that $\overline{\delta}=\delta_i$ on $A_i:=(\tilde{t}_{i},\tilde{t}_{i+1})$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:32:35.574081+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e41f0b739f26bb6027eacf3b08b34476be282aed82e4038a53ce4bfa084548fb","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:Wishart.integrated.deBruijn of arXiv:2606.04859, 'Stein's method for the Wishart distribution'] Under the assumptions of Proposition~(prop:Wishart.deBruijn of the paper), we have
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{Ent}(\mu \, \| \, \xi)
= \int_0^{\infty} J_{\mathcal{W}, \Sigma}(\mu_t \mid \xi) \, \mathrm{d} t
= \int_0^1 \frac{1}{2\tau} J_{\mathcal{W}, \Sigma}(\mu_{\tau} \mid \xi) \, \mathrm{d} \tau.

Assume furthermore that $\mu$ is the law of a random matrix $\mathfrak{X}$ and that this law has Lebesgue density $f_{\mathfrak{X}}$, that is, $\mu(\mathrm{d} X) = f_{\mathfrak{X}}(X) \, \mathrm{d} X$. Equivalently, if $f_{\xi}$ denotes the Lebesgue density of $\xi$, then the initial relative density is $g(X) = f_{\mathfrak{X}}(X)/f_{\xi}(X)$. Assume also that $\mathfrak{X}$ has finite differential entropy
\[
H(\mathfrak{X}) \vcentcolon= -\int_{\mathcal{S}_{++}^d} f_{\mathfrak{X}}(X)\log(f_{\mathfrak{X}}(X)) \, \mathrm{d} X.
\]
If $\mathsf{E}[\mathfrak{X}] = \mathsf{E}[\mathfrak{W}_{\infty}] = \alpha \Sigma$ and $\mathsf{E}[\log(|\mathfrak{X}|)] = \mathsf{E}[\log(|\mathfrak{W}_{\infty}|)]\in \mathbb{R}$ with $\mathfrak{W}_{\infty}\sim \xi$, then
\begin{equation}
H(\mathfrak{W}_{\infty}) - H(\mathfrak{X})
= \int_0^{\infty} J_{\mathcal{W}, \Sigma}(\mu_t \mid \xi) \, \mathrm{d} t
= \int_0^1 \frac{1}{2\tau} J_{\mathcal{W}, \Sigma}(\mu_{\tau} \mid \xi) \, \mathrm{d} \tau.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:45:38.343947+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e41f4766ec987f0bb5a3107a0f5fd2495a0b1918b61a8bb4fb2d6507a7b06ef9","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2604.20617, 'Structured random perturbations of \\ tridiagonal twisted Toeplitz matrices'] Fix a compact set $K\Subset \C\setminus \Sigma$, where
\[
\Sigma:=\left\{z\in\C:\exists x\in[0,1]\text{ such that }|\xi_1(x,z)|=|\xi_2(x,z)|\right\}
\cup
\left\{z\in\C:\exists x\in[0,1]\text{ such that }\xi_1(x,z)^2=1\right\},
\]
and for each $x\in[0,1]$ the numbers $\xi_1(x,z),\xi_2(x,z)$ are the roots of
\[
\lambda^2-\frac{z-b(x)}{c(x)}\lambda+\frac{d(x)}{c(x)}=0
\]
ordered so that $|\xi_1(x,z)|>|\xi_2(x,z)|$ on $K$.

Then, for every fixed block index $j$ and every $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
\prob\!\left(
\left|
\frac{\det(R_{k-1}^{(j)}-zI)}{\det(R_k^{(j)}-zI)}
-\frac{1}{c(jk/n)\,\xi_1(jk/n,z)}
\right|>\varepsilon
\right)=o(1),
\]
and
\[
\prob\!\left(
\left|
\frac{\det(R_k^{(j)'}-zI)}{\det(R_k^{(j)}-zI)}
-\frac{1}{d(jk/n)\,\xi_1(jk/n,z)}
\right|>\varepsilon
\right)=o(1),
\]
uniformly for $z\in K$.

Consequently,
\[
\Theta_k^{(j)}(z):=
\frac{c(jk/n)d(jk/n)\det(R_{k-1}^{(j)}-zI)\det(R_k^{(j+1)'}-zI)}
{\det(R_k^{(j)}-zI)\det(R_k^{(j+1)}-zI)}
\]
satisfies
\[
\Theta_k^{(j)}(z)\longrightarrow
\frac{1}{\xi_1(jk/n,z)^2}
\qquad\text{in probability, uniformly for }z\in K.
\]
In particular, there exists $\delta_K>0$ such that
\[
\prob\!\left(|1-\Theta_k^{(j)}(z)|\ge \delta_K \right)=1-o(1)
\qquad (z\in K).
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.163857+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e444a01e4404c33f58e4f4f48ec3e8fbc8498651ff93b0fc01e5ff4adf5a47a1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 29 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The function $V$ defined by \eqref{e:freeprob.V} is strictly convex on the interval $(z_0,+\infty)$, with $V(z)\to\infty$ as $z\to\infty$.
As a consequence, $V$ has a unique minimizer on the interval $[z_0,+\infty)$, which we denote $z_{\min}$.

\begin{proof} For $z>z_0$, we calculate
    \beq
        
        V'(z)
        = 1 - \alpha \frac{m_2(z)}{m(z)^2} \sum_{j=1}^r \lambda_j
            \bigg(\frac{\hv_j m(z)}{\alpha - \hv_j m(z)}\bigg)^2\,.
    \eeq
Recall that $m:(\hw_1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ is strictly decreasing, and we have
$\alpha - \hv_j m(z) > 0$ for all $z>z_0$. It follows that, on  the interval
$(z_0,\infty)$, the function
    \[
    \frac{m(z)}{\alpha-\hv_j m(z)}
    = \frac{1}{\alpha/m(z)-\hv_j}
    \]
is strictly decreasing, \emph{regardless of the sign of $\hv_j$}. Consequently, in \eqref{e:fp-V-pr}, each term
    \[      \bigg(\frac{\hv_j m(z)}{\alpha - \hv_j m(z)}\bigg)^2\]
is strictly decreasing on $(z_0,\infty)$, again \emph{regardless of the sign of $\hv_j$}. In the special case $s=1$, we have $m_2(z)=m(z)^2$, so we conclude in this case that $V'$ is strictly increasing on the interval $(z_0,\infty)$. For $s\ge2$, we note that $m_2(z)/m(z)^2$ is positive, and
    \[
        \frac{d}{dz}\bigg[ \frac{m_2(z)}{m(z)^2}\bigg]
        = \frac{2}{m(z)^3} \Big(m_2(z)^2 - m(z)m_3(z)\Big)
        < 0
    \]
by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality. It therefore follows in this case as well that $V'$ is strictly increasing, and so $V$ is strictly convex, on the interval $(z_0,\infty)$.
Finally, as $z\to\infty$, $m(z) \to 0$. Therefore the first term of $V(z)$ tends to $\infty$ while the second term remains bounded, and so $V(z) \to \infty$.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

Then T is an open map: the image of every open subset of X is open in Y; equivalently there is c > 0 such that the image of the unit ball of X contains the ball of radius c in Y. Corollaries: a bounded linear bijection between Banach spaces has a bounded inverse (the bounded inverse theorem), and two complete norms on one vector space that are comparable in one direction are equivalent. Completeness of BOTH spaces is needed: the identity from (C[0,1], sup norm) to (C[0,1], L^1 norm) is bounded and bijective and its inverse is unbounded, the target not being complete.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:39:12.424875+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e48d1c31ee50e160fa1e46d567717236adb315c63688f5abb4b567b9c82f86e6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 3. dfn: Polish functor of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [{Polish functor}] 
  We say that a functor $\tau$ is \textit{Polish} if there exist a functor $\tilde{\tau}$
  and, for each $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$,
  a sequence $(\tilde{\tau}_{k}(S))_{k=1}^{\infty}$ of open subsets in $\tilde{\tau}(S)$
  satisfying the following conditions.
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (P\arabic*), leftmargin = *]
    \item 
      The functor $\tilde{\tau}$ is complete, separable and continuous. 
    \item 
      The functor $\tau$ is a topological subfunctor of $\tilde{\tau}$.
    \item 
      For every $(S, d^{S}, \rho_{S}) \in \mathfrak{M}$,
      it holds that $\tau(S) = \bigcap_{k \geq 1} \tilde{\tau}_{k}(S)$.
    \item 
      Let $f: S_{1} \to S_{2}$ be a root-and-distance-preserving map
      between $(S_{i}, d^{S_{i}}, \rho_{S_{i}}) \in \mathfrak{M},\, i=1,2$.
      Then, $\tilde{\tau}_{f}^{-1}(\tilde{\tau}_{k}(S_{2})) = \tilde{\tau}_{k}(S_{1})$
      for each $k \geq 1$. 
      In particular,
      $\tilde{\tau}_{f}^{-1}(\tau(S_{2})) = \tau(S_{1})$.
  \end{enumerate}
  We call $(\tilde{\tau}, (\tilde{\tau}_{k})_{k \geq 1})$ a \textit{Polish system} of $\tau$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:05:09.627544+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e4d170e19da90e73aac5fa058f2cba282166061e38fab6784a5223131b404e67","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem6.5 of arXiv:2411.03528, '\textbf{On a boundary of the central limit theorem for strictly stationary, reversible Mar'] Suppose $\phi: [1,\infty) \to (-\infty, 0]$ is a function

\begin{equation}

\lim_{x \to \infty} \phi(x)\ =\ -\infty 
\indent {\rm and} \indent
\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac {\phi(x)} {x}\ =\ 0.
\end{equation}

   Let $\Gamma$ denote the set of all points $x \in (1, \infty)$ (the open half line)

   Then the following statements (I) and (II) hold:

\medskip

   (II) For any negative number $D$ and any positive number

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:20:33.754498+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e4ee7b1b0c19bb8b82285bdfeda4e24623277fdb17afbb02be376dc92a798f9b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Df 34 of arXiv:2609.03836, 'Koszul Orlik--Solomon Algebras from Non-supersolvable Arrangements'] Let $E$ be a finite set.
    Let $E = E_0 \sqcup E_1 \sqcup E_2$ be a tripartition of $E$.
    Write $E_{01} = E_0 \cup E_1$ and $E_{12} = E_1 \cup E_2$.
    Suppose $M$ is a matroid on $E_{01}$ and $N$ is a matroid on $E_{12}$ such that
    $E_1$ is a modular flat of $M$ and
    $M|_{E_1} = N|_{E_1}$.
    
    One defines the \textbf{generalized parallel connection} of $M$ and $N$ along $E_1$---denoted $P_{E_1}(M, N)$---to be the unique matroid on $E$ whose flats are the subsets $F \subseteq E$ such that 
    $F \cap E_{01}$ is a flat of $M$ and 
    $F \cap E_{12}$ is a flat of $N$.
    The rank of this matroid is $\rk P_{E_1}(M, N) = \rk M + \rk N - \rk_M E_1$.
    When $E_1$ is modular in $N$ also, we say (following Ziegler) that $M$ is the \textbf{modular join} of $M$ and $N$ along $E_1$.
    In this case, $P_{E_1}(N, M)$ also exists and is equal to $P_{E_1}(M, N)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:11:11.693476+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e53b29e59e81738e45376b2c2bf7cd67a9e4cec7a398428857e3bc2fd0e42ba8","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:two-vortex of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $\boldsymbol\kappa=(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)$ satisfy
$\kappa_1>0>\kappa_2$, and let
$(\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\in\Lambda_2(D)$ be a strict local
minimum point of $W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}$.  Choose $\rho>0$ such that
\[
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2})
  \Subset\Lambda_2(D),
\]
and
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)
  &>W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\\
  &\quad\text{for every }(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)\in
  \overline{B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2})}
  \setminus\{(\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\}.
  \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Fix $M_i,R_i>0$ for $i=1,2$.  Then there exist positive constants
$C$, $\eta_0$, and $\varepsilon_0$, depending only on
$D,\rho$, and $\mathbf a_{*,i},\kappa_i,M_i,R_i$, $i=1,2$,
such that the following holds.

For every $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$, let
$(\mathbf a_{1,\varepsilon},\mathbf a_{2,\varepsilon})
\in B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2})$, and let
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\in L^\infty(D)$ be nonnegative and satisfy
\[
  \int_D\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\,\mathrm d\mathbf x=|\kappa_i|,
  \qquad
  \|\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}\|_\infty
  \leq M_i\varepsilon^{-2},
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}
  \subset B_{R_i\varepsilon}(\mathbf a_{i,\varepsilon}),
  \quad i=1,2.
\]
Set
$\omega_{\varepsilon,0}
:=\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,0}-\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,0}$.
Let $\omega_{\varepsilon,t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, be the corresponding Yudovich
solution of (equation eq:euler-intro of the paper), and let
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,t}$ denote the transport of
$\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}$ by the associated Euler flow map.
If
\begin{equation}
  \eta^{(2)}_{\varepsilon,0}
  :=\sum_{i=1}^2\mathcal D(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0})
  +\Bigl[W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{1,\varepsilon},\mathbf a_{2,\varepsilon})
  -W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\Bigr]
  +\varepsilon
  \leq\eta_0,
\end{equation}
then, for every $t\in\mathbb R$,
\begin{equation}
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,t})
  \times\mathsf C(\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,t})
  \subset B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,1})\times
  B_\rho(\mathbf a_{*,2}),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{align}
  &\sum_{i=1}^2\mathcal D(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,t})
  +\sup_{(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)\in
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,t})\times
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,t})}
  \Bigl[
  W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)
  -W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})
  \Bigr] \leq C\eta^{(2)}_{\varepsilon,0}.
  
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:26:40.352891+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e54419eb49572f4b1a442ecc64684351e4ef3ec96a2e3c53ebcaf1a66b6e10cb","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 27 (Language relating to polymer models from \cite{ks}) of arXiv:2511.07350, 'Decoupling of clusters in independent sets in a percolated hypercube'] In these definitions, we use the notation $N(A)$ to denote the \emph{set of neighbors} of $A$ in $\Q$, rather than
the number of neighbors.
Additionally, $\cH$ denotes either $\cE$ or $\cO$.
\begin{itemize}
    \item
    A subset $A \sse \cH$ is said to be \emph{2-linked} if there is no decomposition $A = A_1 \cup A_2$ into
    nonempty sets $A_1$ and $A_2$ which satisfy $N(A_1) \cap N(A_2) = \emptyset$.

    \item 
    For a subset $A \sse \cH$, we denote by $[A]$ the \emph{closure} of $A$,
    defined to be the largest subset of $\cH$ with the same neighborhood set as $A$.
    In other words, $[A] = \{ v \in \cH : N(v) \sse N(A) \}$.

    \item
    A 2-linked set $\fp \sse \cH$ with $|[\fp]| \leq \fr{3}{4} 2^{d-1}$ is called a \emph{polymer}.

    \item
    Polymers $\fp_1$ and $\fp_2$ are said to be \emph{compatible} if $\fp_1 \cup \fp_2$ is not 2-linked.

    \item
		We denote by $\Sep[\cH]$ the set of pairwise compatible collections of polymers.
    
    \item
    The \emph{weight} of a polymer $\fp$ is $\omega(\fp) = \E[\phi_\fp]$, where $\phi_\fp = 2^{-\N(\fp)}$.
    We remind the reader that $\N(\fp)$ denotes the (random) number of vertices neighboring $\fp$
    in the percolated graph $\Qp$.

    \item
    We define \emph{clusters} and their weights as in the previous section, which is a general construction that
    works for all polymer models.
    The set of clusters will be denoted by $\cC^\cH$.

{"assumptions":["P is a set of partial computable functions","P is nontrivial: neither empty nor all partial computable functions"],"created_at":"2026-08-02T17:15:45.378848+00:00","domain":"computability theory","id":"claim_e566adf01a15158b9f7ce6ec58f8cd9ca5acbd8ecb4145e42d80266d80928187","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Every nontrivial semantic property of programs is undecidable. Precisely: let P be any set of partial computable functions that is nontrivial, meaning some partial computable function belongs to P and some does not. Then the index set {encodings of Turing machines M : the partial function computed by M belongs to P} is undecidable. 'Semantic' is essential: the property must depend only on the function computed, not on the machine's text (syntactic properties such as 'has fewer than 100 states' are decidable). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:34:09.927340+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e59ff678b2bc58a245e9f0d44e77da148099443d31c5ff09853596a7a3e1069c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 7 (Supermartingale $C$-monotonicity.) of arXiv:2603.27940, '\Large \bf Stability of supermartingale optimal transport problems'] The Borel set $\Gamma \subset \R \times \Pc_1$ is supermartingale $C$-monotone if and only if there exists $M_0, M_1 \subset \R$, such that for any $N \in \N$, any collection $(x_1, p_1), \cdots, (x_N, p_N) \in \Gamma$ and $q_1, \cdots q_N \in \Pc_1$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^{N} p_i = \sum_{i=1}^{N} q_i$ and 
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \int_{\R} y p_i(dy)= \int_{\R} y q_i(dy), \ \ \forall i \in \mathcal{I}_1; \\
& \int_{\R} y p_i(dy) \geq \int_{\R} y q_i(dy), \ \ \forall i \in \mathcal{I}_0,
\end{aligned}
$$
 we have
 $$
 \sum_{i=1}^N C(x_i, p_i) \leq  \sum_{i=1}^N C(x_i, q_i).
 $$
where, $\mathcal{I}_0=\{i : x_i \in M_0 \}$, $\mathcal{I}_1=\{i : x_i \in M_1 \}$. In the following, we say a coupling $\pi \in \Pi_S(\mu, \nu)$ is Supermartingale $C$-monotone if there exists a Supermartingale $C$-monotone set $\Gamma$ with 
$$
(x, \pi_x) \in \Gamma \ \ \mbox{for } \mu(dx) \mbox{-almost every }x,
$$ 
with $M_0, M_1$ defined as the martingale region of $\pi$ to the left and right of $x^*$ (recall that $x^*$ is defined in Section \ref{sec:irreducible})  {In addition, a probability measure $\P \in \Pc(\R \times \Pc_1$, which is supported on a martingale $C$-monotone set, is called supermartingale $C$-monotone. }","status":"unverified"}

 \[ \limsup_{\varepsilon\to0} \varepsilon\log\mu_\sigma^\varepsilon(F) \leq -\inf_{u\in F}E_{\mathcal A(\sigma)}(u), \] 
 where $E_{\mathcal A(\sigma)}$ is the pullback quasipotential associated with the deterministic limiting equation. If, in addition, the deterministic pullback attractor is a random point, then the matching lower bound holds: for every open set $G$ in the phase space, 
 \[ \liminf_{\varepsilon\to0} \varepsilon\log\mu_\sigma^\varepsilon(G) \geq -\inf_{u\in G}E_{\mathcal A(\sigma)}(u). \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.096857+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e5ace840b7a802a63627f4607d2573244712aad61251eef12fdf70c6287c7bb4","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:ribbon-majorant of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Fix a ribbon record $\Gamma$, a circuit state $\tau$, and a designated

included.  In the monomer--dimer applications of (sec:moments of the paper), the

partial trace-class contraction obtained from the same atoms.  The

{"assumptions":["independent coordinates with finite ranges","f real valued"],"created_at":"2026-10-06T08:50:16.133942+00:00","domain":"Hoeffding (ANOVA) decomposition on finite product spaces","id":"claim_e5bc523adf056d9ffeb113c97a81d7e542e8498e58ad3f632631e5a630f50c3a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) have independent coordinates with finite ranges, f a real function of X, and f = sum over S of f_S its Hoeffding (ANOVA) decomposition over subsets S of {1, ..., n}: f_S depends only on X_S, f_empty = E f, and E[f_S | X_T] = 0 unless S is inside T. Put w_S = E[f_S^2] and W_k = sum over |S| = k of w_S, the variance at interaction order k. Let T_p be a random set, independent of X, containing each coordinate independently with probability p in [0, 1], and J(p) = E over T_p of Var(E[f | X_{T_p}]). Then J(p) = sum over nonempty S of p^|S| w_S = sum_{k=1}^n p^k W_k. Hence J^(k)(0) = k! {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:18:19.220034+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e5da1f660a5af8df7096bc9240824b67d25a665e411ceb9d2690023e730a6afd","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 16 of arXiv:2608.29075, 'The 2-Monoidal Structure of Symmetric Sequences'] Let $(\catname{C},\square, I, \circ, J)$ be a 2-monoidal category. A \textit{bimonoid} in $\catname{C}$ is a quintuple $(H,\mu,\iota,\Delta,\epsilon)$ where $(H,\mu,\iota)$ is a monoid in $(\C,\square,I)$, $(H,\Delta,\epsilon)$ is a comonoid in $(\C,\circ,J)$, and the two structures are compatible in the sense that the following four diagrams commute.
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{(H \circ H)\square (H \circ H)} && {(H\square H)\circ (H \square H)} \\
	{H \square H} & H & {H \circ H}
	\arrow["{\zeta_{H,H,H,H}}", from=1-1, to=1-3]
	\arrow["{\mu \circ \mu}", from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\Delta \square \Delta}", from=2-1, to=1-1]
	\arrow["\mu"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\Delta"', from=2-2, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{H \square H} & {J \square J} && I & H \\
	H & J && {I \circ I} & {H \circ H}
	\arrow["{\epsilon \square \epsilon}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["\mu"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{\mu_J}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["\iota", from=1-4, to=1-5]
	\arrow["{\Delta_I}"', from=1-4, to=2-4]
	\arrow["\Delta", from=1-5, to=2-5]
	\arrow["\epsilon"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{\iota \circ \iota}"', from=2-4, to=2-5]
\end{tikzcd}\]
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	& H \\
	I && J
	\arrow["\epsilon", from=1-2, to=2-3]
	\arrow["\iota", from=2-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\iota_J = \epsilon_I}"', from=2-1, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}\]
    A morphism of bimonoids is a morphism of the underlying monoids and comonoids. 
    
    The category of bimonoids in $(\catname{C},\square, I, \circ, J)$ is denoted by $\text{Bimon}(\catname{C},\square, I, \circ, J)$.","status":"unverified"}
