{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:16:18.687439+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e8a7a64b273f13396ae992a4626c7a30516ec88118f7b0c7a034782b1575de3e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 23 (Weak reparametrisation and reduced uniqueness) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space, and let $\xi:[0,A]\to E$ and $\widetilde\xi:[0,B]\to E$ be continuous bounded-variation paths with $\xi\sim_{\mathrm{rep}}\widetilde\xi$, witnessed by continuous nondecreasing surjections $\sigma:[0,1]\to[0,A]$ and $\widetilde\sigma:[0,1]\to[0,B]$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item If $0\leq u\leq w\leq1$, $s=\sigma(u)$, $t=\sigma(w)$, $\widetilde s=\widetilde\sigma(u)$, and $\widetilde t=\widetilde\sigma(w)$, then
\[
\xi|_{[s,t]}\sim_{\mathrm{rep}}
\widetilde\xi|_{[\widetilde s,\widetilde t]}.
\]
The two subpaths have equal signatures and are constant simultaneously.
\item The equivalent reducedness conditions in \cref{prop:reducedness} are invariant under $\sim_{\mathrm{rep}}$.
\item If neither path has a nontrivial constant subinterval, then there is an increasing homeomorphism $h:[0,A]\to[0,B]$ such that
\[
\xi=\widetilde\xi\circ h.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, two tree-reduced bounded-variation paths with the same initial point and the same signature are weakly reparametrisation-equivalent.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:59:53.370226+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e8aaa88da8e45f68df0cea3b369a8797e21c6a5bb07c5e5d657f02ad49090d1d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:flat-transport of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let $R$ be bounded and restrict to laws with $\log f$ bounded on

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.198114+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e8cafb595cde93cabe7dd8e2c811d511022818a2c6bc1a6d10ec0f19faa71b99","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 123 (L\'evy--Prohorov convergence of derivatives) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The function $(p^N)'$ is nonincreasing, so there exists a nonnegative measure $\nu_N$ on $[q_0,1]$ with
	\[
	\nu_N( (s,t]) = -\Big[(p^N)'(t)-(p^N)'(s)\Big]
	\]
for all $q_0 \le s\le t\le1$, and with $\nu_N(\{0\})=0$. By passing to a subsequence, we may assume that $\nu_N$ converges in the L\'evy--Prohorov metric to a limiting measure $\nu$. Since $(p^N)'$ converges to $p'$ almost everywhere, we immediately conclude that 
	\[\nu((s,t])
	=-\Big[ p'(t)-p'(s)\Big]
	\]
for almost all $s,t$. Now recall that $p'$ denotes the derivative of $p$ from the right, so in particular $p'$ is right-continuous: this implies that the above equality holds for all $s,t\in[0,1]$. For this form of convergence, we hereafter say for short that \textbf{$(p^N)'$ converges to $p'$ in the L\'evy--Prohorov metric.}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:07:17.265310+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e8d07dcbae54a8a318a975413db7e1ed2f732ea663601d00ef4466cf9c2286bc","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:thermo-conv of arXiv:2603.14906, 'Four Levels of Thermodynamic Convergence of Singularly Perturbed Markov Semigroups'] Consider a family of microscopic semigroups $(P_t^\varepsilon,\pi^\varepsilon)$ with macroscopic limit $(\bar P_t,\bar\pi)$, and let
$\mathcal{F}^\varepsilon,\mathcal{I}^\varepsilon,\sigma_{\mathrm{hk}}^\varepsilon,\sigma^\varepsilon$ and $\bar\mathcal{F},\bar\mathcal{I},\bar\sigma_{\mathrm{hk}},\bar\sigma$
be the associated thermodynamic functionals defined in (def:sigmas-single of the paper).
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Level I (free-energy convergence).}
We say that the singular limit exhibits \textbf{free-energy convergence} on \(t\) if
\[
\mathcal{F}^\varepsilon(t)\to\bar\mathcal{F}(t).
\]

\item \textbf{Level II (weak thermodynamic convergence).}
We say that the singular limit exhibits \textbf{weak thermodynamic convergence} on \(t\) if it exhibits free-energy convergence on \(t\) and, in addition, 
\[
\mathcal{I}^\varepsilon(t)\to\bar\mathcal{I}(t).
\]

\item \textbf{Level III (liminf thermodynamic convergence).}
We say that the singular limit exhibits \textbf{liminf thermodynamic convergence} on \(t\) if it exhibits weak thermodynamic convergence on \(t\) and, in addition, 
\[
\liminf_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\sigma_{\mathrm{hk}}^\varepsilon(t)
\;\ge\;\bar\sigma_{\mathrm{hk}}(t),\qquad
\liminf_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\sigma^{\varepsilon}(t)
\;\ge\;\bar\sigma(t).
\]

\item \textbf{Level IV (strong thermodynamic convergence).}
We say that the singular limit exhibits \textbf{strong thermodynamic convergence} on \(t\) if it exhibits liminf thermodynamic convergence on \(t\) and, in addition, 
\[
\sigma_{\mathrm{hk}}^\varepsilon(t)\to\bar\sigma_{\mathrm{hk}}(t),
\qquad
\sigma^\varepsilon(t)\to\bar\sigma(t).
\]
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.163326+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e8e08bb96a63c8aea4a21ab5aecca3913aaacd7568744a4e1a5414ad49c89bba","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Cor 25 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $\tilde{F}^{\riii}(k,\cB)$ be the function from Lemma~\ref{l:F.iii.sqrtk.Lip}. As stated therein, $\E\tilde{F}^{\riii}(k,\cB)$ does not depend on the choice of $\cB \in \scB(\lambda,\mu)$, so we denote this quantity simply $\E\tilde{F}^{\riii}(k)$. We then have
        \[\P\bigg(
    \Big|F^{\riii}(k,\cB) - \E\tilde{F}^{\riii}(k)\Big|
    \ge \frac{\epsilon'}{10}
    ;\cE_{\gd}
    \bigg) \le e^{-ckN}\]
for any fixed partition $\cB \in \scB(\lambda,\mu)$.

$\tilde{F}^{\riii}(k,\cB)$
and $F^{\riii}(k,\cB)$ coincide,
so the claim follows.
\end{proof}","status":"unverified"}

\medskip
{\bf (1)} For $m\ge 2$ (resp.\ $m\ge 3$) we say that $\mu_{X;A}$ has exceptional $+1$ (resp.\ $-1$) jumps or that $\mu_{X;A}$ has jump type $1$ (resp.\ $-1$) if there exists $b\in A\cap\llbracket 1,p^s-1\rrbracket$ such that the function $\mu_{X;b}$ is non-constant and for each such $b$, $\mu_{X;b}$ attains its maximum (resp.\ minimum) at precisely one element of the source.

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} We say that $\mu_{X;A}$ has regular $\pm 1$ jumps if for each $b\in A$ the function $\mu_{X;b}$ is non-constant, attains its maximum at two or more elements of the source, and attains its minimum at two or more elements of the source.

\smallskip
{\bf (4)} For $m=2$ (resp.\ $m\ge 3$), we fix an $s$-tuple $(\epsilon_0,\ldots,\epsilon_{s-1})\in\{0,1\}^s$ (resp. $(\epsilon_0,\ldots,\epsilon_{s-1})\in\{-1,0,1\}^s$). \smallskip
{\bf (5)} We call the $2s$-tuple 
$$(\l_{0,0},|\mathbb J_{X;0}|,\l_{1,0},|\mathbb J_{X;1}|,\ldots,\l_{s-1,0},|\mathbb J_{X;s-1}|)\in(\mathbb N\cup\{0\})^{2s} $$
 as the multiplicity type of $\mu_X$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:33:12.348748+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e91b1cd8927b86ad5e2a7ab443169724c0332be7cebe97a13d24ef45bdb005e0","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 164 ($\bar{\bx}$ is Lipschitz) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Take $\bar{\bx}\equiv \bar{\bx}(q_d)$
 as in \eqref{e:normalized.vectors.x}, so it is measurable with respect to
 $\cG(q_d)$. Then
		\[
		\|\E\bar{\bx}\|^2
		\le \frac{Nq_0}{q_d} \le N\,.\]
and the centered random vector $\bar{\bx}  -\E\bar{\bx}$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $L^{O(1)}$.

\begin{proof} 
Recall $\chi(p)=\E R(p)$ with $R(p)$ as in \eqref{e:p.corr.overlap}, and $q_d=\chi(p_d)$. Note that
	\[
	\frac{\|\E\bar{\bx}\|^2}{N}
	= \frac{\|\E\cA(\bG)\|^2}{Nq_d}
	= \frac{\chi(0)}{q_d} 
	\le \frac{\chi(p_0)}{q_d} = \frac{q_0}{q_d}\le1\,,
	\]
which proves the first claim. Next note that we can write
	\[
	\sqrt{q_d}\bar{\bx}
	\stackrel{\eqref{e:normalized.vectors.x}}{=}
	\E\bigg( \cA
	\Big(\sqrt{p_d}\bar{\bG} +\sqrt{1-p_d}\bG'\Big)
	\,\bigg|\,\bar{\bG}\bigg)\,,
	\]
where $\bar{\bG} = \bG(q_d)/\sqrt{p_d}$ and $\bG'$ are independent $M\times N$ matrices, each with i.i.d.\ standard gaussian entries. Since $\cA$ is $L$-Lipschitz, and $p_d/q_d \le L^{O(1)}$ by \eqref{e:deriv.p.bound}, it follows that $\bar{\bx}$ is $L^{O(1)}$-Lipschitz with respect to $\bar{\bG}$. The claim then follows using Lemma~\ref{l:lip.subgaus}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:47:40.725876+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e940dd33f9b9f494e5ed1fbba768df2995f1711d68a3ebbebc7028ec6f40791a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop propinftyinfty of arXiv:2604.19184, 'Growing random planar network with \\oriented branching and fusion\\'] There exists  a constant $C$ such that for any  measurable function  $f: \mathcal X \rightarrow \mathbb R_+$ with support in $\mathbb R_+^3$  and such that $\parallel f \parallel<\infty$ and for any $t\geq 0$,
  $$M_tf(\infty,\infty, 0) \leq C\parallel f \parallel (1+t)^2$$  and 
  $$ \big\vert M_tf(\infty,\infty, 0) -t^2\Pi(f) \big\vert\leq  C\parallel f \parallel t.$$
Moreover,  the measure  $\Pi$ on $\mathbb R_+^3$  satisfies
$$\Pi(dL,d\ell,da)=g(L,\ell)dLd\ell \delta_L(da)$$

 $g$ with respect to Lebesgue measure for the first and second coordinate writes

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:23:58.615594+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e9428f28481bae9e9505ada1331bf2b01b4592f1c8cddf307f724efe56e4c403","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 130 (Pointwise commutator estimates involving $\angLie$ ; \cite{abbrescia2022emergence}*{Prop.\,14.5}) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $1 \leq N \leq \Ntop$ be an integer, and let $\varphi$ be a scalar function. 
	For any $\Singletan \in \Tanset$ (see definition \eqref{E:COMMUTATIONVECTORFIELDS}),
	iterated commutators can be bounded pointwise as follows
	on $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$:
	\begin{subequations}
		\begin{align} 
			\left|
			[\Singletan, \tander^N] \varphi
			\right|
			& \lesssim 
			\auxbootsmall \left|\tander^{[1,N]} \varphi \right| 
			+ 
			\underbrace{\sum_{\substack {N_1+N_2 \leq N+1 \\ N_1,\,N_2\leq N}} 
				\left|\tander^{[2,N_1]}\controlvars \right| \left|\tander^{[1,N_2]} \varphi \right|}_{\mbox{Absent if $N=1$}},
			\\
			\begin{split}
				\left|[\muX, \tander^N]\varphi \right|,
				\,
				\left|
				[\Singletan, \comder^{N;1}] \varphi
				\right|
				& \lesssim
				\left|\tander^{[1,N]} \varphi \right| 
				+ 
				\underbrace{\sum_{\substack {N_1+N_2 \leq N+1 \\ N_1,\,N_2\leq N}} 
					\left|\tander^{[2,N_1]} \badcontrolvars \right| \left|\tander^{[1,N_2]} \varphi \right|}_{\mbox{Absent if $N=1$}}
				 
				\\
				& \ \
				+ 
				\underbrace{\sum_{\substack {N_1+N_2 \leq N \\ N_1 \leq N-1}} 
					\left|\tander^{[1,N_1]} \muX \wavearray \right| \left|\tander^{[1,N_2]} \varphi \right|}_{\mbox{Absent if $N=1$}}.
			\end{split}
		\end{align}
	\end{subequations}
	
	In particular, 
	for any $\Singletan \in \{\Lunit,\Yvf{2},\Yvf{3}\}$,
	we have the following pointwise estimates
	on $\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubarboot)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}$:
	\begin{subequations}
		\begin{align} 
			\left|[\Singletan, \tander^N] \varphi \right| 
			& 
			\lesssim 
			\auxbootsmall \left| \tander^{[1,N]}\varphi \right|,
			&
			\mbox{if } 1 \leq N \leq \Ntop - 11,
			\\
			\left|[\muX, \tander^N]\varphi \right|,
			\,
			\left|
			[\Singletan, \comder^{N;1}] \varphi
			\right|
			& 
			\lesssim \left|\tander^{[1,N]} \varphi \right|,
			& 
			\mbox{if } 1 \leq N \leq \Ntop - 12.
			
		\end{align}
	\end{subequations}
	
	Moreover, the following pointwise estimates hold:
	\begin{subequations}
		\begin{align} 
			\left|
			[\Singletan, \comder^{N;2}] \varphi
			\right|,
			\,
			\left|
			[\muX, \comder^{N;1}] \varphi 
			\right|
			& 
			\lesssim 
			\left| \comdersmall^{[1,N];1} \varphi \right|,
			&
			\mbox{if } 1 \leq N \leq 5,
			
			\\
			\left|
			[\Singletan, \comder^{N;3}] \varphi
			\right|,
			\,
			\left|
			[\muX, \comder^{N;2}] \varphi 
			\right|
			& 
			\lesssim 
			\left| \comdersmall^{[1,N];2} \varphi \right|,
			&
			\mbox{if } 1 \leq N \leq 4.
			
		\end{align}
	\end{subequations}
	
	Finally, if $\upxi$ is an $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent one-form or an $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent type $\binom{0}{2}$-tensorfield 
	and $\Singletan \in \{\Lunit,\Yvf{2},\Yvf{3}\}$,
	then the following estimates hold:
	\begin{subequations}
\begin{align} 
\left|
	[\angLie_{\Singletan}, \angLie_{\tander}^N] \upxi 
\right|_{\gtorus} 
&
\lesssim 
\auxbootsmall \left| \angLie_{\tander}^{\leq N} \upxi \right|_{\gtorus}  
+ 
\underbrace{\sum_{\substack{N_1+N_2 \leq N+1 \\ N_2\leq N}} 
\left|\tandersmall^{[2,N_1]} \controlvars \right| 
\left|\angLie_{\tander}^{[1,N_2]}  \upxi \right|_{\gtorus}}_{\mbox{Absent if $N=1$}},
	\\
\begin{split} 
\left|
	[\angLie_{\Singletan}, \angLie_{\comder}^{N;1}] \upxi 
\right|_{\gtorus} 
&
\lesssim 
\left| \angLie_{\tander}^{\leq N} \upxi \right|_{\gtorus}  
+ 
\underbrace{\sum_{\substack{N_1+N_2 \leq N+1 \\ N_2\leq N}} 
\left|\tandersmall^{[2,N_1]} \badcontrolvars \right| 
\left|\angLie_{\tander}^{[1,N_2]}  \upxi \right|_{\gtorus}}_{\mbox{Absent if $N=1$}}
	\\
& \ \
	+
	\underbrace{\sum_{\substack {N_1+N_2 \leq N \\ N_1 \leq N-1}} 
	\left|\tander^{[1,N_1]} \muX \wavearray \right| 
	\left|\angLie_{\tander}^{[1,N_2]}  \upxi \right|_{\gtorus}}_{\mbox{Absent if $N=1$}}.
\end{split}
\end{align}
\end{subequations} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:07:48.553467+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e94cca92e4818ba42ebfb9f17f9981d3b9a19f0171745472063dd78554f71e75","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 10 of arXiv:2609.01413, 'Sharp Threshold for Universality of Rational Canonical Forms over a Finite Field'] Every finite $\F_p[t]$-module $G$ admits a unique decomposition
\begin{equation}
G\cong \bigoplus_{f\in S} G_f,
\end{equation}
where only finitely many summands are nonzero, and $G_f$ denotes the $f$-primary submodule of $G$.

Moreover, for each $f\in S$, there exists a unique partition
\[
\l^{(f)}=(\l^{(f)}_1,\l^{(f)}_2,\ldots)\in\Y
\]
such that
\[
G_f\cong \bigoplus_{j\ge 1}\F_p[t]/(f^{\l^{(f)}_j})
\]
as $\F_p[t]$-modules. Equivalently, if $f_1,\dots,f_r\in S$ are the distinct irreducible polynomials such that
$G_{f_i}\neq 0$, then
\[
G\cong \bigoplus_{i=1}^r\bigoplus_{j\ge 1}\F_p[t]/(f_i^{\l^{(f_i)}_j}),
\]
and the collection of partitions
\[
\l^{(f_1)},\dots,\l^{(f_r)}
\]
is uniquely determined by the $\F_p[t]$-module isomorphism class of $G$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:27:56.773278+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e9689f07be8757b3b3405abf734ed997e836e49b13d95f11df9468796fc25828","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 (The Cauchy stability of finite-energy  Einstein areal flows) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Consider one of the three Einstein--matter models in \autoref{theo-main-results} with $\Tbb^2$ symmetry on~$\Tbb^3$.
In the Einstein--Navier--Stokes case, assume that the model is admissible and torus-adapted, and that its matter stress tensor~$T_\chi$ obeys the coercive stress condition in \autoref{def-Tchi-coercive}.
In the Einstein--Euler case, we use the conventions $T_\chi=T_{\rm E}$, $\vNumb_\chi=\vNumb_\Jbb$, and $\zeta=0$.
Prescribe\footnote{Equivalently, prescribe a signed areal time~$t_0$ and initial data $(\mathring\Phi,\mathring\Psi,\mathring\zeta)$ for the \JKL{} formulation of the areal flow, together with the conformal modulus of one symmetry orbit.}
 an initial data set $(\mathring g,\mathring k,\mathring\Jbb,\mathring\zeta)$, consisting of a Riemannian metric, second fundamental form, fluid momentum, and relaxation field (absent for the Einstein--Euler model) satisfying Einstein's constraint equations and invariant under two commuting Killing fields $Y,Z$ with closed orbits, and assume that the orbit area constant and equal to $|t_0|\neq 0$.

Consider a regular Cauchy development $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$ on $\Tbb^3\times[t_0,t_1]$ of these initial data for the chosen Einstein--Euler or Einstein--Navier--Stokes model in the areal foliation, with an areal time interval $I = [t_0,t_1] \subset \RR\setminus\{0\}$.
\bei
\item Assume that the initial spatial volume, the initial energy norm~$\mathcal E(t_0)$, and the bounded-variation norm of $\mathring\Psi=(\mathring\ell,\log\mathring\Omega,\mathring\Kpar)$ on~$\Tbb^3$ are bounded by a constant~$\mathcal I_0$.

\item In the future-contracting regime, assume that the conformal length has a positive lower bound $\mathcal L_{\min}$ on $I$; in the future-expanding regime, this lower bound is $\mathcal L_{\min}=\mathcal L(t_0)>0$, which is part of the initial data controlled by~$\mathcal I_0$.

\item Assume either that the fluid velocity is orthogonal to the symmetry orbits or, more generally, that the parallel momentum per particle is uniformly bounded in the sense that~\eqref{intro-parall-perpart-bounded} holds at $t=t_0$ for some constant $C^\parallel>0$.
\eei
Then the following Cauchy stability properties hold.

\begin{enumerate}

\item The parallel momentum per particle remains uniformly bounded at all times by~$C^\parallel$ in the sense that~\eqref{intro-parall-perpart-bounded} holds on $[t_0,t_1]\times\Tbb^3$.

\item There exists a constant
\be
C=C\bigl(\mathcal I_0,t_0,t_1,\mathcal L_{\min}^{-1},C^\parallel\bigr)
\ee
such that the $L^2$ norms of~$\Phi$ and bounded-variation norms of~$\Psi$ on areal time slices (constant~$t$) and on timelike slices orthogonal to the areal foliation (constant~$x$ in the \JKL{} formulation) are controlled as
\bel{equajKD93}
\aligned
& \sup_{t\in I}\bigl(
\|\Phi\|_{L^2(\Tbb^3,\dVtrois)}
+ \|\Psi\|_{\BV(\Tbb^3)}
\bigr)
\\
& + \sup_{x\in\Sbb^1}\bigl(
\|\Phi\|_{L^2(\Interval\times\Tbb^2,\dVundeux)}
+ \|\Psi\|_{\BV(\Interval\times\Tbb^2)}
\bigr)
+\int_{I\times\Tbb^3}\!\!\mathfrak d_*\,\dVuntrois
\leq C.
\endaligned
\ee
Here, $\dVuntrois,\dVtrois,\dVundeux$ are volume forms of the (Lorentzian) metric~$g$ and of (Riemannian) induced metrics on spatial and temporal slices.

\item The last term in \eqref{equajKD93} represents the total non-negative production measure and vanishes for the Einstein--Euler system.  For the particle-production Einstein--Navier--Stokes system it is the produced particle number density $\mathfrak d_*=\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}$, while for the dissipated-energy Einstein--Navier--Stokes system it is the dissipated mass-energy density $\mathfrak d_*=\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}/(-n_\alpha\beta^\alpha)$.

\item Moreover, these conclusions allow vacuum, arbitrarily large mass-energy density, and arbitrary finite rapidity. For the two Einstein--Navier--Stokes systems, the constant $C$ is independent of the relaxation rate map~$\mathscr B$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["subadditivity of the doubly indexed array X_{m,n} under the relation X_{m,n}<=X_{m,k}+X_{k,n}","joint stationarity of the array under the shift (m,n) -> (m+1,n+1)","integrability, E[X_{0,1}^+]<infinity, together with a lower bound preventing a degenerate -infinity limit","for an almost-surely-constant limit: ergodicity, not merely measure-preservation, of the underlying shift"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.997492+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e96ecd8a6581efaccba61539497e251c17654ec41003ba9f77fa5109ab6ea0af","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). Let (X_{m,n})_{0<=m<n} be a doubly indexed family of random variables satisfying subadditivity X_{m,n} <= X_{m,k} + X_{k,n} for m<k<n, stationarity, that the joint law of (X_{m+1,n+1})_{m<n} equals that of (X_{m,n})_{m<n} under a measure-preserving shift, and integrability, E[X_{0,1}^+] < infinity together with a lower bound such as E[X_{0,n}] >= -cn preventing a trivially degenerate -infinity limit. Then X_{0,n}/n converges almost surely and in L^1 to a random variable X, equal to lim_n E[X_{0,n}]/n = inf_n E[X_{0,n}]/n, and X is almost surely constant if the underlying shift is ergodic rather than merely measure-preserving. This is the random, non-i.i.d. generalization of Fekete's lemma, which is its deterministic special case, and of the classical ergodic theorem, which is its additive special case, and it is the fundamental tool establishing existence of limiting growth rates in first-passage percolation (the time constant), longest increasing subsequence problems, and last-passage percolation, with the closely related Furstenberg-Kesten theorem giving Lyapunov exponents for random matrix products via an analogous but distinct subadditive argument. It does not give the value of the limit X, only its existence as an abstract limit or infimum, and does not by itself give a rate of convergence or determine whether X is almost surely constant unless ergodicity, not merely stationarity, of the shift has been separately established. Typical failure: Invoking Kingman's theorem to conclude the limiting growth rate is deterministic without separately verifying ergodicity of the underlying probability-preserving transformation, checking only stationarity; stationarity alone gives convergence to a possibly random limit X that can be a genuine mixture over ergodic components, so asserting a single deterministic time constant or growth rate without checking ergodicity is a common gap, especially in models built from a mixture of environments. Canonical reference: Kingman, 1968, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B; Kingman, 1973, Annals of Probability; Steele, Probability Theory and Combinatorial Optimization, 1997, SIAM.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:12:13.499191+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e9979437a9ab76877d877011ebe035d48a8bd74dc5e29de8371742174c8331cb","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.28528, 'Strong solutions of SDEs with critical discontinuities in diffusion coefficients'] Let $d \geq 3$. Assume that the diffusion coefficients $\sigma \in [L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{1+d})]^{d \times d}$ satisfy the uniform ellipticity condition: for every $t \in \mathbb R$
$$
\sigma(t,\cdot) \sigma(t,\cdot)^{\top} \geq \kappa I \quad \text{a.e.\,on $\mathbb R^{d}$ for some fixed $\kappa>0$}
$$
and have \textit{form-bounded} derivatives, i.e.\,condition \eqref{nabla_sigma} holds.

We also impose the following auxiliary condition on the time-dependence of $\sigma$:

\begin{itemize}

\item[{\rm ($\mathbf{H}$)}] 
$$
\sup_{y \in \mathbb R^d}\|\sigma(t,\cdot)-\sigma(s,\cdot)\|_{L_{\rho_y}^2(\mathbb R^d)} \leq C|t-s|^\gamma \quad t,s \in \mathbb R, |t-s| \leq 1
$$
with the H\"{o}lder continuity exponent $\gamma \in ]0,1]$.
\end{itemize}

Let  $$\sigma_n \in \big[L^\infty(\mathbb R, C_b^\infty(\mathbb R^d))\big]^{d \times d} \cap [C_{\text{unif},\loc}^\gamma(\mathbb R,L^2_\rho(\mathbb R^d))]^{d \times d}$$ be a sequence of bounded matrix fields having bounded  derivatives in the spatial variables, $$\|\sigma_n\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{1+d})} \leq \|\sigma\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{1+d})}, \quad \sigma_n\sigma_n^{\top} \geq \frac{\kappa}{4}I$$ such that 
$$
\sigma_n \rightarrow \sigma \quad \text{ in $[L^\infty_{\loc}(\mathbb R,L^2_{\rho}(\mathbb R^d))]^{d \times d}$},
$$
and that satisfy \eqref{nabla_sigma} and ${\rm (\mathbf{H})}$ uniformly in $n$, i.e.\,with the same parameters $\nu$, $c_\nu$ and $C$, $\gamma$. It is not difficult to see that the spatial mollification of $\sigma$ produces such $\{\sigma_n\}$, see Appendix \ref{approx_app}. By the classical theory, for each $n$, there exists a pathwise unique strong solution $X_{r,t}^{x,n}$ to the approximating equation
\begin{equation} 

X_{r,t}^{x,n}=x + \int_r^t \sigma_n(s,X^{x,n}_{r,s})\, dW_s,
\end{equation}
considered on the same (fixed) complete probability space  $(\Omega,\{\mathcal F^W_{t}\}_{0 \leq t \leq T},\mathcal F^W,\mathbf{P})$.

Then, if the form-bound $\nu$ of $|\nabla \sigma|$ in \eqref{nabla_sigma} is smaller than a certain constant that only depends on the dimension $d$, the ellipticity constant $\kappa$ and $\|\sigma\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^{1+d})}$, the following are true:

\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] There exists a subsequence $\{\sigma_{n_k}\}$  and a continuous random field $X$ such that, for every $N \geq 1$,
$$
\sup_{0\leq r\leq t\le T, |x|\le N} |X_{r,t}^{x,n_k}-X_{r,t}^x| \rightarrow 0 \quad \mathbf{P}-a.s.,
$$
where $X^x_{r,t}$ is a strong solution of SDE \eqref{sde1_}
on $(\Omega,\{\mathcal F^W_t\}_{0 \leq t \leq T},\mathcal F^W,\mathbf{P})$.

\medskip

    \item[(ii)] The operators
    \[
    P_\sigma^{r,t}f(x) := \mathbf{E}[f(X^x_{r,t})], \quad f \in C_\infty, \quad r,t \in [0,T], r<t,
    \]
    constitute a backward Feller propagator on $C_\infty$, 
and, furthermore, if $\{\sigma_n\}$ additionally satisfies
$$
\nabla a_n \rightarrow \nabla a \quad \text{ in } L_{\loc}^2(\mathbb R,L^2_\rho(\mathbb R^d)),
$$
where $a=\sigma\sigma^{\top}$, $a_n=\sigma_n(\sigma_n)^{\top}$ (once again, mollifying $\sigma$ in the spatial variables produces this convergence, see Appendix \ref{approx_app}), then
$$
P_\sigma^{r,t}=s\mbox{-}C_\infty\mbox{-}\lim_n P_{\sigma_n}^{r,t} \quad \text{loc.\,uniformly in $r,t \in [0,T]$, $r<t$.}
$$
There is no need to pass to a subsequence of $\{\sigma_n\}$. In this sense, the law of $X^x_{r,t}$ does not depend on the choice of the subsequence in {\rm (\textit{i})}.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the pool protocol: members fitted on training data, the test rows split 40/60 into calibration and evaluation with a fixed permutation, metric = mean per-sample relative L2","the small-calibration arms subsample the calibration rows only; evaluation rows are never touched"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T07:07:15.583115+00:00","domain":"ensemble learning / covariance estimation","id":"claim_e9a54df9848e9c966074eb757b8cd899d5745113e3c0dcbfb1a664e5434d1869","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT stacking pool (23 members, 285 outputs, the per-sample relative metric; PLACEHOLDER_CELLS). The error covariance of the members is rank-deficient in practice: $\\lambda_{\\max}/\\lambda_{\\min}$ of $10^{6}$ to $10^{17}$, three to five eigenvalues below $0.05\\,\\sigma^2$ (members that are near-linear combinations of one another). Inside the long-only minimum-variance stack, eight cleaners of that covariance were compared on the same cells, the same split and the same small-calibration draws: the raw sample covariance, the $\\eta$-regularised rotationally invariant estimator with floors $0, 0.05, 0.2, 1.0\\,\\sigma^2$, Ledoit-Wolf 2004 linear shrinkage, Ledoit-Wolf 2020 analytical nonlinear shrinkage and Lam's NERCOME. Result: raw, RIE without floor, LW2020 and NERCOME tie - PLACEHOLDER_TIE - at full calibration ($n = 932$) and in the $n = 60/120/240$ arms; the floor $0.05\\,\\sigma^2$ is marginally negative, floors $0.2$ and $1.0$ lose PLACEHOLDER_FLOORS, linear shrinkage loses PLACEHOLDER_LW2004, and the sum-to-one (unconstrained-sign) forms of the same cleaners lose PLACEHOLDER_S1. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:50:30.564479+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e9bb566451f72fc6a61e3b2e944b8d6ffc53423f1090d6f1609f2b45f8d56cfb","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 12 of arXiv:2605.30616, 'Brownian motion: the hyperbolic number setting'] Let $\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right),\mu\right)$ be a $\mathbb{H}$-valued
probability space with its $\mathbb{H}$-valued probability $\mu=\mu_{+}e_{+}+\mu_{-}e_{-}$,
where $\mu_{e}$ are bounded non-negative $\mathbb{R}$-valued measures
for all $e\in\left\{ \pm\right\} $, and let $L^{2}\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right),\mu\right)$
be the corresponding $\mathbb{R}$-Banach space equipped with its
$\mathbb{H}$-indefinite inner product $\left[,\right]$. Suppose
either 
\[
\mu_{+}\textrm{ is a classical probability, and }\mu_{-}=O,
\]
or 
\[
\mu_{+}=O,\;\textrm{and }\mu_{-}\textrm{ is a classical probability,}
\]
and hence, 
\[
\mu=\mu_{+}e_{+}+Oe_{-},\;\;\mathrm{respectively,\;\;}\mu=Oe_{+}+\mu_{-}e_{-}.
\]
Then
\[
L^{2}\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right),\mu\right)=L^{2}\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right),\mu_{+}\right)e_{+}\oplus L^{2}\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right),O\right)e_{-},
\]
respectively,
\[
L^{2}\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right),\mu\right)=L^{2}\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right),O\right)e_{+}\oplus L^{2}\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right),\mu_{-}\right)e_{-}.
\]
and hence, if $f=f_{+}e_{+}+f_{-}e_{-}$ and $g=g_{+}e_{+}+g_{-}e_{-}$
in $L^{2}\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right),\mu\right)$, then 
\[
\left[f,g\right]=\left\langle f_{+},g_{+}\right\rangle _{2}e_{+}+0e_{-}=\left(\int_{X}f_{+}g_{+}d\mu_{+}\right)e_{+}\in\mathbb{H},
\]
respectively,
\[
\left[f,g\right]=0e_{+}+\left\langle f_{-},g_{-}\right\rangle _{2}e_{-}=\left(\int_{X}f_{-}g_{-}d\mu_{-}\right)e_{-}\in\mathbb{H}.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:31:49.913848+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e9c2fb67efd2926bab5a5216bf59d660799149a20096cd8b591f04094cde7e1c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:annulus-transfer of arXiv:2608.28330, 'Realising atomless laws as distance distributions on metric measure spaces'] Let $\zeta$ and $\eta$ be finite Borel measures on $\mathbb R_+$ such that
		$\Theta=\zeta+\eta$ is an atomless probability measure and
		\[
		\operatorname{supp}\zeta\subseteq[0,R],\qquad
		0\in\operatorname{supp}\zeta,\qquad
		\operatorname{supp}\eta\subseteq[R,2R]
		\]
		for some $R>0$.  Then there are an integer $N\ge0$, compact metric
		probability spaces $(X_i,d_i,\mu_i)$, $i=1,\ldots,N$, positive
		numbers $p_1,\ldots,p_N,p_\ast$, and $1$-Lipschitz maps
		$\phi_i:X_i\to[R,2R]$ such that $\operatorname{diam} X_i<R$, $i=1,\ldots,N$ and $p_\ast+\sum_{i=1}^N p_i=1$.
		For independent $U_i,V_i\sim\mu_i$, let
		$\nu_i=\operatorname{Law}(d_i(U_i,V_i))$ and set $\tau=\sum_{i=1}^N p_i^2\nu_i$.
		Then $\tau\le\frac12\zeta$.  Moreover, the atomless measure
		$\zeta'=\zeta-\tau$ satisfies
		\[
		\operatorname{supp}\zeta'\subseteq[0,R],\qquad
		\zeta'(\mathbb R_+)=p_\ast^2,\qquad
		\zeta'\ge\frac12\zeta,\qquad
		0\in\operatorname{supp}\zeta'.
		\]
		Finally,
		\[
		\eta=\sum_{i=1}^N c_i\eta_i,\qquad
		\eta_i=(\phi_i)_\#\mu_i,\qquad
		c_i=2p_i\Big(
		p_\ast+\sum_{j=i+1}^N p_j
		\Big).
		\]
		If $\zeta'/p_\ast^2$ has a compact realisation of diameter at most
		$R$, then $\Theta$ has a compact realisation. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:33:01.744533+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_e9d70fb42acc26a95574354f47f14636e8df0b65c75a626cd78581f0bfa171c1","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] The language $G$ admits a well-defined decomposition into primitive languages:
\begin{align*}
  G = \Big[\Big(\C_1^{\geqslant 0} \circ \D_1^{\geqslant 1}\Big).\C_1
    \cup \C_1^{\geqslant0} \Big]
  \circ \cdots \circ
  \Big[
    \Big(\C_m^{\geqslant 0} \circ \D_m^{\geqslant 1}\Big).\C_m
    \cup \C_m^{\geqslant0} \Big].
\end{align*}
Its exponential generating function is hence
\[
  \hat\phi_G(z) = \left[ (1-p) \left( e^{z/m} - 1 \right) + 1 \right]^m.
\]
\begin{proof}
  It holds for all $i$ that
  \begin{align*}
    \hat\phi_{{\C_i^{\geqslant0}} \circ {\D_i^{\geqslant1}}}(z)
    
    &= e^{z/m} - e^{(1-p)z/m}\\
    &= \sum_{n=0}^\infty
        \frac{(z/m)^n - ((1-p)z/m)^n}{n!},\\
    \phi_{{\C_i^{\geqslant0}} \circ {\D_i^{\geqslant1}}}(z)
    &= \sum_{n=0}^\infty 
        (z/m)^n - ((1-p)z/m)^n.
  \end{align*}
  Then we multiply by $\phi_{\C_i}(z) = \left(1-p\right)z\,m^{-1}$,
  \begin{align*}
    \phi_{\left({\C_i^{\geqslant0}} \circ {\D_i^{\geqslant1}}\right).\C_i}(z)
    &= \frac{\left(1-p\right)z}{m} \sum_{n=0}^\infty \left[
      \left(\frac{z}{m}\right)^n - \left(\frac{\left(1-p\right)z}{m}\right)^n
      \right]\\
    &= (1-p)\sum_{n=1}^\infty
        (z/m)^{n}
      - \sum_{n=1}^\infty
      ((1-p)\,z/m)^{n},\\
    \hat\phi_{\left({\C_i^{\geqslant0}} \circ {\D_i^{\geqslant1}}\right).\C_i}(z)
    &= (1-p)\sum_{n=1}^\infty
        \frac{(z/m)^{n}}{n!}
      - \sum_{n=1}^\infty
        \frac{((1-p)z/m)^{n}}{n!}\\
    &= (1-p)\left(e^{z/m} - 1\right)
    - e^{(1-p)z/m} + 1.
  \end{align*}
  Finally add $\hat\phi_{\C_i^{\geqslant 0}}(z)
  = e^{(1-p)z/m}$ to achieve
  \begin{align*}
    \hat\phi_{
      {\left({\C_i^{\geqslant0}} \circ {\D_i^{\geqslant1}}\right).\C_i}
      \cup {\C_i}
    }(z)
    &= (1-p) \left( e^{z/m} - 1 \right) + 1,\\
    \hat\phi_G(z)
    &= \left[(1-p) \left( e^{z/m} - 1 \right) + 1\right]^m. \qedhere
  \end{align*}
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:21:10.899765+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ea0642ce49366d6d114e9360fb78404fba23608c7df6fc02c893da81d12c9df1","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 28 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Given a configuration $\boldsymbol{\ell} \in \W_\N$ in a discrete ensemble of Section~\ref{Section_general_model}, the \emph{empirical measure} is the $H$-tuple of nonnegative atomic measures $\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\N} = (\mu_{\N,h})_{h = 1}^{H}$ given by
\[
\forall h \in [H] \qquad \mu_{\N,h} = \frac{1}{\N} \sum_{i = 1}^{N_h} \delta_{\N^{-1}\ell_i^h}.
\]
This tuple $\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\N}$ is equivalently specified by the measure $\mu_{\N} = \sum_{h = 1}^{H} \mu_{\N,h} = \frac{1}{\N} \sum_{i = 1}^{N} \delta_{\N^{-1}\ell_i}$. The empirical resolvent is the tuple $\boldsymbol{G}(z) = (G_h(z))_{h = 1}^{H}$ defined for any $h \in [H]$ and $z \in\amsmathbb{C} \setminus [\hat{a}_h,\hat{b}_h]$ by
\begin{equation}
 G_h(z) = \sum_{i = 1}^{N_h} \frac{1}{z - \frac{\ell_i^h}{\N}} = \N \int_{\hat{a}_h}^{\hat{b}_h} \frac{\dd \mu_{\N,h}(x)}{z - x} = \N \Gm_{\mu_{\N,h}}(z).
\end{equation}
It is a holomorphic function of $z$ in this domain, such that for any $h \in [H]$, we have $G_h(z) \sim \frac{N_h}{z}$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$.

We sometimes recenter the empirical measure by subtracting the equilibrium measure $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ and introduce $\Delta \boldsymbol{G}(z) = \boldsymbol{G}(z) - \N \Gm_{\boldsymbol{\mu}}(z)$. In other words, for any $h \in [H]$ and $z \in \amsmathbb{C} \setminus \amsmathbb{A}_h^{\mathfrak{m}}]$ we have
\[
\Delta G_h(z) = G_h(z) - \N\Gm_{\mu_h}(z).
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X and Y are normed spaces over the same field R or C","T: X -> Y is linear"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:46.571085+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, operator theory","id":"claim_ea377968f9c0845c7f4fd6c6c2aa4f7c83561cc34ce0b88f7e0503bd67c3c35c","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X and Y be normed spaces over R or C. A linear map T: X -> Y is compact if the image T(B_X) of the closed unit ball B_X = {x : ||x|| <= 1} is relatively compact in Y, i.e. its closure in Y is compact. Equivalent forms: (i) for every bounded sequence (x_n) in X the sequence (T x_n) has a subsequence that converges in Y; (ii) when Y is a Banach space, T(B_X) is totally bounded. Every compact operator is bounded, and every bounded operator of finite rank is compact. The set of compact operators X -> Y is written K(X,Y), and K(X) = K(X,X). The identity operator of X is compact if and only if X is finite-dimensional (Riesz's lemma). Terminology warning: older texts say 'completely continuous' for compact; in current usage 'completely continuous' means 'maps weakly convergent sequences to norm convergent sequences', which is implied by compactness but is weaker in general (it is equivalent to compactness when X is reflexive).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:22:08.521083+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ea3b28480bb46496d7d97bd1152f16281b0a0e958d9ab539625d242ded353d48","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:PTASEP-kernel of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] We have
\[
\mathbb{P}_y\Bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^m
\{Y_{n_i}(t) > a_i\}\Bigr)
= \det(I - K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}})_{\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})},
\]
where
\[
K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}(x, x')
= \sum_{1 \le j \le i \le m}

  \phi_{t, r', n_j}(x').

This identifies $K_{t, \mathbf{a}, \mathbf{n}}$ with the

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:54:34.574907+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ea40f777cc3d908ec38943901950a052988a536448232c55825bed854e89d909","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 33 of arXiv:2606.14564, 'Upper tails for irregular graphs \\ beyond the mean-field regime'] Suppose that $J_0, J \in \cJ_\emptyset^*$ satisfy $J_0 \subsetneq J$.
  The \emph{span} of a set $E$ of edges of $J$ over $J_0$ is the graph
  \[
    \spn_{J_0}E \coloneqq \bigcap \bigl\{J' \in \cJ^* : J_0 \cup E \subseteq J'\bigr\}.
  \]
  The \emph{dimension} of $J$ over $J_0$ is
  \[
    \dim_{J_0}J \coloneqq \min\bigl\{|E| : E \subseteq J \wedge \spn_{J_0}E = J\bigr\}.
  \]
  A set $E$ of edges of $H$ is a \emph{basis} of $J$ over $J_0$ if $\spn_{J_0}E = J$ and $|E| = \dim_{J_0}J$.
  Finally, a vertex $v \in V(J_0)$ is a \emph{root} of $J$ over $J_0$ if $\deg_Jv > \deg_{J_0}v$;
  the set of all roots of $J$ over $J_0$ is denoted by $R_{J_0}(J)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:54:12.598301+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ea4d54c2fcea4bad3b66f389cf9f253614105039f56a6e4d1d144ea2db6ca8a8","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem T:half-space-full-tails of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] For $n, m\in \mathbb{N}$ and any $\alpha>0$, let
$$
\Delta_\alpha(n) = \mu_\alpha(n) - \mu(n)
$$
be the gap in the limit shape on the diagonal, and
$$
\nu_\alpha(n, m) = \mu(n, m) +  \Delta_\alpha(m).
$$
Fix $\alpha_0>0$, and take any $\alpha \ge \alpha_0$.
Then there exists a constant $c> 0$ depending only on $\alpha_0$, such that for all $v + (1, 1), v + (n, m) \in \mathbb{Z}^2_\ge$ with $n/m \in [\alpha_0, \alpha_0^{-1}]$ and all $\epsilon \in (0, m^{-1/3}]$ we have
\begin{align}

	\mathbb{P}\Big(X_\alpha(v + (1, 1); v + (n, m)) \ge \nu_\alpha(n, m) + \epsilon n\Big) &\le 2\exp\left(-c \epsilon^{3/2}n \left(1 \wedge \frac{\epsilon^{1/2}}{(1/2 - \alpha)\vee 0}\right) \right).
    \end{align}
Moreover, for all $v + (1, 1), v + (n, m) \in \mathbb{Z}^2_\ge$ with $n/m \in [\alpha_0, \alpha_0^{-1}]$ and all $\epsilon \in (0, 1)$ we have
    \begin{align}
	
	\mathbb{P}\Big(X_\alpha(v + (1, 1); v + (n, m)) \le \mu(n, m) - \epsilon n\Big) &\le 2 \exp\left( - c\epsilon^3 n^2 \right).
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:33:17.688229+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ea7b499213de40992d9499eb91691fdf94350d6ac7fc47d029167ac63e27cf6b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 20 (Gaussian functional inequalities after centering) of arXiv:2607.10769, '\fontsize{14}{17}\selectfont\bfseries Sharp Poincar\'e interpolation along Wasserstein geo'] Let $\mu$ be $1$-strongly log-concave, let $m=\int x\,\d\mu$, and denote
\[
 \mathcal D=\Ent_\gamma(\mu)-\frac12|m|^2,

 \quad
 \mathcal W^2=W_2^2(\mu,\gamma)-|m|^2.
\]
Then $\mathcal D\geq0$, $\mathcal I\geq0$, and
$0\leq\mathcal W^2\leq n$.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 e^{\mathcal D/n}
 \leq
 \cos\!\left(\sqrt{\frac2n}\,\mathcal W\right)
 +\frac{\sin\!\left(\sqrt{2/n}\,\mathcal W\right)}{\sqrt{2n}}
  \sqrt{\mathcal I},
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 4\mathcal D

 \leq\mathcal D.

Moreover, for every $s\geq0$,

 \Ent_\gamma(P_s^*\mu)

In particular, the assumptions and conclusions in \textup{(ii)} hold if

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:02:34.835963+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_eab040056f84b7edfa33cddc602e4b25469aac9fa05ff8b0f1a6bb9949121110","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.20646, 'The Independence-Preserving Property and Planar Web Geometry'] Let $d$ be a positive integer and $\Omega\subset\R^2$ be an open connected set.
    A \emph{nonsingular planar $d$-web} on $\Omega$ is a $d$-tuple $\W=(h_i)_{i=1}^d$ of real-analytic functions such that $\dd h_i\neq 0$ and $\dd h_i\wedge\dd h_j\neq 0$ everywhere on $\Omega$ whenever $i\neq j$.
    \footnote{
    Geometrically, each function \(h_i\) represents the family of its level curves $\mathcal{F}(h_i) = \{\{(x,y)\in\Omega \mid h_i(x,y)=t\} \mid t\in h_i(\Omega) \}$. 
    Since for a one-variable diffeomorphism $\rho_i$ one has $\mathcal{F}(h_i) = \mathcal{F}(\rho_i\circ h_i)$, the web $(\rho_i\circ h_i)_{i=1}^d$ is identified with $(h_i)_{i=1}^d$.
    }

    A \emph{measurable Abelian relation} for $\W$ is a $d$-tuples $(\Phi_i)_{i=1}^d$ of real-valued measurable functions $\Phi_i$ on $h_i(\Omega)$ satisfying
    \begin{align}
        \Phi_1(h_1(x, y)) + \cdots + \Phi_d(h_d(x, y)) = (\text{constant})
    \end{align}
    for every $(x, y)\in\Omega$.
    This equation is called an \emph{Abelian functional equation}.
    For differentiable components, this is equivalent to
    \[
        \Phi_1'(h_1(x, y)) \dd h_1 + \cdots + \Phi_d'(h_d(x, y)) \dd h_d = 0.
    \]
    Continuous and real-analytic Abelian relations are defined analogously.
    Two measurable Abelian relations are identified if their corresponding components differ by additive constants.
    The real vector space of real-analytic Abelian relations modulo this equivalence is denoted by $\A(\W)$, and its dimension is called the rank of $\W$.","status":"unverified"}

	Then, $X_t$ is called \emph{a reflected Brownian motion with semipermeable barriers $B_i$ and local times $\Lc{i}_t$} if the following properties hold with probability one:
	\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2.5em, label = (\roman*)]
		\item
		      $
			      \intd X_t =  \intd W_t +  \sum_{i=0}^{\nb} s_i(\Lc{i}_t) \vec{n}_i(X_t) \bb1\{X_t \in B_i \}\intd \Lc{i}_t.\nonumber
		      $
		\item For $i \leq {\nb}$, $\Lc{i}_t$ is nondecreasing, satisfies $\Lc{i}_0 =0$, and increases at time $t$ if and only if $X_t \in  B_i$.
		      That is,
		      \begin{align}
			      \Lc{i}_t = \int_0^t \bb1\{X_r\in B_i \}\, \intd \Lc{i}_r.\nonumber
		      \end{align}
		\item For $i \leq {\nb}$, if $s_i(\Lc{i}_t) = +1$ then $X_t$ is on the positive side of $B_i$.
		      Similarly, if $s_i(\Lc{i}_t) = -1$ then $X_t$ is on the negative side of $B_i$.
	\end{enumerate}
	The process $X_t$ may also be referred to as a \emph{snapping-out Brownian motion}.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:45:32.093666+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_eae6ccbf63efc8eb091be350e312350763bc3ea312937a763b95e1bc41c83357","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn def Mixing of arXiv:2411.14350, 'Randomized Geodesic Flow on Hyperbolic Groups'] Let $G$ be a group acting on a probability space $(X,\mu)$ and let $r\geq 2$ be an integer. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item [(1)] We say that the action of $G$ on $(X,\mu)$ is {\bf mixing of order $r\geq 2 $}, if for all $f_1,...,f_r \in L^{\infty}(X,\mu)$, and for all $g_1,g_2,\dots, g_r \in G$ we have 
$$
\bigg| \int_{X}\prod_{i=1}^r ( f_i\circ g_i){\rm{d}} \mu- \prod_{i=1}^r  \int_{X}f_i{\rm{d}} \mu\bigg| \to 0  \qquad\mbox{as $\min_{\ell\neq k} \, d(g_\ell,g_k)\to \infty$}.
$$

\item [(2)] We fix an $G$-invariant sub-algebra $\mathcal A$ of $L^{\infty}(X,\mu)$, and a family $N = (N_s)_{s\in \mathbb{N}}$ of semi-norms on $\mathcal A$. Then we say that the action of the group $G$ on  $(X,\mu)$ is {\bf exponentially mixing of order $r$} with respect to $d$ and $(\mathcal A,N)$, if there exist $\delta_r > 0$ and an integer $s_r\in \mathbb{N}$ such that for all $s > s_r$, $f_1,...,f_r \in  \mathcal A$ and $g_1,\dots,g_r\in G$, 
$$
 \bigg| \int_{X}\prod_{i=1}^r ( f_i\circ g_i){\rm{d}} \mu- \prod_{i=1}^r  \int_{X}f_i{\rm{d}} \mu\bigg|  \leq C {\rm e} ^{-\delta_r d_r(g_1,..,g_r)} \prod_{i=1}^r N_s(f_i) 
$$
for some finite constant $C=C(s,r)$. In this case, $\delta_r>0$ is called {\bf the rate of mixing}. 
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:57:28.735462+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_eb1a4e3a7e43ae50d30296220ad5d188d2da624a42c741f4df03f966d1c8b274","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2609.01268, 'Resultant multiplicity via projective degrees\\ and applications to tensor eigenvalues'] Assume that $I\neq (0)$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:56:37.652876+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_eb1a55346ce127bdb7a56979e5b75aa5a67209493c2a21e694c7b7614fe8e168","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Mainthm thm:density of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] Let $d\ge1$ and $r>0$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item \emph{(Positivity, uniformly in $\lambda$.)} For every $\mu\in(0,\infty]$ there is
  $\bar\eta=\bar\eta(\mu,r,d)>0$ such that
  \[
    \eta_c(\lambda,\mu)\ \ge\ \bar\eta(\mu,r,d)\qquad\text{for every admissible }\lambda\in(0,\infty] ,
  \]
  that is, for every $\lambda\in(0,\infty]$ when $\mu<\infty$ and for $\lambda=\infty$ when
  $\mu=\infty$. Equivalently, the infection started from a single particle dies out almost surely
  at every intensity below $\bar\eta$, whatever the infection rate.
\item \emph{(Finiteness at $\lambda=\infty$.)} For every $\mu\in(0,\infty]$ and every $d\ge1$,
  $\eta_c(\infty,\mu)<\infty$.
\item \emph{(The Boolean bound, $d\ge2$.)} For $d\ge2$ and every $\mu\in(0,\infty]$,
  \[
    \eta_c(\infty,\mu)\ \le\ \eta_c(\infty,\infty)\ \le\ \eta_c^{\mathrm{B}} ,
  \]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:54:18.240162+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_eb24eba2a35807b6907d63b68a2d325680cbf7cc6945f5e2e85c832ba30b57d8","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:rational-point-dimensions of arXiv:2608.29561, 'Ball codes: A coding characterization of Hausdorff and packing dimensions'] Fix an optimal oracle prefix-free Turing machine \(V\) whose outputs are rational
points in \(\mathbb Q^n\).  For an oracle \(A\subseteq\omega\) and
\(q\in\mathbb Q^n\), define
\[
K^A(q)
=
\min\{|p|:V^A(p)=q\}.
\]
For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(r\in\omega\), define
\[
K^A_r(x)
=
\min\{K^A(q):q\in\mathbb Q^n,\ |x-q|<2^{-r}\}.
\]
Define the effective Hausdorff and packing dimensions of \(x\) relative to
\(A\) by
\[
\dim_e^A(x)
=
\liminf_{r\to\infty}\frac{K^A_r(x)}{r}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Dim_e^A(x)
=
\limsup_{r\to\infty}\frac{K^A_r(x)}{r}.
\]
For nonempty \(E\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), put
\[
\dim_e^A(E)
=
\sup_{x\in E}\dim_e^A(x)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Dim_e^A(E)
=
\sup_{x\in E}\Dim_e^A(x).
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:25:55.440533+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_eb48a11c558d7b2e83b5cc9bf64f2828d98fd3b8111d55645c6461582145397a","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 17 of arXiv:2607.28215, 'Almost stochastic dominance via optimal transport'] a) A function $\psi: E \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to be \emph{$c$-convex}, if there is a function $\zeta: E \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all $x \in E$ 
$$
\psi(x) = \sup \{ \zeta(y) - c(x,y): y \in E  \}.
$$
b) We define the set of all 1-Lipschitz functions with respect to $c$ as 
$$
\mathcal{L}_1(E,c) := \{ f: E \to \mathbb{R}: f(x) - f(y) \le c(x,y) \mbox{ for all } x,y \in E  \}.
$$
c) For a $c$-convex function we define the \emph{$c$-transform}
$$
\psi^c(x) := \inf \{ \psi(y) + c(y,x): y \in E  \}.
$$","status":"unverified"}

# Target 1: joint head, key and query training retains open inferior basins

Version 1. Proof unaudited. Own work; global novelty unestablished.

## Statement

Let n>=2, b_i,kappa_i>0 and 0<a_i<b_i. Set
h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s),
L(v,k,q)=mean_i log(1+exp(-v h_i(kq))).
Train all three scalar parameters by simultaneous Euclidean GD, at any fixed eta>0.
Write r_min=min_i atanh(-a_i/b_i)/kappa_i<0.
The following nonempty open subsets of R^3 are forward invariant:

 B_-={v<0,k>0,q<0,kq<r_min},
 B_+={v>0,k>0,q>0}.

The simultaneous sign reversal (k,q)->(-k,-q) supplies two more invariant regions.
On B_-: v->-infinity, k->+infinity, q->-infinity, kq->-infinity,
L->0, and (v,k,q)/sqrt(v^2+k^2+q^2)->(-1,0,0).
On B_+ the three coordinates tend to +infinity and the normalized limit is
(1,0,0). The normalized minimum signed margins, defined here as
min_i v h_i(kq)/sqrt(v^2+k^2+q^2), tend respectively to
Gamma_-=min_i(b_i-a_i) and Gamma_+=min_i(b_i+a_i).
The largest attainable limiting normalized margin is Gamma_+; Gamma_+>Gamma_-.
Consequently the inferior basin has positive three-dimensional Lebesgue measure.
These are invariant-region results, not a classification of all initializations.

The two-token cross-attention and genuine first-token self-attention embeddings
in proofs/004 and 006 remain exact after replacing their attention parameter p
by kq. Thus the claim includes distinct examples and both labels.

## Exact updates and invariance

For s=kq put g_i=1/(1+exp(v h_i(s))),
F=mean g_i h_i(s), G=mean g_i h_i'(s)>0. The exact simultaneous updates are

 v_+=v+eta F, k_+=k+eta vqG, q_+=q+eta vkG.

In B_-, F<0, vq>0 and vk<0. Each sign is therefore preserved and the
product becomes more negative. In B_+ all increments are positive, since
s>0 and h_i(s)>a_i>0. No restriction on eta is needed.

Analyze either branch using positive variables u,w,r. On B_- take
u=-v,w=k,r=-q, x=wr=-s, t_i(x)=b_i tanh(kappa_i x)-a_i.
On B_+ take u=v,w=k,r=q,x=wr=s,t_i(x)=b_i tanh(kappa_i x)+a_i.
Both obey exactly

 Delta u=eta mean g_i t_i, w_+=w+delta r, r_+=r+delta w,
 delta=eta u mean g_i t_i', g_i=(1+exp(u t_i))^-1.

Here x,u,w,r increase, and t_i(x)>=c:=min_i t_i(x_0)>0.
Let H=max_i(a_i+b_i), M=max_i b_i kappa_i, kappa_0=min_i kappa_i.
All t_i<=H and t_i'<=4M exp(-2 kappa_0 x).

## Escape

If u remained bounded, u t_i<=u H would keep every g_i bounded below,
contradicting Delta u>=eta c mean g_i. Hence u->infinity.
If x remained bounded, min_i t_i' would have a positive lower bound d>0.
The exact product update is

 Delta x=delta(w^2+r^2)+delta^2 x.

Using w^2+r^2>=2x_0>0 and
delta/Delta u=u(mean g_i t_i')/(mean g_i t_i)>=u d/H,
we obtain Delta x>=2x_0 d u Delta u/H. The sum of u Delta u diverges
(already u>=u_0>0 and sum Delta u=infinity), contradicting bounded x.
Thus x->infinity, and the loss tends to zero.

## Factor growth is negligible relative to the head

This step is essential: it compares the margin in the actual three parameters,
not the collapsed (v,p) norm. Let D=w-r. The exact relation is
D_+=(1-delta)D. Since g_i<=exp(-c u),
0<delta<=eta M u exp(-c u)->0. Hence eventually delta<=1, and |D| is
bounded by a finite constant D_* (a finite earlier excursion is harmless).
Therefore w^2+r^2=2x+D^2<=2x+D_*^2.
Eventually delta<=1, so

 Delta x<=delta(3x+D_*^2),
 delta<=4 eta M u exp(-c u) exp(-2 kappa_0 x).

The function (3x+D_*^2)exp(-2 kappa_0 x) is bounded for x>=x_0>0.
Consequently Delta x->0, and eventually Delta x<=1. Also

 delta/Delta u<=4M u exp(-2 kappa_0 x)/c.

The mean value theorem now gives

 Delta exp(kappa_0 x)
 <=kappa_0 exp(kappa_0) exp(kappa_0 x) Delta x
 <=C (3x+D_*^2)exp(-kappa_0 x) u Delta u
 <=C' u Delta u.

Summing, using 2u Delta u<=Delta(u^2), yields
exp(kappa_0 x)<=C''(1+u^2). Thus x=O(log u), and
w^2+r^2=O(log u). In particular w/u,r/u->0. Since x->infinity and
|w-r| is bounded, both w,r tend to infinity. This proves every stated
coordinate and normalized limit.

## Margin optimality and positive measure

Endpoint limits give Gamma_+ and Gamma_-. For any parameters, let
N=sqrt(v^2+k^2+q^2). If v>=0, choose an index minimizing a_i+b_i:
min_i v h_i/N<=Gamma_+. If v<0, choose an index minimizing b_i-a_i:
min_i v h_i/N<=Gamma_-. These inequalities remain valid when that
chosen signed prediction is negative. B_+ attains the larger endpoint
asymptotically. Gamma_+>=Gamma_-+2 min_i a_i>Gamma_-.
B_- is nonempty and open; for example take v=-1,k=R,q=-R with
R^2>-r_min. A sufficiently small ball around that point lies in B_-.

## Finite stationary set (flow stability, separate from the GD basin claim)

The only finite stationary points are v=0, kq=p_bar, where
mean_i h_i(p_bar)=0. Indeed v!=0 would force k=q=0 from the factor
gradients, but F(v,0)=mean_i a_i/(1+exp(v a_i))>0.
At v=0 the remaining condition is exactly the displayed mean root.
It is negative, so k,q are nonzero. Put A=mean_i h_i(p_bar)^2/4>=0,
B=mean_i h_i'(p_bar)/2>0. The loss Hessian is

 [[A,-Bq,-Bk],[-Bq,0,0],[-Bk,0,0]].

It has one zero tangent eigenvalue and eigenvalues
(A +/- sqrt(A^2+4B^2(k^2+q^2)))/2 of opposite sign. Thus each point
on this critical curve is a saddle with one attracting and one repelling
normal direction for gradient flow. This does not assert a global
stable-manifold classification or small-step GD stability uniformly along
the noncompact curve.

## Prior work and limits

Tarzanagh et al., arXiv:2308.16898, PDF pp.3-4 defines KQ-ERM with
the explicit phrase 'for a fixed head'; Theorem 2 treats the factored
regularization path and nuclear-norm bias. Sheen et al., arXiv:2403.08699,
source sections/preliminariesAr.tex line 17 likewise fixes the linear
prediction head; its main diagonal/general theorems concern gradient flow
and exponential loss. Neither checked scope is this joint-head logistic
arbitrary-step invariant-region statement. This is a bounded comparison,
not a claim that no such result exists elsewhere. Factor-balance identities
and nuclear-norm bias are prior work, not claimed as discoveries here.
The result does not cover matrices, multiple heads, or the full R^3 basin partition.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:27:08.852796+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ec046ef5bfbae7d7c5f49984291891d74af12d504cff7374a41c044c4d9ece2f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 17 (Eigenvector master equation — Wishart case) of arXiv:2511.12623, 'The eigenvector bead process'] Fix integers $N, T \ge 1$, and let $\{\lambda_i^{(N)}\}_{i=1}^{N}$ 
denote the (ordered, positive) eigenvalues of the Wishart matrix 
\(
W^{(N)} := X_{N}^{\!\top} X_{N} \in \mathbb{R}^{N\times N}.
\)
Let $\{\mathbf{u}_i^{(N)}\}_{i=1}^{N}$ be the associated orthonormal eigenvectors. 
Consider the rank–one extension
\[
X_{N+1} = \big( X_N \;\; g \big),
\qquad g \in \mathbb{R}^{T},
\]
that is, $X_{N+1}$ is obtained by appending the column vector $g$ to $X_N$.
Let $W^{(N+1)} = X_{N+1}^{\!\top} X_{N+1}$, with eigenvalues 
$\{\lambda_i^{(N+1)}\}_{i=1}^{N+1}$ and eigenvectors $\{\mathbf{u}_i^{(N+1)}\}$.
We define
\(
g_i^{(N)} \;=\; \langle v_i^{(N)},\, g \rangle,
\)
where $v_i^{(N)}$ denotes the eigenvector associated with the eigenvalue 
$\lambda_i^{(N)}$ of the matrix $X_N X_N^{\!\top}$.

\smallskip
\noindent
Then the overlap coefficients
\(
\Omega^{(N)}_{ij} := 
\big\langle \mathbf{u}_i^{(N+1)},\, \mathbf{u}_j^{(N)} \big\rangle
\)
satisfy the relation
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\Omega^{(N)}_{k j}}{\Omega^{(N)}_{k i}} 
&= 
\frac{g_j^{(N)}}{g_i^{(N)}}
\sqrt{\frac{\lambda_j^{(N)}}{\lambda_i^{(N)}}}
\frac{\Delta_{k,i}^{(N)}}{\Delta_{k,j}^{(N)}},
\qquad 1 \le i,j \le N, \qquad
\frac{\Omega^{(N)}_{k,\,N+1}}{\Omega^{(N)}_{k i}} 
&= 
\frac{\Delta_{k,i}^{(N)}}{g_i^{(N)}}
\sqrt{\frac{1}{\lambda_i^{(N)}}}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where
\(
\Delta_{k,i}^{(N)} := \lambda_k^{(N+1)} - \lambda_i^{(N)}.
\)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:11:11.707487+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ec0bac36bb42256900aa5e2f7f0f606691963f8b054eda059b123828712ca568","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:angular-moments-comp of arXiv:2609.00698, 'Kinetic Wedge Layers and Diffusive Limit of Neutron Transport in Polygonal Domains'] Let $\phi$ be a smooth scalar function on $\Omega$ and let $q\geq0$ be an integer. Then the angular moments of the directional derivatives of $\phi$ satisfy, pointwise in $\Omega$,
\begin{align}
 \mathbf P\bigl((w\cdot\nabla)^{2q+1}\phi\bigr)
 &=0,
 \\
 \mathbf P\bigl((w\cdot\nabla)^{2q}\phi\bigr)
 &=c_q\Delta^q\phi,
 \qquad
 c_q=\frac{(2q)!}{2^{2q}(q!)^2}.
 
\end{align}
Let now $k\geq0$, let $\rho_0,\ldots,\rho_k$ be smooth and harmonic in $\Omega$, and let $U_0:=\rho_0$ while $U_\ell$ is defined recursively by (equation eq:interior-recursion-comp of the paper) for $1\leq\ell\leq k$. Then the profiles are given explicitly by a finite alternating sum of derivatives of the densities, and their velocity averages obey the solvability identities:
\begin{align}
 U_\ell
 &=
 \sum_{j=0}^{\ell}
 (-1)^j(w\cdot\nabla)^j\rho_{\ell-j},
 \qquad 0\leq\ell\leq k,
 \\
 \pkU_\ell
 &=
 \rho_\ell,
 \qquad
 \mathbf P(w\cdot\nablaU_\ell)=0,
 \qquad 0\leq\ell\leq k.
 
\end{align}
Therefore, the recursively defined profiles satisfy (equation eq:interior-coefficient-equations-comp of the paper), and $\mathbf P(w\cdot\nablaU_k)=0$ is the compatibility condition needed to continue the construction to order $k+1$. Only $\rho_0,\ldots,\rho_{k-1}$ are required to be harmonic for these identities at order $k$, which is the precise sense in which harmonicity is the solvability condition of the next order rather than an ansatz.","status":"unverified"}

write $g_S = \frac{1}{\mu(S)}\mathbb{I}_S$ for the density of the 
random variable $U_S$ having the uniform distribution on $S$ and 
being independent of $Y$. Then,
\begin{equation} 
    \int_{G}(f_Y\ast g_S(x) - 1)^2\, dx \leq \eta_S\int_{G}(f_Y(x)-1)^2\, dx,
\end{equation}
where,
$$\eta_S = \left(\frac{\sin(\pi \mu(S))}{\pi \mu(S)}\right)^2.$$
Equivalently, 
\begin{equation} 
\chi^2(Y+U_S\,\|\,U_{G}) = \chi^2(Y+U_S\,\|\,U_{G} +  U_S)
\le
\eta_S\,\chi^2(Y\,\|\,U_{G}),
\end{equation}
where
$U_{G}$ is uniformly distributed on $G$ and independent of $U_S$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T00:15:08.952685+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ec214d36c45f14904c0ade077e85e245ac0134eb43375087c297ce075f537c03","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition defn:bIs of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] For $x>0$, and $h, g\ge 0$, we define
\[
\mathbf F(x;h,g) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi x}} \left( \exp\left(-\frac{(g-h)^2}{2x}\right)-\exp\left(-\frac{(g+h)^2}{2x}\right)\right),
\]
and
\[
\mathbf I(x;h,g) = \mathbf F(x;h,g)\mathbb E\left[ \exp\left( \beta^{-1}\int_0^x B(y) \mathrm d y \right) \right],
\]
where $B:[0, x]\to \mathbb R$ is a Brownian bridge with $B(0)=g$ and $B(x)=h$, conditional on $B\ge 0$. We also define
\[
\mathbf F_0(x;h) = \frac{2h}{\sqrt{2\pi x^3}} \exp\left(-\frac{h^2}{2x}\right), \qquad
\mathbf I_0(x;h) =\mathbf F_0(x;h)\mathbb E\left[ \exp\left( \beta^{-1}\int_0^x B_3(y) \mathrm d y \right) \right],
\]
where $B_3:[0, x]\to \mathbb R_{\ge 0}$ is a Bessel$_3$ process, conditional on $B_3(x)=h$.
Finally,
\[
\mathbf F_{0,0}(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi x^3}}, \qquad \mathbf I_{0,0}(x) = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi x^3}} \mathbb E\left[ \exp\left( \beta^{-1}\int_0^x B_e(y) \mathrm d y \right) \right],
\]
where $B_e:[0, x]\to \mathbb R_{\ge 0}$ is a Brownian excursion.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:01:39.519862+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ec26ea6ce99e056615d49c97378f2403a0f962b57b74c1121e85cdc548548ce3","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:a7 of arXiv:2607.24164, 'The KLS constant is $O(\log^{1/4} n)$'] Let $W\sim\lambda$ be centered, full-dimensional, and log-concave with
finite second moments, and let $\tau_\lambda$ be a symmetric Stein kernel with
$\mathbb{E}\norm{\tau_\lambda(W)}_{\mathrm{HS}}^2<\infty$. For every $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$, the
Stein identity extends from $C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)$ to every locally Lipschitz
function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $f\in L^2(\lambda)$ and
$\nabla f\in L^2(\lambda)$:
\[
  \mathbb{E}\!\left[\inner{W}{v}f(W)\right]

\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:39:11.671750+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ec285511def467c9a0f5b4cc56a7440330929154434848666fd8fb693871fd96","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 13 (Polynomial continuity on bounded sets) of arXiv:2608.04824, 'Strong Convergence for a General Class of Random Matrix Models'] Let \(Q=\sum_w\alpha_ww\) be a noncommutative \(*\)-polynomial in
\(d\) variables.  For \(M\geq1\), set
\[
 \operatorname{Lip}_M(Q)
 =\sum_{|w|\geq1}|\alpha_w|\,|w|M^{|w|-1}.
\]
If two tuples \(A=(A_1,\ldots,A_d)\) and \(B=(B_1,\ldots,B_d)\) satisfy
\[
 \max_\kappa\bigl(\|A_\kappa\|,\|B_\kappa\|\bigr)\leq M,
 \qquad
 \delta=\max_\kappa\|A_\kappa-B_\kappa\|,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \|Q(A,A^*)-Q(B,B^*)\|\leq\operatorname{Lip}_M(Q)\delta.
\end{equation}
The same right-hand side bounds the difference of the normalized traces when
\(A\) and \(B\) are matrix tuples of the same size.
More generally, if \(Q=\sum_w C_w\otimes w\) has coefficients in a fixed
matrix algebra, the conclusions hold with
\[
 \operatorname{Lip}_M(Q)
 =\sum_{|w|\geq1}\|C_w\|\,|w|M^{|w|-1}
\]
and with the tensor-product operator norm and normalized trace.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:53:51.338619+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ec71c22ff6e741882fa6560c61dd70df01801ba7e0e6d750508e56869b94ff98","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:regions_in_limit_shape of arXiv:2605.03896, 'Dimer models on astroidal zig-zag graphs'] We say that \((x,y)\in \mathcal D_c^\circ\):

\begin{enumerate}
\item lies in the \emph{rough region} \(\mathcal L\) if \(\lambda_c(x,y)\) has a
\(\sigma\)-conjugate pair of zeroes. In this case, there is a unique zero
\(\zeta\in \Sigma_+^\circ\), and we define
\[
\Omega:\mathcal L \to \Sigma_+^\circ,
\qquad
\Omega(x,y):=\zeta.
\]

\item lies in the \emph{frozen region} \(\mathcal F_{(\alpha,\beta)}\), where
\((\alpha,\beta)\subset A_0\) is the open interval between two consecutive
angles \(\alpha,\beta\) with \(e(\alpha)\neq e(\beta)\), such that
\(\lambda_c(x,y)\) has exactly two simple zeroes in \((\alpha,\beta)\) when
the vertex \(e(\alpha)\cap e(\beta)\in V(N)\) is convex, and {two or} three
simple zeroes when it is concave.

\item lies in the \emph{quasi-frozen region} \(\mathcal Q_{(\alpha,\beta)}\),
where \((\alpha,\beta)\subset A_0\) is the open interval between two consecutive
angles \(\alpha,\beta\) with \(e(\alpha)=e(\beta)\), if \(\lambda_c(x,y)\) has
three simple zeroes in \((\alpha,\beta)\).

\item lies in the \emph{smooth region} \(\mathcal G_j\), for \(1\le j\le g\), if
\(\lambda_c(x,y)\) has four simple zeroes in \(A_j\).

\item lies on the \emph{frozen-rough boundary}
\(\mathscr{A}_{(\alpha,\beta)}\), where
\((\alpha,\beta)\subset A_0\) is the open interval between two consecutive
angles \(\alpha,\beta\) with \(e(\alpha)\neq e(\beta)\), if \(\lambda_c(x,y)\)
has a zero \(\zeta\) of order two or three in \((\alpha,\beta)\). In this case,
\(\zeta\) is unique, and we define
\[
\Omega:\mathscr{A}_{(\alpha,\beta)}\to (\alpha,\beta),
\qquad
\Omega(x,y):=\zeta.
\]
If \(\zeta\) is a zero of order three, which can occur only when the vertex
\(e(\alpha)\cap e(\beta)\in V(N)\) is concave, we call \((x,y)\) a
\emph{frozen cusp}.

\item lies on the \emph{quasi-frozen-rough boundary}
\(\mathscr{A}_{(\alpha,\beta)}\), where
\((\alpha,\beta)\subset A_0\) is the open interval between two consecutive
angles \(\alpha,\beta\) with \(e(\alpha)=e(\beta)\), if \(\lambda_c(x,y)\) has
a zero \(\zeta\) of order two or three in \((\alpha,\beta)\). In this case,
\(\zeta\) is unique, and we define
\[
\Omega:\mathscr{A}_{(\alpha,\beta)}\to (\alpha,\beta),
\qquad
\Omega(x,y):=\zeta.
\]
If \(\zeta\) is a zero of order three, we call \((x,y)\) a
\emph{quasi-frozen cusp}.

\item lies on the \emph{smooth-rough boundary} \(\mathscr{A}_{A_j}\), for
\(1\le j\le g\), if \(\lambda_c(x,y)\) has a total of four zeroes in $A_j$ (counted with multiplicity), one of which is a zero \(\zeta\) of order two or three. In this case, \(\zeta\) is unique: if \(\lambda_c(x,y)\) had
two double zeroes on \(A_j\), then it would have constant sign on \(A_j\),
forcing
\[
\int_{A_j}\lambda_c(x,y)\neq 0,
\]
contradicting imaginary-normalization. We therefore define
\[
\Omega:\mathscr{A}_{A_j}\to A_j,
\qquad
\Omega(x,y):=\zeta.
\]
If \(\zeta\) is a zero of order three, we call \((x,y)\) a
\emph{smooth cusp}; an order four zero is excluded by the same argument that rules out two double zeroes.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

To this end, we first construct a different sequence $C'=(g_n',\ldots, g_1')$ of graphs. Here, $g_n'$ consists of $A_n+F_n$ many isolated vertices, and the vertices are labelled by the elements of $\mathcal{A}_n$. Note that $C'\notin \mathcal{J}_n^{(m)}(\mathbf x)$  due to the different labelling. First, we define the sets of edges that are added in each step $i\in\mathcal{A}_n$ of the construction process of $C'$. To this end, for each $(i,x)\in V(G)$, where $i\in\mathcal{A}_n$ and $x=a$ or $x\in \mathcal{F}_n$, define the vertex set 
\begin{equation} 
V_i \coloneq \{v\colon ((i,x),(v,y)) \in E(G) \text{ for some } (v,y)\in\mathcal{A}_n \times ({\{a\}\cup\mathcal{F}_n})\}.
\end{equation} 
Here, we keep only $v$ from the tuple $(v,y)$, as the vertices in the sequence $C'$ have a number as their label (from either $\mathcal{A}_n$ or $\mathcal{F}_n$), whereas the vertices in the construction of $G$ have tuples as labels. Note that $|V_i|=m\wedge A_{i-1}$ for all $i \in \mathcal{A}_n\setminus\{1\}$. We then set $E_i \coloneq \{(i,v)\colon v \in V_i\}$ for $i\in \mathcal{A}_n\setminus\{1\}$. Note that, by this construction, $A_n$ many vertices in $g'_1$ have a label from the set $\mathcal{A}_n$, and $F_n$ vertices from $g'_1$ have a label from the set $\mathcal{F}_n$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:19:06.755778+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_eca5b37134b61b64fac3fe777ea4a0422ad19ece704ece23783fc3856b35006b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:freedman-classical of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] Let \((\mathcal F_n)_{n\ge0}\) be an increasing sequence of
\(\sigma\)-fields, and let \(X_1,X_2,\ldots\) be real-valued random variables
such that \(X_n\) is \(\mathcal F_n\)-measurable. Assume that
\[
\lvert X_n\rvert\le 1,
\qquad
\mathbb{E}\left(X_n\mid \mathcal F_{n-1}\right)=0
\]
almost surely for every \(n\ge1\). Define
\(S_0=0\), \(S_n=X_1+\cdots+X_n,\)
and
\[
V_n=\operatorname{Var}\left(X_n\mid\mathcal F_{n-1}\right),
\qquad
T_n=V_1+\cdots+V_n,
\qquad T_0=0.
\]
Then, for all \(a,b>0\),
\[
\mathbb{P}\left(
S_n>a \ \text{and}\ T_n\le b
\ \text{for some } n
\right)
\le
\exp\left(
-\frac{a^2}{2(a+b)}
\right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Bernoulli percolation on a locally finite TRANSITIVE infinite graph","the exponential-decay statement is asserted for finite-range models","the mean-field bound is quoted in the form stated in the paper's abstract"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.543363+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ece8d7f1c3d22584194ee5dead73ab7ab9a536555aea7cc7a03d5465c516a331","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For Bernoulli percolation on an arbitrary locally finite transitive infinite graph, the phase transition is SHARP: (a) for every p < p_c the susceptibility is finite, chi(p) = E_p |C(0)| < infinity, and for FINITE-RANGE models the probability of an open path from the origin to distance n decays exponentially in n; (b) for every p > p_c the mean-field lower bound P_p(0 <-> infinity) >= (p - p_c)/p holds. There is therefore no intermediate regime in which the cluster size has a heavy polynomial tail without an infinite cluster - the subcritical decay is exponential right up to p_c. The same paper proves the corresponding statements for the Ising model, with finiteness of the susceptibility below the critical inverse temperature and the mean-field magnetisation bound above it. Historically this recovers the Aizenman-Barsky and Menshikov theorems by a much shorter argument based on a differential inequality for a well-chosen family of finite-volume quantities. The result is about BERNOULLI percolation on a TRANSITIVE graph; the transitivity hypothesis is used and the statement is not asserted here for general graphs. {"assumptions":["a finite, irreducible, reversible Markov chain arising from a weighted graph with conductances c_e","the two states a, b are distinct vertices of the graph","the graph is connected, so hitting and commute times, and R_eff, are all finite","consistent normalization of the total conductance c_G matching the specific convention used for R_eff"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.993395+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ecfa965d432e2bd30d8bada02d7468db0f78ae6ff3009f102b45977594aa17a9","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For an irreducible, reversible Markov chain arising from a weighted graph with conductances c_e and total conductance c_G equal to the sum of conductances over all edges, the commute time C(a,b) = E_a[tau_b] + E_b[tau_a] between two vertices a, b satisfies the exact identity C(a,b) = 2 c_G R_eff(a,b), where R_eff(a,b) is the effective resistance in the associated electrical network. The identity is derived by checking that h(x) = P_x(hit a before b) is harmonic away from {a,b} and coincides with the network's voltage function, then relating expected hitting times to the network's energy dissipation. It converts questions about hitting, commute, and cover times of a reversible random walk into purely electrical or combinatorial resistance computations, enabling resistance-based bounds via series-parallel laws, Rayleigh monotonicity, or the Nash-Williams inequality on infinite graphs, on quantities such as cover time and mixing time. It does not directly give the individual one-way hitting time E_a[tau_b] alone, only the symmetrized commute time; and it is specific to reversible chains, since non-reversible walks lack the electrical-network correspondence and require substantially different techniques. Typical failure: Using the commute-time identity to bound a one-directional hitting time E_a[tau_b] alone by simply halving C(a,b), which is valid only under a separate symmetry argument between a and b; in general E_a[tau_b] and E_b[tau_a] can differ substantially even though their sum equals 2 c_G R_eff(a,b), so treating the identity as giving each one-way time individually, without additional justification, is a common overreach. Canonical reference: Chandra, Raghavan, Ruzzo, Smolensky and Tiwari, 1996, Random Structures and Algorithms; Lyons and Peres, Probability on Trees and Networks, 2016, Cambridge University Press, Chapter 2.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:02:18.035732+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ed00ebc639fd95ec66d355daa0bdde662fadad9abeba7ea7aefc13b8abaa1265","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:constant-escape of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a send sequence~$\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:07:35.020696+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ed0ffd4b12f7995d8d423830dc3a8aaf9d1a97b601ac94daf24df36ec3d473ff","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 40 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(Z\) be a connected complete normal klt complex space of dimension

 \qquad\text{on }\Reg Z.
\]
Assume the finite-time
tangent-space package used in \cref{thm:singular-product}: its analytic and metric
regular loci agree, \(Z\) is the metric completion of its regular locus,

\[
 d\mathfrak m=(4\pi)^{-(m+1)}e^{-f_Z}\,dV_{g_Z}

is normalized to be a probability measure.  Suppose there is a globally

{"assumptions":["2D DGFF in admissible domains; extremal process with Poisson-cluster structure (Biskup-Louidor)","Exchange of limits requires uniform integrability not currently available"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T15:09:50+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ed315b917a49a5586e8545dda8762df7dee0b7d1acded753da3ac58be204b190","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"PRIVATE REDUCTION, author-recorded. By the cluster-process structure of the DGFF extremal process (Biskup-Louidor), the number of points of the level set at depth t inside A is a Poisson sum over extremal local maxima in A of i.i.d. cluster sizes at the corresponding depths, so its conditional expectation given the extremal measure Z^D equals Z^D(A) times the integral over depth of e^{alpha s} E[cluster size at depth s] ds. Conjecture 16.5 (the count normalised by (1/t) e^{-alpha t} converges to c Z^D(A)) therefore reduces to the existence of lim e^{-alpha h} E_nu(f_h) (Conjecture 16.6) plus (i) uniform integrability of cluster sizes at depth t uniformly in N, to exchange the N and t limits, and (ii) concentration of the Poisson sum, which needs its own argument (a second-moment bound on deep cluster sizes, or truncation under the same uniform integrability): uniform integrability gives no variance bound. Conversely, 16.5 gives the limit in 16.6 by taking expectations only if the normalised counts are uniformly integrable; convergence in probability alone does not move expectations. The open content is thus 16.6 together with the uniform-in-N control of deep clusters, which the concentric decomposition delivers only at bounded depth.","status":"unverified"}

 \quad
 \widehat \mathsf{T}_2(U_n)=0,
\end{align*}
and every other vertex is unlabelled.

Suppose that $q$ is an exploration time immediately after a vertex addition. For $i\in\{1,2\}$, define the active oriented boundary of label $i$ by
\begin{align*}
 \widehat\partial_i(q)
 :=
 \big\{(a,b):
 a\in\widehat\mathcal{A}_i(q),\
 b\notin\widehat\mathcal{A}_1(q)\cup\widehat\mathcal{A}_2(q),\
 \{a,b\}\in\mathcal{E}_n^{(\ell)}
 \big\}.
\end{align*}
If an unlabelled vertex remains, the next vertex-addition time is
\begin{align*}
 q^+
 :=
 \min_{i\in\{1,2\}}
 \min_{(a,b)\in\widehat\partial_i(q)}
 \big\{\widehat\mathsf{T}_i(a)+\go_{a,b}\big\}.
\end{align*}
On $\Omega_*$, this minimum has a unique minimizing triple $(i,a,b)$.
At time $q^+$, assign label $i$ to $b$ and set
\begin{align*}
 \widehat\mathsf{T}_i(b):=q^+,
 \qquad
 \widehat\mathcal{A}_i(q^+)
 :=\widehat\mathcal{A}_i(q)\cup\{b\},
 \qquad
 \widehat\mathcal{A}_{3-i}(q^+)
 :=\widehat\mathcal{A}_{3-i}(q).
\end{align*}
The labelled sets remain unchanged between successive vertex-addition times.

An edge is called a \emph{bridge} once its endpoints carry different labels. From that time onward, the bridge is censored: its weight is not tested against any further threshold, and the edge is never used for a subsequent vertex addition. The exploration is run without stopping at the first collision. After all vertices are labelled, the process is held fixed.

In rescaled time, define for $s\geqslant0$
\begin{align*}
 \mathcal{C}_i(s):=\widehat\mathcal{A}_i(s/\mathfrak{a}_\ell ),
 \qquad
 N_i(s):=|\mathcal{C}_i(s)|,
 \quad i=1,2,
\end{align*}
and let the bridge set and its cardinality be
\begin{align*}
	\mathcal{B}_s:=\big\{\{u,v\}\in\mathcal{E}_n^{(\ell)}:u\in\mathcal{C}_1(s),\ v\in\mathcal{C}_2(s)\big\},
 \qquad
 B_s:=|\mathcal{B}_s|.
\end{align*}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T18:47:41.430489+00:00","domain":"first-order PDE","id":"claim_ed54d7f2f7b7a7d96dbbc8a67228d4b6ca38b4b45884e2cb0b37af76ddb0e0a2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"For a first-order quasilinear PDE a(x,y,u) partial u/partial x + b(x,y,u) partial u/partial y = c(x,y,u) for unknown u(x,y), the method of characteristics reduces the PDE to a family of ODEs. Parametrize characteristic curves (x(s),y(s)) together with z(s)=u(x(s),y(s)) along them by dx/ds=a(x,y,z), dy/ds=b(x,y,z), dz/ds=c(x,y,z). Along a solution of this system, u is automatically consistent with the PDE, since the chain rule gives dz/ds = (partial u/partial x)(dx/ds) + (partial u/partial y)(dy/ds) = a(partial u/partial x)+b(partial u/partial y), which equals c(x,y,z) exactly when the PDE holds. Solving the PDE with data prescribed on a noncharacteristic initial curve reduces to solving the characteristic ODEs from each point of that curve and assembling the resulting family into the solution surface, then, where the map from characteristic parameters to (x,y) is invertible, reading off u(x,y). The same idea extends to fully nonlinear first-order PDE F(x,u,Du)=0 via characteristic ODEs derived from F, which also propagate Du along the curves.","status":"unverified"}
