{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:27:32.354372+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ed57b4f180cc69b9c9546b15383284d42808233005536637f4e78d3d1a98da54","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Propn PR3 of arXiv:2509.20657, 'Scaling limit for Brownian motions \\\\ on the $l$-level Sierpinski gaskets: \\\\ The fractal '] There exist constants $c_1$ and $\\gamma$, independent of $l$ and $\\lambda$, such that if $f_l:\\mathrm{SG}(l)\\rightarrow\\mathbb{R}$ is a bounded, measurable function, then\n\\[\\left|U^l_\\lambda f_l(x)-U^l_\\lambda f_l(y)\\right|\\leq c_1 \\left(\\tau^l+\\lambda^{-1}\\right) \\left(\\left|x-y\\right|\\vee l^{-1}\\right)^{\\gamma} \\|f_l\\|_\\infty,\\qquad\\forall x,y\\in\\mathrm{SG}(l).\\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:33:01.747035+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ed581388fad192fa6e9c8864deb4a8c8567e01328d7f749d001c0ddead79debf","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 25 (Supercritical shape) of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] If $p = \omega(1 / m)$ then $p \, (1-p)^m \,
  (T_{m,p} - m \log{m})$
  converges in law to an exponential distribution with rate $1$.
  \begin{proof}
    Recall from Lemma \ref{thm:coupling} that we can
    decompose $p \, (1-p)^m \, (T_{m,p} - m \log{m})$ as
    the sum of independent random variables
    $p\,(1-p)^m\,(T_{m, 0} - m\log{m})$
    and $p\,(1-p)^m \, (T_{m,p} - T_{m,0})$.
    The second random variable~has an exponential limit
    by Theorem~\ref{thm:supercritical}.

    The classical problem has mean
    $\E T_{m, 0} = m\log{m} + O(m)$ and
    variance $\Var(T_{m,0}) = O(m^2)$. Therefore,
    the first random variable's mean is 
    \[
      \E \left[ p\,(1-p)^m\left(T_{m,0} - m\log{m}\right) \right] = p \, (1-p)^m \, O(m) =
      O\left((p\,m) \, e^{-pm}\right) = o(1),
    \]
    and its variance is
    \[
      \Var\left( p\,(1-p)^m\,\left(T_{m, 0} - m\log{m}\right) \right) =
      p^2 \, (1-p)^{2m} \, O(m^2) =
      O\left((p\,m)^2 \, e^{-2pm}\right) = o(1).
    \]
    This implies $p\,(1-p)^m \, (T_{m,0} - m \log{m}) 
    \stackrel{P}{\to} 0$.
    Extend the convergence result using Slutsky's theorem.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:30:07.956801+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ed5e3a50a1132e73e1f8165fbbde316114c64f9f9b71bf6396311094cda9f6ba","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:F-function of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Let \(\mu_{\mathrm{sc}}\) be the semicircle distribution on \([-2,2]\), with
density
\[
    f_{\mathrm{sc}}(x)=\frac{\sqrt{4-x^2}}{2\pi}.
\]
We define
\[
    F(x):=2x_+
    =
    \begin{cases}
        2x, & x\in[0,2],\\
        0,  & x\in[-2,0].
    \end{cases}
\]
Let
\[
    P_j(x):=U_j\left(\frac{x}{2}\right),
\]
where \(U_j\) is the \(j\)-th Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind.  Then
\(\{P_j\}_{j\ge0}\) is an orthonormal basis for
\(L^2([-2,2],\mu_{\mathrm{sc}})\), with \(P_0=1\) and \(P_1=x\).

We write the Chebyshev expansion of \(F\) as
\[
    F(x)=C_F+x+\sum_{j\ge2}b_j \cdot P_j(x),
\]
where
\[
    C_F=b_0=\mathbb E_{X\sim\mu_{\mathrm{sc}}}[F(X)]
    =\frac{8}{3\pi},
    \qquad
    b_1=1,
\]
and, for \(j\ge2\),
\[
    b_j\coloneqq \mathbb{E}_{x\sim \mu_{\mathrm{sc}}}[F(x)]
\]","status":"unverified"}

Zhao, Theorem 6.5.1 (lopsided local lemma): let A_1, ..., A_n be events and for each i let N(i) ⊆ [n] be such that P(A_i | ∧_{j∈S} Ā_j) ≤ P(A_i) for all S ⊆ [n] \\ (N(i) ∪ {i}) (6.1). If there are x_1, ..., x_n ∈ [0,1) with P(A_i) ≤ x_i Π_{j∈N(i)} (1 − x_j) for all i, then P(none of the events A_i occur) ≥ Π_{i=1}^n (1 − x_i). Corollary 6.5.2: if |N(i)| ≤ d and P(A_i) ≤ p for all i, and ep(d+1) ≤ 1, then with positive probability none of the events occur. A graph with these neighbourhoods is called a negative dependency graph; Zhao's example is the random injection model of Lu and Székely (2007).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["X_i independent and mean zero","each X_i sub-exponential with finite psi_1 norm K_i","no boundedness and no identical distribution required","c is an absolute constant"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:37.627795+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_eda4180819f0b7157752389f126936b1be16f6ab1c12b592bae8cb80e5ad04c2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X_1, ..., X_N be independent, mean-zero, SUB-EXPONENTIAL random variables, and write K_i for the Orlicz norm ||X_i||_{psi_1} = inf{ s > 0 : E exp(|X_i|/s) <= 2 }. Then there is an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every t >= 0, P( | sum_{i=1}^N X_i | >= t ) <= 2 exp( - c min( t^2 / sum_{i=1}^N K_i^2 , t / max_i K_i ) ). The bound has TWO regimes and that is intrinsic, not an artefact: for small t the tail is Gaussian with variance proxy sum K_i^2, and for large t it is exponential with rate 1/max_i K_i. No almost sure bound on the summands is assumed, which is what distinguishes this from the classical bounded-summand Bernstein inequality; the price is that the sub-Gaussian regime ends at t of order sum K_i^2 / max K_i rather than continuing forever. Squares of sub-Gaussian variables are sub-exponential, which is why this is the inequality behind chi-square tail bounds and the Hanson-Wright inequality. The constant c is absolute and no attempt should be made to read a specific numerical value out of this statement. [standard; e.g. Vershynin, High-Dimensional Probability, Theorem 2.8.1]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:24:47.660216+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_edb1719bbf891ca09a000a2aeddc3b01b83a954c684d37ff15859bbb70863c52","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 24 of arXiv:2605.08844, 'Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential '] Let $\mathbf X \in G\Omega_p(V)$. For each $N\in\mathbb N$ and each $1\le i\le d$, let
\(
A_i^N:\Omega\to\mathfrak h_N
\)
be a Hermitian random matrix defined on a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$. Assume that the following hold.

First, for every $k\in\mathbb N$,
\[
\sup_{N\in\mathbb N}\sup_{1\le i\le d}\sup_{1\le m,l\le N}
\mathbb E\big[|A_i^N(m,l)|^k\big]\le c_A(k)<\infty,
\]
and moreover
\[
\mathbb E[A_i^N(m,l)]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E[|A_i^N(m,l)|^2]=1.
\]

Second, there exists $K>0$ such that, for every $r\in\mathbb N$,
\[
\sup_{N\in\mathbb N}\sup_{0\le s<t\le T}
\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{1}{N^{r/2}}\|A_i^N(m,l)\|_{\mathrm{op}}^r\right]
\le K^r\Gamma\!\left(\frac{r}{2p}+1\right).
\]

Finally, assume that the sigma-algebras
\[
\bigvee_{i=1}^d \sigma(A_i^N(m,l)),
\qquad 1\le m\le l\le N,
\]
are independent, and that
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[A_i^N(m,l)A_j^N(m,l)\right]=0,
\qquad i\ne j.
\]

Define
\[
M^N\in\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb R^d,\mathfrak h_N),
\qquad
M^N(\eta)=\sum_{i=1}^d A_i^N\,\eta^{(i)}.
\]
Let $Z^N(\mathbf X)\in\mathcal D^p([0,T],U(N;\mathbb C))$ denote the solution of
\begin{equation} 
dZ^N(s,t)=\frac{i}{\sqrt N}M^N(d\mathbf X_t)\,Z^N(s,t),
\qquad
Z^N(s,s)=I_N.
\end{equation}

Then, for every $0\le s\le t\le T$ and for $\xi_N \in \mathcal{P}(\mathfrak{h}^d_N)$ denoting the law of the hermitian matrices $A^N_i$, the limit
\[
K(s,t)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\,
\mathbb E_{\xi_N}\!\left[\operatorname{Tr}(Z^N(s,t))\right]
\]
exists and is given by
\begin{equation}
K(s,t)=\sum_{|L|=0}^\infty i^{|L|}\varphi(L)\,S^{(L)}(\mathbf X)_{s,t}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, \(K\) solves the two-parameter RDE
\begin{equation}
K(s,t)=1-\int_s^t\int_s^r f(K(s,u),K(u,r))\,d\mathbf X_u\,d\mathbf X_r,
\end{equation}
where
\[
f:\mathbb R^2\to \mathrm{Hom}(V\boxtimes V, \mathbb{R}),
\qquad
f(z_1,z_2)[\eta,\xi]=z_1z_2\langle \eta,\xi\rangle_V.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["A_n and A are self-adjoint on a common Hilbert space H","the mode of convergence (strong or norm resolvent) is as in the definition of resolvent convergence","in (a) the function f is continuous and vanishes at infinity","in (b) the function f is continuous and bounded on R","f(A) means the bounded functional calculus supplied by the spectral theorem for self-adjoint operators"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:20:07.091074+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, spectral theory, functional calculus","id":"claim_edb40d994798192517bbbdee299a16a72daef10511a135ab38712d7a8be01de0","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let A_n and A be self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space H, with no assumption relating their domains. (a) If A_n -> A in the NORM resolvent sense, then f(A_n) -> f(A) in operator norm for every continuous f : R -> C vanishing at infinity. (b) If A_n -> A in the STRONG resolvent sense, then f(A_n) -> f(A) strongly for every BOUNDED CONTINUOUS f : R -> C, where f(A) is given by the functional calculus of the spectral theorem. In particular exp(i t A_n) -> exp(i t A) strongly for every real t, and for a fixed vector the convergence is uniform for t in compact sets. WHERE IT FAILS: (i) 'bounded continuous' cannot be relaxed to 'bounded Borel'. On H = C take A_n = multiplication by 1/n and A = 0 (convergence in every sense) and f the indicator of (0, infinity): then f(A_n) = 1 for every n while f(A) = 0. Convergence of spectral projections therefore needs a separate hypothesis - typically that the endpoints of the interval carry no spectral mass for A - and even then it is only strong convergence. (ii) In (b) one gets strong, never norm, convergence, because strong resolvent convergence does not imply norm resolvent convergence: on l^2 let P_n be the orthogonal projection onto the coordinates with index at least n and set A_n = P_n, A = 0; then A_n -> 0 strongly and in the strong resolvent sense, while the resolvent difference has constant operator norm. (iii) Unbounded f is outside the theorem and the natural statement is false: strong resolvent convergence does not give A_n psi -> A psi, even for psi in every domain (rank-one examples with growing coefficients show this). (iv) Nothing is assumed about domains - that is exactly why the hypothesis is phrased through resolvents rather than as pointwise convergence of the operators.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-13T03:42:25.818122+00:00","domain":"probability, Brownian motion, ergodic theory","id":"claim_edd3ee191057c39ca763758870773c942f09e028e8ea0142c98e648c2215a077","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Burdzy and Scheutzow, Forward Brownian motion (arXiv:1302.6958), Problem 7.5 (p. 26) asks: for any process {X_t, t >= 0} whose law is equivalent to Brownian motion, can one find a random piece to put in front of X so that the new process is a Brownian motion? Our result (id P0032, 2026-09-08): YES - and under absolute continuity rather than equivalence, which is weaker than the problem assumes. The mechanism is a filling-scheme lemma: for theta an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a standard Borel space (E, P) and Q = f P, there is an almost surely finite integer N >= 0 with law(theta^N Z) = Q for Z distributed as P. Apply it with E = C_0(R) under two-sided Wiener measure and (theta w)(t) = w(t+1) - w(1), lifting the one-sided density of X's law to two-sided paths; the lemma returns a finite N for which {Z(N+t) - Z(N)} has X's law while {Z(t) - Z(0)} is a Brownian motion whose first N units are exactly the prefix. Verification as the source words it: the filling construction was implemented on a finite ergodic system (Z/n with the +1 shift) for n = 5, 7, 12, 60 with random densities - total accepted mass 1.000000000000 every time, the law of theta^N Z matching f P to about 1e-16, E[N] finite - and the negative control is the informative one, since with a non-ergodic theta exactly half the mass is ever accepted and half survives forever. The L^1 ergodic-theorem step in the infinite-dimensional setting was not verified, only read; it is standard but checked by eye only. NOVELTY IS THE WEAK POINT and the campaign's own proof file volunteers it: the lemma is a filling construction related to classical work of Chacon-Ornstein, Rost and Thorisson - sound mathematics, very likely a known consequence. X's law absolutely continuous with respect to Brownian motion (weaker than the problem's equivalence) theta the unit shift with recentering on two-sided Wiener space, ergodic and invertible","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:15:16.654974+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ede87e85ab88b50d85698211cc2e4fc95319ba63dc471ed5ec8f3229248bc55a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 27 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] Let
\(
  u_0:\Sigma\to S
\)
be an orientation-preserving covering of degree \(d\) between
closed surfaces, and let \(X_g\in\mathcal T(\Sigma)\) be the conformal
structure determined by the domain metric \(g\). Denote by
\(u_0^*\Delta_q\) the pullback measured foliation on \(\Sigma\). Then
\begin{equation}

  \mathscr E_{\Delta_q}(u_0)
  =
  \frac12\,
  \operatorname{Ext}_{X_g}\!\left(u_0^*\Delta_q\right).
\end{equation}
More explicitly, write the pullback  multicurve as
\(u_0^*\Delta_q=\sum_{i=1}^r\sum_{a=1}^{r_i}\widehat\delta_{i,a}\). Let
\(\widehat\Phi=\Phi_{u_0^*\Delta_q,X_g}\) be the Hubbard--Masur
differential on \(X_g\), and let \(\widehat A_{i,a}\) be its characteristic
cylinder with core curve \(\widehat\delta_{i,a}\). If
\(\widehat M_{i,a}=\operatorname{Mod}(\widehat A_{i,a})\) denotes its
actual conformal modulus, then
\begin{equation}

  \mathscr E_{\Delta_q}(u_0)
  =
  \frac12\int_{X_g}|\widehat\Phi|
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^{r}\sum_{a=1}^{r_i}
  \frac{1}{\widehat M_{i,a}}.
\end{equation}

Suppose, in addition, that the  conformal structure on $\Sigma$ is the pullback
of the initial target structure, namely \(X_g=u_0^*X_0\in T(\Sigma)\). Then
\begin{equation}

  \mathscr E_{\Delta_q}(u_0)
  =
  \frac d2\,
  \operatorname{Ext}_{X_0}(\Delta_q)=\frac d2
  \sum_{i=1}^{r}\frac1{M_i}.
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:49:15.475043+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_edf32a2bac89d6234b6fb24909230c5760fa4e020b225f32bac46de19693cda4","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The functor $((eq:ext-orth-spc of the paper))$ is topologically enriched.
    \begin{proof}
        Recall that mapping spaces in enriched functor categories are topologized as a subspace of the product. By the universal property of the latter, the claim therefore amounts to saying that
        \[
            \textbf{\textup{maps}}_{\cat{$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}}(X,Y)\to\textbf{\textup{maps}}_{\textbf{\textup{Top}}}(\overline{X}(V),\overline{Y}(V))
        \]
        is continuous for all $X,Y\in\cat{$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}$ and $V\in{\widehat{{\smash{\textbf{\textup{L}}}\vphantom{t}}\kern-1.75pt}\kern1.75pt}$. Adjoining over and plugging in the definition of $\overline{X}(V)$, this is equivalent to continuity of
        \[X(U)\times\textbf{\textup{maps}}_{\cat{$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}}(X,Y)\to \overline{Y}(V)\]
        for all finite-dimensional $U\subset V$. But this map is simply the composite
        \[
            X(U)\times\textbf{\textup{maps}}(X,Y)\xrightarrow{\;X(U)\times\ev_U\;}X(U)\times\textbf{\textup{maps}}(X(U),Y(U))\xrightarrow{\;\ev\;} Y(U)\xrightarrow{\;\;}\overline{Y}(V),
        \]
        and each of these maps is evidently continuous.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.231143+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ee317ec81aaaaeb724ab14041ac23efa150a0c3a827a4dac1cad6b2dd5882df3","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 26 (Stokes--Betti coordinate formula) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Under the preceding hypotheses,
\begin{equation}
 [\gamma_u]
 =
 \sum_{\alpha=1}^{\mu}
 C^{\mathrm{Betti}}_{u\alpha}[\Gamma_\alpha].
 
\end{equation}
Consequently
\[
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}\in
 \operatorname{Mat}_{N\times\mu}(\mathbb Z)
\]
is locally constant on \(\mathfrak C\).  If the representatives are
transverse, then
\begin{equation}
 C^{\mathrm{Betti}}_{u\alpha}
 =
 \#_{\mathrm{or}}
 \bigl(\gamma_u\pitchfork\check\Gamma_\alpha\bigr),
 
\end{equation}
the finite signed intersection count.  Its rank, integral kernel,
cokernel, and elementary divisors are therefore computed exactly by the
Smith normal form.

Across a Stokes wall, write the change of integral descending basis as
\[
 \boldsymbol\Gamma^+
 =
 S_{\mathrm{top}}\boldsymbol\Gamma^-,
 \qquad
 S_{\mathrm{top}}\in\operatorname{GL}_\mu(\mathbb Z).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}^+
 =
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}^-S_{\mathrm{top}}^{-1}.
 
\end{equation}
Along a generic path crossing successively walls with matrices
\(S_1,\ldots,S_k\),
\begin{equation}
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}(\lambda_1)
 =
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}(\lambda_0)
 S_1^{-1}\cdots S_k^{-1}.
 
\end{equation}

If an analytically normalised thimble frame is related to the integral
frame by
\[
 \boldsymbol\Gamma^{\mathrm{an}}
 =
 G\,\boldsymbol\Gamma^{\mathrm{top}},
 \qquad
 G\in\operatorname{GL}_\mu(\C),
\]
then its selected-cycle coordinate matrix is
\begin{equation}
 C_{\mathrm{sel}}
 =
 C_{\mathrm{Betti}}G^{-1}.
 
\end{equation}
Thus nonintegral multipliers caused by analytic normalisations do not
contradict the integral Picard--Lefschetz coefficients.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:26:40.360998+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ee323e9acd1fe6027c178124fe9757153f65e1fe01bec2c76bbd5a0134405fd6","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 44 ($\delta$-coalescent vertices) of arXiv:2511.09517, 'From Cannings model to Brownian motion conditioned on local time profile'] For \(n \ge 1\) and \(\delta > 0\),  define
\begin{equation}  H = H(n,\delta) := \left\lfloor \frac{h(q_n)}{\lfloor\delta n\rfloor} \right\rfloor. 
\end{equation}
The interval $\big[s\lfloor\delta n\rfloor,(s+1)\lfloor\delta n\rfloor\big)$ is called the \textit{$s$-th height interval}. We focus on the coalescent process starting from height \((s+1)\lfloor\delta n\rfloor\) for \(s = 1, \dots, H-2\). Recall that $\cX_{s\lfloor\delta n\rfloor}\big(n, (s+1)\lfloor\delta n\rfloor\big)$
 consists of all vertices at height \(s\lfloor\delta n\rfloor\) that have at least one descendant at height \((s+1)\lfloor\delta n\rfloor\). Those vertices are referred to as the \textit{\(\delta\)-coalescent vertices} at the \( s \)-th height interval. The collection of all \(\delta\)-coalescent vertices at these height intervals is denoted by
    \[
        \bar{\cX}(n,\delta) := \bigcup_{s=1}^{H-2} \cX_{s\lfloor \delta n \rfloor}\big(n,(s+1)\lfloor \delta n \rfloor\big).
    \]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:31:20.863608+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ee65f7ce8f796ef704dd111b50a83716c68b98a02bd912c123476de1e13a2c89","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2506.10856, 'The space of multifurcating ranked tree shapes: enumeration, lattice structure, and Markov'] The space $\mathcal{T}_{N,K}$ is in bijection with the set of vectors $\{t, l\}$, each of length $K$ that satisfy the following constraints:

{"assumptions":["One FCFS server","Poisson arrival rate lambda>0","Independent exponential service rate mu>lambda","Deterministic nonnegative setup tau and grace g","Setup is never cancelled; setup arrivals queue"],"created_at":"2026-10-10T08:07:30.221932+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ee901e9ab6079a52e8000f515d63eeed51c6cfe36449a529fc20f5c928a510cc","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"PROOF OF THE STATED SCOPED RESULT; independent audit pending. Consider one FCFS server with Poisson arrival rate lambda>0 and independent exponential service rate mu>lambda. After becoming empty it remains on for deterministic grace g in [0,infinity], then switches off. A cold arrival triggers deterministic setup tau>=0, which is never cancelled; arrivals during setup wait. Put p=exp(-lambda g), x=lambda tau, rho=lambda/mu and y=p/(1+xp), with p=0 at g=infinity. The stationary mean queueing wait is lambda/[mu(mu-lambda)] + tau(1+x/2)y. If busy, on-idle, off and setup powers are B,I,O,U, average power is rho B+(1-rho)I+(1-rho)[O+xU-(1+x)I]y. Hence varying the grace period traces an affine waiting-power curve. The formula includes arrivals during setup and the subsequent busy period. It addresses k=1 and does not claim the many-server frontier or optimality among other policies.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:27:08.851897+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ee995522ed1e15c70f74b190d4e70387624f9742de07d15197ca3b2f7a63597a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 5 (Hard edge, \(q=1\)) of arXiv:2511.12623, 'The eigenvector bead process'] Fix \(K\in\mathbb{N}\) and an integer \(\alpha > K\).
Let \(T - N = \alpha\).
For each \(s\in\{0,\dots,K\}\), let \(\{\lambda^{(s)}_{j}\}_{j=1}^{N+s}\) denote the spectrum of the matrix \(X_{N+s}^\top X_{N+s}\),
and define the point process
\[
\Theta_{N}^{(s)} \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{N+s} \delta_{\,4N\,\lambda_{j}^{(s)}}.
\]
Then the process \(\big(\Theta_{N}^{(s)}\big)_{s=0}^{K}\) forms a Markov chain in \(s\) and converges in distribution to the Markov chain driven by the operator \(\mathcal{T}\).
The limiting point process of eigenvalues
\(
\Theta^{(s)} \;=\; \lim_{N\to\infty} \Theta_{N}^{(s)}
\)
is the \emph{Bessel point process} of parameter~\(\alpha\), describing the universal statistics at the hard edge of the spectrum. \cite{forrester1993hard,tracy1994bessel,forrester2010log} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:31:49.913183+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_eea87c0f43aa8479a23ce621c44877c8bd712f1671994b46602d58143e6b6ae3","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:mass-selection of arXiv:2608.28330, 'Realising atomless laws as distance distributions on metric measure spaces'] Let $I=\{1,\ldots,N\}$ for some $N\in\mathbb N$, or let

		\[
		\begin{alignedat}{2}
			&p_0+\sum_{i\in I}p_i

			&\qquad
			&\sum_{i\in I}p_i^2

		\end{alignedat}
		\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:45:10.120657+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_eeb1ede202905a69c010b7a27531edd642bba0c9a3f90f02e0930060574d855c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:basic_properties_of_PPPs of arXiv:2505.07145, 'Nonamenable Poisson zoo'] Let $\mathcal{X} = \sum_{i \in I} \delta_{(x,H)_i} \sim \mathcal{Q}_{\nu}^\lambda$ be as in Definition (def:Poisson_zoo_as_PPP of the paper) and given any $A \in \mathcal{Z}$ introduce the restricted measure $\nu_A(\cdot) := \nu ( \cdot \cap A)$.
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:36:44.527446+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_eec33edf4ae78009e0b5b174b9c69aad0c4d069c0fef2aa28876ddd785928871","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Dfn 8 of arXiv:2604.01748, 'Largest-loop-first loop-erased random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^{4}$'] \begin{itemize}
   \item[(D1)] Let $b_{n} = n (\log n)^{-2}$ and $M = (\log n)^{2}.$ We divide the time interval $[0,n]$ into $M$ subintervals of equal length ($= b_{n}$) as follows. Let 
$$I^{1} (j) = \big[ n - j b_{n}, n - (j-1) b_{n} \big] =: [t^{1}_{j}, t^{1}_{j-1}] \ \ \ \text{ for \ \  $j =1, 2, \cdots , M$.} $$
 Note that $ 0 = t^{1}_{M} < t^{1}_{M-1} < \cdots < t^{1}_{1} < t^{1}_{0} = n. $

Similarly, we divide the time interval $[n,2n]$ in the same way as follows. Let 
$$I^{2} (j) = \big[ n + (j-1) b_{n}, n + j b_{n} \big] =: [t^{2}_{j-1}, t^{2}_{j}] \ \ \ \text{ for \ \  $j =1, 2, \cdots , M$.}$$
 Note that $ n= t^{2}_{0} < t^{2}_{1} < \cdots < t^{2}_{M-1} < t^{2}_{M} = 2n.  $

\item[(D2)] We set 

$$ L^{1} (j) = \text{len} \, \Big( \text{LE}^{\ast} \big( S [t^{1}_{j}, t^{1}_{j-1}  ] \big) \Big) \ \ \ \text{and } \ \ \ L^{2} (j) = \text{len} \, \Big( \text{LE}^{\ast} \big( S [t^{2}_{j-1}, t^{2}_{j}  ] \big) \Big). $$

As in (20) of \cite{DS-SW-4d}, we let 
$$ L^{\ast} = \max \big\{ j + k \ : \ I^{1} (j) \leftrightarrow I^{2} (k) \big\} $$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:11:02.359645+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_eec83666d4540435c0cbc9338be88813d17adac64ba25bc87e580084160f651f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop of arXiv:2507.09421, 'Stability of randomly switching stochastic reaction networks with asymptotically linear tr'] In Example (ex:different-stability-in-each-environment of the paper), the mixed process is exponentially ergodic for any choice of $\kappa>0$.
\begin{proof}
    Fix $\kappa>0$, and consider the function defined by
    \[
        h_\kappa(x,i)=\begin{cases}
            90 x^{\kappa/3} & i=1\\
            57 x^{\kappa/3} & i=2
        \end{cases}.
    \]
    Notice that
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal L_\kappa h_\kappa(x,1)
        &=(2x+1)(90(x+1)^{\kappa/3}-90x^{\kappa/3})
        +x(90(x-1)^{\kappa/3}-90x^{\kappa/3})
        +\kappa(57x^{\kappa/3}-90x^{\kappa/3})\\
        &=(2x+1)(30\kappa x^{\kappa/3-1}+o(x^{\kappa/3-1}))
        -x(30\kappa x^{\kappa/3-1}+o(x^{\kappa/3-1}))
        -33\kappa x^{\kappa/3}\\
        &=-3\kappa x^{\kappa/3}+o(x^{\kappa/3}),
    \end{align*}
    and similarly
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal L_\kappa h_\kappa(x,2)
        &=(x+1)(57(x+1)^{\kappa/3}-57x^{\kappa/3})
        +3x(57(x-1)^{\kappa/3}-57x^{\kappa/3})
        +\kappa(90x^{\kappa/3}-57x^{\kappa/3})\\
        &=(x+1)(19\kappa x^{\kappa/3-1}+o(x^{\kappa/3-1}))
        -3x(19\kappa x^{\kappa/3-1}+o(x^{\kappa/3-1}))
        +33\kappa x^{\kappa/3}\\
        &=-5\kappa x^{\kappa/3}+o(x^{\kappa/3}).
    \end{align*}
    The desired result follows from Theorem (thm:Lyapunov-exponential-ergodicity of the paper).
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em,
series=limitingpackage]
\item The regular locus \(\mathcal R\) is connected and dense,
\(d|_{\mathcal R}\) is its intrinsic length distance, and \(Z\) is a
complete locally compact length space equal to the metric completion of
\(\mathcal R\).
\item There is a smooth function \(f\) on \(\mathcal R\) for which
\begin{equation}
 \Rc_g+\nabla^2f=\frac12g\qquad\text{on }\mathcal R;
\end{equation}
the distinguished probability measure satisfies
\begin{equation}
 d\mathfrak m=(4\pi)^{-n}e^{-f}\,dV_g\quad\text{on }\mathcal R,
 \qquad \mathfrak m(Z\setminus\mathcal R)=0,
 \qquad \mathfrak m(Z)=1,
\end{equation}
and \(\mathfrak m\) has finite second moment.
\item The tangent space is an exact self-similar metric soliton flow.
On regular convergence charts, in time-compatible gauges, the rescaled
metrics and distinguished densities converge smoothly to \(g\) and the
positive density in \eqref{sp:eq:measure}.
\item For every compact \(K\subset Z\) and every \(p\in(2,4)\), the
zero extension of \(r_{\rm Rm}\) is one-Lipschitz and
\begin{equation}
 \Vol_g\bigl(\{r_{\rm Rm}<\varepsilon\}\cap K\cap\mathcal R\bigr)
 \le C_{K,p}\varepsilon^p,
 \qquad 0<\varepsilon<1;
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{K\"ahler conclusions.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em,
resume=limitingpackage]
\item The regular soliton \((\mathcal R,g,J)\) is K\"ahler, \(J\) is
parallel and time invariant, and the rescaled complex structures converge
smoothly to \(J\) on regular convergence charts.
\item If \(n=2\), then \(Z\) is a K\"ahler orbifold and
\(\Sing Z\) consists of isolated orbifold points.
\end{enumerate}

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Complex-analytic conclusions.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em,
resume=limitingpackage]
\item The space \(Z\) is a normal klt complex space.  Its analytic and
metric topologies agree, and its analytic and metric regular loci
coincide.  The regular K\"ahler form extends locally across \(\Sing Z\)
as a positive current with bounded potential.  Every point has a local
closed analytic embedding \(V\hookrightarrow\Omega_V\subset\C^L\) such
that, on \(V\cap\mathcal R\),
\begin{equation}
 \omega_g\ge c_V\omega_{\C^L}|_V.
\end{equation}
\item The function \(f\) extends uniquely to a locally Lipschitz function
on \(Z\).  The flow of \(\nabla f\) is complete, preserves
\(\mathcal R\), and extends to a one-parameter group of biholomorphisms
of \(Z\).
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:59:58.430110+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ef1a0d92385511f20c92ada76cd9dcdfaba73515e539fad46827078b69a68363","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:extended.filtered.gaussian of arXiv:2604.22453, 'Adapted Wasserstein Barycenters of Gaussian Processes'] Let
\[
\mathscr L_K(T,d):=\{\mathbf L = (\mathbf{L}_{t,s})_{s,t = 1}^T \in (\mathbb{R}^{d\times Kd})^{T \times T}: \mathbf L_{t,s}=0\textup{ whenever }s>t\},
\]
where each $\mathbf{L}_{t,s}$ has $K$ column blocks $\mathbf{L}_{t,s}^{k} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$. For $a \in \mathbb{R}^{Td}$ and $\mathbf{L} \in \mathscr{L}_K(T, d)$, define the filtered process
\[
\mathbb{G}_K^{a,\mathbf L}:=\left(\mathbb{R}^{TKd},\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^{TKd}),\mathcal{N}_{TKd}(0,I),\mathbb{F}^{\boldsymbol{\epsilon}},X=a+\mathbf {L}\boldsymbol{\epsilon}\right),
\]
where $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}=(\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_t)_{t=1}^T$, $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_t=(\epsilon_t^1,\ldots,\epsilon_t^K)$, is the canonical process and $\mathbb{F}^{\boldsymbol\epsilon}$ is the filtration generated by $\boldsymbol\epsilon$. Explicitly, for each $t$ we have
\begin{equation} 
X_t = a_t + \sum_{s = 1}^t \mathbf{L}_{t,s} \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_s = a_t + \sum_{s = 1}^t \sum_{k = 1}^K \mathbf{L}_{t,s}^{k} \epsilon_s^k. 
\end{equation}
We call $\mathbb{G}_K^{a,\mathbf L}$ an ensemble filtered Gaussian process and denote the corresponding space by $\mathcal{FG}_K(T,d)$, and its $\mathcal{AW}_2$-completion by $\mathrm{FG}_K(T,d)$. Letting $K=1$ recovers the standard filtered Gaussian process.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Deterministic initial coordinates with h_j e0,j squared=j^-gamma","Bt mutually independent fresh Gaussian inputs with covariance diag(j^-alpha)","Finite expected risk at deterministic t; finite-variance independent centered label noise","Updates lie in the span of observed inputs; data-dependent coefficients allowed","Independent review pending; optional optimal-step corollary depends on unaudited C02/C03."],"created_at":"2026-10-21T19:59:03.292447+00:00","domain":"stochastic optimization","id":"claim_ef32f8b8a5c7f1a6674c7630d45b5382c9f5f570bddb934911b55c4caa2768ce","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"PROOF (UNAUDITED), w741-T422-C06 v1. Not independently checked.
# T422 Target 2: a finite-sample-span upper confidence bound

Status: proof (unaudited), C06 v1. The constants below are explicit but the
bound is not asserted to have the sharp epsilon exponent of a typical noise
scale. The fixed-time theorem does not depend on C02 or C03; its final optional
optimal-step corollary inherits their unaudited status.

## Statement

Use the fresh Gaussian online least-squares model: H=diag(h_j),
h_j=j^(-alpha), alpha>1, deterministic initial errors satisfying
h_j e_0,j^2=j^(-gamma), gamma>1. Gaussian L2 predictions are used if the
coefficient vector is not in ordinary l2, as explained in model_conventions.md.
Labels have independent centered noise of finite variance sigma2>=0.
Each of t>=1 deterministic steps uses B>=1 independent fresh samples,
B an integer. A fixed positive step suffices. More generally, the proof
only requires that every update be a finite linear combination of that
step's input vectors, that the Bt inputs remain mutually independent with
law N(0,H), and that expected risk at t is finite.

For ell=1,2 define

    V(e)=sum_j h_j e_j^2,
    W_(ell+1)(e)=sum_j h_j^(ell+1)e_j^2,
    v_t=E V(e_t), Z_r=zeta(r),
    R_ell(e)=1+Z_(ell alpha)(V(e)+sigma2)/W_(ell+1)(e).

These are the single-example instantaneous noise scales: ell=1 is unweighted,
ell=2 is Hessian-weighted. Fix confidence parameter theta in (0,1), and put

    K=Bt, d=K+1,
    A_d=sum_(j=1)^d e_0,j^2/h_j=sum_(j=1)^d j^(2alpha-gamma)>0,
    L_den=h_d^(ell+2) A_d theta^2/(16d)>0.

Then

    P(W_(ell+1)(e_t)>=L_den)>=1-theta/2.                  (S1)

Consequently, with probability at least 1-theta, e_t!=0 and

    1+Z_(ell alpha) <= R_ell(e_t)
      <=1+[16d Z_(ell alpha)/(h_d^(ell+2)A_d theta^2)]
                   [2v_t/theta+sigma2].                  (S2)

The probability of e_t=0 is zero. If t is a finite first EXPECTED-risk
hit v_t<=epsilon Z_gamma, substitute that upper bound for v_t in (S2).
The hitting index is deterministic here; a realized-risk stopping time
requires an additional argument.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:14:57.719523+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_ef5880d642179271a2a05bcc6de6a1b9a16fae55691fc18aeb34dde63f8df92b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defin def:spect of arXiv:2605.31054, 'On the empirical spectral distribution of matrix perpetuities'] \ 
    For any $N\times N$ real  random matrix ${\mathbf Y}$ with eigenvalues $(\lambda_k({\mathbf Y}))_{k=1}^N$, we define the empirical spectral distribution and the expected empirical spectral distribution by $\hat{\mu}_{{\mathbf Y}}$ and $ \mu_{{\mathbf Y}}$ respectively, by 
    \[
    \hat{\mu}_{\mathbf Y} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^N \delta_{\lambda_k({\mathbf Y})},\qquad \mu_{{\mathbf Y}}={\mathbb E}[\hat{\mu}_{\mathbf Y}],

    \[
        \gamma_-(t) = \frac{2(x_0 L_0(t) + b)}{\sigma^2 K(0)} \ \text{ and } \ \gamma_+(t) = \frac{2\Lambda(t)}{\sigma^2 K(0)},

{"assumptions":["entries of Z i.i.d., mean zero, variance one (finite second moment suffices for the almost-sure convergence in the Bai-Silverstein form)","the spectral distribution of Sigma converges weakly to H; p/n -> c in (0, infinity)","Sigma and Z independent (Sigma may be random)"],"created_at":"2026-09-05T07:53:48.737960+00:00","domain":"random matrix theory","id":"claim_ef9d87ff35f4c090aed907a91632374e92ff38ec27c2bf7bbb3585b46a41183e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $X = Z\\Sigma^{1/2}$ be $n \\times p$ with $Z$ having i.i.d. entries of mean $0$ and variance $1$, $\\Sigma$ positive semidefinite, and let $S = \\frac{1}{n}X^T X$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:26:26.793675+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_efa604d873ca34fb3510b8a992cac5039fbcd6a7bc5e8a096ac40717b46a2b51","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:construction-until-explosion of arXiv:2608.05105, 'Cluster-Cluster model in $\mathbb{Z}^d$'] Let \(\alpha<0\), and write \(\beta=-\alpha>0\). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:11:02.357815+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_efb2b986b6fe624f2e4292375b08dfc23949dd7d8ed64d88f7f754414b70d840","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop evanescent of arXiv:2507.09421, 'Stability of randomly switching stochastic reaction networks with asymptotically linear tr'] Let $X$ be a CTMC on $\mathbb S\subseteq \mathbb Z^d$, and let $x\in\mathbb S$. Then $x$ is evanescent for $X$ iff when started from state $x$ with positive probability the process never enters a recurrent state.
\begin{proof}[Proof Sketch]
    First, assume that $\lim\limits_{t\to\infty}\@ifstar{\oldnorm}{\oldnorm*}{X(t)}_{\ell^1}\to\infty$ occurs with positive probability. Given this event, the process almost surely does not enter a recurrent state because if a recurrent state is visited once then it is a.s.~visited infinitely many times [Norris_1997].
    
    For the reverse implication, suppose that $\liminf\limits_{t\to\infty}\@ifstar{\oldnorm}{\oldnorm*}{X(t)}_{\ell^1}$ is finite with probability one. Note that for all $R\in\mathbb R$, the event that the process ever enters a recurrent state contains, up to a set of measure zero, the event that $\liminf\limits_{t\to\infty}\@ifstar{\oldnorm}{\oldnorm*}{X(t)}_{\ell^1}\le R$. Indeed, otherwise we could use the fact that $\{y\in\mathbb Z^d:\@ifstar{\oldnorm}{\oldnorm*} y_{\ell^1}\le R\}$ is finite to conclude that there existed a specific transient state $y$ which was visited infinitely often with positive probability, contradicting transience of $y$. Sending $R\to\infty$, the result follows from continuity of probability. 
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["independent coordinates with finite ranges","f real valued"],"created_at":"2026-10-06T08:50:16.134016+00:00","domain":"Hoeffding (ANOVA) decomposition on finite product spaces","id":"claim_efbdb008ccb6e350f19afa4b831a7f5eb8be29254ef907e1f0e1aedf7377ba81","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) have independent coordinates with finite ranges, f a real function of X, and f = sum over S of f_S its Hoeffding (ANOVA) decomposition over subsets S of {1, ..., n}: f_S depends only on X_S, f_empty = E f, and E[f_S | X_T] = 0 unless S is inside T. Put w_S = E[f_S^2] and W_k = sum over |S| = k of w_S, the variance at interaction order k. Let A_q be a random set, independent of X, containing each coordinate independently with probability q in [0, 1], and M(q) = E over A_q of E Var(f | X_{A_q^c}). Then M(q) = sum over nonempty S of [1 - (1 - q)^|S|] w_S = Var(f) - J(1 - q), with J the Bernoulli reveal profile, and M(q) = (1/2) E[(f(X) - f(X^(A_q)))^2], where X^(A) redraws X_A independently from its own law. For every r >= 1, (-1)^(r+1) M^(r)(q) = sum_{k=r}^n (k)_r (1 - q)^(k - r) W_k >= 0 with (k)_r = k(k - 1)...(k - r + 1); so M is increasing and concave, M'(0) = sum_k k W_k = sum_i E Var(f | X_{-i}), and the derivatives at any q determine the spectrum. For a pure order-d function, J(p) = p^d Var(f) and M(q) = [1 - (1 - q)^d] Var(f).","status":"unverified"}

\[

=

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:01:22.619863+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_efe18efd23b33db04725be1aa644693c5c20d0ef2dd75cbe7d84c4866c540a24","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Th th_2d_structure of arXiv:2606.23648, '\textsc{Optimal Stopping for a Diffusion with Unobserved Bernoulli Drift}'] In the setting of Theorem~(th_fixed_x_solution of the paper), the two-dimensional continuation region $\mathcal{C}$ has the sectional representation
    (equation C_sectional_representation of the paper), where each nonempty section \(\mathcal C_x\) is a bounded interval \((a(x),b(x))\). On this region the value function is given by
    \[
        U(x,y)=Q(x)G(y)+R(x)-cyG(y),
        \qquad a(x)<y<b(x),
    \]
    in the notation of (equation def_q_R_coefficients of the paper), (equation def_G of the paper),
    while \(U(x,y)=k(x+y)\) outside \(\mathcal C\).

    \noindent \textbf{(i)} \quad 
    The continuation region expands diagonally: if \((x,y)\in\mathcal C\) and
    \(h\ge0\), then
    \(
        (x+h,y-h)\in\mathcal C.
    \)
    Consequently, \(\mathcal I\) of (equation def_I_active of the paper) is a right-interval, \(d(x)=x+a(x)\) is non-increasing on \(\mathcal I\), and diagonal contact is sticky: if
    \(a(\bar x)=-\bar x\) for some \(\bar x\in\mathcal I\), then
    \(
        a(x)=-x,\, x\in\mathcal I,\, x\ge\bar x.
    \)
    
    \noindent If, in addition, (ass_3 of the paper) holds, then the continuation region expands vertically:
    \[
        (x,y)\in\mathcal C,\ h\ge0
        \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
        (x+h,y)\in\mathcal C.
    \]
    In particular,
    \[
        a(x+h)\le a(x),
        \qquad
        b(x+h)\ge b(x),
        \qquad x\in\mathcal I,\ h\ge0.
    \]

    \noindent \textbf{(ii)} \quad 
    The free boundaries satisfy the integral equations (equation interior_boundary_system_2d of the paper), (equation active_boundary_system_2d of the paper) below. If the relevant side branches of \(y\mapsto\Phi(x,y)\) have no flat portions, then the boundary functions are continuous on intervals where the boundary regime is fixed. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-13T03:42:25.818859+00:00","domain":"stochastic partial differential equations, critical spaces","id":"claim_effba42cec25ae591c3110d1d76f924fec66cce67e2576dd849ba846dfc69a4f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Agresti and Veraar, Nonlinear parabolic stochastic evolution equations in critical spaces (journal version 2025, p. 130), Problem 4 asks whether in the variational setting of their Theorem 6.4 there is a constant C_T with E sup_{t <= T} ||u(t)||_H^2 <= C_T (1 + E ||u_0||_H^2) for all u_0 in L^2(Omega; H). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:58:01.581348+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f005a16c2578467f8120ac4ffbda0cca52795b28e495fd11270552b131d1bf53","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 55 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Fix $N,n\ge1$, $K_{\rm feat}<\infty$, $\beta>0$, and
		$\vartheta\ge1$.  Let
		$W\in\R^N$ be a $(K_{\rm feat},\tau)$-regular feature with
		covariance matrix $\Sigma$, put
		$\lambda_{\Sigma}=\|\Sigma\|_{\op}>0$, and let $G$ be the matching centered
		Gaussian feature.  Let $W_1,\ldots,W_n$ and $G_1,\ldots,G_n$ be
		independent arrays of iid copies of $W$ and $G$, respectively.
		There are constants $C<\infty$ and $c_0>0$, depending only on
		$K_{\rm feat}$, with the following property.

		Let
		$\mathcal D\subset\R^N$ be nonempty, bounded, convex, and relatively
		open in its affine hull, and let
		$\mathcal B:\mathcal D\to[0,\infty)$ be a
		$\vartheta$-self-concordant barrier.  Fix $(\theta_{\rm ref},b_{\rm ref})\in\mathcal D\times\R$, and set
		\[
			K_{\rm ref}:=
			1+\lambda_{\Sigma}\|\theta_{\rm ref}\|_2^2+b_{\rm ref}^2
			+\mathcal B(\theta_{\rm ref}).
		\]
		Put
		\[
			\mathfrak L_n:=1+\vartheta\log n
		\]
		and
		\[
			\Delta_n:=
			(1+\beta^{-1})^2K_{\rm ref}^2\left[
			\frac{\sqrt{\dim\mathsf V_{\mathcal D}}(\tau/\lambda_{\Sigma}+1)}{n}
			+\left(\frac{\mathfrak L_n}{n}\right)^{1/3}
			\right]
			+\frac{(1+\beta)K_{\rm ref}}{n}.
		\]
		If $\mathfrak L_n\le c_0n$, then
		\begin{equation}
			
			\left|
			\E\Phi_W(\mathcal D;\beta)
			-\E\Phi_G(\mathcal D;\beta)
			\right|\le C\Delta_n.
		\end{equation}
		Moreover, for every $t>0$,
		\begin{equation}
			
			\Pp\left\{
			\left|\Phi_W(\mathcal D;\beta)-\Phi_G(\mathcal D;\beta)\right|
			>C\Delta_n+t
			\right\}
			\le\frac{C(1+\beta^{-1})^2K_{\rm ref}^2}{nt^2}.
		\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:13:22.516900+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f01dc5eef7bf6f6e35fb169c089c433a1ee54ef7f465d58e7e53f8cc31f2d4ee","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm conformal invariance aut H of arXiv:2505.16093, 'Multiple chordal SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Moser system'] For conformal map $\tau \in {\rm Aut}(\mathbb{H})$, the drift term

   \log(\psi)-\log(\psi \circ \tau)+\frac{\kappa-6}{2\kappa}\sum_i \log(\tau'(z_i)) = F(\tau,u)

    and $F$ satisfies the following functional equation:
   \begin{equation} 
      F(\tau_1 \tau_2 ,u)= F(\tau_1,\tau_2(u))+F(\tau_2,u)
   \end{equation}

    \]

    \[
   \psi_2 = g(u) \cdot \psi_1.
    \]

    \item[(iv)] For \( \tau \in \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{H}) \) and $u \in \overline{\mathbb{H}}$, we define:
    \begin{itemize}

    \[
    F(\tau, u) = d \cdot \log \left(\tau'(u)\right),
    \]

    F(\tau, u)= F(-\frac{1}{\tau},u)
    \]
    \item If $\tau(u)\neq \infty$, $u= \infty$
    \[
    F(\tau, u)= F(-\frac{1}{\tau},0)
    \]

    \[
    F(\tau,\infty) = -d \cdot \log(a)
    \]
        \end{itemize}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:24:20.646987+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f01efc4c1dae1d5ba2c3d43b8a0c4eb7d59495e3d46b36542a90b2f8eb385184","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma LemGroundStateVisitation of arXiv:2608.11178, 'A submartingale for the probability of avoiding the origin in one-point interaction ground'] Fix \(d\in\{2,3\}\), \(T,\gamma>0\), and \(x\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}\). {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:29:00.763741+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f03b3d2f17cb0c0e4939269befce52ca52c06989d6166c07e7deb999b918fd50","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 8 (Integration regimes) of arXiv:2512.04646, '\textbf{Canonical Rough Path over Tempered Fractional Brownian Motion: Existence, Construc'] Let $B_{H,\lambda}$ be a tfBm and $X$ a suitable integrand path.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.542735+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f03dd267f4dbe993abe345addd53bd73d98a6535068e27ed077b61bcdaa98a66","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"In BOND percolation on a graph G with parameter p in [0,1], each edge is declared open with probability p and closed otherwise, independently; P_p denotes the resulting product measure on {0,1}^{E(G)}. The open cluster C(x) of a vertex x is the set of vertices reachable from x through open edges. Write theta(p) = P_p( |C(0)| = infinity ) for a fixed origin. Coupling all parameters on a common family of independent uniform variables - edge e open at level p exactly when U_e <= p - shows theta is nondecreasing, so the CRITICAL PROBABILITY p_c(G) = sup{ p : theta(p) = 0 } = inf{ p : theta(p) > 0 } is well defined. SITE percolation is defined analogously with vertices; the two have different critical values on the same graph, and p_c^{bond} <= p_c^{site} on any graph. On Z^d with d >= 2 one has 0 < p_c < 1, with the explicit elementary bounds 1/(2d-1) <= p_c^{bond}(Z^d) < 1. The value is known exactly only in special cases, most famously p_c^{bond}(Z^2) = 1/2. Whether theta(p_c) = 0 in every dimension is a celebrated open problem: it is known for d = 2 (Harris and Kesten) and, by lace-expansion methods, in high dimensions - Hara and Slade for large d, later reduced to d >= 11 by Fitzner and van der Hofstad - and it was still open for the intermediate dimensions 3 <= d <= 10 at the time this node was written. [standard; e.g. Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Chapters 1 and 8]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["U bounded open subset of R^n, T > 0","coefficients a^{ij}, b^i, c continuous and bounded on U_T, a^{ij} symmetric","uniform parabolicity a^{ij} xi_i xi_j >= theta |xi|^2, theta > 0","u in C^2_1(U_T) cap C(closure of U_T)","(i) c identically 0; (ii) c >= 0; (iii) c bounded, any sign"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:49.105343+00:00","domain":"parabolic partial differential equations","id":"claim_f03e386fb9557b285d496bfc6d87098fa7e50ca3e1ef3cd59aee58e564394ae8","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $U\\subset\\mathbb R^n$ be bounded and open, $T>0$, and let $\\partial_t+L$, $Lu=-a^{ij}u_{x_ix_j}+b^iu_{x_i}+cu$, be uniformly parabolic with coefficients continuous and bounded on $U_T$. Let $u\\in C^2_1(U_T)\\cap C(\\overline{U_T})$. (i) If $c\\equiv0$ and $u_t+Lu\\le0$ in $U_T$, then $\\max_{\\overline{U_T}}u=\\max_{\\Gamma_T}u$ (and if $u_t+Lu\\ge0$, then $\\min_{\\overline{U_T}}u=\\min_{\\Gamma_T}u$). {"assumptions":["i.i.d. nonnegative weights on Z^d, d >= 2","F(0) < p_c(d), so the time constant is a norm and the shape is bounded","E min{t_1^d, ..., t_{2d}^d} < infinity, equivalently E[Y^d] < infinity for Y the minimum of 2d independent copies of tau_e - and this condition is necessary, not just sufficient","no curvature, strict convexity or differentiability of B_nu is asserted; those are open"],"created_at":"2026-10-12T16:00:40+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f04b0c4ede53c43a4b671c5940e1cf1f891850e48c1cc9a9a34d6b9355fd1e2f","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Consider i.i.d. first-passage percolation on Z^d, d >= 2, with edge-weight law nu. Assume the two conditions (i) E min{ t_1^d, ..., t_{2d}^d } < infinity, where the t_i are 2d independent copies of tau_e - equivalently E[Y^d] < infinity where Y is the MINIMUM of 2d copies, the two being the same because x -> x^d is increasing on [0, infinity) - and (ii) F(0) < p_c(d). Let B(t) = {x : T(0, x) <= t}, the random ball. Then there is a DETERMINISTIC, convex, COMPACT set B_nu in R^d with NON-EMPTY INTERIOR, symmetric about the axes, such that for every eps > 0, P( (1-eps) B_nu is contained in B(t)/t which is contained in (1+eps) B_nu for all large t ) = 1. The set B_nu is the unit ball of the time constant. Condition (i) is NOT merely convenient: if it fails then for every C > 0 the sum over x of P(m(x) > C|x|) diverges, where m(x) is the minimum weight over the edges at x, and Borel-Cantelli forces T(0,x)/|x| > C for infinitely many x almost surely, so the shape statement itself fails. Condition (ii) is what keeps the shape bounded: if F(0) >= p_c the time constant vanishes (Kesten) and B_nu is all of R^d; zero-weight edges percolate when F(0) > p_c, but at F(0) = p_c they do not in d = 2 or in high dimensions, so it is the vanishing time constant, not percolation of zero-weight edges, that unbounds the shape. What is NOT known, and is repeatedly imported elsewhere as an unproven hypothesis: whether the boundary of B_nu is STRICTLY CONVEX, whether it is DIFFERENTIABLE, and whether it has uniformly positive CURVATURE. Those are open for every non-degenerate weight distribution in every dimension, which is why the Newman-Piza exponent bounds and the directed-geodesic results carry non-constructive curvature or differentiability hypotheses. B_nu is not computed explicitly for any non-trivial F. [Cox and Durrett (1981), verified against Auffinger, Damron and Hanson, 50 Years of First-Passage Percolation, Section 2.2]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:29:23.338984+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f078cf83609ed2d9bd2aed521d1d5181cc133405cb3d1b3bf45468da67038da4","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 15 of arXiv:2512.05687, '$L^p$-Boltzmann-Gibbs principle \\ via Littlewood-Paley-Stein inequality'] (Iteration lemma,
cf.\ Lemma 5.5 of \cite{BFS})
Let $p\ge 4$ and let $f$ be a local $L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})$ function on
$\mathcal{X}_N$ for some $p'>p$ depending only on $\eta_{\La_{\ell_0}}$ 
such that $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ and $\tilde f'(u_0)=0$.
Then, there exists a constant $C=C(u_0, \ell_0)>0$ such that, for $\ell \geq \ell_0$, 
and a function $h$ on $[0,T]\times \T_N$, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x) \\
& \hskip 20mm \times \Big\{ E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)] 
-E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x \eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(2\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big] 
\notag  \\
&\hskip 10mm \leq \ CT^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2} \ell^{p/2} \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}
\int_0^T \frac{1}{N}\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} |h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}
On the other hand, when only $\tilde f(u_0)=0$ is known, we have
\begin{align}  
&E_{\mu_{u_0}}\Big[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\Big|\int_0^t\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} h(s,x)\\
&\hskip 20mm  \times \Big\{E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(\ell)}(x)]
-E_{\mu_{u_0}}[f(\tau_x\eta_s^N)|\eta_s^{N,(2\ell)}(x)]\Big\} ds \Big|^p\Big] 
\notag \\
&\hskip 10mm  \leq \ CT^{(p-2)/2} N^{-p/2} \ell^p \|f\|^p_{L^{p'}(\mu_{u_0})}
\int_0^T \frac{1}{N}\sum_{x\in{\T_N}} |h(t,x)|^p dt.
\notag
\end{align}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:28:49.058637+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f0903974414ce0f370d25f92ad54071dbaf20374994364585b064d57969c3435","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:pole-calibration of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Let $x_0=0$, let $b_a$ be defined by (equation eq:pole-reference-drift of the paper), and suppose
(equation eq:pole-coefficient-class of the paper) holds.  There exists
$K_{\mathrm{th}}=K_{\mathrm{th}}(T,\lambda,\Lambda)\geq1$ such that the following
holds.  For each $0<\theta<1$, define the threshold
\begin{equation}
 K_\theta^\star(a):=K_{\mathrm{th}}\theta^{-1}\mathcal M_d(a).
 
\end{equation}
Choose any $K\geq K_\theta^\star(a)$.  Set
$\omega_K(t):=e^{-K(T-t)/2}$ and, for
$\alpha\geq0$, write
$\overline w_{\alpha,K}(t):=t^\alpha\omega_K(t)$.  For
$\kappa\geq0$, set
$w_{\alpha,K;\kappa}:=(\overline w_{\alpha,K})_\kappa$ according to
Definition~(def:regular-time-weight of the paper).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The reference pair $(b_a,a)$ satisfies
Assumptions~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper) and~(ass:bochner-regularity of the paper).
Its time-$t$ diffusion law is $\mu_t=\gamma_t=N(0,tI_d)$, with current
velocity $c(t,y)=y/(2t)$.
\item If $\alpha\geq1/2$, then
\begin{equation}
 C_{\overline w_{\alpha,K}}(X^a)\leq2/\sqrt{1-\theta}.

\item If $0\leq\alpha<1/2$ and
$0<\theta<1-4/(C_\alpha^{\mathrm{Br}})^2$,
put
\begin{equation*}
 \Delta_{\mathrm{hi}}
 :=1-\theta-\frac4{(C_\alpha^{\mathrm{Br}})^2}>0.
\end{equation*}
There are constants with the following dependencies:
\begin{equation*}
 C=C\bigl(T,\lambda,\Lambda,\alpha,\theta,\Delta_{\mathrm{hi}}^{-1}\bigr)>0,
 \qquad

 \bigr)\geq1

For every $\kappa\geq\kappa_0$, these constants give

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:31:20.614713+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f095806e14f492f8c5bceb88a484f121cbe04e69a3351e38d6a59e6b3b2e4414","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 14 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] We define the following two bornologies:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For a family of bornological spaces $\{(S_\lambda, \mathcal{B}_\lambda)\}_{\lambda\in \Lambda}$, the set-theoretical direct product $\Pi_{\lambda\in \Lambda}\mathcal{B}_\lambda$ forms a bornological base on $\Pi_{\lambda\in \Lambda} S_\lambda$.
        We call $\langle \Pi_{\lambda\in \Lambda}\mathcal{B}_\lambda\rangle$ the \emph{direct product bornology} on $\Pi_{\lambda\in \Lambda} S_\lambda$.
        \item Let $P$ be a set and $f$ a map from $P$ to the bornological space $S$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:46:25.368236+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f0a55cb3301770f006ba55fd2ddd09f040b5e72894962c83a8b49b7e136449cf","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop CLEcoupling1 of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Consider a zero boundary GFF $\Phi_D$ on $D$ and the nested CLE$_4$ determined by exploring consecutively two-valued sets $A_{-2\lambda, 2\lambda}$. Then, for all boundary conditions $v \in 2\lambda \mathbb{Z}$, we have the following properties in coupling with $\Phi_D + v$: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item The labels $s_\ell \in \{-2\lambda, 2\lambda\}$ attached to each loop $\ell \in \text{CLE}_4^{n}$ are i.i.d. symmetric conditionally on the loops, 
and in terms of distributions,
$$\sum_{\Gamma \in \text{CLE}^{\rm nest}_4}(v1_{\Gamma \text{ outermost}}+s_\Gamma)
\1_{\operatorname{Int}(\Gamma)} = \Phi_D +v.$$
\item 
We assign the height $v$ to the boundary of the domain. Thereby, each gasket in CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ can be uniquely attached a height corresponding to the sum of labels of loops $s_\ell$ in CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ strictly surrounding this gasket, including the boundary of the domain. If this sum equals $h$, then we say that the gasket is at height $h$. Equivalently we can attach a height to each loop in CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ by considering the sum of labels of loops surrounding and including this loop and the boundary. This way the height of the gasket corresponds to the height of its outermost loop.   
\item In this coupling, conditionally on the loops, for each $z \in D$, the heights $h$ of the gaskets in 
CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ surrounding $z$ form a simple symmetric random walk $S^z(m)$ with step-size $2\lambda$ and starting point $v$. 
\item For $v \neq 0$, consider $A_0$, the first passage set of $\Phi_D + v$ with boundary values $0$. Then $A_0$ is almost surely equal to taking the connected component of the boundary of the closed union of all gaskets of non-zero height. In particular, for each $z \in D \cap \mathbb{Q}^2$, the boundary of the connected component of 
$D \setminus A_0$ containing $z$ is constructed as follows: we consider the nested loop sequence surrounding $z$ until the first time that a loop of height $0$ appears and that is the boundary. 
\item Further, the sign excursion sets of $\Phi_D + v$ have the following description using nested CLE$_4$: we consider the closed union of all the gaskets in CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$ of height different than zero. The connected components have then the law of sign excursion sets.
\item Finally, the dual of the excursion sets, i.e. the complement of the excursion sets in $D$, is given by the disjoint union of all the gaskets of height $0$ in the nested CLE$_4^{\rm nest}$. 
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:47:32.871096+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f0afe268d180a6d8173a1598b426836aab1df7356089b0d17665fa3e0f8edcc5","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 5 (Chebotarev density theorem) of arXiv:2609.02444, 'The Hasse norm principle for $A_4$-quartic extensions of global function fields'] Let \(G\) be a finite group, \(\phi \colon X \to Y\) a \(G\)-torsor defined over \(\FF_q\), and \(\Phi \subset G\) a conjugacy class.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T18:58:38.059781+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f0b26a2fc30c94c70681f66708903515cb14d89bda4e0b00d14641f974860b5f","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem kernel of arXiv:2606.19507, 'The $t$-Split Two-Periodic Aztec Diamond Model'] Let $-N \leq \xi,\xi' \leq -1$ and $0 < m, m' < N$. The correlation kernel $t$-split two-periodic Aztec diamond of size $2N$ with $t < 1/2$ can be written as a piecewise expression depending on whether $m' \leq tN$ or $m' > tN$. For $0 < m' \leq tN$ the kernel is:
    \begin{multline} 
        \left[\mathbb{K}_N(4m',2\xi'+j;4m,2\xi+i)\right]_{i,j=0,1} = -\frac{\1_{m>m'}}{2\pi \mathrm{i}} \oint_{\gamma_{0,1}}\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{z} z^{\xi'-\xi}\phi_{m'\to m,N}(z)\\
        +\frac{1}{(2\pi\mathrm{i})^2}\oint_{\gamma_1} \mathrm{d}w \oint_{\gamma_{0,1}} \frac{\mathrm{d}z}{z(z-w)}\frac{w^{\xi'+N}(z-1)^N}{z^{\xi+N}(w-1)^N}r_{\alpha,1}(w)^{tN-m'}F_{\alpha,1}(w) \\
        \times \Phi_{\beta}(w)^{(1/2-t)N} \Phi_{\beta}(z)^{(t-1/2)N}\Phi_{\alpha}(z)^{-tN}\phi_{0\to m,N}(z) \\
        + \frac{1}{(2\pi\mathrm{i})^2}\oint_{\gamma_1}\mathrm{d}w\oint_{\gamma_{0,1}} \frac{\mathrm{d}z}{z(z-w)}\frac{w^{\xi'+N}(z-1)^N}{z^{\xi+N}(w-1)^N}r_{\alpha,2}(w)^{tN-m'} c(w) F_{\alpha,2}(w) F_{\beta,1}(w)F_{\alpha,1}(w) \\
        \Phi_{\beta}(w)^{(1/2-t)N} \Phi_{\beta}(z)^{(t-1/2)N} \Phi_{\alpha}(z)^{-tN}\phi_{0\to m,N}(z).
    \end{multline}
    For $tN < m' < N$ the kernel is:
    \begin{multline} 
        \left[\mathbb{K}_N(4m',2\xi'+j;4m,2\xi+i)\right]_{i,j=0,1} = - \frac{\1_{m>m'}}{2\pi\mathrm{i}} \oint_{\gamma_{0,1}}\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{z} z^{\xi'-\xi} \phi_{m' \to m,N}(z) \\
        + \frac{1}{(2\pi\mathrm{i})^2}\oint_{\gamma_1} \mathrm{d}w \oint_{\gamma_{0,1}} \frac{\mathrm{d}z}{z(z-w)}\frac{w^{\xi'+N}(z-1)^N}{z^{\xi+N}(w-1)^N}r_{\beta,1}(w)^{N/2-m'} F_{\beta,1}(w)\\
        \Phi_{\beta}(z)^{(t-1/2)N}\Phi_{\alpha}(z)^{-tN}\phi_{0\to m,N}(z) \\
        + \frac{1}{(2\pi\mathrm{i})^2}\oint_{\gamma_1}\mathrm{d}w\oint_{\gamma_{0,1}} \frac{\mathrm{d}z}{z(z-w)}\frac{w^{\xi'+N}(z-1)^N}{z^{\xi+N}(w-1)^N}r_{\beta,1}(w)^{(2t - 1/2)N - m'}c(w)F_{\beta,1}(w)F_{\alpha,1}(w)F_{\beta,2}(w)\\
        \times \Phi_{\beta}(z)^{(t-1/2)N}\Phi_{\alpha}(z)^{-tN}\phi_{0\to m,N}(z).

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-08-02T17:15:45.378087+00:00","domain":"set theory","id":"claim_f0d630daf2b020660e71ada6912cbc65cadaabb956acfe1ff58ddf76f6278e47","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"The axiom of choice (AC) states: for every family {A_i : i in I} of nonempty sets, indexed by any set I, there exists a choice function c defined on I with c(i) in A_i for every i. Equivalently: every Cartesian product of nonempty sets is nonempty; every surjection has a right inverse; every set of nonempty pairwise disjoint sets has a transversal selecting one element from each. Over the Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms ZF, the axiom of choice is equivalent to Zorn's lemma and to the well-ordering theorem, and also to Tychonoff's theorem for arbitrary compact spaces. AC is independent of ZF: Godel (1938) showed ZF plus AC is consistent if ZF is (constructible universe), and Cohen (1963) showed ZF plus the negation of AC is consistent if ZF is (forcing). Countable and finite choices do not follow from ZF alone in general, but AC is provable in ZF for finite index sets I by induction.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:25:06.144882+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f0fc6f2de4695ac93f905fa80028c07ca29602ec265ab1ffc97fa70d2fa10760","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 (EPI on compact groups) of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a compact and metrizable topological abelian group, equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Assume that $G$ has no open subgroups except $G$ itself and possibly $\{0\}$. Let $X,Y$ be independent random variables on $G$ with finite entropies. Then
$$h(X+Y)-\frac{1}{2}h(X)-\frac{1}{2}h(Y) \geq 0.$$
Moreover:
\begin{itemize}
\item[$(i)$]
If $G$ is connected, then there is equality if and only 
if $X$ and $Y$ are both uniform on $G$.
\item[$(ii)$]
If $G$ is finite, then there is equality if and only if 
either both $X$ and $Y$ are uniform on the whole group $G$ 
or both $X$ and $Y$ are deterministic.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

$$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T21:00:30.492911+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f1049bf4169b66ec7c6384db8ed87960c912531b374b2a5583e3cd6a99db9c4f","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 6 (Rhombus concavity) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{def:rhomb}
Given a function $h:T \ra \R$, and a positive integer $n$,  let $h_n$ denote the function from $T_n$ to $\R$ such that for $(nx, ny) \in T_n$, $h_n(nx, ny) = n^2 h(x, y).$
A function $h:T \ra \R$ is called {\bf rhombus concave} if for any positive integer $n$, 
and any $i$, $\De_i h_n$ is nonpositive on $E_i(T_n),$ and $h$ is continuous on $T$.
The corresponding function $h_n$ is called {\bf discrete (rhombus) concave}.  
Note that a necessary and sufficient condition for a function $h_n$ from $T_n$ to $\R$ to be discrete concave,  is that the piecewise linear extension (which we denote $\tilh_n$) of $h_n$ to $nT$ is  concave.
Here each piece is an isosceles right triangle with a $\sqrt{2}-$length  hypotenuse parallel to the vector $(1, 1).$","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:15:16.652975+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f109537594b0900804d470c77d7ea62e778c46fc9f5f9d964e6ab5f7804411a6","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] Set
\(
  U_1
  :=
  |\Phi_1|_{\sigma_0}^2
  =
  \frac{|\phi_1|^2}{\rho^2}.
\)
Then
\begin{equation}
  \dot H_0=0,
  \qquad
  \ddot H_0
  =
  -4(\Delta_0-2)^{-1}U_1.
  
\end{equation}
Consequently, for every $k\ge 0$,
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  \widehat\sigma_t
  ={}&
  \sigma_0
  +2t\operatorname{Re}\Phi_1
  \\
  &+
  \frac{t^2}{2}
  \left[
    2\operatorname{Re}\Phi_2
    +
    \left(
      2U_1-4(\Delta_0-2)^{-1}U_1
    \right)\sigma_0
  \right]
  +O_{C^k}(t^3).
  \end{aligned}
  
\end{equation}
Here $O_{C^k}(t^3)$ means that, after subtracting the displayed
terms up to order two, the remainder $R_t$ satisfies
\(
  \|R_t\|_{C^k(X_0,\sigma_0)}\le C_k |t|^3
\)
for $|t|$ sufficiently small. Equivalently, all covariant derivatives
of $R_t$ up to order $k$, computed with respect to $\sigma_0$, are
uniformly $O(t^3)$.
Equivalently, in the coordinate $z$,
\begin{equation}
  \begin{aligned}
  \widehat\sigma_t
  ={}&
  \rho\,dz\,d\bar z
  +
  t\left(
    \phi_1\,dz^2+\overline{\phi_1}\,d\bar z^2
  \right)
  +
  \frac{t^2}{2}
  \Bigg[
    \phi_2\,dz^2+\overline{\phi_2}\,d\bar z^2
  \\
  &+
    \left\{
      \frac{2|\phi_1|^2}{\rho^2}
      -
      4(\Delta_0-2)^{-1}
      \left(
        \frac{|\phi_1|^2}{\rho^2}
      \right)
    \right\}
    \rho\,dz\,d\bar z
  \Bigg]
  +O_{C^k}(t^3).
  \end{aligned}
  
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:31:49.841252+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f1155990d025719407b6f04adea3caa4a71611a38f90282f5945adf6dec4967c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Satz 2 of arXiv:2506.13661, 'Box-Covariances of Hyperuniform Point Processes'] Let $\eta$ be a stationary hyperuniform point process on $\mathbb{R}$ with 
	truncated pair correlation measure $\beta$ such that $|\beta|(\mathbb{R})<\infty$. If   
	
	
	\quad \emph{(i)} the function $H(y)=-\int_0^y \beta([x,\infty))\mathrm{d}x= \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Var}(\eta(\Lambda_y))$ is regularly varying with parameter $a\in[0,1],$ then,
	
	\quad \emph{(ii)} for all $z\in\mathbb{R}$ we have  
	\begin{align}
		\mathrm{cov}(z)=
		\frac{|z-1|^{a}}{2}+ \frac{|z+1|^{a}}{2}-|z|^{a},
	\end{align}
    for $a\in (0,1]$, and $\mathrm{cov}(z)=\delta_0(z)-\frac{1}{2} \delta_{-1}(z)-\frac{1}{2}\delta_{+1}(z)$ for $a=0$ (as in \eqref{eq:thm_cov}).
	
	Conversely, if we additionally assume that $\beta([x,\infty))$ is non-positive (or non-negative) for $x$ sufficiently large, then \emph{(i)} and \emph{(ii)} are equivalent. Moreover, if
	
	\quad \emph{(iii)} the limit $\mathrm{cov}(z)<\infty$ 
	exists for $z=1$ and $z=2$,

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:01:56.374499+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f130a7a0169cb96d4d3f8abe60a662d845b92d54f3be46b2a7fc770cee8b5cdc","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Let $Q$ be a quiver with stability parameters $\theta_i\in\bR$, $i\in Q_0$, functions $f_a$, $a\in Q_1$ as before, and a representation $(E,\rho)$ over $K$ with a non-Archimedean norm on each $E_i$, $i\in Q_0$.

We define a quiver $Q^\star$ with $\theta_i^\star$, $i\in Q^\star_0$, and a representation $E^\star$ of $Q^\star$ over $\bC$ as follows.

The $\lambda_{a,k}$ are as before and, by Lemma~(lem:limsvd of the paper) and its proof, are the well-defined values where the increasing filtration $\cF^-(\rho(a))_{\lambda}$ (equivalently: the decreasing filtration $\cF^+(\rho(a))_{\lambda}$) jumps.
The quiver $Q^\star$ has vertices of three types:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
    \item A vertex for each vertex $i\in Q_0$ with 
    \[

    \]

    \]
    and with an arrow to $s(a)$.

    \[
    E^{\star}_{a,k,-}\coloneqq\begin{cases} \cF^-(\rho(a))_{-\infty}\coloneqq\cF^-(\rho(a))_{<\lambda_1}, & k=0 \\ \cF^-(\rho(a))_{\lambda_k}, & k=1,\ldots,k_a-1 \end{cases} 
    \]
    and assign the inclusion map to the arrow.
    \item A vertex $(a,k,+)$ for each pair $(a,k)$, $a\in Q_1$, $1\leq k\leq k_a$, with

    \theta_{a,k,+}^\star \coloneqq \begin{cases} -f_a'(\lambda_{a,1}), & k=1 \\ f_a'(\lambda_{a,k-1})-f_a'(\lambda_{a,k}), & k=2,\ldots,k_a \end{cases}

    and with an arrow to $t(a)$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:33:43.753349+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f173236382e18b027b540cc59368ce0ce0d194be3859e2c53b6e45b17e3489dd","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem thm:krylov_lp_estimate of arXiv:2609.01984, 'Instantaneous shrinking of supports for stochastic PDEs\footnote{JY was supported by a KIA'] Let $p\ge2$, $\eta\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $\tau\le T$ be a bounded stopping time.
Assume that the coefficients of $L$ satisfy
Assumption (asp:coefficients of the paper). Suppose
\[
    u_0\in U_p^\eta,
    \qquad
    f\in\mathbb H_p^{\eta-2}(\tau),
    \qquad
    g\in\mathbb H_p^{\eta-1}(\tau,\ell_2).
\]

\begin{equation}

where $N=N(p,\eta,\nu,T)$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:35:04.097744+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f18629db32e48374cb4b82d7680a0d8b4f70ac60958fed0cba184539f77192fc","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:singleton-order-sum of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] Let $\mathsf M_j$ be any typed passive copy of the coordinate pure-Weyl
multiplier in (lem:singleton-renewal of the paper), with arbitrary passive
Hilbert-space amplification.  Put
\[
 \mathsf V_j=\mathsf Q\mathsf M_j\mathsf Q,
 \qquad A_j=\mathscr E\mathsf M_j\mathscr T,
 \qquad \mathfrak H_a=\mathscr G\mathcal K^a\mathscr G^*.
\]
Then
\[
 \mathscr T^*\mathsf M_j\mathscr T
 =\mathscr E\mathsf M_j\mathscr E^*=0,
 \qquad
 \mathscr G^*\mathsf V_j\mathscr G
 =-\mathcal KA_j-A_j^*\mathcal K.
\tag{3.2.10q$_1$}
\]
There is a numerical $C$ such that
\[
 \sum_{a,b\ge0}
 \|\mathfrak H_a\mathsf V_j\mathfrak H_b\|
 \le C\frac{\log(n+2)}{\sqrt n}.
\tag{3.2.10q$_2$}
\]
Consequently, for every fixed $L<\infty$ there is $A_L<\infty$ such
that a passive-singleton component with $2\le s\le L\log n$ labelled
vertices satisfies, after summing every strict chronological order and
every allowed finite-gap simplex,
\[
 \sum_{\sigma\in S_s}
 \|\mathcal X_{s,\sigma}\|
 \le \frac{A_L^s}{N}.
\tag{3.2.10q$_3$}
\]
After the proved circuit-anchored root/pass rewrite, its one free
translation, and a fixed terminal ribbon gluing, its scalar contribution is at most
$A_L^s(m/N)\mathfrak a_\Gamma$, where
$\mathfrak a_\Gamma$ is the positive projective majorant of the already
normalized non-temporal atom.
The same conclusion holds for several Haar-separated passive-singleton
components after their labelled vertex sets have been fixed, with one
factor $m/N$ per component and no interleaving multinomial.  This last
sentence does not sum over varying component-label decompositions; the
physical maximal passive-only components are instead annihilated exactly
in (lem:haar-passive-zero of the paper) below.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:52:57.674714+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f1b8f83343792a4f9b6990d619b4dfba6e5168dd8bb6f1e2602b63a42d5dd632","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 7 of arXiv:2609.02686, 'The Bonnet-Myers theorem on Finsler manifolds with integral weighted Ricci curvature bound'] Let $(M, F, m)$ be an $n$-dimensional $(n \geq 2)$ forward complete Finsler metric measure manifold with $\Lambda_F<\infty$. Assume that $\mathbf{S}\geq -\vartheta$ for some $\vartheta \geq 0$.
Given constants $p \in (\frac{n}{2}, n]$, $\alpha\in [\frac{1}{2},1)$ and a fixed point $x_{0}\in M$. Then,  for $0 \leq r < R_{0}$ and an arbitrarily fixed point $x\in M$ satisfying that $d_{F}(x_{0}, x) \leq \Lambda_{F}^{-1}\left( R_{0}-r\right)$, there exist positive constants $D_{1}=D_{1}(n, p, \vartheta , R_{0})$ and $D_{2}=D_{2}(n,p,\Lambda_{F},\vartheta,\alpha,R_{0})$, such that, when $\overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{0}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}<D_{1}^{-\frac{2p-1}{p}}$, we have
\beq
&& \left(\frac{m\left(B_{\Lambda_{F}^{-1}r}^{+}(x)\right)}{m\left(B_{R_{0}}^{+}(x_{0})\right)}\right)^{\frac{1}{2 p-1}} \geq  \Big[\frac{1}{4} \left(1-D_{1} \overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{0}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}^{\frac{p}{2p-1}}\right)
e^{-\frac{\vartheta R_{0}}{2 p-1}}\Lambda_{F}^{-\left(2 \vartheta R_{0}b(p,\alpha)+\frac{5n}{2p-1}\right)}   \nonumber \\
&& \times \left(\frac{r}{R_{0}}\right)^{\vartheta R_{0} b(p,\alpha)+\frac{4n-2p}{2p-1}}  -  \frac{D_{2}\overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{0}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}^{\frac{p}{2p-1}}}{1-D_{1} \overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{0}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}^{\frac{p}{2p-1}}} \Big] \left(\frac{r}{R_{0}}\right)^{\frac{2p-n}{2p-1}}, 
\eeq
where

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:52:08.670726+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f1c4700c58c3f86c8072fba202cc40b74fb3bdf273ac72de1e6a59cdfed91b71","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 25 (Stage preparation, stability, and regular restart) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] There are constants

{"assumptions":["Abel: sum a_n converges","Tauber: f(x) -> s as x -> 1 from below and n a_n -> 0 (Littlewood: a_n = O(1/n) suffices, with a harder proof)"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T14:24:13.476957+00:00","domain":"real analysis","id":"claim_f1cba3555b43f0874b98c5a0afc289242890ff7c78565e100e36b9d11679d3e9","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Abel's theorem (the Abelian direction): if the series sum a_n converges to s, then the power series f(x) = sum a_n x^n converges for |x| < 1 and f(x) -> s as x -> 1 from below. The converse is false in general: f(x) = sum (-1)^n x^n = 1/(1 + x) tends to 1/2 while sum (-1)^n diverges. Tauber's theorem (the Tauberian direction): if f(x) = sum a_n x^n converges for |x| < 1, f(x) -> s as x -> 1 from below, and n a_n -> 0, then sum a_n converges to s. Littlewood strengthened the condition to a_n = O(1/n) (Littlewood's Tauberian theorem, 1911), and Hardy and Littlewood showed that a one-sided bound n a_n >= -C also suffices. 'Abelian' theorems pass from a summability method's convergence to a weaker one; 'Tauberian' theorems go back under an extra growth condition on the terms.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:57:07.304129+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f1d46960c6d62b35183a7af58fd40405eef057473203829635afbe23b3cf3c7d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 (Distance theorem for sparse simple random tensors) of arXiv:2606.24090, 'Sparsity-adaptive concentration inequalities for random polynomials'] Let \(0<\alpha\le 1\), \(p\in(0,1]\), and let
\[
     X=X^{(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes X^{(d)}\in\mathbb R^{n^d},
\]
where \(X_i^{(k)}=\delta_i^{(k)}\xi_i^{(k)}\), the variables \(\delta_i^{(k)}\) are i.i.d. Bernoulli\((p)\), and the variables \(\xi_i^{(k)}\) are independent, mean zero, variance one, and satisfy  $\|\xi_i^{(k)}\|_{\Psi_\alpha}\le 1$. All variables are assumed to be mutually independent.
Set
\[
    \Lambda_{n,p,d}:=\max_{0\le s\le d-1}(np)^{s/2}.
\]
Then for every deterministic nonzero matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{n^d\times n^d}\) and every \(t\ge 0\),
\begin{align}
&\mathbb P\left\{
\left|\|B X\|_2-p^{d/2}\|B\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\right|\ge t
\right\}\nonumber\\
&\qquad\le 2\exp\left[
-c_{\alpha,d}
\min\left\{
\frac{t^2}{\Lambda_{n,p,d}^2\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2},
\left(\frac{t}{n^{(d-1)/2}\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}}\right)^\alpha,
\left(\frac{t}{\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}}\right)^{\alpha/d}
\right\}
\right].
\end{align}
In particular, if \(np\ge 1\), then
\[
    \Lambda_{n,p,d}=(np)^{(d-1)/2}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the operator is trace class, or the kernel is continuous and positive semidefinite (Mercer) on a compact space with a finite Borel measure of full support","the kernel is a continuous representative, so that its diagonal values are defined","an L^2 kernel alone determines only a Hilbert-Schmidt operator, whose diagonal is undefined"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:46.573486+00:00","domain":"functional analysis, integral operators, operator ideals","id":"claim_f1fc0fc20e90cd54d10bec9762389999f830637cbe5b30da36ffa8f104d5b56e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"For an integral operator T_k on L^2 with kernel k, the formula tr T_k = integral of k(x,x) dx is not a definition and not automatic. (1) An L^2 kernel is an equivalence class modulo null sets, and on a nonatomic space the diagonal is a null set, so k(x,x) has no meaning at all without choosing a distinguished representative; different representatives give different 'diagonal integrals'. (2) Continuity of the kernel is not enough for trace class. Carleman's example: there are continuous 2pi-periodic functions g whose Fourier coefficients are not absolutely summable. The convolution operator (T f)(x) = (1/(2 pi)) times the integral over the circle of g(x - y) f(y) dy has the continuous kernel k(x,y) = g(x - y)/(2 pi), is normal with eigenvalues the Fourier coefficients of g and eigenfunctions the exponentials, so its singular values are the moduli of those coefficients; hence T is Hilbert-Schmidt but not trace class, while the naive diagonal integral is the finite number g(0). (3) What does hold: if T is trace class on L^2([a,b]) and has a continuous kernel on [a,b] x [a,b], then tr T = integral of k(x,x) dx; and by Mercer's theorem, if k is continuous, symmetric and positive semidefinite on a compact interval (more generally on a compact metric space with a finite Borel measure of full support), then the associated operator is trace class, the eigenfunction series converges absolutely and uniformly, and tr T = integral of k(x,x) dx = sum of the eigenvalues. So the safe routes are positivity plus continuity (Mercer), or an independent proof of trace class plus continuity; 'the kernel is nice' by itself is not a proof.","status":"unverified"}
