## Statement and experiment

Integers d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K. Each of d context pairs has one A
and one S, with VC-d orientation class; N-2d remaining contexts are
known S. S has all K truths; each A has an independent uniform r-subset.
The factual source chooses contexts uniformly, then truths uniformly.
Training consists of actual iid factual context/candidate samples,
without partition tags. An independent verifier may supply ell true
candidates per variable context, uniformly without replacement, also
without orientation labels. Include those identities in the known
truth union C_x. Condition on ANY positive-probability data outcome
with sizes j_x=|C_x|<r in EVERY variable context. Counts and identities
may differ arbitrarily between siblings. Every orientation remains
compatible; compatible A supports contain C_A. The actual posterior
orientation probabilities need not be uniform.

Require exact source Mis_infinity=0 in EVERY compatible world, using
the uniform coarsening within exact g-probability bins. Allow all g.
Set h_i=min(j_left,j_right) for pair i and

 b_h=[1/K+(r-h)/(r(K-h))]/(2N).

The proposed exact CONDITIONAL worst-world false-mass frontier is

 V(0)=sum_{i=1}^d (K-r)*b_{h_i}.                        (1)

An attainer has this risk in every actual compatible world. This is
not an assertion that all other generators have a pointwise lower
bound (C015's varying-count control disproves that). No unconditional
expected minimax value is inferred from (1).

For the same known truths with the partition additionally supplied,
the conditional worst-world oracle value is

 O_worst(0)=sum_i (K-r)*(r-h_i)/(Nr(K-h_i)).              (2)

Thus the exact worst-oracle estimation gap is

 V(0)-O_worst(0)
   =sum_i h_i*(K-r)^2/(2NrK(K-h_i)).                    (3)

The oracle in (2) takes a maximum over supplied orientations; it is
not the average actual-orientation oracle. Formula (3) weights the
conditional 1/N-per-pair classification error of the specified fair
completion of support-consistent ERM. No statistically optimal ERM
rate or general unweighted-error identity is claimed.

## Residual support variability forces one score level

Fix ANY robustly zero-calibrated generator g and its exact score
partition Pi. In every bin B, p_world(B)=g(B) for every compatible
world, hence its source mass is invariant under changing supports or
orientations. For a context x possibly A, let Q_x be its K-j_x
uncertified atoms. Since 1<=r-j_x<K-j_x, any two atoms of Q_x can be
swapped in a compatible A support while all other truth identities
remain fixed. If one were in B and the other outside, this swap would
change p(B) by 1/(Nr), contradicting invariance. Therefore each bin
contains either ALL or NONE of Q_x. Equivalently all Q_x atoms have
one common score; denote their unique bin B_x.

This argument FAILS if j_x=r, since there is then no residual truth
to swap. C016's neutral-bundle counterexample exploits exactly this
boundary, rather than contradicting the present strict hypothesis.

## Classifying each pair's invariant bins

Write s=j_L<=t=j_R<r for one pair; relabel siblings if necessary.
For a bin B let u_x=|B intersect C_x| and epsilon_x=1 if Q_x is in B,
else zero. The difference between its A-context and S-context source
contributions is

 delta_x(B)=(K-r)/(NrK)*(u_x-epsilon_x*j_x).

Independent flipping of this pair's orientation while holding all
other pairs fixed implies delta_L(B)=delta_R(B) for EVERY bin.

If B_L!=B_R, then in B_L the left delta is nonpositive and the right
delta nonnegative. Equality forces u_L=s,u_R=0. Similarly B_R has
u_R=t,u_L=0. Thus each context lies entirely in its own one score bin.

If B_L=B_R=B*, equality gives

 k=s-u_L=t-u_R, 0<=k<=s.

Outside B* every bin contains only known truths from these contexts
and contains the SAME number of known truths from each sibling.
Exactly k known truths from each sibling lie outside B*.

## Reduction to the balanced-count game

For each pair retain the smaller context's complete known set C_L.
In the larger context retain a subset C'_R of size s. If the residual
bins are different, choose any such subset. If they coincide in B*,
retain ALL k larger-context known truths outside B* and choose any
s-k additional known truths inside B*. This is possible since there
are t-k>=s-k such inside truths. The sets may depend on g; this is
a proof comparison, not the algorithm.

Expand the compatible world set by forgetting the t-s surplus truths
in the larger context. In the distinct-bin case both contexts had
one score, so every source bin mass and every false-atom count per
bin are unchanged under this expansion. In the common-bin case all
newly uncertified atoms lie in B*. Every other bin retains the same
known-true counts; in B* the A context always has r-k true atoms and
K-r false atoms, in either orientation and for every expanded support.
Thus again each source bin mass and each actual false-count-per-bin
vector is unchanged.

Do this independently for every pair. For the same fixed g,

* robust zero calibration holds on the EXPANDED balanced-count game;
* the set of possible false masses across its worlds equals the set
  across the original compatible worlds, orientation by orientation.

The expanded game has balanced known counts h_i and arbitrary known
identities. It need not preserve the original sample/verifier labels:
it is an enlarged source-world comparison, not a claimed posterior.
C015's general balanced-count lower bound at c=0 therefore yields
max_original H(g)=max_expanded H(g)>=sum_i(K-r)b_{h_i}.
Dependence of the selected balanced sets on g causes no problem:
the balanced theorem is uniform over all sets of the stated sizes.

## Balanced comparison lower bound, stated here for completeness

For the expanded known sets of balanced sizes h_i, average orientations
fairly and average compatible residual supports uniformly. This is an
artificial lower-bound distribution, not the actual posterior. Its
mean factual law mu gives density a=(1/r+1/K)/(2N) to known truths,
b_h to uncertified atoms in count-h pairs, and 1/(NK) to fixed S.
The false probability of each uncertified atom is tau_h=(K-r)/(2(K-h)).
As h increases b_h decreases and tau_h increases; safe densities are
at least 1/(NK)>=b_h. For E_h the union of uncertified atoms in pairs
with count at least h, every inside density is <=every outside
density. Uniform coarsening in any bin transfers mass INTO E_h, so
mu_Pi(E_h)>=mu(E_h)=T_h with T_h as in (6). Robust feasibility and
TV convexity imply TV(mu_Pi,g)<=c, hence g(E_h)>=(T_h-c)_+.
The artificial average false risk is exactly
tau_0*g(E_0)+sum_{h=1}^{r-1}(tau_h-tau_{h-1})*g(E_h).
It is at least (6), and the maximum original risk equals the maximum
expanded risk and is at least this average. This proves the needed
balanced lower bound directly, for c=0 and throughout (4), without
requiring a prior-card theorem or any actual posterior identity.

## Attainment and oracle comparison

Select h_i known truths from each sibling before constructing g. Put
their two known-true groups at score (1/r+1/K)/(2N); put the remaining
2(K-h_i) pair atoms at b_{h_i}, and fixed S atoms at 1/(NK).
Each pair group has invariant p mass under all original worlds.
Exact-score mergers preserve invariance. This g is robustly calibrated
with zero budget, and each actual world's K-r false atoms per pair
all receive b_{h_i}. This proves the matching upper bound in (1).

If a supplied orientation chooses A at count j, the zero-budget oracle
has risk (K-r)*(r-j)/(Nr(K-j)), by the ordered known-A-group argument
of C009/C015. This quantity decreases with j, so its maximum over
independent orientations picks j=h_i in every pair, proving (2).
Subtracting gives (3) exactly.

This is a whole strict-unsaturation data region for arbitrary d,N,K,r,
not a theorem deduced from nine small finite partition searches. It
uses robust zero calibration critically and does not extend to c>0
by continuity alone. Saturated-context neutral bins are a real excluded
mechanism. Primary source statistic: Kalai--Vempala 2311.14648v3,
Definitions 1--2 pp.8--9. C015 is an own unaudited draft whose balanced
lower-bound proof is required here; its primary-source priority and
all current independent mathematical/target-scope audits are pending.

## A nonzero calibration-budget interval via discrete TV jumps

The reduction extends to EVERY budget

 0<=c<c_star=(K-r)/(2NrK).                               (4)

Let Pi be the exact score partition of any robustly c-feasible g.
For any two compatible worlds w,w', the triangle inequality gives

 TV(p_w,Pi,p_w',Pi)<=2c.                                (5)

If a context's uncertified atoms occupy two different score bins,
swap one true and one false uncertified atom in its A support. This
is possible since j_x<r<K. The coarsened source laws then differ
by exactly 1/(Nr) in TV. But 2c<(K-r)/(NrK)<1/(Nr), contradicting (5).
Thus all uncertified atoms still occupy one score bin, as before.

Consequently coarsened source masses are independent of residual
supports. On flipping a single pair's orientation their bin-mass
changes are integer multiples of

 eta=(K-r)/(NrK),

by the delta formula above. If any bin changes, the changes sum to
zero, so the sum of their positive parts is at least eta. Uniform
coarsening preserves each bin mass, hence the TV of these two
coarsened laws is at least eta. This contradicts 2c<eta. Therefore
ALL coarsened source laws are identical across every compatible world.
In particular the invariant-bin classification and balanced-set
expansion apply without assuming g equals this common coarsened law.
They preserve both calibration distance to g and false mass, bin by
bin, for each orientation. The earlier reduction is valid throughout (4).

Let D_h count pairs with h_i=h,0<=h<=r-1. Put

 tau_h=(K-r)/(2(K-h)), M_h=D_h*(2-h/r-h/K)/N,
 T_h=sum_{t=h}^{r-1}M_t.

C015's balanced-game formula gives the exact all-generator conditional
frontier for the ORIGINAL unequal-count experiment:

 V(c)=tau_0*(T_0-c)_+
      +sum_{h=1}^{r-1}(tau_h-tau_{h-1})*(T_h-c)_+,       (6)

for every c in (4). The matching construction discards surplus truths
and transfers mass from the balanced uncertified groups to fixed S
in decreasing h order. It works even for larger c as an upper bound;
the exact lower bound is asserted only on (4).

For the same-data partition-supplied worst-orientation oracle set

 alpha_h=2tau_h, A_h=D_h*(r-h)/(Nr), Q_h=sum_{t=h}^{r-1}A_t.

Its exact frontier is

 O_worst(c)=alpha_0*(Q_0-c)_+
      +sum_{h=1}^{r-1}(alpha_h-alpha_{h-1})*(Q_h-c)_+.    (7)

For any supplied orientation, ignoring surplus A truths down to h_i
gives a feasible generator attaining the minimum-count oracle bound,
so that orientation's oracle value is at most (7). The orientation
that chooses the smaller-known-count context as A in EVERY pair is
compatible and has exactly that oracle game, proving the reverse
inequality for the worst orientation. Thus (6)-(7) is an exact matching
conditional decomposition; at zero it simplifies to (3).

No endpoint c=c_star is claimed, nor is c_star asserted to be the
largest valid interval. A nonzero TV jump cannot be ruled out by the
triangle argument at the endpoint. No global expected minimax identity
is inferred, and no statement about actual-world-only calibration is
made. The rigidity proof is a deterministic discrete-bin argument;
finite checks validate its steps but do not supply the general proof.

On this interval both formulas simplify: let H=max_i h_i and
tau_H=(K-r)/(2(K-H)). Every nonempty M_h group has mass at least

Therefore no highest-risk group is exhausted and

 V(c)-O_worst(c)
   =sum_i h_i*(K-r)^2/(2NrK(K-h_i))+tau_H*c.             (8)

{"assumptions":["bond percolation on Z^d, d >= 2","(b) uses planar duality and is stated for d = 2; higher d follows by monotonicity of p_c in d","the counting bounds are deliberate over-counts and the resulting numerical bounds are not sharp"],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:38.543147+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f60f52594dd7b9b53fb61d3949deca10e914add0476709c51deaa67169ca6e9e","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"For bond percolation on Z^d with d >= 2: (a) p_c >= 1/(2d - 1), and in particular p_c > 0. (b) p_c < 1, and for d = 2 the Peierls contour argument gives an explicit bound: p_c^{bond}(Z^2) <= 1 - q_0 where q_0 > 0 is any solution of sum_{n >= 4} 4 n 3^{n-1} q^n < 1. The two halves use completely different mechanisms: (a) is a first-moment count on self-avoiding paths, comparing the cluster to a branching process with mean offspring (2d-1)p, and (b) is a first-moment count on DUAL CIRCUITS surrounding the origin. Note that (a) gives only a bound and not the value; the true p_c(Z^d) is strictly larger than 1/(2d-1) in every dimension, and for Z^2 the bound 1/3 is far from the exact value 1/2. Since p_c(Z^d) is nonincreasing in d - a d-dimensional slab embeds in dimension d+1 - part (b) for d = 2 gives p_c < 1 in every d >= 2 at once. [standard; e.g. Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Sections 1.4 and 1.5]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Finite number of Markov states and finite dimension d","Exogenous time-homogeneous chain and deterministic state-dependent matrices","Homogeneous recursion, without additive forcing","Mean-square decay quantified over every deterministic initial state and vector","Departure-state matrix H_i and columnwise vectorization"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T16:05:57.431602+00:00","domain":"Markov jump linear systems; reinforcement learning","id":"claim_f6119956ebdd50b26bd8f1f5fb660ce93dd30782c6f77c84c876d5fa06ffa8dc","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let z_k be an exogenous time-homogeneous Markov chain on {1,...,N}, with row-stochastic transition matrix P=(p_ij), and let H_1,...,H_N be fixed real d-by-d matrices. Then the following are equivalent: (i) E[||xi_k||^2 | z_0=i,xi_0=x] tends to zero as k tends to infinity for EVERY state i and EVERY x in R^d; (ii) rho(L)<1; (iii) there are C<infinity and 0<r<1 such that E[||xi_k||^2 | z_0=i,xi_0=x]<=C r^k ||x||^2 for every i,x,k. {"assumptions":["(K_eps) is an approximate identity in L^1(R^d): unit integral, uniformly bounded L^1 norms, L^1 mass outside every fixed ball tending to 0","(a): f in L^p with 1 <= p < infinity (p = infinity excluded)","(b): f bounded and uniformly continuous","(c): f essentially bounded and continuous at x_0","(d): dilation structure K_eps = eps^{-d}K(x/eps) with an integrable radially nonincreasing majorant of |K|"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.262794+00:00","domain":"real and harmonic analysis","id":"claim_f623f2e2243c7f63bc96371f3968c4c5673aace5e7e9f3012d91cf0237f9680b","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $(K_\\varepsilon)$ be an approximate identity on $\\mathbb R^d$ ($\\int K_\\varepsilon=1$, $\\sup\\|K_\\varepsilon\\|_1<\\infty$, $\\int_{|x|\\ge\\delta}|K_\\varepsilon|\\to0$ for each $\\delta>0$). (a) If $f\\in L^p(\\mathbb R^d)$ with $1\\le p<\\infty$, then $\\|f*K_\\varepsilon-f\\|_p\\to0$. (b) If $f$ is bounded and uniformly continuous, $f*K_\\varepsilon\\to f$ uniformly. (c) If $f\\in L^\\infty$ and $f$ is continuous at $x_0$, then $(f*K_\\varepsilon)(x_0)\\to f(x_0)$. (d) If $K_\\varepsilon(x)=\\varepsilon^{-d}K(x/\\varepsilon)$ where $\\int K=1$ and $|K|\\le\\psi$ for some radial, radially nonincreasing, integrable $\\psi$, then for $f\\in L^p$, $1\\le p\\le\\infty$, $(f*K_\\varepsilon)(x)\\to f(x)$ at every Lebesgue point $x$ of $f$, hence almost everywhere, and $\\sup_\\varepsilon|f*K_\\varepsilon|\\le\\|\\psi\\|_1Mf$ with $M$ the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function. Part (a) fails for $p=\\infty$ (each $f*K_\\varepsilon$ is continuous, so an $f\\in L^\\infty$ with no continuous representative cannot be a uniform limit of them). The same statements hold on $\\mathbb T$ with the kernels $F_N$ (Fejer) and $P_r$ (Poisson).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:57:16.073393+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f625483b64e58598b6cfa8ed9a254c09274dc7f44a9bb180844f0a5bbdfc0aa3","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Good blocks of arXiv:2507.00329, 'Oriented bond-site percolation in random environment and contact processes with periodic r'] At fixed scale $k\in\mathbb{N}$, we partition $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}$ into blocks of length $L_k$, that is,
    \[

    \]
    so that each scale-\((k+1)\) block $I_{k+1,i}$ consist of $\lfloor L_{k}^{\gamma-1}\rfloor$ many scale-$k$ blocks, i.e., $\#\{m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0} \colon  I_{k,m}\cap I_{k+1,i}\neq\emptyset\} = \lfloor L_{k}^{\gamma-1}\rfloor$.

A compact set $\\Lambda \\subset M$ with $f(\\Lambda) = \\Lambda$ is (uniformly) hyperbolic if there are constants $C > 0$, $0 < \\lambda < 1$ and, at every $x \\in \\Lambda$, a splitting $T_x M = E^s(x) \\oplus E^u(x)$ such that (i) the splitting is $Df$-invariant: $Df_x E^s(x) = E^s(f x)$ and $Df_x E^u(x) = E^u(f x)$; (ii) $\\|Df^n_x v\\| \\le C \\lambda^n \\|v\\|$ for $v \\in E^s(x)$, $n \\ge 0$; (iii) $\\|Df^{-n}_x v\\| \\le C \\lambda^n \\|v\\|$ for $v \\in E^u(x)$, $n \\ge 0$. The subbundles are then automatically continuous in $x$, and the constant $C$ can be made 1 by changing to an adapted (Lyapunov) metric. {"assumptions":["d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K and gcd(r,K-r)=1","Paired A/S VC-d family; uniform contexts then truths, uniform independent r-subsets in A, all K truths in S","Actual iid factual samples without tags and optional independent uniform partial verifier; known truth counts j_x<=r, no logically identified pairs","Robust exact-level source Mis_infinity<=c for EVERY compatible world,0<=c<1/(2NrK); arbitrary generators; conditional worst-world objective"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T21:04:06.350847+00:00","domain":"statistical learning; calibrated generation; source-bin rigidity","id":"claim_f63d27667aecff51f3c3a2cde5580627be35364031ec5e239606e9551fea2ef5","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent mathematical, priority and target-scope audit pending. # Coprime alphabet/support sizes remove the saturation obstruction

T379-C019 v2: proof (unaudited), exact checks PASS; independent audit pending.
Target 1, secondary target 2. Arbitrary VC dimension and unequal known
truth counts, including saturation; conditional robust small-budget
game only. General noncoprime saturated mixtures and larger budgets
remain open here.

## Model and statement

Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K be integers with gcd(r,K-r)=1. There
are d unresolved A/S context pairs and N-2d fixed known S contexts.
Each S has all K truths; each A has an independent uniform r-subset.
The factual law chooses contexts uniformly then uniformly true within
context. Actual iid factual samples have no orientation tags. An
optional independent verifier supplies a uniform ell-subset of truths
in each variable context, including S, without orientation labels.
Let C_x be the distinct observed-plus-certified truth union. Condition
on ANY positive-probability data outcome with j_x=|C_x|<=r in every
variable context. Thus no orientation is logically excluded. Some
contexts may have j_x=r; sibling counts and sample repetitions may
differ arbitrarily. Actual orientation likelihoods need not be equal.

Write h_i=min(j_left,j_right) and D_h=#{i:h_i=h},0<=h<=r. Put

 tau_h=(K-r)/(2(K-h)), M_h=D_h*(2-h/r-h/K)/N,
 T_h=sum_{t=h}^r M_t.

For every 0<=c<1/(2NrK), the proposed exact all-generator conditional
worst-world frontier under source Mis_infinity<=c in EVERY compatible
world is

 V(c)=tau_0*(T_0-c)_+
       +sum_{h=1}^r(tau_h-tau_{h-1})*(T_h-c)_+.          (1)

Source miscalibration is TV(g,p_Pi) using uniform coarsening of p in
exact g-probability bins. The same-data partition-supplied WORST-
ORIENTATION oracle has frontier

 O(c)=alpha_0*(Q_0-c)_+
       +sum_{h=1}^r(alpha_h-alpha_{h-1})*(Q_h-c)_+,       (2)

where alpha_h=2tau_h,A_h=D_h*(r-h)/(Nr),Q_h=sum_{t=h}^r A_t.
In particular A_r=0: a saturated oracle group has zero residual mass,
so its risk-one coefficient must NOT be used to infer a nonzero slope.
The exact zero-budget estimation penalty is

 V(0)-O(0)=sum_i h_i*(K-r)^2/(2NrK(K-h_i)).              (3)

No exact endpoint, largest interval, actual-world-only calibration or
global expected minimax identity is claimed. This extends C017 to
saturation under the coprime arithmetic hypothesis, using a possibly
smaller interval. It does not contradict C016/C018's noncoprime cases.

## Discrete source-bin mass rigidity

Fix any robustly c-feasible generator g and its exact score partition
Pi. For every compatible world and every cell B, p(B) is an integer
multiple of 1/(NrK), since the original atom masses are 0,1/(Nr) or
1/(NK). This is a lattice statement about BIN MASSES; individual
coarsened atom probabilities have the additional bin-size divisor.
For two worlds w,w', uniformity within the SAME cells gives

 TV(p_w,Pi,p_w',Pi)=(1/2)*sum_B |p_w(B)-p_w'(B)|.

If any bin mass differs, the nonzero integer differences sum to zero,
so this TV is at least 1/(NrK). Triangle inequality and feasibility
instead give TV<=2c<1/(NrK). Therefore EVERY source bin mass is
world-invariant. This quantization argument itself needs no coprimality.

## Coprimality restores rigidity at a saturated sibling

For an unsaturated context j_x<r, swapping a residual true and false
candidate in a compatible A support shows that all uncertified atoms
occupy one score bin, as in C017. Consider an unequal pair with counts
s<t. The smaller context is unsaturated. If t<r both contexts already
have this property. If t=r, in any score bin let u_L be its known-L
count and epsilon_L indicate inclusion of all K-s uncertified L atoms;
let u_R be its known-R count and v_R its count outside C_R. Independent
orientation invariance gives

 (K-r)*(u_L-epsilon_L*s-u_R)=-r*v_R.

Hence (K-r)|r*v_R. Since gcd(r,K-r)=1, Bezout implies (K-r)|v_R.
Because 0<=v_R<=K-r, a cell contains either all or none of the
saturated context's outside atoms. Thus their score is also constant.
This is the step that fails for the noncoprime neutral bundles in C016.
The standard Bezout identity was returned in recall/walk004.txt,
card claim_63c5ddfd2e7e4d178b7628c572034232.

Both saturated counts r,r are already balanced; they need no expansion
and no assertion that their outside atoms occupy one score bin.

## Reduction to balanced minima

For each unequal pair both outside-known sets now occupy unique bins.
For any cell write u_x for its known-truth count and epsilon_x for
whether it contains the entire outside-known set. The A-minus-S source
contribution is (K-r)*(u_x-epsilon_x*j_x)/(NrK), so equality under the
orientation flip makes these expressions equal for the two siblings.

If the two outside-known bins differ, each contains an ENTIRE context
and none of the other context. If they coincide in B*, the number k
of known truths outside B* is equal in both siblings and at most s,
the smaller count. Retain all smaller-context truths. In the larger
context retain its k known truths outside B* and any s-k of its known
truths inside B*. Forget all other larger-context truths.

Expanding compatible supports by this forgetting preserves every source
bin mass: outside B* known counts are unchanged; in B* the A context
always has r-k truths. It also preserves each bin's false count for
each orientation: all K-r A false atoms remain in the same outside-
known bin. If entire contexts were separate bins, both facts follow
from fixed context mass 1/N and fixed false count K-r. Balanced pairs,
including r,r, are kept unchanged. This works independently across pairs.

Thus for the same g the enlarged balanced-minimum source game is still
robustly c-feasible and has exactly the same possible false masses.
The retained sets may depend on g, solely as a proof device. No claim
about their actual posterior or original sampling probability is made.

## Arbitrary-bin lower bound and construction

In the balanced comparison game average orientations fairly and
compatible supports uniformly. The mean factual law mu has density
(1/r+1/K)/(2N) on known truths, density
b_h=[1/K+(r-h)/(r(K-h))]/(2N) on uncertified atoms in count-h pairs,
and 1/(NK) in fixed S. Their artificial false probability is tau_h.
Increasing h decreases b_h and increases tau_h, including h=r.
Safe densities are >=1/(NK)>=b_h.

For the union E_h of uncertified groups at counts >=h, every inside
density is <=every outside density. In EACH cell, uniform averaging
therefore transfers mass into E_h: mu_Pi(E_h)>=T_h. Convexity of TV
over compatible worlds and robustness give TV(mu_Pi,g)<=c, so
g(E_h)>=(T_h-c)_+. The artificial average false risk is the layer-cake
sum tau_0*g(E_0)+sum_{h>0}(tau_h-tau_{h-1})g(E_h), which is at least
(1). The original worst risk equals the expanded worst risk and is
at least this average. Unequal actual posterior weights never enter.

For attainment select h_i known truths in each sibling, before seeing
any hidden orientation or residual support. Start at the balanced
comparison mean law; remove mass from uncertified groups in decreasing
h order, uniformly inside each count group, and transfer it to fixed S.
Each paired selected-known group and residual group has invariant p
mass under ALL original worlds. The generator is constant on each,
so exact-score mergers preserve invariance and Mis_infinity<=c.
Their false fractions are tau_h in EACH actual world; the false mass
is exactly (1) worldwise. The algorithm uses observed unions and model
parameters only, not hidden labels or future observations.

For a supplied orientation, ignoring its surplus A truths down to h_i
attains the min-count oracle bound. Conversely the compatible orientation
choosing the smaller-count sibling as A in every pair gives exactly
that oracle game. Ordered known-A residual density/risk tails yield (2),
including the zero-mass saturated group. This proves the worst-oracle
comparison. At c=0 subtracting the individual terms gives (3).

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:21:52.493891+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f65b8e754daeb977e1e56fe557d498909015fe75ad792d53eee07d0db22997e2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 258 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Assume $\boldsymbol{\Theta}$ is realized by a non-bipartite gluing graph $\mathsf{G}$. Then the vector $\boldsymbol{v} = \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_1}$ has $\mathfrak{G}$-orbit $\{\tau\,\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_i}\,\,|\,\,\tau \in \{\pm 1\}\,\,i \in [m]\}$, this orbit is good and has minimal size $2m = 2\,\textnormal{rank}(\boldsymbol{\Theta})$. For any $i \in [m]$ and $h \in \mathcal{H}_i$, we have
\[
T^{(h)}(\tau \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_i}) = \left\{\begin{array}{ccc} \tau \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_i} && \textnormal{if}\,\,h \notin \mathcal{H}_i \\[0.6ex] - \tau \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{H}_{i'_h}} && \textnormal{if}\,\, h \in \mathcal{H}_i. \end{array}\right.
\]
The spectral curve $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ has genus $\mathsf{g}_{\boldsymbol{v}} = 2\,\textnormal{corank}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}) + 1$, and is equipped with a holomorphic involution $\varsigma : \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}} \rightarrow \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ sending $p$ in the $\boldsymbol{w}$-th sheet to $p'$ in the $(-\boldsymbol{w})$-th sheet such that $Z_{\boldsymbol{v}}(p) = Z_{\boldsymbol{v}}(p')$. The group $\hat{\mathfrak{G}}$ is the Weyl group of type $D_{m}$.

The bidifferential $\mathcal{B}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{v}}}$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:Bcont} is defined on the spectral surface $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v} \otimes\boldsymbol{v}}^{[2],\circ} = \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}} \times \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}} / (\varsigma,\varsigma)$. Its pullback $\mathcal{B}_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ to $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}} \times \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ has biresidues \foreignlanguage{russian}{B}${}_{\boldsymbol{w}_1,\boldsymbol{w}_2} = \delta_{\boldsymbol{w}_1,\boldsymbol{w}_2} - 1 - \delta_{\boldsymbol{w}_1 + \boldsymbol{w}_2, \boldsymbol{0}}$, and is equal to
\[
\mathcal{B}_{\boldsymbol{v}} = \mathcal{B}^{\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\mathcal{L}} - (\textnormal{id},\varsigma)^*\mathcal{B}^{\Sigma,\mathcal{L}} - \frac{\dd z_1 \dd z_2}{(z_1 - z_2)^2},

and we have $(\textnormal{id},\varsigma)^* \mathcal{B}^{\Sigma,\mathcal{L}} = (\varsigma, \textnormal{id})^* \mathcal{B}^{\Sigma,\mathcal{L}}$. Here $\mathcal{L}$ is the same Lagrangian as in Theorem~\ref{thm:Omegav} and $\mathcal{B}^{\Sigma,\mathcal{L}}$ is the fundamental bidifferential of Section~\ref{sec:fund02}.

From the analytic continuation of first-kind functions in Proposition~\ref{Lem:Holo1form}, we get an linear isomorphism
\[
\begin{array}{ccc} \textnormal{Ker}(\boldsymbol{\Theta}) & \longrightarrow & H^1(\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\amsmathbb{C})^- \\
\boldsymbol{v}' & \longmapsto & \mathfrak{u}_{\boldsymbol{v};\boldsymbol{v}'} \end{array}
\]
where $H^1(\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}},\amsmathbb{C})^-$ is the space of holomorphic $1$-forms that are anti-invariant under the involution. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:51:33.327203+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f669b7380ef83b4fdac8c4a5ff8ca364ec3a81ad3f19c493c5d705e2aba9ef4a","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop smash-gl-left-Quillen of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The smash product of orthogonal spectra defines a left Quillen bifunctor 
    \[
        \cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}_\textup{$G$-global}\times\cat{$\bm{H}$-OrthSp}_\textup{$H$-global}\to
        \cat{$\bm{(G\times H)}$-OrthSp}_\textup{$(G\times H)$-global}.
    \]
    \begin{proof}
        To see that the pushout product axiom for cofibrations holds, it suffices to treat the case of generating cofibrations. Using that the enriched Yoneda embedding $\textbf{\textup{O}}^{\textup{op}}\to{\textbf{\textup{OrthSp}}}$ admits a strong symmetric monoidal structure, we then compute that the pushout product of $\textbf{\textup{O}}(V,-)\smashp_{\varphi} G_+\smashp (\partial D^n\hookrightarrow D^n)$ with $\textbf{\textup{O}}(W,-)\smashp_\psi G_+\smashp (\partial D^m\hookrightarrow D^m)$ (where $\varphi\colon K\to G$ and $\psi\colon L\to H$ are homomorphisms) is given by
        \[
            \textbf{\textup{O}}(V\oplus W,-)\smashp_{\varphi\times\psi}(G\times H)_+\smashp\big((\partial D^n\hookrightarrow D^n)\mathbin{\raise.25pt\hbox{\scalebox{.67}{$\square$}}}(\partial D^m\hookrightarrow D^m)\big)_+,
        \]
        where we view $H\times K\subset {\textup{O}}(V)\times {\textup{O}}(W)$ as a subgroup of ${\textup{O}}(V\oplus W)$ via block sum. As $\textbf{\textup{Top}}$ is cartesian and $\cat{$\bm{(G\times H)}$-OrthSp}$ is topological, this is then indeed a cofibration, completing the proof of the pushout product axiom for cofibrations.

        Next, we will show that $i\mathbin{\raise.25pt\hbox{\scalebox{.67}{$\square$}}} f$ is a $(G\times H)$-global weak equivalence for any cofibration $i\colon A\to B$ between cofibrant objects and any $H$-global weak equivalence $f\colon X\to Y$ between cofibrant objects; this then in particular applies to the generating (acyclic) cofibrations, proving (up to exchanging the roles of $G$ and $H$) the remaining case for the pushout product axiom. For this we consider the defining pushout
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                A\smashp X\arrow[r,"i\smashp X"]\arrow[d,"A\smashp f"']\arrow[dr,phantom,"\ulcorner"{very near end}] & B\smashp X\arrow[d]\arrow[ddr, bend left=15pt,"B\smashp f"]\\
                A\smashp Y\arrow[r]\arrow[drr, bend right=15pt,"i\smashp Y"'] & P\arrow[dr,dashed,"i\mathbin{\raise.25pt\hbox{\scalebox{.67}{$\square$}}} f"{description}]\\
                && B\smashp Y\rlap.
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        By the previous proposition applied to ${\textup{triv}}_HA$ and ${\textup{triv}}_Gf$, the map $A\smashp f$ is a $(G\times H)$-global weak equivalence, and likewise for $B\smashp f$. Moreover, $i\smashp X$ is a cofibration by the previous step, so that $B\smashp X\to P$ is also a $(G\times H)$-global weak equivalence by left properness. We conclude from $2$-out-of-$3$ that also $P\to B\smashp Y$ is a $(G\times H)$-global weak equivalence, as claimed.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:34:20.707136+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f66eccff4d216fdf233f78b59bde6dd95dd28b44da63c559528c75ba7fda95cf","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 8 (WKBC bridge-weighted regression and numerical consistency) of arXiv:2609.02196, 'Schr\"odinger Bridges on Lie Group Manifolds for Probabilistic Intrinsic Generation'] The population minimizer is \(\bm s^*=\nabla_{\bm\xi}\log h_t^{\beta^*}\), and
\begin{equation}
\mathcal J_{\rm WKBC}^{\rm br}(\bm s)-\mathcal J_{\rm WKBC}^{\rm br}(\bm s^*)
=\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T
\int\norm{\bm s(t,x)-\bm s^*(t,x)}^2
P_t^{\rm SB}(\dd x)\,\dd t.
\end{equation}
Let \(P^{\bm s,\pi_0}\) denote the controlled law with normalized control
\(\sqrt{2\gamma}\,\bm s\) and initial law \(\pi_0\). If
\(P_0^{\rm SB}\ll\pi_0\) and the relevant Girsanov exponentials are true martingales, then
\begin{equation}
\KL(P^{\rm SB}\|P^{\bm s,\pi_0})
=\KL(P_0^{\rm SB}\|\pi_0)
+\gamma T\bigl[\mathcal J_{\rm WKBC}^{\rm br}(\bm s)
-\mathcal J_{\rm WKBC}^{\rm br}(\bm s^*)\bigr].
\end{equation}
In particular, when \(\pi_0=P_0^{\rm SB}\),
\begin{equation*}
d_{\rm BL}(P^{\rm SB},P^{\bm s,P_0^{\rm SB}})
\le
\sqrt{2\gamma T\bigl[\mathcal J_{\rm WKBC}^{\rm br}(\bm s)
-\mathcal J_{\rm WKBC}^{\rm br}(\bm s^*)\bigr]}.
\end{equation*}
Thus the regression-to-path-law conversion has the explicit constant \(\gamma T\) and requires no auxiliary occupation-density-ratio constant.

For positive numerical factors \((f_{0,N},g_{T,N})\), the same reverse-KL argument applies to the corresponding numerical bridge and yields the path-space decomposition in Eq.~\eqref{eq:wkbc-total-error}. Under the approximation conditions in \cref{app:wkbc-implementation}, its numerical-bridge term tends to zero as the lattice, quadrature, Sinkhorn, interpolation, and initial-law approximations are refined, while its regression term vanishes with bridge-weighted risk consistency. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:57:30.978276+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f69c0fe872d6b0c2de0d5b127f6bc48ad18dca028b41e0c3661273348c09782c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 (Structural representation and exact extraction) of arXiv:2608.12492, 'Weak Limits of Wiener Chaos: Primitive--Fock Classification and Hilbert--Stein Extraction'] For every represented subsequence of \eqref{overview:eq:packet}, the
following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\Roman*)}]
 \item Labeled block evaluation extends uniquely, at every physical
 weight $q$, to a unitary
 \begin{equation}
 \mathbb U_q:
 \cW_q\!\left(\bigoplus_{s\le q}\cK_s\right)
 \xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }\cH_q.
 
 \end{equation}
 This unitary gives the direct implication in
 \eqref{overview:eq:weak-closure}; collision-null replicas give the
 converse realization and the convergence of the finite contraction
 register.

 \item Put
 \begin{equation}
 a_Q=\sum_{r=1}^{Q-1}\binom{Q-1}{r}^2\binom{2r}{r},
 \qquad
 \mu_Q=\left\lfloor\frac{Q^2+Q+1}{3}\right\rfloor.
 
 \end{equation}
 There are nested common graded modules $M^{[J]}$ such that the separated
 feedback energy and the coherently aggregated Gaussian self-plus-interface
 defect satisfy
 \begin{equation}
 \mathfrak H_Q(A^{[J]},r^{[J]})\le\frac{a_QR^4}{J},
 \qquad
 \Delta_{\mathrm{res}}(r^{[J]})+\Delta_{\mathrm{mix}}(A^{[J]},r^{[J]})
 \le\frac{\mu_Qa_QR^4}{J}.
 
 \end{equation}
 Consequently, along a further subsequence,
 \begin{equation}
 F_n\Longrightarrow A_*+G_C,
 \qquad G_C\indep A_*.
 
 \end{equation}
 This factorization is quantitative and unconditional, but the active
 factor $A_*$ need not be canonical.

 \item Suppose that the packet is carried by one chaos order $q$, and let
 $\xi_a=[f_{n,a}]_{\mathcal U}\in\cH_q$.  A Gram-reduced trajectory
 admits a sufficiently slow diagonal $J(n)\to\infty$ for which
 \begin{equation}
 (A_n^{[J(n)]},B_n^{[J(n)]})
 \Longrightarrow
 \left(
  \mathbb U_q^{-1}P_{\cD_q}\xi,
  \mathbb U_q^{-1}P_{\cK_q}\xi
 \right).
 
 \end{equation}
 The second component is Gaussian and independent of the first.  The
 reduced feedback may be stopped after fewer than $J$ promotions with
 \begin{equation}
 \mathfrak H_q(A^{[J]},r^{[J]})\le \frac{d\,a_qR^4}{J}.
 
 \end{equation}
 If $\kappa_{n,a}$ denotes the fourth cumulant of the $a$th component,
 then, along the represented subsequence,
 \begin{equation}
  P_{\cD_q}\xi=0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \lim_{\mathcal U}\sum_a\kappa_{n,a}=0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  F_n\Longrightarrow_{\mathcal U}N_d(0,\Sigma),
  
 \end{equation}
 and the finite-level characteristic-function error is bounded by a
 constant times $|t|^2(\sum_a\kappa_{n,a})^{1/2}$.

 \item For a finite mixed-degree terminal $T$, let $\cN_s(T)$ be the
 closed span of the ranges of its nonlinear one-leg flattenings of
 primitive weight $s$.  Then
 \begin{equation}
 T=\mathsf A^{\can}+\mathsf G^{\can},
 \qquad \mathsf G^{\can}\indep\mathsf A^{\can},
 
 \end{equation}
 where the covariance of $\mathsf G^{\can}$ is maximal among graded
 Gaussian factors annihilated by the complete raw one-leg nonlinear
 register.  Simultaneous extraction can fail to reach this split; a
 lexicographic, weight-by-weight extraction does reach it.
\end{enumerate}
The $J^{-1/2}$ law-level bound derived from
\eqref{overview:eq:HS-rate} concerns only the noncanonical factorization
\eqref{overview:eq:noncanonical}; no quantitative rate toward
\eqref{overview:eq:canonical} is asserted. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

	\]
    Let \(\{S\geq h_n\} = \{S_k\geq h_n(k)\ \forall k =-n,\dots,n\}\), \(P_{0}^{h_n} = P(\cdot \given S_{-n} = S_n = 0, S\geq h_n)\) and \(\rS_0 = n^{-\alpha_p}(S_0-n)\).

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.177619+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f6cf902830d44196232726e732f11132c890f43f7349e2277ad075f47de1989b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 78 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For $\hat{Y}$ the stopped martingale defined above, we can construct a deterministic time change $\tilde{Y}$ that can be expressed as the stochastic integral
    \[
    \tilde{Y}(t)
    =\tilde{Y}(q_0) + \int_0^t \tilde{w}_t\,d\tilde{W}(t)
    \]
for $t\in[q_0,\gamma(1)]$,
where
$\tilde{Y}(q_0)=\hat{Y}(q_0)=Y(q_0)$,
$\tilde{W}$ is a standard Brownian motion, and $\tilde{w}$ satisfies
the constraint $\E[(\tilde{w}_t)^2]=1$ for all $t\in[q_0,\gamma(1)]$.

\begin{proof} We will construct a  martingale $\tilde{Y}$ to essentially be the deterministic time-change of $\hat{Y}$ such that $\E[\tilde{Y}(t)^2]=t$ for all $t\in[q_0,\gamma(1)]$. Then, for $t\in[\gamma(1),1]$, we will take $\tilde{Y}$ to be any martingale ending at $\pm1$ almost surely, which exists by Lemma~\ref{lem:Yt-process-always-is-completable} below. To formalize the time reparametrization, since $\gamma:[q_0,1]\to[q_0,\gamma(1)]$ is nondecreasing, we can define its right-continuous generalized inverse 
\[\lambda:[q_0,\gamma(1)]\to[q_0,1]\,.\]
As a consequence of \eqref{e:gamma.prime} we must have $\gamma(t)-\gamma(s)\le t-s$ and $\lambda(t)-\lambda(s)\ge t-s$ for all $q_0 \le s\le t\le1$. It  follows by combining these inequalities with Proposition~\ref{p:gamma-1} that
    \beq
    \begin{aligned}
    s &\ge \gamma(s) \ge \gamma(1)+s-1 \ge s-4\epsilon^{1/2}\,,\\
    t &\le \lambda(t) \le \lambda(\gamma(1)) + t-\gamma(1)
    =1+t-\gamma(1) \le t+4\epsilon^{1/2}
    \end{aligned}
    \eeq
for all $s\in [q_0,1]$, and $t\in [q_0,\gamma(1)]$. It is clear from this that we must define $\tilde{Y}(t) = \hat{Y}(\lambda(t))$, so that
we will have $\E[\tilde{Y}(t)^2] = \E[\hat{Y}(\lambda(t))^2] = \gamma(\lambda(t))=t$. Since
    \[
    \hat{Y}(\lambda(t)) = Y(q_0) + \int_{q_0}^{\lambda(t)}
        w_u \ind\{u\le\tau\} \,dW(u)\,,
    \]
by considering the change of variables $u=\lambda(s)$ it is natural to define
    \beq
    \tilde{W}(t) = \int_{q_0}^{\lambda(t)} \gamma'(u)^{1/2} dW(u)\,.
    \eeq
Then $\tilde{W}$ is a local martingale with quadratic variation
    \[
    \langle \tilde{W}\rangle_t 
    = \int_{q_0}^{\lambda(t)} \gamma'(u)\,du
    = \gamma(\lambda(t))-\gamma(q_0) = t-q_0
    \]
for all $t\in[q_0,1]$, so by the L\'evy characterization it is a standard Brownian motion on $t\in[q_0,1]$, and is progressively measurable with respect to the time-changed filtration
$\tilde{\cF}_Y(t)\equiv\cF_Y(\lambda(t))$. We then define the modified control
    \[
    \tilde{w}_s
    \equiv
    \frac{w_{\lambda(s)}}{\gamma'(\lambda(s))^{1/2} }
      \ind\{\lambda(s)\le \tau\}\,,\]
where we define $\tilde{w}_s\equiv1$ in the case $\gamma'(\lambda(s))=0$ --- by Lemma~\ref{l:generalized.inverse.fn}, the set of such times $s$ is of measure zero. If $\gamma'(\lambda(s))=0$ then clearly we have $\E[(\tilde{w}_s)^2]=1$, and otherwise 
\eqref{e:gamma.prime} gives
	\[\E[(\tilde{w}_s)^2]
    =\frac{\E[(w_{\lambda(s)})^2 \ind\{
        \lambda(s)\le\tau\}]}
        {\gamma'(\lambda(s))}
    = 1\,.
    \]
We can then express the desired process as
    \[
    \tilde{Y}(t)
    = \hat{Y}(\lambda(t))
    =\tilde{Y}(q_0) + \int_{q_0}^t \tilde{w}_s\,d\tilde{W}(s)\,,
    \]
where $\tilde{Y}(q_0)=\hat{Y}(q_0)= Y(q_0)$. This concludes the proof.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T16:22:59.719078+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f6eba7d20cf15f2978075642c099f507acb92ae1e47b9510c6abae0b1d005602","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:modal-gg-translation of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] {das_intuitionistic_2023}}] 
  We inductively define the \emph{modal (G\"odel--Gentzen) double negation translation}
  $(\cdot)^N: \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond} \to \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$:
  \begin{align*}
    \bot^N &\coloneq \bot, &
    p^N    &\coloneq \neg \neg p, \\
    (\varphi \land \psi)^N &\coloneq \varphi^N \land \psi^N, &
    (\varphi \lor \psi)^N  &\coloneq \neg(\neg \varphi^N \land \neg \psi^N), \\
    (\varphi \to \psi)^N &\coloneq \varphi^N \to \psi^N, \\
    (\Box\varphi)^N &\coloneq \Box\varphi^N, &
    (\Diamond\varphi)^N &\coloneq \neg \Box \neg \varphi^N.
  \end{align*}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:16:18.664083+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f70c928b376b6f60597a43fae1e743d3682e0d69eac9b55e32d06b808cd26188","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $k,d\in\mathbb{N}$ with $d\ge 2$, and let $a,b>0$. Set
\[
\beta_1:=\frac{1}{2k(d-1)+1}
\quad\text{and}\quad
s:=\frac{d(2k-1)}{4k(d-1)}.
\]
Then, for every pair of mappings $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ and $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_k)$ with
$f_j,g_j\in \mathcal{P}_d(\gamma)$,
\[
\int_E \Delta_f\,d\gamma\ge a,
\quad
\int_E \Delta_g\,d\gamma\ge a,
\]
and
\[
\max_{1\le j\le k}\operatorname{Var}_\gamma(f_j)\le b,
\quad
\max_{1\le j\le k}\operatorname{Var}_\gamma(g_j)\le b,
\]
one has, for every $\beta\in(0,\beta_1)$,
\begin{equation}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C_1k^{3/2}d\,(\beta_1-\beta)^{-s}
\bigl(1+a^{-\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}}b^{\frac{2k-1}{4k(d-1)}}\bigr)\,
d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)^\beta,
\end{equation}
where $C_1>0$ is an absolute constant. In particular, if $d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)>0$, then
\begin{equation}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C_2k^{3/2}d
\bigl(1+a^{-\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}}b^{\frac{2k-1}{4k(d-1)}}\bigr)
\bigl(1+\ln\tfrac{2}{d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)}\bigr)^s
d_{\mathrm{KR}}(f,g)^{\beta_1},
\end{equation}
where $C_2>0$ is an absolute constant.

More generally, for every $r\in\mathbb{N}$, setting
\[
\beta_r:=\frac{1}{2rk(d-1)+1},
\]
one has, for every $\beta\in(0,\beta_r)$,
\begin{equation}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C_1(r,k)\,d\,(\beta_r-\beta)^{-s}
\bigl(1+a^{-\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}}b^{\frac{2k-1}{4k(d-1)}}\bigr)\,
d_r(f,g)^\beta,
\end{equation}
where $C_1(r,k)>0$ depends only on $r$ and $k$. Moreover, if $d_r(f,g)>0$, then
\begin{equation}
d_{\mathrm{TV}}(f,g)
\le
C_2(r,k)\,d
\bigl(1+a^{-\frac{1}{2k(d-1)}}b^{\frac{2k-1}{4k(d-1)}}\bigr)
\bigl(1+\ln\tfrac{2}{d_r(f,g)}\bigr)^s
d_r(f,g)^{\beta_r},
\end{equation}
where $C_2(r,k)>0$ depends only on $r$ and $k$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:37:08.315653+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f719255e06f6f9de992a413b02946463e46b5faae29dffcbf889cd8607f70ba9","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \((N,R_{+},R_{-},\gamma)\) be a sutured manifold and \(S\) be a properly embedded surface in \(N\).
We call \(S\) a \emph{decomposition surface} for \((N,\gamma)\) if the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any sutured torus \(T\), the intersection \(S\cap T\) is either empty or a collection of essential simple closed curves, all of which represent the same homology class in \(H_{1}(T)\).
\item For any sutured annulus \(A\), \(S\cap A\) is either empty, a simple closed curve with the same homology class as the suture \(A\cap s(\gamma)\), or a properly embedded nonseparating arc.
\item No component of \(\partial S\) bounds a disc in \(R(\gamma)\) and no component of \(S\) is a disc \(D\) with \(\partial D\subset R_{+}\cup R_{-}\).
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:38:13.648450+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f721a0fc3932ce77e99e32722ed09256cb9bcf14c3dc9fea1afe7a28652e1337","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defn 9 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] [See \cite[Definitions~3.8, 3.9 and 3.11]{Ya}.]
A pre-log Dieudonn\'e algebra
\[
\sA^*=(A^*,d,F,\alpha:L\to A^0,\delta:L\to A^1)
\]
over $\sR$ is \emph{saturated} if its underlying Dieudonn\'e algebra is
saturated in the sense of \cite[Definition~3.4.1]{BLM}. Let
\[
i_A\colon A^*\longrightarrow\Sat(A^*)
\]
be the saturation map of the underlying Dieudonn\'e algebra. We equip
$\Sat(A^*)$ with the same monoid $L$ and with maps
\[
\alpha_{\rm sat}:=i_A^0\circ\alpha,
\qquad
\delta_{\rm sat}:=i_A^1\circ\delta.
\]
The resulting pre-log Dieudonn\'e algebra is denoted by $\Sat(\sA^*)$.

A saturated pre-log Dieudonn\'e algebra is \emph{strict} if its
underlying saturated Dieudonn\'e algebra is strict in the sense of
\cite[Definition~3.5.6]{BLM}. If
\[
\rho_A\colon A^*\longrightarrow W(A^*)
=
\varprojlim_r A^*/\mathrm{Fil}^rA^*
\]
is the strictification map of the underlying Dieudonn\'e algebra, we
equip $W(A^*)$ with the same monoid $L$ and with maps
\[
\alpha_W:=\rho_A^0\circ\alpha,
\qquad
\delta_W:=\rho_A^1\circ\delta.
\]
We write $W(\sA^*)$ for the resulting strict pre-log Dieudonn\'e
algebra and set
\[
\WSat(\sA^*):=W(\Sat(\sA^*)).
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:51:11.643858+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f74cebb82afe43a42a2c76e3f62e0debe1495ee8bf0289ca82d55627e735df2c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 21 of arXiv:2605.31471, 'Convergence Rates of Continuous-Time Random Walks to Time-Fractional Diffusions with Unbou'] Let $F_t = e^{tL}$ be a strongly continuous bounded semigroup on a Banach space $(B,\|\cdot\|_B)$:
        \[
            \max_{s \in [0,t]} \|F_s\|_{B \to B} \leq e^{\bar m t}.
        \]
        
        Let $L$ be the generator of $F_t$, and let $D \subset \operatorname{dom} L$ be another Banach space with $\|\cdot\|_D \geq \|\cdot\|_B$ such that
        \[
        \|Lf\|_B \leq l \|f\|_D \, \forall f \in D.
        \]
        Assume also that $F_t$ is bounded in $D$:
        \[
        \max_{s \in [0,t]} \|F_s\|_{D \to D} \leq e^{m t},
        \]
        for some $m \geq 0$.
        
        
        Let $U_h$ be a family of linear bounded operators in $B$ with 
        \[
          \| U_h \|_{B \to B} \leq e^{q h},
          \qquad q\ge0,
        \]
        and let
        \begin{align} 
        \left\| \left( \frac{U_h - 1}{h} - L \right) f \right\|_B &\leq \epsilon_h \|f\|_D, \\
        
        \left\| \left( \frac{F_h - 1}{h} - L \right) f \right\|_B &\leq \chi_h \|f\|_D, 
        \end{align}
        where $\epsilon_h,\chi_h>0$ are monotone and tend to zero as $h\to0$.
        
        Then
        \begin{equation} 
        \begin{aligned}
            \sup_{s \leq t} \left\| (U_h)^{\lfloor s/h\rfloor} f - F_s f \right\|_B
            &\leq
            (\chi_h + \epsilon_h) \|f\|_D
            \int_0^t e^{ms + q (t-s)} \, ds  \\
            &\quad
            + e^{\bar m t} h (l + \epsilon_h) \|f\|_D .
        \end{aligned}
        \end{equation}

        For the killed semigroups with rate $c>0$,
        \begin{equation} 
        \begin{aligned}
            \sup_{s \leq t}
            \left\| e^{-c\lfloor s/h\rfloor h } (U_h)^{\lfloor s/h\rfloor} f
            - e^{-cs} F_s f \right\|_B
            &\leq
            (\chi_h + \epsilon_h) \|f\|_D
            \int_0^t e^{(m-c)s + (q-c) (t-s)} \, ds  \\
            &\quad
            + e^{(\bar m - c) t} h (l + \epsilon_h + c) \|f\|_D .
        \end{aligned}

{"assumptions":["d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2,1<=r<K,0<=ell<=r integers","Paired A/S VC class; uniform contexts then uniform truths; independent uniform r-subsets in A, all truths in S","Actual iid factual samples without tags; independent uniform ell-subset verifier in every variable context including S","Unresolved sibling pairs have equal distinct observed-plus-certified counts h<=r; identified pairs are logically certified by an S context with >r known truths; each identified A count j is >= maximum unresolved h (vacuous if none)","All generators; robust exact-level source calibration across every compatible orientation and residual support"],"created_at":"2026-10-21T21:03:39.295480+00:00","domain":"statistical learning; calibrated generation; partial truth verification","id":"claim_f75b182c10094807f8f65295a7c116ffcea2d51b7b906b0cc0c6c75d7a006c10","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); independent review pending. # Pair-balanced factual identities under partial verification

T379-C015 v2, proof (unaudited). Both exact verification suites PASS;
independent mathematical, priority and target-scope review pending.
Targets 1 and 2. This is a conditional data-regime result, not a global
expected minimax claim. The unresolved unequal-sibling-count regime is
the hardest missing piece; C010 shows why its ordering cannot be assumed.

## Model and data region

Use the paired VC-d experiment: d>=1,N>=2d+1,K>=2,1<=r<K integers;
one A and one S per pair, all remaining contexts known S. S has K true
candidates, A has an independent uniform r-subset. The source p chooses
contexts uniformly, then true candidates uniformly. Observe n>=0 iid
factual context/candidate samples without orientation tags. Independently
a perfect verifier supplies a uniform ell-subset of truths in each
variable context, including S, 0<=ell<=r. Let C_x be the union of
distinct observed and verified candidate identities in context x.

Condition on any positive-probability data outcome for which every pair
has |C_left|=|C_right|=h_j<=r. The actual identities may differ. Thus no
orientation is logically excluded, and every one of 2^d orientations
is compatible. Counts and likelihoods of repeated observations can be
unequal: uniform orientation weights below are an ARTIFICIAL proof
distribution, not the actual Bayesian posterior. Under a chosen
orientation, the A support ranges uniformly over r-subsets containing
C_A. Put D_h=#{j:h_j=h}, ell<=h<=r.

Define

 b_h=[1/K+(r-h)/(r(K-h))]/(2N),
 tau_h=(K-r)/(2(K-h)),
 M_h=(D_h/N)*(2-h/r-h/K),
 T_h=sum_{t=h}^r M_t.

Over ALL generators, with source Mis_infinity<=c required in every
compatible world (including every compatible A support), the proposed
exact conditional worst-world false-mass frontier is

 V_D(c)=tau_ell*(T_ell-c)_+
        +sum_{h=ell+1}^r (tau_h-tau_{h-1})*(T_h-c)_+.       (1)

All formulas allow missing D_h and c in [0,1]. Exact score bins define
source Mis_infinity=TV(g,p_Pi), with p uniformly coarsened in each bin.

## Lower bound across arbitrary mixed bins

Average orientations fairly and A supports uniformly conditional on
containing their known identities. Let mu be the resulting mean law.
Every known true atom in a variable context has density

 a=(1/r+1/K)/(2N).

The uncertified atoms of a pair at count h have density b_h and false
probability tau_h under this artificial prior. Their total mu mass is
M_h across the D_h pairs. Known S atoms have density 1/(NK).

As h increases, tau_h increases and b_h decreases: directly,
b_h-b_{h+1}=(K-r)/(2Nr(K-h)(K-h-1)) when h<r. All safe densities
are >=1/(NK)>=b_h. Thus E_h, the union of uncertified atoms in pairs
with count at least h, consists of lower-density atoms than its entire
complement. For ANY partition Pi, uniform coarsening increases its mass:

 mu_Pi(E_h)>=mu(E_h)=T_h.

Indeed in each cell the mean density over E_h is at most the mean over
its complement, so replacing both means by the cell mean transfers
mass into E_h. This proves the assertion per bin, not merely globally.

Robust feasibility and linearity/TV convexity give TV(mu_Pi(g),g)<=c.
Hence g(E_h)>=(T_h-c)_+. Layer-cake decomposition of the artificial
average false risk gives

 max_world H(g)>=tau_ell*g(E_ell)
                   +sum_{h>ell}(tau_h-tau_{h-1})*g(E_h)
                >=V_D(c).

No joint-probability multiplication or actual-posterior identity is used.

## Matching construction

Start from mu. Remove mass min(c,T_ell) from uncertified groups in
decreasing h order, uniformly within each h group, and add it uniformly
to the fixed known S reservoir. All remaining g(E_h)=(T_h-c)_+.
Each pair's known-true group has h atoms from each sibling and invariant
source mass h*(1/r+1/K)/N. Its uncertified group has K-h atoms from
each sibling and invariant source mass (2-h/r-h/K)/N, regardless of
orientation or which residual truths occupy A. The constructed g is
constant on every such group. Exact score bins only merge invariant
groups, so p_Pi=mu_Pi in every compatible world. Since g_Pi=g,
Mis_infinity<=TV(mu,g)<=c. The uncertified false-atom fraction in each
h group equals tau_h in every world. Thus actual H equals V_D(c)
worldwise, proving conditional sharpness of (1).

## Same-data oracle and exact estimation penalty

If the true partition is additionally supplied, let

 A_h=D_h*(r-h)/(Nr), Q_h=sum_{t=h}^r A_t,
 alpha_h=(K-r)/(K-h)=2tau_h.

The same-data known-partition frontier, by the ordered known-A groups,
is

 O_D(c)=alpha_ell*(Q_ell-c)_+
        +sum_{h>ell}(alpha_h-alpha_{h-1})*(Q_h-c)_+.       (2)

Here A_h is the posterior mass of unknown true candidates of the actual
A contexts, and their densities decrease while their false risks rise.
The same mixed-bin tail proof and transfer-to-S construction apply.
Thus V_D(c)=O_D(c)+[V_D(c)-O_D(c)] is an exact matching decomposition,
with nonnegative difference because giving the partition enlarges
feasibility. At c=0 it simplifies to the explicit positive penalty

 V_D(0)-O_D(0)
   =sum_{h=ell}^r D_h*h*(K-r)^2/(2NrK(K-h)).             (3)

The penalty is zero at h=0, and at h=r contributes kappa/(2N) per pair,
recovering C013's unresolved full-verifier value. In general it depends
on the factual-support histogram, not merely VC dimension or a single
unweighted classification-error scalar. A fair completion among the
2^d support-consistent ERM orientations has conditional expected
classification error 1/N per pair; (3) weights that error by
h*(K-r)^2/[2rK(K-h)]. This is a specified ERM, not an optimal posterior
classification claim. The conditional minimax lower bound is not
silently averaged into a global expected lower bound; C014 forbids
that shortcut at positive budgets.

## Scope

This removes supplied tags and retains actual factual identities for
every balanced outcome, all n,K,r,ell and all calibration budgets. It
allows different h across pairs, but does not cover unequal sibling
counts, already identified pairs, or an unconditional exact expected
frontier. Equal h in every pair reduces the conditional formula to the
corresponding earlier C008 experiment with that many known truths;
the histogram, actual untagged-data applicability and explicit oracle
penalty are the proposed extension, not a claim that C008 was unknown.
Primary basis: Kalai--Vempala 2311.14648v3 Definitions 1--2 pp.8--9;
own earlier C008/C009 are unaudited drafts. No novelty or target score
is certified until independent mathematical and priority review.

## Extension: include identified pairs under a coverage ordering

The same theorem extends as follows. Partition the d pairs into resolved
and unresolved pairs. A resolved pair has a context with >r distinct
known truths, logically forcing S and identifying its sibling as A.
Let E_j count these known A contexts with j distinct known truths,
ell<=j<=r. Each unresolved pair still has balanced count h<=r; D_h
now counts just these unresolved pairs. Require

 j>=h_max for every resolved A, where
 h_max=max{h:D_h>0}.                                    (4)

If no unresolved pairs exist, condition (4) is vacuous. Known facts
in identified S and fixed S contexts are all safe and have density
1/(NK), irrespective of their observed identities or counts.

There are two positive-risk group types under the artificial compatible
prior (independent fair unresolved orientations and uniform compatible
A supports):

* Unresolved count h: mass M_h as before, risk tau_h, density b_h.
* Resolved A count j: mass L_j=E_j*(r-j)/(Nr), risk
  alpha_j=(K-r)/(K-j), density a_j=(r-j)/(Nr(K-j)).

Groups at j=r can have zero factual mass and risk one; retain them
without dividing by their mass. All safe groups have density >=1/(NK).
For resolved groups, j increasing makes risk increase and density
decrease. Across the two types condition (4) implies

 alpha_j>=alpha_hmax=2tau_hmax>=tau_h,
 a_j<=a_hmax<=b_hmax<=b_h.

Thus ALL groups are ordered in opposite directions by density and risk.
Let 0<xi_1<...<xi_s<=1 be their distinct risk values; aggregate masses
at equal risk into m_i, and let R_i=sum_{k=i}^s m_k, xi_0=0. The exact
combined conditional robust frontier is

 V(c)=sum_{i=1}^s (xi_i-xi_{i-1})*(R_i-c)_+.             (5)

The same arbitrary-bin tail argument proves the lower bound. Remove
mass in decreasing risk order, uniformly inside each group, and transfer
to fixed S for the upper bound. Resolved A certified and uncertified
groups have world-invariant p masses because all residual supports
have the same size and contain the known truths. Unresolved balanced
groups have the invariance proved earlier. Consequently exact score
mergers remain valid for every compatible support and orientation.
False fractions equal the specified risks in EACH actual world, so
the construction attains (5) worldwise, not just on artificial average.

The same-data partition oracle is formula (2) with A_h replaced by

 (D_h+E_h)*(r-h)/(Nr).

At c=0 its exact difference from (5) is still formula (3), now summed
over unresolved pairs only. The identified-pair terms cancel. At any
c, both explicit formulas match their respective conditional minima.
When ell=r, every resolved A has j=r and condition (4) always holds;
this reduces (5) to C013's conditional frontier for arbitrary mixtures
of resolved and unresolved pairs. For ell<r this is a larger untagged
partial-verifier data regime than the all-unresolved case.

Unequal sibling counts or failure of (4) are NOT covered. No exact
global expected minimax value follows by averaging (5). This extension
has a separate route check, logs/route_014_extension_check.txt, and its
finite exact verification is kept separate from the general derivation.

## Zero-budget pointwise scope and an explicit control

If all pairs are unresolved and share ONE count h, every atom of the
artificial mean law has density at least b_h. Robust zero calibration
implies g=mu_Pi, hence g(atom)>=b_h. Each actual world has exactly
d(K-r) false atoms. Consequently every such generator obeys the
POINTWISE bound H>=d(K-r)b_h=V_D(0), and the construction attains it.
This separate observation applies regardless of actual orientation
likelihoods. It does not extend to varying h by the same argument.

In fact varying h can destroy even a zero-budget pointwise version of
the conditional bound. Take N=5,d=2,K=3,r=2,ell=0 and counts h_0=0,
h_1=1; use C_2=C_3={0}. These are possible actual untagged data, e.g.
the two observations (2,0),(3,0). Form a bin B containing all three
atoms of context 0 and the four uncertified atoms of contexts 2 and 3.
Its source mass is 1/5+7/30=13/30, independent of orientations and
residual A supports; set g=13/210 on its seven atoms. Other bins are
all of context 1 (g=1/15), both certified atoms of contexts 2 and 3
(g=1/12), and all fixed-S context 4 (g=1/15). Merging the equal 1/15
scores preserves invariance. This g is robustly source-calibrated at
zero in every compatible world.

If context 0 is A its actual false mass is 13/105, strictly below
V_D(0)=1/8 by 1/840. If context 1 is A, its false mass is 9/70,
strictly above 1/8. This is a real compatible-world control, not a
violation of (1) or (5): the theorem is conditional WORST-WORLD, and
the latter world meets that lower bound. It forbids silently replacing
the conditional maximum by a per-world bound even at zero budget in
the varying-count family. No claim about the global sampling minimax
value follows from this single outcome.

Verification logs: pair_balanced_partial_check.json records 5212
arbitrary-bin tail checks, 1806 mixed-bin generator bounds, 2356
world/budget attainer checks and 622 oracle checks. The mixed extension
log pair_balanced_mixed_check.json adds 2400 tail checks, 2125 attainer
checks, 850 oracle checks and 11 exact oracle-gap identities. Controls
show actual failure of score-bin invariance without pair balance,
density ordering without sufficient identified-A coverage, and the
zero-budget pointwise extension under varying pair counts. Finite
verification supports, and does not replace, the general proof above.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:26:00.621248+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f762608aa7ec4bb93d946804d638eb8baf3ab6594907405661c51734d442b82e","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2511.01245, 'A curiously slowly mixing Markov chain'] For the binary Burnside process on $C_2^n$, we have the following:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\displaystyle\chi_{\text{avg}}^2(\ell) = \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} \binom{n}{2k} \left(\frac{1}{2^{4k}} \binom{2k}{k}^2\right)^{2\ell}$.
    \item Take any $\varepsilon > 0$. If $\ell \le (1-\varepsilon) \frac{\log 2}{2} \frac{n}{\log n}$, then $\chi_{\text{avg}}^2(\ell) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$. Then the entire

\[

\qquad

For the sum-reinforcement scheme, the limiting proportions are
characterized as follows. For each generator $g\in G$, the limit

\displaystyle
\sum_{p:p\rightsquigarrow v}r\big((p,v)\big),
& \text{if }v\in V\setminus S,\\[0.25cm]
1, & \text{if }v\in S,

is referred to as the \emph{total balance} of the vertex $v$.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:27:36.726576+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f7bacdbed8ff1ea0cf24fa2ced285143dad4a7dc572e10dffd9e1a17c0a5743b","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 45 (Watson's Lemma) of arXiv:2511.13559, 'Asymptotic analysis of rare events in high dimensions'] Let $f,h\in C^L([0,T])$ and suppose  $h(0)=0$ and $h'(t)>b>0$ for all $t\in[0,T]$. Define the operator $D_h$ by $(D_hf)(t):=\frac{d}{dt}\left(\frac{f(t)}{h'(t)}\right)$. Then
\be
\int_0^Tf(t)e^{-\la h(t)}\dd t=\frac{1}{h'(0)}\sum_{k=1}^{L-1}(D_h^{k-1}f)(0)\la^{-k}+\Rem_{L},
\ee where
\bs
|\Rem_{L}|\leq  b^{-1}\|D_h^{L-1}f\|_\infty\la^{-L} + b^{-1}e^{-\la b T}\sum_{k=1}^{L-1}\la^{-k}|(D_h^{k-1}f)(T)|.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:30:52.738674+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f7c07005240df6336cc489faef498718a6b9e9b3832e787e3b33b5e4940e9828","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] [\cite{Bogachev:Gaussian}, Corollary 6.4.11, \cite{DaPrato:PDEHilbert}, Theorems  1.3.9 and 1.3.10]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:17:10.025609+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f7cde993eb901f898589cf771b1b4dbf5af4083ab20a61c3263c28a0e72ea03f","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 17 (Secant row-sum identity) of arXiv:2608.17374, '\textbf{On the Pseudo-Mixing of Kac's Walk}'] Let $X,Y\in \mathrm{St}(n,k)$ and set $K=Y-X$. Define
\[
q_{ij}=r_i(X)\cdot r_j(K)-r_j(X)\cdot r_i(K),\qquad 1\leq i<j\leq n.
\]
Then
\be
\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}^{2}
=\|K\|_{F}^{2}-\mathrm{Tr}\bigl((K^{\top}X)^{2}\bigr).
\ee
Moreover,
\be
\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}^{2}
\geq \|K\|_{F}^{2}-\frac14\|K\|_{F}^{4}.
\ee
In particular, if $\|K\|_{F}\leq 1$, then
\[
\sum_{i<j}q_{ij}^{2}\geq \frac34\|K\|_{F}^{2}.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:49:49.204465+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f7eb8993ced6a5a30eaf669e1d59bbb453f63aab5960c3325dfbe770e82ab095","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 6 (Matrix Freedman) of arXiv:2604.27119, '\Large Applied Random Matrix Theory\relatedversion'] Consider a finite matrix martingale sequence $(\mtx{S}_0, \dots, \mtx{S}_n)$
consisting of $d_1 \times d_2$ matrices, real or complex.

Suppose that the elements of the difference sequence 
$(\mtx{X}_1, \dots, \mtx{X}_n)$ are uniformly bounded:
$\norm{ \mtx{X}_k } \leq B$.

Introduce the \term{conditional quadratic variation} sequence:
\[
V_k \coloneqq
	\lnorm{ \sum_{j=1}^k \Expect\big[ \mtx{X}_j \mtx{X}_j^* \condbar \coll{F}_{j-1} \big] }
	\vee \lnorm{ \sum_{j=1}^k \Expect\big[ \mtx{X}_j^* \mtx{X}_j \condbar \coll{F}_{j-1} \big] }
	\quad\text{for $k = 1, \dots, n$.}
\]
For parameters $v, t \geq 0$, we have the probability inequalities
\begin{align}

\Prob{ \exists k : \norm{\mtx{S}_k - \mtx{S}_0 } \geq \sqrt{2 v t} + Bt/3 \ \text{and} \
	V_k \leq v } &\leq (d_1+d_2) \, \econst^{-t}; \\

\Prob{ \exists k : \norm{\mtx{S}_k - \mtx{S}_0 } \geq t \ \text{and} \
	V_k \leq v } &\leq (d_1+d_2) \exp\left( \frac{-t^2/2}{v + Bt/3} \right).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["U bounded open in R^n with C^1 boundary","u, tilde u smooth on the closure of U_T and solving the heat equation in U_T (enough regularity that the difference lies in H^1_0(U) at each time and the integrations by parts are valid)","u = tilde u on the lateral boundary partial U x [0,T]","u(.,T) = tilde u(.,T) on U","abstract version: A nonnegative self-adjoint on a Hilbert space, v(t) = e^{-tA} v_0"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:53:49.106658+00:00","domain":"parabolic partial differential equations / backward uniqueness","id":"claim_f7f2eb2e2320ffd0bdf2bf37d3704275ba86518b95b676f9fd0173971587d4a4","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let $U\\subset\\mathbb R^n$ be bounded and open with $C^1$ boundary, $T>0$, and let $u,\\tilde u$ be smooth on $\\overline{U_T}$ and solve $u_t=\\Delta u$ and $\\tilde u_t=\\Delta\\tilde u$ in $U_T$ with the same values on $\\partial U\\times[0,T]$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T23:48:35.820831+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f8133eb2abaaa0d099df45667c7e5cd34a5973f80e5f7bb261d591ebb82917af","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma Analogue of lemma 3.9 of arXiv:2411.09614, 'Moment estimates for the stochastic heat equation on Cartan-Hadamard manifolds'] Suppose $u_0\in L^\infty(M)\cap L^r(M)$, $1\leq r\leq +\infty$.
    Let $b=b(r)=\frac{(n-1)^2}{2\max(2,r)}K_1$ (it is 0 if $r=+\infty$). There exist three functions $F_1,F_2,F_3:\mathbb{R}_+\to\mathbb{R}_+$ such that for every $t>0$, $x\in M$, the following holds for $\alpha>\frac{n-2}{4}$ and $\rho >0$,
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item If $\frac{n-2}{4}<\alpha<\frac{n}{4}$, $$\norm{f_k(\cdot,t,x)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}}^2\leq C^k e^{-2bt}\frac{\beta^{2k}}{k!}\norm{u_0}_{\infty}^2e^{\rho t}F_1(\rho)^k.$$
        \item If $\alpha=\frac{n}{4}$, $$\norm{f_k(\cdot,t,x)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}}^2\leq C^k e^{-2bt}\frac{\beta^{2k}}{k!}\norm{u_0}_{\infty}^2e^{\rho t}F_2(\rho)^k.$$
        \item If $\alpha>\frac{n}{4}$, $$\norm{f_k(\cdot,t,x)}_{\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}}^2\leq C^k e^{-2bt}\frac{\beta^{2k}}{k!}\norm{u_0}_{\infty}^2e^{\rho t}F_3(\rho)^k.$$
    \end{enumerate}
    Here $C>0$ depends on $\alpha,K_1,n,$ and $r$. 
    The functions $F_i:\mathbb{R}_+\to \mathbb{R}_+$ are differentiable and satisfy the following properties:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item For $i\in \set{1,2,3}$, and $K_1>0$ we have  
        \[ \dv{F_i}{\rho}<0,\quad\sup_{\rho\in\mathbb{R}_+}F_i(\rho)=F_i(0)<\infty,\text{ and }\lim_{\rho\uparrow+\infty}F_i(\rho)=0.\]
        
        Note that this implies $F_i:\mathbb{R}_+\to (0,F_i(0)]$ is invertible.
        \item For $K_1>0$, we have the asymptotics \begin{equation}
        F_i(\rho)\sim_{\rho\uparrow+\infty} \begin{cases}
            \left(\frac{1}{\rho}\right)^{2\alpha-\frac{n}{2}+1}& i=1,\\
                \frac{(\ln \rho)^2}{\rho}& i=2,\\
                \frac{1}{\rho}& i=3.
            \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["Rate-independent random recursive tree attachment.","The cited recursive-tree height estimate and standard root-subtree size limit."],"created_at":"2026-10-10T06:51:51.364062+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f8302037ad42a1dd803c8611710c6292f630e9af8a604deb9e7eedb3628d95f2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; the combinatorial identities (layer = second-largest branch height, maximum layer = floor(diam/2) <= height) were verified by brute-force leaf stripping on 40 random recursive trees of sizes 6 to 120 (480 vertices), with the 5-vertex path as a control] This is the layer part of the campaign answer to Conjecture 2 of H. Stepanyants, P. L. Krapivsky, H. Hartle and D. Krioukov, The rank and layer distributions in random recursive trees, arXiv:2608.04303. For each integer n>=3, let T_n be a random recursive tree on vertices 1,...,n, in which each vertex j>=2 chooses its parent independently and uniformly from 1,...,j-1. Repeatedly remove all vertices of degree at most one, assigning layer zero to the first removed set and successively increasing the layer. Let L_n be the maximum layer. As n tends to infinity, L_n=e log n-(3/2)log log n+O_P(1), where logarithms are natural and O_P(1) means that the centered sequence is bounded in probability. Under this removal rule, L_n=floor(diameter(T_n)/2); other conventions for the last vertex left standing change the maximum by at most one. The proof uses the recursive-tree height estimate of Addario-Berry and Ford (Corollary 1.3) and the fact that the root's normalized subtree sizes have a stick-breaking limit whose second-largest term is positive almost surely. The maximum-rank part of Conjecture 2 is not addressed. This is an unrefereed campaign result.","status":"unverified"}

\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:54:53.440643+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f84c0ef64adcd7a45454d206ca9e8be870346432f815b78d7dc0d19ef57b543c","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 17 (\cite{AgrestiVeraarNonLinParab}) of arXiv:2606.15425, 'Well-posedness of stochastic parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities and applicat'] Let $\mathcal B_1\hookrightarrow \mathcal B$ be Banach spaces. Set $\mathcal B_{1-\theta}=[\mathcal B,\mathcal B_1]_{1-\theta}$ or $\mathcal B_{1-\theta} = (\mathcal B,\mathcal B_1)_{1-\theta,r}$, where the latter denotes real interpolation for $r\in [1, \infty]$. Assume that $p\in (1,\infty)$, $\beta\in [0,p-1)$, $\theta\in (0,1)$ and $T\in (0,\infty]$. Then the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item If $\theta>\frac{1+\beta}{p}$, then
$$
H^{\theta,p}([0,T],w_{\beta};\mathcal B_{1-\theta})\cap L^p([0,T],w_{\beta};\mathcal B_1)
\hookrightarrow C\left([0,T];(\mathcal B,\mathcal B_1)_{1-\frac{1+\beta}{p},p}\right)_0
$$
\item If $\theta>\frac{1}{p}$, then for any $0<\varepsilon<T$
$$
H^{\theta,p}([0,T],w_{\beta};\mathcal B_{1-\theta})\cap L^p([0,T],w_{\beta};\mathcal B_1)\hookrightarrow
 C\left([\varepsilon,T];(\mathcal B,\mathcal B_1)_{1-\frac{1}{p},p}\right)_0.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T20:04:59.424290+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f86e5b7499bf5ed8ed32178485677a83cf9456d8c6f90d356413d0a742862c1a","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition lem:discrete_antitrap_from_CT of arXiv:2605.17725, 'Limit theorems for random walks with spatio-temporal drift'] Let $(\mathcal F_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a filtration, and let $(G_n)_{n\ge0}$ be an

$$
G_{n+1}-G_n=\upsilon_{n+1}F_n+c_{n+1}(\varepsilon_{n+1}+r_{n+1}),

where $(\upsilon_n)_{n\ge1}$ and $(c_n)_{n\ge1}$ are deterministic nonnegative
sequences such that $\sum_{n=1}^\infty c_n^2<\infty$ and $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\upsilon_n=\infty$; for each $n\ge 0$, $F_n$, $\varepsilon_{n+1}$ and $r_{n+1}$ are $\mathcal F_n$-measurable, and
$$
\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n]=0, \quad \mathbb{E}\|\varepsilon_n\|^2<\infty.
$$

Let $\Gamma\in\mathcal F_\infty$ be an event, where
$\mathcal F_\infty:=\sigma\bigl(\bigcup_{n\ge0}\mathcal F_n\bigr)$.
Assume that there exist a deterministic constant $\rho>0$, a finite random
integer $T_0$, a deterministic nonincreasing sequence $(b_n)_{n\ge0}$, and an
event $\Omega_*\in\mathcal F_\infty$ with $\mathbb P(\Omega_*)=1$ such that the
following hold.

$$
\langle G_n, F_n\rangle\ge0
\text{ whenever }\|G_n\|<2\rho; \quad \text{and}\quad
\upsilon_{n+1}\|F_n\|<\rho.
$$

\item[(b)] There exist deterministic constants $a_0,a_1>0$ such that on $\Gamma$,
$$
0<a_0\le \liminf_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{E}[\|\varepsilon_{n+1}\|^2\mid\mathcal F_n]
\le
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{E}[\|\varepsilon_{n+1}\|^2\mid\mathcal F_n]
\le a_1<\infty.
$$

\item[(c)] On $\Omega_*$, for all sufficiently large $n$,
$
c_{n+1}\|\varepsilon_{n+1}\|\le b_n.
$

\item[(d)] $
b_n^2=O(\alpha_n^2).
$ with 
$
\alpha_n:=\left(\sum_{k\ge n+1}c_k^2\right)^{1/2}.
$

\item[(e)] On $\Gamma$,
$
\sum_{n=1}^\infty \|r_n\|^2<\infty.
$
\end{itemize}

Then
$

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T19:37:08.311265+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f89142b3ce3207a5f8a77e9d9fadf6b6d2e60a06c33b0f009a7d0dd0e6b49e25","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:quagmire of arXiv:2608.28505, 'Quagmires and large Suslin forests'] Given an uncountable cardinal $\kappa$ and a set $S \subseteq \mathrm{Lim}(\kappa)$, a\linebreak \emph{$(\kappa, S)$-quagmire} is a quadruple $(T, {<}, {\lhd}, Q)$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label={(Q\arabic*)},  start=0]
\item 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $(T, <)$ is a $\kappa$-Kurepa tree,
\item $\lhd$ is a binary relation on $T$ whose restriction to each level of $T$ is a strict linear order; nodes of distinct heights are $\lhd$-incomparable,
\item the function $Q$ is a partial function from $T^2$ to $T$ whose domain consists of the pairs $(x, y) \in T^2$ such that $\mathrm{ht}(x) < \mathrm{ht}(y)$ and $x \lhd \pi_{\mathrm{ht}(x)}(y)$,
\end{enumerate}

\item if $(x, y) \in \mathrm{dom}(Q)$, then $x < Q(x, y) \lhd y$,
\item if $(x, y) \in \mathrm{dom}(Q)$ and $y < z$, then $Q(Q(x, y), z) = Q(x,z)$,
\item if $(y, z) \in \mathrm{dom}(Q)$ and $x \lhd y$, then $Q(x, Q(y, z)) = Q(x, z)$,
\item if $x \lhd y$ and $\mathrm{ht}(x) \in S \cup \{\kappa\}$, then there exists $\alpha < \mathrm{ht}(x)$ such that $\pi_\alpha(x) \lhd \pi_\alpha(y)$ and $x = Q(\pi_\alpha(x), y)$.
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

		\begin{align}\begin{split}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:38:04.491046+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f8d05297e5d3764a5b489eb2619e5696dc6c1f881f025b71d7e76a8b89469178","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma improved-one-step of arXiv:2607.05054, 'Root Dynamics of Differentiated Polynomials with Rotationally Invariant Structure'] Let $(r_j)_{1 \le j \le n}$ be an increasing sequence of positive real numbers, and let  
\[
\alpha \ge \max_{1 \le j \le n-1} \frac{r_j}{r_{j+1}} .
\]  
Suppose the $j$-th smallest root of $Q$ is exactly $r_j$ for $1 \le j \le n$. Define  
\begin{align}
y = \frac{2 + \log_{-}(\log(\alpha^{-1}))}{\log(\alpha^{-1})}, \qquad \log_{-}(x) = \max(0, -\log x).
\end{align}

Then, for integers $m \ge 1$ and $1 \le q \le m-1$, the $j$-th smallest root $z_j$ of  
\[
S(z) = q Q(z) + m z Q'(z), \qquad 2 \le j \le n,
\]  
satisfies  

\[
\left(1 - \frac{1}{\max(1,\, j-1 - y)}\right) r_j \;\le\; z_j \;\le\; \left(1 - \frac{\alpha}{j+1+2y}\right) r_j .
\]

For $q = 0$ and $3 \le j \le n$, the $(j-1)$-th smallest root of $Q'$ satisfies the same upper bound, and for $2 \le j \le n$ the same lower bound.","status":"unverified"}

		Let $Q$ be a probability measure on $(\varOmega,\varSigma)$.   \smallskip
		
		\noindent\textbf{(a)} If $\mathcal G{\,\subseteq\,}\varSigma$ is a $\sigma$-algebra of subsets of $\varOmega$, then  $Q$ is \textit{absolutely continuous}  with respect to $P$ on $\mathcal G$ (in symbols $Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G{\,\ll\,}P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G$) if
		\[
		\forall\; A\in\mathcal G\quad  \Big( P(A)=0\Rightarrow Q(A)=0 \Big).
		\] 
		In addition, if $P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G{\,\ll\,} Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G$, then $Q$ and $P$ are \textit{equivalent} on $\mathcal G$ (in symbols $Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G{\,\sim\,}P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G$). For $\mathcal G{\,=\,}\varSigma$ simply write $Q{\,\ll\,} P$ and $Q{\sim}P$.  
		\smallskip
		
		\noindent  	\textbf{(b)} If $\{\mathcal G_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R_+}$ is a filtration for $\varSigma$, then $Q$ and $P$ are \textit{progressively equivalent} on $\{\mathcal G_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R_+}$, if $Q$ and $P$   are equivalent on each  $\mathcal G_t$ (i.e., $Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t{\,\sim\,} P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t$). If $P$ and $Q$  are progressively equivalent with respect to $\{\mathcal G_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R_+}$, we write
		\[
		\frac{dQ}{dP}{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t:=\frac{d(Q{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t)}{d(P{\upharpoonright}\mathcal G_t)} \,\,\text{ for all }  t\in\mathbb R_+
