{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:27:56.777843+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f8f52a7e05acc89b83e8617baed86520f71863de4a0ee9b6906540e8539892b8","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 11 of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Let $\chi$ be a Navier--Stokes potential on an open fiber domain  \(\mathscr F\subset\mathscr E\) (containing its zero section) of a relaxation bundle \(\mathscr E\subseteq\Sym^2T^*\Mcal\). Then, a \textbf{relaxation rate map} consists of a smooth fiberwise map $\mathscr B=\mathscr B(\beta,\zeta)\in\mathscr E^*$ defined for all future timelike $\beta$ and all $\zeta \in \mathscr F$, satisfying the following conditions.

\bei 

\item \emph{Stable equilibrium property:}
\bel{eq:pot-relax-map}
\mathscr B(\beta,0)=0,
\qquad
\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}(\beta,\zeta)\geq0,
\qquad
\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}(\beta,\zeta)=0
\Longleftrightarrow
\zeta=0.
\ee

\item \emph{Positivity property:}  Its linearization along the equilibrium manifold $\mathbb M$ given by 
\bel{eq:pot-relax-linearization}
\mathbb M^{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}(\beta)
\coloneqq
\frac{\del\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}}{\del\zeta_{\gamma\delta}}(\beta,0)
\ee
must be symmetric under interchange of the two index pairs and positive definite on~$\mathscr E$, namely
\be
\eta_{\alpha\beta}\mathbb M^{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}(\beta)\eta_{\gamma\delta}>0
\qquad
\text{for every nonzero }\eta\in\mathscr E.
\ee
\eei
Furthermore, the associated \textbf{production term} is
\bel{production-term-value}
\mathfrak d_{\mathscr B}
\coloneqq
\zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}
\geq0.
\ee","status":"unverified"}

\begin{enumerate}

	then we define its $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$-divergence 
	to be the scalar function
	$\nullangDiv \Xi \eqdef \gnulltori^{-1} \cdot \nullangD \Xi$. 
	Similarly, if $V$ is an $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$-tangent vectorfield, 
	then we define its $\doublenulltoritwoarg{\ubar}{u}$-divergence to be the scalar function

	\eqdef

	\left[\nullangD_{\nullgeop{x^B}} \upxi \right]\left(\nullgeop{x^C},\nullgeop{x^A} \right).
	\end{align}
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["(a_n)_{n >= 0} is a real sequence","the second differences a_n - 2a_{n+1} + a_{n+2} are nonnegative for every n >= 0 (convexity)","a_n -> 0 as n -> infinity","consequences used and derived from these: a_n >= 0, a_n nonincreasing, n(a_n - a_{n+1}) -> 0, sum (n+1)(a_n - 2a_{n+1} + a_{n+2}) = a_0","integrability is with respect to Lebesgue measure on the circle"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:07:38.815245+00:00","domain":"Fourier analysis, trigonometric series","id":"claim_f95cf78453cad9016df951c8497b0e8bcbb54049fe66f88a10ab868d7db99aa2","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let (a_n)_{n >= 0} be real numbers which are CONVEX, meaning the second differences D2 a_n := a_n - 2 a_{n+1} + a_{n+2} are >= 0 for every n >= 0, and which tend to 0. (These two hypotheses already force a_n >= 0 and a_n nonincreasing: the first differences a_{n+1} - a_n are nondecreasing, so if one of them were positive the sequence would tend to +infinity. They also force n(a_n - a_{n+1}) -> 0, since the differences are monotone.) THEOREM (Young; Zygmund, Trigonometric Series, Ch. V). Put S(x) = a_0/2 + sum_{n >= 1} a_n cos(nx). Then: (1) the series converges for every x not in 2 pi Z, uniformly on every compact subset of (0, 2 pi); (2) S(x) >= 0 for all such x; (3) S is Lebesgue integrable on (-pi, pi), with (1/(2 pi)) times the integral of S over (-pi,pi) equal to a_0/2; (4) the series IS the Fourier series of S, that is a_n = (1/pi) times the integral over (-pi,pi) of S(x) cos(nx) dx for every n >= 0. The whole theorem rests on one identity: with K_n(x) = (1/(n+1)) (sin((n+1)x/2) / sin(x/2))^2 >= 0 the Fejer kernel, normalised so that (1/(2 pi)) times the integral of K_n over (-pi,pi) is 1, double summation by parts gives S(x) = sum_{n >= 0} (n+1) (D2 a_n) (1/2) K_n(x), with sum_{n >= 0} (n+1) D2 a_n = a_0 < infinity. Nonnegativity is then read off from D2 a_n >= 0 and K_n >= 0, and integrability from the normalisation. SHARP EDGES. (a) It is CONVEXITY, not monotone decrease, that does the work: monotone decrease to zero gives convergence off the origin by Dirichlet's test, but it does not produce the Fejer representation and therefore gives neither nonnegativity nor integrability of the sum. (b) The SINE analogue is false in this form. If (b_n) is convex and decreases to 0, then sum b_n sin(nx) still converges pointwise off 2 pi Z, but its sum is Lebesgue integrable if and only if sum b_n / n converges. The classical counterexample is b_n = 1/log n for n >= 2, which is convex and decreases to 0 while sum 1/(n log n) diverges: the resulting series converges everywhere but is not the Fourier series of any Lebesgue integrable function. Never transport the cosine statement to the sine case. (c) 'Integrable' cannot be improved to 'bounded': for a_n of order 1/n the sum behaves like log(1/|x|) near 0, which is integrable and unbounded. (d) The conclusion S >= 0 is on (0, 2 pi); nothing is claimed at x in 2 pi Z, where the series may diverge (it diverges precisely when sum a_n = infinity). (e) Convexity is only assumed for n >= 0 on the given sequence; a sequence that is eventually convex gives the same conclusions after subtracting a trigonometric polynomial, but then nonnegativity of the sum is lost.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:34:33.545854+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f986deb0243b0fdeb46824059e927a217b9dd4adfc062cb50b1c5255b34023da","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 56 (Villain model) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix $d\in\Z_{\geq 1}$ and $\beta\in\R_{\geq 0}$.
    For any domain $\Lambda$ and $\zeta:\Z^d\to\S^1$,
    the \emph{Villain model} on $\Lambda$ with boundary condition $\zeta$
    at inverse temperature $\beta$ is the probability measure  on $\sigma\in(\S^1)^\Lambda$ given by
    \[
        \diff\mu_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma) = \frac1{Z_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta} e^{-H_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma)} \diff\sigma,
    \]
    where $Z_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta$ is the normalising constant,
    $\diff\sigma$ the Haar measure, and
    \begin{multline}
         e^{-H_{\Villain,\Lambda,\beta}^\zeta(\sigma)}
         =
         \Big(\prod_{\substack{\{x,y\}\subset\Lambda\\x\sim y}}p_\beta(\sigma_x,\sigma_y)\Big)
            \Big(\prod_{\substack{x\in\Lambda,\,y\in\Lambda^c\\x\sim y}}p_\beta(\sigma_x,\zeta_y)\Big);
            \\
         p_\beta(z,z'):=\sum_{m\in\Z} e^{-\frac{\beta}{2}\big(\arg(z)-\arg(z')+2\pi m\big)^2}.
    \end{multline}
    Notice that the Hamiltonian is defined somewhat atypically and incorporates
    the dependency on $\beta$; more on this later.
    The \emph{critical inverse temperature} is defined as the largest $\beta_c^{\Villain}=\beta_c^{\Villain}(d)\in(0,\infty)$
    such that $\mu_{\Villain,\Lambda_n,\beta}^{+1}[\sigma_0]$ decays exponentially fast in $n$
    for any fixed $\beta\in[0,\beta_c^{\Villain})$.
    Classical arguments based on correlations inequalities imply the existence of an infinite-volume Gibbs measure with $+1$ boundary conditions at inverse temperature $\beta\geq 0$, that we refer to as $\mu^{+1}_{\Villain, \beta}$.
    The label $\Villain$ is omitted from notations when it is clear from the context.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T05:33:17.742275+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f99f13972b0f2210ac324d0b64dbb26246970424a68182403f08bf02de00314f","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 121 (Complexified momentum-fiber disintegration) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let
\[
 \mathcal G_a^{\mathbb R}
 :=\{F\in L^2([0,T]\times\R^3;\mathbb C):
 F(s,-\eta)=\overline{F(s,\eta)}\}
\]
with the real inner product from
\eqref{eq:hermitian-gaussian-hilbert-space}, and let
$\mathcal G_a^{\mathbb C}$ be its Hilbert-space complexification.  The map
from $\mathcal G_a^{\mathbb C}$ to the full complex space
$L^2([0,T]\times\R^3;\mathbb C)$ is unitary.  Consequently the changes of
variables
\[
 (\eta,\zeta)\mapsto(m=\eta+\zeta,\eta),
 \qquad
 (\eta,\zeta,r)\mapsto(\xi=\eta+\zeta+r,\eta,\zeta)
\]
induce the complex Hilbert direct-integral identifications
\begin{align}
 \mathcal G_a^{\mathbb C}\otimes_2\mathcal G_b^{\mathbb C}
 &\simeq\int_{\R^3}^{\oplus}
 L^2([0,T]^2\times\R^3_\eta)\dd m,
 \\
 \mathcal G_a^{\mathbb C}\otimes_2\mathcal G_b^{\mathbb C}
 \otimes_2\mathcal G_a^{\mathbb C}
 &\simeq\int_{\R^3}^{\oplus}
 L^2([0,T]^3\times\R^6_{\eta,\zeta})\dd\xi.
 
\end{align}
At finite cutoff, normalize the deterministic Wiener kernels so that the
first-Picard field and the linear field have measurable momentum fibers
$m\mapsto F_m^{\Lambda,\epsilon_{\mathrm P}}(t)$ and
$r\mapsto g_r^\Lambda(t)$.  With
\begin{equation}
 q_{a^\perp,0,\Lambda}^{[\epsilon_{\mathrm P}]}(t,m)
 :=|m_\Lambda(m)|^{2\epsilon_{\mathrm P}}
 q_{a^\perp,0,\Lambda}(t,m),
\end{equation}
their fiber norms satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \|F_m^{\Lambda,\epsilon_{\mathrm P}}(t)\|^2
 =q_{a^\perp,0,\Lambda}^{[\epsilon_{\mathrm P}]}(t,m),
 \qquad
 \|g_r^\Lambda(t)\|^2
 =p_{a,\Lambda}(t,r)
\end{equation}
for almost every $m,r$.  Since the admissible multipliers are uniformly
bounded, the flagged density in
\eqref{eq:cubic-flagged-first-picard-density} is uniformly dominated by a
fixed multiple of the unflagged density.  Swapping the two color-$a$
slots preserves the total momentum $\xi$ and is unitary on every fiber of
\eqref{eq:three-noise-direct-integral}.  Hence
$\Sym_a=(I+\tau_{13})/2$ is a fiberwise orthogonal projection.

All these statements are made in the complexification of the same real
isonormal process.  The reality relation appears as conjugacy between the
$\xi$- and $-\xi$-fibers.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T21:53:10.207321+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f9d0739d9e23ab53e239f28ab875855eaf9b4d07e87c68393341a2de9cc9aac1","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Defi Def:Bary-Subdiv-Weighted of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] \ \vskip 0.1cm
 For a weighted simplicial complex $(K,\mu)$, define the weight of the barycenter $b_{\sigma}$ of any simplex $\sigma$ in $K$ to be $\mu(\sigma)$. Then define a weight  $Sd(\mu)$ on $Sd(K)$ by:
    \begin{equation} 
     Sd(\mu)\big([ b_{\sigma_0},\cdots, b_{\sigma_l}]\big)=\mu(\sigma_l),\ \sigma_0\subsetneq \cdots\subsetneq \sigma_l \in K.
     \end{equation}
   
   Note that we have either
   $\mu(\sigma_0)\, | \, \cdots \, | \,\mu(\sigma_l)$ or 
    $\mu(\sigma_l) \, |\, \cdots\, |\, \mu(\sigma_0)$ depending on whether $\mu$ is ascending or descending. Then it is easy to 
    check that $Sd(\mu)$ is a divisible weight on $Sd(K)$ which is ascending (or descending) if so is $\mu$.  
     We call $(Sd(K),Sd(\mu))$ the \emph{barycentric subdivision} of $(K,\mu)$. For any integer $m\geqslant 1$, let $(Sd^m(K),Sd^m(\mu))$ 
 denote the $m$ iterated barycentric subdivisions of $(K,\mu)$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:07:35.014292+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f9f11b2cef699280406131b0616cabc55e67dab81fb1661a6541cc44001fcfc3","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] A \emph{limiting point} at time \(T\) is an element
\(\xi\in M_T\) of Bamler's metric-flow slice at the limiting time
\cite[Definition~2.32 and the paragraph following
equation~(2.34)]{BamlerStructure}.  We represent it by a probability
conjugate heat flow
\[
 \xi=(\mu_t)_{t<T},\qquad d\mu_t=v_t\,dV_{g(t)},
\]
where
\[
 \partial_tv_t=-\Delta_{g(t)}v_t+R_{g(t)}v_t,
 \qquad v_t>0,
 \qquad \int_Xv_t\,dV_{g(t)}=1.
\]
The representation has the following two properties of the limiting slice:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(P\arabic*)},leftmargin=3em]
\item \(\xi\) is a subsequential limit of point conjugate heat flows
whose pole times increase to \(T\);
\item for \(D=2n\),
\begin{equation}
 \Var_{g(t)}(\mu_t)
 :=\iint_{X\times X}d_{g(t)}(x,y)^2\,d\mu_t(x)d\mu_t(y)
 \le H_{2n}(T-t).
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
The limiting point is called \emph{fixed} when it is chosen before any
sequence of blow-up scales.  Every tangent argument below keeps this
same limiting point while the scales vary.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["an i.i.d., or ergodic and suitably mixing, random environment","a directional transience condition, typically Sznitman's (T) or (T'), or an equivalent ballisticity condition, in some direction l","uniform ellipticity of the transition probabilities, standard though sometimes relaxed in specific results","existence of well-defined regeneration times with positive probability of never backtracking, verified from the environment's independence or mixing structure"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.988973+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_f9f2aaae6b2438ff5a64f4f66dc265aa11c167d9a714a9526edfe927fb576ab3","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For random walk in a random environment on Z^d satisfying a directional transience condition, such as Sznitman's condition (T) or the stronger (T') in a direction l, or a simpler ballisticity/non-nestling condition, one constructs regeneration times tau_1 < tau_2 < ... at which the walk achieves a new running maximum in direction l and never backtracks below that level afterward. Under condition (T'), or the weaker (T), the increments (X_{tau_{k+1}} - X_{tau_k}, tau_{k+1} - tau_k), for k >= 1, form an i.i.d. sequence, reducing the walk, which is not itself Markovian once the environment is averaged out, to a genuine i.i.d.-increment structure from which a law of large numbers (a deterministic limiting velocity) follows directly, and, with additional finite-moment control on the regeneration increments, a central limit theorem follows via classical tools for sums of i.i.d. variables. This does not establish the directional transience condition itself, verifying (T) or (T') for a given environment law is typically the hard remaining step; it does not directly give a central limit theorem without separately checking finite second moments of the regeneration increments, which can genuinely fail in slow or near-critical regimes; and it is specific to the static, fixed-in-time environment model. Typical failure: Assuming the regeneration increments automatically have finite variance, and hence a central limit theorem follows, once ballisticity or condition (T') has been established; ballisticity under (T') only guarantees a finite mean regeneration time, and a genuine central limit theorem requires an additional, often delicate, verification of finite second moments, a point on which the Kesten-Kozlov-Spitzer branching-with-migration machinery exists precisely because these moments can fail. Canonical reference: Sznitman and Zerner, 1999, Annals of Probability; Sznitman, 2002, Ecole d'Ete de Probabilites de Saint-Flour, Springer Lecture Notes in Mathematics.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:34:33.543019+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fa18f25af7b7b7bf663f7e66579a87c2a4d4c15e3c11603a7ee5fb076d7082d4","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 19 (The models are EFIIDs) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] All three models alluded to above are EFIIDs.

        Then the infinite-volume Gibbs measure $\mu_{\XY,\beta}^{+1}$
        is an EFIID.
        \item[\emph{\textbf{SWM}}] Consider the SWM in dimension $d\in\Z_{\geq 2}$
        at inverse temperature $\beta\in\R_{\geq 0}$.

    \end{itemize}
    In the case of the Coulomb gas, we are careful not to call this measure a Gibbs measure, as the Hamiltonian of the model is non-local and therefore it is not so clear what it means exactly to be a Gibbs measure.

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T08:26:47.190930+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fa474a8a4624814fe97709dafbef801fb0755ea4276210b20d5a5f868b3d8f3d","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lem 109 (regularity for spatially smoothed coefficients) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] The coefficients from Definition~\ref{d:sp.smooth} are continuously differentiable in the space coordinate, and satisfy the bounds
	\[
	\Big(
	\|\sB^N\|_\infty
    +
    \|\partial_y\sB^N\|_\infty\Big)^2
	+ \max\bigg\{
    \|\tilde{A}\|_\infty
    +\|\partial_y\tilde{A}\|_\infty
    : \tilde{A}\in\{ \sV,\sU,\srrr,\swww\}^N
    \bigg\}
	\le 
	\bigg(\frac{\trK L}{\sep}\bigg)^{O(1)} 
	(\MAX_N)^2\,,
	\]
with $\MAX_N$ as in \eqref{e:MAX.N} and Proposition~\ref{p:Y.kolmogorov}.

\begin{proof}
We continue to use the abbreviations introduced above. To simplify notation, we mostly suppress the dependence on $N$ inside the proof. Consider
	\[
	\sB(t,y)
	=\frac{\overline{\varrho_{D,t}*\sphi}(y)}
		{\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)}
	\equiv \frac{\Num(t,y)}{\Den(t,y)}\,.
	\]
We first aim to lower bound the denominator $\Den$.
Recall from Definition~\ref{d:sp.smooth} that $\sphi$ has support $[-\sep,\sep]^3$, and is $\ge \Omega(1)/\sep^3$ on $[-\sep/2,\sep/2]^3$. 
From the construction of $\vX^\frozen$ and $\vY^\frozen$
(Definitions \ref{d:trunc}--\ref{d:rerand.Ising}), we see that $\varrho_t$ gives measure at least $\Omega( \sep^3 /\trK^{O(1)} )$ to any box of side length $\sep$ contained in $[-2\trK,2\trK]^3$. It follows that, for all $\vy\in[-2\trK+1,2\trK-1]^3$,
	\[
	\varrho_t*\sphi(\vy)
	\ge \int_{[-\sep/2,\sep/2]^3}
		\sphi(\vy-\vx)\,\varrho_t(d\vx)
	\ge \frac{1}{\trK^{O(1)}}\,.
	\]
Integrating over $\vy\in H(y)$ (as defined by \eqref{e:hspace.y}) gives
	\beq
	\Den(t,y)
	= \overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)
	\ge \frac{1}{\trK^{O(1)}}
	\eeq
for all $y\in[-5\trK,5\trK]$. Next note that since particles outside $[-\trK,\trK]^3$ are frozen (see Definition~\ref{d:trunc}), the numerator $\Num(t,y)$ must be zero for $y\notin[-3\trK-1,3\trK+1]$. For $y\in[-3\trK-1,3\trK+1]$, we bound
	\begin{align*}
	|\Num(t,y)|
	&=\Big|\overline{\varrho_{D,t}*\sphi}(y)\Big|
	=\bigg| \int_{H(y)}
	\int_{\R^3} \sphi(\vy-\vx)B(t,\vx)\,\varrho_t(d\vx) \,d\vy\bigg|\\
	&=\bigg| \int_{\R^3}
	B(t,\vx) \overline{\sphi}(y-(\underline{1},\vx))\,\varrho_t(d\vx)\bigg|
	\le \|\overline{\sphi}\|_\infty \cdot \int_{\R^3}
	|B(t,\vx)|\,\varrho_t(d\vx)
	\le  \bigg(\frac{L}
		{\sep}\bigg)^{O(1)}
		\MAX_N\,,
	\end{align*}
where the last step uses the quenched moment bound on $\bbb$ from Lemma~\ref{l:barD.I.second.quenched}, together with the bound $(p^N)' \le  L^2$ from \eqref{e:sdelimits.pprime}. Combining with \eqref{e:denominator.lbd} gives
	\[\|\sB\|_\infty 
	\le \bigg(\frac{\trK L}
		{\sep}
		\bigg)^{O(1)}
		\MAX_N\,.
	\]
We can also apply \eqref{e:denominator.lbd} to obtain
	\beq
	\Big|\partial_y \tilde{B}(t,y)\Big|
	\le \trK^{O(1)}
	\bigg|
	\frac{\partial}{\partial y} \Num(t,y)
	- \tilde{B}(t,y)
	\frac{\partial}{\partial y} \Den(t,y)
	\bigg|\,.\eeq
The first term on the right-hand side of \eqref{e:sB.quotient.rule} can be bounded by
	\begin{align*}
	\bigg|\frac{\partial}{\partial y} \Num(t,y)\bigg|
	&=\bigg|\frac{\partial}{\partial y}
	\overline{\varrho_{D,t}*\sphi}(y)\bigg|
	=\bigg| 
	\int_{\R^3} B(t,\vx)
	\overline{\sphi}' (y-(\vec{1},\vx))
	\,\varrho_t(d\vx)
	\bigg|\\
	&\le
	\|\overline{\sphi}' \|_\infty
	\int_{\R^3} | B(t,\vx) | \,\varrho_t(d\vx)
	\le \bigg(\frac{L}
		{\sep}\bigg)^{O(1)} \MAX_N\,.
	\end{align*}
The second term on the right-hand side of \eqref{e:sB.quotient.rule} can be controlled using the preceding bound on $\tilde{B}$, together with a similar  calculation as above:
	\[
	\bigg|\frac{\partial}{\partial y}
		\Den(t,y) \bigg|
	=\bigg|\frac{\partial}{\partial y}
	\overline{\varrho_t*\sphi}(y)\bigg|
	\le  \| \overline{\sphi}' \|_\infty \cdot
	\int_{\R^3} \varrho_t(d\vx)
	\le \frac{1}{\sep^{O(1)} }\,.
	\]
Combining the above gives the claimed bound on $\partial_y \sB$.
The bounds on $\sV$, $\sU$, $\srrr$, and $\swww$ follow by the same argument, using the quenched moment bounds from Lemma~\ref{l:tQ.first.quenched}.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:27:14.769809+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fa48243c80ce4e69e562c8c331adb1f868ff460ad305090003ca693b3b649371","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.22693, 'Uniformity of extremal behaviour along geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] Fix $\gamma \in (0,2)$ and $\alpha \in [-2,2]$, and let $h$ be a whole-plane GFF. 
Then, there exist deterministic constants $\Delta^{\mathrm{Euc}}, \Delta_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{Euc}}, \Delta_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{LQG}}, \chi, \chi', \alpha_{\mathrm{min}}$, and $\alpha_{\mathrm{max}}$, such that the following holds almost surely. For any $D_h$-geodesic $P\colon [0,T]\rightarrow \CC$ parametrised by $D_h$-length and any $[s,t]\subseteq (0,T)$, we have

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:54:34.576894+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fa483578692ebb64fd65c90d7dd282dc4a175130c5fa82aad1ee8b96558013a2","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop 10 of arXiv:2606.14812, 'Joint convergence in Wiener chaos via transport hierarchy and Malliavin covariances'] Consider two integers $p, q\geq 2$ and let
		\[
		X_N = I_p(f_N), \qquad Y_N = I_q(g_N),
		\]
		where $f_N\in H^{\odot p}$, $g_N\in H^{\odot q}$, and assume that $X_N$ 
		satisfies \eqref{c1} and $Y_N$ is bounded in $L^2(\Omega)$. Write 
		$q = ap + r'$ with $a\geq 1$ and $0\leq r' < p$. For $r\geq 1$, let 
		$Y_{r,N}$ be given by \eqref{yr}. Then the following hold.
		
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item For every integer $r\geq 1$ with $rp\leq q$,
			\begin{equation}
				Y_{r,N} = C_{r,p,q}\,
				I_{q-rp}\!\left(f_N\widetilde\otimes_p^{(r)} g_N\right)
				+ R_{r,N},
			\end{equation}
			where $f_N\widetilde\otimes_p^{(r)} g_N$ denotes the 
			$r$-fold iterated contraction of $f_N$ with $g_N$, 
			defined recursively by $f_N\widetilde\otimes_p^{(1)} g_N 
			= f_N\widetilde\otimes_p g_N\in H^{\odot(q-p)}$ and
			\begin{equation*}
				f_N\widetilde\otimes_p^{(r)} g_N 
				:= f_N\widetilde\otimes_p 
				\left(f_N\widetilde\otimes_p^{(r-1)} g_N\right)
				\in H^{\odot(q-rp)},
				\quad r=2,\ldots,a,
			\end{equation*}
			i.e.\ at each step the $p$ variables of $f_N$ are 
			fully contracted with $p$ of the remaining variables 
			of the kernel from the previous step. Also,  $C_{r,p,q} = (p!)^r\frac{q!}{(q-rp)!}$ and 
			$R_{r,N}\to 0$ in $L^2(\Omega)$ as $N\to\infty$.
			
			\item \textbf{Non-critical case} $ap < q < (a+1)p$: 
			\begin{equation}
				Y_{a+1,N} \to _{N \to \infty}0 \quad \text{in } L^2(\Omega).
			\end{equation}
			
			\item \textbf{Critical case} $q = ap$: taking $r=a$ in \eqref{14m-2b} gives
			\begin{equation*}
				Y_{a,N} - \mathbf{E}[Y_{a,N}] \to  _{N \to \infty}0 \quad \text{in } L^2(\Omega).
			\end{equation*}
			In particular, if $\mathbf{E}[Y_{a,N}]\to _{N \to \infty}\rho_a$ for some $\rho_a\in\mathbb{R}$, 
			then $Y_{a,N}\to _{N \to \infty}\rho_a$ in $L^2(\Omega)$. Moreover,
			\begin{equation}
				Y_{a+1,N} \to_{N \to \infty}  0 \quad \text{in } L^2(\Omega).
			\end{equation}
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["G = PSL(2,R) and Gamma < G is discrete with finite covolume (a lattice)","m is the G-invariant probability measure on Gamma\\G","the flow is right translation by the one-parameter unipotent subgroup u_t","no cocompactness, torsion freeness or arithmeticity is assumed for (1)-(3); cocompactness is needed only for minimality and unique ergodicity, which are NOT claimed here","mixing is understood with respect to the normalised invariant probability measure"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T19:20:07.090417+00:00","domain":"homogeneous dynamics, unipotent flows, mixing","id":"claim_fa58123752f92f96ece864fcf1e4a8975e90b2041eda5d1899f3190c01222269","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let G = PSL(2,R) and let Gamma be a LATTICE in G: a discrete subgroup such that the quotient M = Gamma\\G carries a G-invariant Borel probability measure m (finite covolume, normalised). Gamma is not assumed torsion free, cocompact, or arithmetic. For real t let u_t denote the image in G of the unipotent matrix with rows (1, t) and (0, 1), and define the horocycle flow on M by h_t(Gamma g) = Gamma g u_t. Then: (1) each h_t preserves m; (2) HEDLUND: the flow is ergodic with respect to m; (3) PARRY: the flow is strongly mixing, that is for all F1, F2 in L^2(M, m) the inner product of F1 composed with h_t against F2 converges, as |t| -> infinity, to the product of the integral of F1 and the conjugate of the integral of F2; equivalently m(A intersect h_{-t}B) -> m(A) m(B) for all Borel A, B. Moreover the flow is mixing of all orders. WHERE THE HYPOTHESES BITE: (i) finite covolume is essential. Mixing as stated is a statement about a probability measure; for a discrete subgroup of infinite covolume the correct statements concern Burger-Roblin and Patterson-Sullivan measures and carry extra hypotheses (for instance on the critical exponent), so (3) must not be quoted there. (ii) Ergodicity and mixing hold for EVERY lattice, but MINIMALITY (every orbit dense), Hedlund's other theorem, needs Gamma cocompact: a noncompact finite-volume quotient has closed horocycle orbits encircling each cusp, so the flow there is mixing yet neither minimal nor uniquely ergodic. Confusing the two Hedlund statements is the usual error. (iii) The result concerns the unipotent direction. The geodesic flow a_s is also mixing but has positive entropy and a huge simplex of invariant measures, whereas the horocycle flow has zero entropy and (in the cocompact case) is uniquely ergodic; rigidity statements do not transfer between them. (iv) Nothing here gives a RATE; quantitative mixing needs a spectral gap input and the rate depends on the lattice.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:26:52.675062+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fa97832749f5ba14f0a0a6e7f2aefbd508f15a7765b318b44d9e160b783f671e","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 7 of arXiv:2609.03750, '\bf Pullback Measure Attractors, Zero-Noise Limits, and Moderate Deviations for 2D Stochas'] Let
		\[

		\]

		\[
		S(\tau,\tau)=I,\qquad

		\quad t\geq s\geq\tau.
		\]
		A family
		$\mathscr A=\{\mathscr A(\tau):\tau\in\mathbb R\}
		\in\mathfrak D$
		is called a $\mathfrak D$-pullback measure attractor for $S$ if:

			$(\mathcal P(H),d_{\mathcal P(H)})$;

			\[

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:25:06.135376+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fa9a803be9844db7375f91bafd050fc295e46c3963d12076c7e010859ee4da39","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Thm 2 of arXiv:2608.22514, 'Diffusion limits of cyclic finite-velocity random motions\\ along vector fields'] Suppose that assumptions
$\mathbf{A}_V$,

$\mathbf{A}_{V,\mu}$ and
$\mathbf{A}_\varkappa$ hold. Then, for any initial values $y\in\bR^d$ and $\iota\in \{1,\dots,p\}$,
the gliding evolutions $\{Y^{\e,\delta}\}$ converge weakly in $C(\bR_+,\bR^d)$
to a diffusion $Y$ starting at $y$ with the generator
\ba

Bf
&=\frac{\varkappa^2}{2\mu} \sum_{i}  \sigma_{i}^2  \langle \nabla^2 f V_i ,V_i\rangle

The diffusion $Y$ is a solution to an It\^o-SDE

\ea
where $W^1,\dots,W^p$ are independent standard one-dimensional Brownian motions.
The SDE \eqref{e:SDEY} can be rewritten in the Stratonovich form
as
\ba

\di Y_t= \frac{\varkappa}{\sqrt\mu}  \sum_{i} \sigma_{i} V_i(Y_t)\circ\di W^i_t

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:29:23.333195+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_faa4e138737d200615f316a29936e4a269dc95da3217fcdb0ba1a9544e94cd48","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 (BESQ flow; {\cite[Definition 3.3) of arXiv:2512.05466, 'Stochastic Flows and Marked Stable Processes'] {aidekon2023stochastic}, \cite[Definition 2.2]{AWYskew}}]

Let $\delta \in \bR$ and ${\mathcal W}$ be a white noise on $\bR_+\times \bR$.  We call ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow  driven by ${\mathcal W}$ a collection ${\mathcal S}$ of continuous processes $({\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)_{r\in \bR,a\ge 0}$ such that: 
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item
for each $(a,r)\in \bR_+\times \bR$, the process $({\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)$ is almost surely the unique strong solution of the following SDE  
\begin{equation}
{\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a) = 
a + 2 \int_r^x  {\mathcal W}([0,{\mathcal S}_{r,s}(a)], \dd s) + 
\delta (x-r),\, x\ge r
\end{equation}
where, if $\delta\le 0$, the process is absorbed when hitting $0$.
 \item Almost surely,
 \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
 \item for all $r\in \bR$ and $a\ge 0$, $ {\mathcal S}_{r,r}(a)=a$,
 \item for all $r\le x$, $a\mapsto  {\mathcal S}_{r,x}(a)$ is c\`adl\`ag,
 \item (Perfect flow property) for any $r\le x \le y$ and $a\ge 0$, $\cS_{r,y}(a)=\cS_{x,y}\circ \cS_{r,x}(a)$. 
\end{enumerate} 
\end{enumerate}

We call killed ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow driven by $\cW$ the flow obtained from the ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow by absorbing at $0$ the flow line $\cS_{r,\cdot}(a)$ at time $\inf\{x>r\,:\,\cS_{r,x}(a)=0\}$. 

We call general ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow  a  ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow or a  killed ${\rm BESQ}^\delta$ flow.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:06:21.667881+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_faa9705b72fd293bd94ec319bd953d1b7fca22e4fb16d94f7e81c486d6f2200b","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.20838, 'Long-memory Markov chains with power-law intensities'] Let $\{ \varepsilon_n \}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed random variables. 
	Suppose there exists a stochastic process $\{ \mathbf{X}_n \}$ taking values in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for some $d \ge 1$, which governs the distribution of inter-arrival times $\{ \tau_n \}$.
	Let \(\Phi(t,\mathbf{x})\) be a function defined for \(t \ge 0\) and \(\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^d\), and assume that \(\Phi(\cdot,\mathbf{x})\) is strictly increasing in \(t\) for each fixed \(\mathbf{x}\).
	The inter-arrival time \(\tau_n\) is related to \(\varepsilon_n\) by
	\begin{equation}
		\varepsilon_n = \Phi(\tau_n, \mathbf{X}_{n-1}) 
		\qquad \text{equivalently,} \qquad
		\tau_n = \Phi^{-1}(\varepsilon_n, \mathbf{X}_{n-1}) ,
		
	\end{equation}
	where the inverse is taken with respect to $t$, holding $\mathbf{x}$ fixed.
	The process $\mathbf{X}_n$ evolves according to an update function $\Psi$ such that
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbf{X}_n = \Psi(\mathbf{X}_{n-1}, \tau_n). 
	\end{equation}
	The associated point process \(N\) on \(\mathbb{R}^+\) is defined by
	\[
	N = \sum_{n \in \mathbb N} \delta_{T_n}, 
	\qquad  \qquad 
	T_n = \sum_{i=1}^n \tau_i
	\]
	where \(\delta_t\) denotes the Dirac measure at \(t\).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["H_k the Sylvester Hadamard matrix of order 2^k, disc(A) = min over sign vectors x of ||A x||_inf"],"created_at":"2026-09-24T23:46:59.335012+00:00","domain":"combinatorics/Boolean functions","id":"claim_face5f144efa4b4e9a635b179d81577f","kind":"counterexample","schema_version":1,"statement":"Conjecture 13 of the Randomstrasse 2024 problem list asks whether the Sylvester Hadamard matrix H_k of order 2^k has discrepancy disc(H_k) = sqrt(2) sqrt(2^k) for odd k, where disc(A) = min over sign vectors x of the sup-norm of Ax. In plain terms: take the 2^k x 2^k matrix of plus and minus ones whose entry in row a and column u is (-1) to the mod-2 dot product of the k-bit strings a and u, and ask for the smallest possible largest absolute entry of the product Hx over sign vectors x. Indexing H_k by (-1)^{a.u} and reading x as the +-1 truth table of a Boolean function f on k variables, H_k x is the Walsh transform W_f, so disc(H_k) = min_f max_a |W_f(a)| = 2^k - 2 NL_max(k), where NL_max(k) is the largest nonlinearity of a Boolean function on k variables (the covering radius of the Reed-Muller code RM(1, k)). The conjectured value is exactly the bent-concatenation bound NL = 2^{k-1} - 2^{(k-1)/2}, which is beaten for odd k = 15 (Patterson and Wiedemann, 1983) and for every odd k > 7 (Kavut, Maitra and Yucel, 2006), and is optimal for k <= 7. So the conjecture holds exactly for k in {1, 3, 5, 7} and fails for every odd k >= 9. The numbers: for k <= 7 the maximum nonlinearity equals the bent-concatenation value (the covering radius of RM(1,5) is 12, Berlekamp and Welch 1972; of RM(1,7) is 56, Mykkeltveit 1980; k = 1, 3 by hand); for k = 9 functions of nonlinearity 242 exist (Kavut, Maitra and Yucel 2006), so disc(H_9) <= 512 - 484 = 28 < 32; for every odd k = 9 + 2j the direct sum of such a function with a bent function on 2j variables has largest Walsh coefficient 28 * 2^j, below 32 * 2^j, since the Walsh spectrum of a direct sum is the product; and Patterson and Wiedemann's nonlinearity 16276 on 15 variables gives disc(H_15) <= 216 < 256.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["the point process is exactly determinantal, or Pfaffian with the analogous but distinct formula, with a well-defined correlation kernel K satisfying the standard positivity and boundedness conditions","the conditioning event is of the specific form covered by the Schur-complement formula, i.e. an exact configuration on a subset, or the corresponding L-ensemble conditioning","invertibility, or a well-defined limiting or pseudo-inverse procedure, for the relevant diagonal block appearing in the formula, e.g. K_AA - I","the block partition A, B is taken with respect to the same index set on which K is originally defined"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.998694+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_faf3e83a28894a41c1931704cf7a671a579f690c334933aa41076761cbab8d22","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For a determinantal point process with correlation kernel K, Hermitian and satisfying 0<=K<=I in the discrete finite-space setting, the conditional law of the process restricted to a subset given the exact configuration on the complementary subset is again determinantal, with a kernel given by a Schur-complement formula. Partitioning the index set into A, the observed subset, and B, the remaining subset, and writing K in block form with entries K_AA, K_AB, K_BA, K_BB, the conditional kernel on B given the exact points observed in A is expressed via a Schur-complement expression such as K_BB - K_BA (K_AA - I)^{-1} K_AB, with the precise form depending on the convention used (correlation kernel versus L-ensemble) and on whether one conditions on points being present or absent in A. This identity is the fundamental tool for analyzing conditioning, dynamics, and Gibbs-type properties of determinantal processes, including eigenvalues of random matrices, non-intersecting paths, discrete orthogonal polynomial ensembles, and, via the transfer-current theorem, uniform spanning trees, reducing conditional analysis to linear algebra on the kernel matrix. It does not apply outside the determinantal class of point processes, or its Pfaffian analogue for orthogonal and symplectic ensembles, which has a related but distinct formula, and the exact form of the Schur complement depends sensitively on the specific conditioning event and on invertibility of the relevant block, which can fail or require a pseudo-inverse or limiting argument at special parameter values. Typical failure: Applying a Schur-complement conditional-kernel formula derived under one convention, such as conditioning an L-ensemble on a fixed exact sample, to a different conditioning question, such as conditioning on a sub-event like at least one point in a region, or mixing up the correlation-kernel and L-ensemble conventions, without re-deriving the correct formula; determinantal-process conditioning identities are convention-sensitive, and mixing them up produces a kernel that still looks plausible, expressed via some Schur complement, but does not correctly describe the actual conditional process. Canonical reference: Shirai and Takahashi, 2003, Journal of Functional Analysis; Borodin and Rains, 2005, Journal of Statistical Physics; Lyons, 2003, Annals of Probability.","status":"unverified"}

Moreover, the limit process is such that

	Let $Z\subset \R^2$ denote the critical set of~$f$
	(i.e. the set of all points where $f$ is not differentiable, or has $\nabla f = 0$).
	Let $E^*$ be the union of all connected components of the level sets

	\end{equation*}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["f is Lebesgue integrable on R^d","convention: kernel e^{-2 pi i x.xi} with no normalizing constant"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:39.261959+00:00","domain":"harmonic analysis on Euclidean space","id":"claim_fb60e476216b9503fe6cf25758a518637c753a94a69a4d29f3d7163257a33360","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"For $f \\in L^1(\\mathbb{R}^d)$ define $\\hat f(\\xi) = \\int_{\\mathbb{R}^d} f(x) e^{-2\\pi i x\\cdot\\xi}\\,dx$ for every $\\xi \\in \\mathbb{R}^d$; the integral converges absolutely for every $\\xi$. The inverse transform of $g\\in L^1$ is $\\check g(x)=\\int g(\\xi)e^{2\\pi i x\\cdot\\xi}\\,d\\xi$. With this convention Plancherel reads $\\|\\hat f\\|_2=\\|f\\|_2$. Convention warning: texts using $\\int f(x)e^{-ix\\cdot\\xi}dx$ have inversion with a factor $(2\\pi)^{-d}$ and $\\|\\hat f\\|_2=(2\\pi)^{d/2}\\|f\\|_2$; the unitary convention puts $(2\\pi)^{-d/2}$ in front of both. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T15:07:17.278359+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fb7ad4a12802669de55b7a8d7b5b38bb5858572b45b895048d0db220509d3d9a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:averaging-close of arXiv:2603.14906, 'Four Levels of Thermodynamic Convergence of Singularly Perturbed Markov Semigroups'] Let $E=\mathbb{R}^{d_x}\times\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$ and let
\[

\]
be a probability measure on $E$, where $V\in C^1(E)$.
Let $a_2:E\to\mathbb{R}^{d_y\times d_y}$ be measurable and symmetric, and assume that $a_2$ is locally bounded and uniformly elliptic on compact sets (as in (sec:setting of the paper)). Define the pre-form on $L^2(\Pi)$ with core $\mathcal D_0:=C_c^\infty(E)$ by

$(\mathcal E_y,\mathcal D(\mathcal E_y))$ and equip $\mathcal D(\mathcal E_y)$ with the norm

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T22:11:11.696375+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fb7ce0904ba6cc883fce5c582837e5c506adcefa9c9da36941d7a705dd34d6b5","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma lem:centers of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Let $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ be nonzero and nonnegative, and set
$\kappa:=\|f\|_1$.  Then $\mathsf C(f)$ is nonempty and compact, and
$\mathcal A(f)<2\kappa$.  Moreover, the following statements hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item if $\operatorname{supp}f^*\subset B_r(\mathbf0)$ for some $r>0$,
then every $\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(f)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \int_{\mathbb R^2\setminus B_r(\mathbf b)}f
  \,\mathrm d\mathbf x
  \leq\frac12\mathcal A(f);
\end{equation}
\item if, for some $r,s>0$ and $\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^2$,
\[
  \operatorname{supp}f^*\subset B_r(\mathbf0),
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}f\subset B_s(\mathbf a),
\]
then
\begin{equation}
  |\mathbf b-\mathbf a|\leq r+s
  \qquad(\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(f));
\end{equation}
moreover, the mass center $\mathbf X_f$ defined by (equation eq:mass-center of the paper) satisfies
\begin{equation}
  |\mathbf b-\mathbf X_f|
  \leq\frac{r+2s}{\kappa}\mathcal A(f)
  \qquad(\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(f));
\end{equation}
\item if $\operatorname{supp}f^*\subset B_r(\mathbf0)$ for some $r>0$
and $\mathcal A(f)<\kappa$, then
\begin{equation}
  \operatorname{diam}\mathsf C(f)\leq2r;
\end{equation}
\item for any nonzero, nonnegative $f,g\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$,
\[
  |\mathcal A(f)-\mathcal A(g)|\leq2\|f-g\|_1;
\]
\item the set-valued map $f\mapsto\mathsf C(f)$ has a closed graph with respect
to strong $L^1$ convergence: if $f_n,f\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ are nonzero and
nonnegative, then
\[
  f_n\to f\ \text{in }L^1(\mathbb R^2),\qquad
  \mathbf b_n\to\mathbf b\ \text{in }\mathbb R^2,\qquad
  \mathbf b_n\in\mathsf C(f_n)
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathbf b\in\mathsf C(f);
\]
\item the set-valued map $f\mapsto\mathsf C(f)$ is upper semicontinuous\footnote{See
[AubinFrankowska2009] for this standard definition.} with
respect to strong $L^1$ convergence: for every nonzero, nonnegative
$f\in L^1(\mathbb R^2)$ and every open set $O\subset\mathbb R^2$ with
$\mathsf C(f)\subset O$, there exists $\delta>0$ such that
\[
  g\in L^1(\mathbb R^2),\quad g\geq0,\quad g\not\equiv0,\quad
  \|g-f\|_1<\delta
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \mathsf C(g)\subset O.
\]
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["two-dimensional planar lattice model satisfying the FKG inequality","translation invariance and, in the classical gluing constructions, reflection symmetry of the lattice","an a priori lower bound on square-crossing probabilities, which is a hypothesis to be separately established, not a free consequence of RSW","independence, or at least positive association, of the underlying edge or site variables"],"created_at":"2026-09-07T08:44:20.974286+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fb8fff362c8249e98704b89baabf231efeaf842e818303da3b033c4ea1e6cfba","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). In two-dimensional critical or near-critical percolation, RSW theory states that if crossing probabilities of n x n squares are uniformly bounded away from 0 as n grows, then crossing probabilities of rho n x n rectangles, for any fixed aspect ratio rho, are also uniformly bounded away from 0 (and from 1) by a constant depending on rho but not on n. The classical proof glues together several square-crossing events using the FKG inequality and translation and reflection symmetry of the lattice. RSW estimates are the essential multi-scale input for proving arm-exponent bounds, conformal-invariance-adjacent results, and, via the Duminil-Copin-Tassion approach, for establishing sharpness of the phase transition without relying on exact self-duality. RSW does not by itself prove existence of a scaling limit as n -> infinity, does not give the exact value of any crossing probability, only two-sided bounds; and the classical form required exact self-duality (p=1/2 on the square lattice), so extending the theory to general planar lattices or to p != 1/2 required a genuinely new, duality-free argument (Tassion, 2016). Typical failure: Assuming that RSW-type bounded-away-from-0/1 crossing estimates transfer automatically to a new planar model merely because it is monotone and planar; RSW requires either exact self-duality or the more robust but still nontrivial Tassion-style construction, and models without FKG, or with strong enough long-range dependence, can fail to admit the needed gluing arguments even though they look superficially similar to Bernoulli percolation. Canonical reference: Russo, 1978, Zeitschrift fur Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und verwandte Gebiete; Seymour and Welsh, 1978, Annals of Discrete Mathematics; Tassion, 2016, Probability Theory and Related Fields.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:04:39.235504+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fb9088199ad67aea9aba7c58a198461df85cba2f5705f8c3799d318efcf3df86","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Corollary 47 (Normal root with a Gaussian tangential fibre) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let \(B\in\Sym_d(R_0)\) be invertible. For a top form,

 \left[

Thus normal restriction at the connected root and complete tangential Wick

\end{equation}
Hence a connected root produces exactly one simple pole and its residue is

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T20:47:22.240140+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fb9862a2488133bba57e0be0d2081c6835a6c395bc2605d27905391c44db74af","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2605.25715, '2605.25715'] Let $(L^{A,G},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ be given as in \eqref{LAG}, where $A$ is symmetric and positive definite and $G$ is arbitrary. $$
Then $S$ is negative definite and $\mu=e^{\langle x, Sx\rangle}\text{d}x$ is the unique infinitesimally invariant measure for $(L^{A,G},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ and the unique (finite) invariant measure for the semigroup associated to the closed extension of $(L^{A,G},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ and its associated stochastic process, both constructed in \cite{LST22}. $$
Sx+(G-AS)x
$$
is the unique SOHHD of $\tilde Gx$, and $(L^{A,G},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ and $(L^{\widetilde{G}},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ have the same unique (finite) infinitesimally invariant measure $\mu$.
\item[(iii)] Suppose that the semigroup $(T_t)_{t>0}$ associated to the closed extension of $(L^{A,G},C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ or its associated stochastic process, both constructed in \cite{LST22}, admit a finite invariant measure. {"assumptions":["Ω bounded open with Lipschitz boundary, n ≥ 2","1 ≤ p < ∞ for existence, boundedness and kernel; 1 < p < ∞ for the fractional-space range description","Green's identity form: u ∈ H^2(Ω), v ∈ H^1(Ω)"],"created_at":"2026-09-13T01:59:57.492614+00:00","domain":"Sobolev spaces, boundary traces, elliptic boundary value problems","id":"claim_fb9c6a675246add69d2d408b990ef27f4904b933fa93e1e739f05b2304fd2786","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let Ω ⊂ R^n (n ≥ 2) be a bounded open set with Lipschitz boundary, dS the surface measure and ν the outward unit normal (defined dS-a.e.), and let 1 ≤ p < ∞.

(1) Existence and boundedness. There is a unique bounded linear operator T : W^{1,p}(Ω) → L^p(∂Ω, dS) such that Tu = u|_{∂Ω} for every u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω) ∩ C(Ω̄). Tu is the trace of u, and ||Tu||_{L^p(∂Ω)} ≤ C(Ω, p) ||u||_{W^{1,p}(Ω)}.

(2) Kernel. ker T = W^{1,p}_0(Ω), the closure of C_c^∞(Ω) in W^{1,p}(Ω). A W^{1,p} function vanishes on ∂Ω in the trace sense exactly when it is a W^{1,p}-limit of compactly supported smooth functions.

(3) Range (Gagliardo). For 1 < p < ∞ the range of T is exactly the fractional Sobolev space W^{1−1/p, p}(∂Ω), and T has a bounded linear right inverse W^{1−1/p, p}(∂Ω) → W^{1,p}(Ω). In particular T : H^1(Ω) → H^{1/2}(∂Ω) is bounded and onto, and every g ∈ H^{1/2}(∂Ω) has an extension u ∈ H^1(Ω) with Tu = g and ||u||_{H^1(Ω)} ≤ C ||g||_{H^{1/2}(∂Ω)}. For p = 1 the range is all of L^1(∂Ω). Since H^{1/2}(∂Ω) ↪ L^2(∂Ω) is compact, T : H^1(Ω) → L^2(∂Ω) is a compact operator.

(4) Integration by parts with traces. For u ∈ W^{1,p}(Ω), v ∈ W^{1,p'}(Ω) with 1/p + 1/p' = 1 (p' = ∞ for p = 1) and each i,
   ∫_Ω u ∂_i v dx + ∫_Ω v ∂_i u dx = ∫_∂Ω (Tu)(Tv) ν_i dS.
Hence for u ∈ H^2(Ω), v ∈ H^1(Ω) Green's first identity ∫_Ω ∇u·∇v dx + ∫_Ω (Δu) v dx = ∫_∂Ω (∂_ν u)(Tv) dS holds with ∂_ν u := ν · T(∇u) ∈ L^2(∂Ω), and for u ∈ H^1_0(Ω) all boundary terms vanish.

Where it fails. There is no trace operator on L^p(Ω): ∂Ω has Lebesgue measure zero, an L^p class has no boundary values, and an estimate ||Tu||_{L^p(∂Ω)} ≤ C||u||_{L^p(Ω)} is false (the full W^{1,p} norm is needed). For p > 1 the range is NOT L^p(∂Ω): a general g ∈ L^2(∂Ω) has no H^1(Ω) extension. The kernel and range statements use the Lipschitz boundary (a segment / extension property); for domains with cracks, slits or cusps the boundary is not Lipschitz and these statements need modification (a crack has two sides with two different traces). The trace of ∇u exists for u ∈ H^2(Ω), not for a general u ∈ H^1(Ω), so ∂_ν u is not defined in L^2(∂Ω) for arbitrary H^1 functions.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T14:01:56.364915+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fbb58ff759c3c23f495f87c097e34e0a87e51a8497070adbb0d0c229ce87a7eb","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:HNabelian of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] Let $\cA$ be an abelian category with central charge $Z$.
A filtration
\[
0=E_0\subset E_1\subset E_2\subset\ldots\subset E_n=E
\]
of an object $E\in\cA$ is a \textbf{Harder--Narasimhan (HN) filtration} if $A_i\coloneqq E_i/E_{i-1}$ is non-zero and semistable for $i=1,\ldots,n$ with $\phi(A_1)>\phi(A_2)>\ldots>\phi(A_n)$.

The central charge $Z$ has the \textbf{Harder--Narasimhan (HN) property} if every object in $\cA$ has a Harder--Narasimhan filtration.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:57:59.861947+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fbd5718058d1f0cb264c841ba513e9a8e94847a5b889598c36ff99354efc8134","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition def:osi of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] {CamanoEtAl2025}}]

Fix integers $r \le k \le n$ and a parameter $\alpha \in (0,1]$. A random  $n\times k$ matrix $S$
is \emph{$(r,\alpha)$-OSI} if it satisfies the following two conditions:
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(1)] \emph{Isotropy:} for every vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$,
    \[
        \mathbb{E} \|S^\top x\|_2^2 = \|x\|_2^2.
    \]
    \item[(2)] \emph{Injectivity:} for every fixed $r$-dimensional subspace $V \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, with probability at least $9/10$,
    \[
        \alpha \|x\|_2^2 \le \|S^\top x\|_2^2

    \]
\end{itemize}
The probability $9/10$ in the second condition
can be replaced with another number close to one.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:51:11.954305+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fbda79203ede6d57ec8d3728064ded883d9621c89fa12574c9dcd8f137c061bc","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 17 (Vanishing diagonal regularization) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Let \(\widetilde H\) be a bounded centered array with zero diagonal and an
exactly stochastic, uniformly flat off-diagonal variance matrix
\(\widetilde S\).  Let \(\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_N\) be independent, centered,
variance-one, uniformly bounded random variables, independent of
\(\widetilde H\).  For fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\), set
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde H^{(\eta)}_{ij}
 :=\sqrt{1-\eta/N}\,\widetilde H_{ij}\quad(i\ne j),
 \qquad
 \widetilde H^{(\eta)}_{ii}:=\sqrt{\eta/N}\,\chi_i.
\end{equation}
Then the variance matrix of \(\widetilde H^{(\eta)}\) is exactly stochastic
and satisfies the uniform lower and upper bounds required by the
generalized-Wigner theorem, with constants allowed to depend on \(\eta\).
For every finite family of functions analytic near \(\Gamma\),
\begin{align}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\left|
 \E\Tr\varphi(\widetilde H^{(\eta)})
 -\E\Tr\varphi(\widetilde H)
 \right|&\le C_{\varphi,\Gamma}\eta,
 \\
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}\Var\!\left(
 \Tr\varphi(\widetilde H^{(\eta)})
 -\Tr\varphi(\widetilde H)
 \right)&\le C_{\varphi,\Gamma}\eta.
 
\end{align}
Moreover, the Li--Xu expectation and covariance formulas converge to their flat
zero-diagonal versions in the order \(N\to\infty\), then
\(\eta\downarrow0\).  Consequently the joint CLT for
\(\widetilde H^{(\eta)}\) transfers to \(\widetilde H\).","status":"unverified"}

Using the statistics $S_{00}(A)$ and $S_{rs}(A,U)$ defined in Section 2.4, fix target moments $m_{00}\\in\\mathbb{R}$ and $(m_{rs})_{(r,s)\\in\\mathcal{I}}$ and define $\\mathcal{Q}(m):=\\Bigl\\{Q\\text{ pmf on }\\Omega:\\;\\mathbb{E}_{Q}[S_{00}(A)]=m_{00},\\;\\mathbb{E}_{Q}[S_{rs}(A,U)]=m_{rs}\\ \\ \\forall(r,s)\\in\\mathcal{I}\\Bigr\\}.$ Assume $\\mathcal{Q}(m)\\neq\\varnothing$. {"assumptions":["driftless subordinator, Levy measure nu = sum_{m>=1} a_m delta_{x_m}","x_m = 4^{-m^2}, a_m = 2^{-m} 4^{m^2}"],"created_at":"2026-09-24T23:46:59.329215+00:00","domain":"probability/Levy processes","id":"claim_fc2810725f4f4b23a924b0d3f7cc75c4","kind":"counterexample","schema_version":1,"statement":"Question 5 of Hu and Sun's survey on Hunt's hypothesis (H) (arXiv:1908.06825) asks whether every pure-jump subordinator with infinite Levy measure satisfies (H). The classical sufficient conditions bound Im psi by a multiple of 1 + Re psi; the oldest, Kanda-Forst, asks |Im psi(z)| <= M (1 + Re psi(z)) for all z. The driftless subordinator with Levy measure nu = sum_{m>=1} a_m delta_{x_m}, x_m = 4^{-m^2}, a_m = 2^{-m} 4^{m^2}, has sum a_m x_m = 1 and sum a_m = infinity, and along z_m = 1/(m x_m) its exponent psi(z) = int (1 - e^{izx}) nu(dx) satisfies |Im psi(z_m)| / (1 + Re psi(z_m)) = 4m + O(1) (computed at high precision: 23.999 at m = 6, 32.000008 at m = 8), so the Kanda-Forst ratio is unbounded and the classical route to (H) is closed for it. It is not a counterexample to (H): an octave-by-octave estimate of the Kesten-Bretagnolle integral int Re(1/(1 + psi(z))) dz suggests the integral diverges, so points would be polar - a heuristic, not a proof. The example is atomic, outside the survey's type-(alpha, beta) density class, and the survey's Theorem 2.8 and Remark 2.21 anticipate processes of this kind, so it is an explicit witness with a computed rate rather than a new phenomenon.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T12:33:11.982000+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fc28eb85803580647f89a5389a4a780406a83d14e881b69122aaf6a682d3cc56","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition Interval extension of arXiv:2608.19050, 'Online Permutation Embedding: \\ Optimal Stopping and Scaling Laws'] For the remainder of this section, an \textit{interval} is a closed interval with rational endpoints. An \textit{interval enclosure} of a variable $x$ is an interval $[x] := [\underline{x},\overline{x}] \ni x$. Its width is \(\operatorname{wd}([x])=\overline{x}-\underline{x}\). 
    For a real function $F(x_1,\dots,x_m)$, a function $[F]([x_1],\dots,[x_m])$ is said to be an \textit{interval extension} of $F$ if
    \[
        x_j\in[x_j]\quad (1\le j\le m)
        \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
        F(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in [F]([x_1],\dots,[x_m]).
    \]
    Interval extensions also naturally define operations on intervals. For example,
    \[
    I+J=[\underline I+\underline J,\overline I+\overline J],
    \qquad
    I/c=[\underline I/c,\overline I/c]\quad(c>0).
    \]
    We henceforth implicitly assume all interval operations are performed with ``outward'' rounding (lower endpoints rounded downward and upper endpoints upward) to maintain rationality of the endpoints.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:07:48.566545+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fc38cad5596897daed2d2be8002e6feb9e18c80afa03e5ecaecf7e18b92fee3a","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2609.01460, 'On cost-induced Santal\'o-type inequalities \\ in Polish measure spaces'] Let $L\subset M_{n,m}(\R)$ and $K\subset \R^n$ be compact sets of positive volume whose convex hulls contain the (appropriate) origin in their interiors. Then, 
    \[
    \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n](K)^m \leq \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n]((K^{\star,Q})_{\circ,Q})^m 
    \] 
    and 
    \[ 
    \vol[nm](L)\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m \leq \vol[nm]((L_{\circ,Q})^{\star,Q})\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m,
    \]
    with equality only for invariant sets (up to sets of Lebesgue measure zero). 
    
    In particular, the following two statements are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item if $K$ or $K^\circ$, has center of mass at the origin, then
    \[
    \vol[nm](K^{\star,Q})\vol[n](K)^m \leq \vol[nm]((\B)^{\star,Q})\vol[n](\B)^m 
    \]
    with equality if and only if $K=E$ for a centered ellipsoid $E\subset\R^n$ up to removal of null sets; 
    \item  if $L_{\circ,Q}$ or $(L_{\circ,Q})^\circ$ has center of mass at the origin, then
    \[
    \vol[nm](L)\vol[n](L_{\circ,Q})^m \leq \vol[nm]((\B)^{\star,Q})\vol[n](\B)^m
    \]
    with equality if and only if $L=E^{\star,Q}$ for a centered ellipsoid $E\subset \R^n$ up to removal of null sets.
    \end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["mu(Omega) < infinity for the global statement; a set of finite measure for the local statement","f_n measurable, f_n -> f mu-almost everywhere, all functions finite a.e."],"created_at":"2026-09-03T13:20:36.752876+00:00","domain":"measure theory","id":"claim_fc6b659554c68f681ea95004be9535b37b79d34316ba22807d81906efef118ad","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"Egorov's theorem states that on a FINITE measure space, almost everywhere convergence of measurable functions implies almost uniform convergence: for every eps > 0 there is a measurable E with mu(E) < eps such that the convergence is uniform on the complement of E. Finiteness cannot be dropped. On R with Lebesgue measure let f_n = 1_{[n, n+1]}; then f_n -> 0 at every point, but for ANY set E of finite measure the complement meets [n, n+1] for infinitely many n, so sup over the complement of E of |f_n| equals 1 for infinitely many n and the convergence is not uniform off any set of small measure. What survives on a sigma-finite space is the LOCAL statement: for every measurable A with mu(A) < infinity and every eps > 0 there is E contained in A with mu(E) < eps and uniform convergence on A minus E; equivalently, almost everywhere convergence implies almost uniform convergence on each set of finite measure. The converse implication holds in general: almost uniform convergence always implies convergence almost everywhere and in measure, on any measure space. [standard; e.g. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorem 2.33 and Exercise 2.39]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T13:54:12.567809+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fc7bc3237410cbf6b684188ecc94f3fab7661bb876adf67616a89e224e9e86d5","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Prop P:half-space-KPZ-horizon-marginals of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] As $n\to\infty$, the process $R^{(n)}$ has a distributional limit $R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}=\{R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}_i\}_{i=1}^k$, under the uniform-on-compact topology. 
    We can describe the process $R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}$ explicitly as follows.
	
Let $\mathcal{B} = (\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2, \ldots, \mathcal{B}_{2k})$ be $2k$ independent Brownian motions on $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ of diffusivity $1$, with drift $-\gamma_i$ for $\mathcal{B}_i$ and $\gamma_i$ for $\mathcal{B}_{2k+1-i}$, for each $i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket$.
We consider the O'Connell-Yor polymer partition function (see [OYbb]) across $\{\mathcal{B}_i\}_{i=1}^{2k}$, defined as
\[
Z_{\mathcal{B}}(x,i;y,j) = \idotsint_{x=x_i\le \cdots \le x_j \le x_{j+1}=y} \exp\left( \sum_{i'=i}^j \mathcal{B}_{i'}(x_{i'+1})-\mathcal{B}_{i'}(x_{i'}) \right) dx_{i+1}\cdots dx_j,
\]
for any $1\le i \le j \le 2k$, and $0\le x \le y$.

Next, let $\{X(-i, j) : i\in\llbracket1, k \rrbracket, j\in\llbracketi, 2k +1 - i \rrbracket\}$ be an array of inverse gamma random variables, independent of each other and $\mathcal{B}$, satisfying 
\[X(-i, j) \sim \begin{cases}
1 & j =i,\\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(\gamma_j-\gamma_i), \qquad &j\in\llbracket i + 1, k \rrbracket, \\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(-\gamma_i- \gamma_{2k + 1 -j}), \qquad &j\in\llbracketk + 1, 2k - i \rrbracket, \\
\operatorname{Gamma}^{-1}(-\gamma_i+\alpha), \qquad &j =  2k + 1- i.
\end{cases}
\]
Then:
\[
R^{\mathsf{KPZ}}_i(x)=
\begin{cases}
\log\left(\frac{\sum_{i\le \ell \le 2k} \big(\sum_{\pi\in P[i,\ell]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v)\big)Z_{\mathcal{B}}(0,\ell; x, 2k)}{
\sum_{\pi\in P[i,2k]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v) }\right), \qquad & x\ge 0,\\
\log\left(\frac{\sum_{i\le \ell \le 2k} \big(\sum_{\pi\in \hat{P}[i,\ell]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v)\big)Z_{\mathcal{B}}(0,\ell; |x|, 2k)}{
\sum_{\pi\in \hat{P}[i,2k]}\prod_{v\in \pi}X(v) }\right), \qquad & x< 0,
\end{cases}
\]
where $P[i,\ell]$ is the collection of all up-right paths in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ from $(-i,i)$ to $(-1,\ell)$, and  
$\hat{P}[i,\ell]$ is the subset of such paths that intersect $\{(x,x+2k+1): x\in \mathbb{Z}\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-06T03:36:16.740440+00:00","domain":"harvested statement (arXiv 2603.27659, 2026): owner_math","id":"claim_fc8a3d9866d34e7685dd03fa09662144","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 3.11 of arXiv:2603.27659, 'Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory'] Let $m,k,N\\in\\mathbb{N}$, let $\\sigma_{1},\\ldots,\\sigma_{k}\\in\\mathcal{P}^{\\prime}([m])$ be partial permutations, let $A_{1},\\ldots,A_{m}\\in M_{N}(\\mathbb{C})^{\\otimes k}$, let $Y$ be the matrix resulting from the partial trace evaluation $(\\mathrm{Tr}_{\\sigma_{1}}\\otimes\\cdots\\otimes\\mathrm{Tr}_{\\sigma_{k}})(A_{1},\\ldots,A_{m})$, and let $q=\\sum_{j=1}^{k}(m-|D(\\sigma_{j})|)$ with $D(\\sigma_{j})$ the domain of $\\sigma_{j}$, so that $Y$ acts on a space of dimension $N^{q}$. For every $p\\in\\mathbb{N}$, $N^{2pM(\\sigma_{1},\\ldots,\\sigma_{k})+q}\\leq\\max_{\\|A_{1}\\|,\\ldots,\\|A_{m}\\|\\leq 1}\\mathrm{Tr}((YY^{*})^{p})\\leq N^{2pC(\\sigma_{1},\\ldots,\\sigma_{k})+q}.$ (3.2) Moreover, for any configuration $\\bm{\\pi}_{0}$ with $M(\\sigma_{1},\\ldots,\\sigma_{k};\\bm{\\pi}_{0})=M(\\sigma_{1},\\ldots,\\sigma_{k})$, it holds that $Y_{\\bm{\\pi}_{0}}Y_{\\bm{\\pi}_{0}}^{*}=N^{2M(\\sigma_{1},\\ldots,\\sigma_{k})}I_{N^{q}},\\qquad\\mathrm{Tr}((Y_{\\bm{\\pi}_{0}}Y_{\\bm{\\pi}_{0}}^{*})^{p})=N^{2pM(\\sigma_{1},\\ldots,\\sigma_{k})+q}\\quad(p\\in\\mathbb{N}).$ Thus, the tuple $(A_{1},\\ldots,A_{m})=(E_{\\pi_{1}},\\ldots,E_{\\pi_{m}})$, which is independent of $p$, attains every lower moment bound $N^{2pM(\\sigma_{1},\\ldots,\\sigma_{k})+q}$. Here, for the graph $G_{\\sigma_{1},\\ldots,\\sigma_{k}}$ of the permutations, $M(\\sigma_{1},\\ldots,\\sigma_{k})$ is the maximum over blue-edge configurations of the number of directed cycles, and $C(\\sigma_{1},\\ldots,\\sigma_{k})=\\min_{G^{\\prime}}R_{G^{\\prime}}$, the minimum over full simple partial graphs $G^{\\prime}$ (partial graphs keeping every rectangle and containing no directed cycle for any blue-edge configuration) of the number $R_{G^{\\prime}}$ of colored edges removed to obtain $G^{\\prime}$ (Definition 2.1).","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:16:18.663820+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fc99fa27a2cf04e3db73477c60c3ceca1b51c7646fcf9ee065086a3c193e4d27","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $k,d\in\mathbb{N}$ with $d\ge 2$, and let $a,b>0$. {"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T11:40:59.388433+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fcabd78a1b5baf06f82ad667588fc40d3ca83a9d05fd86df92049096bfee8354","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.03968, 'A one-parameter family of local-time conditioned processes : the generalized Brownian burg'] Let $g_0$ be a stretching morphism from some capacity $\lambda$ on an interval $I$ to the constant capacity 1, and fix $x_0\in\overline I$. This means that for $z_0:=g_0(x_0)\in\overline\R$, $g_0$ is a $\mathcal C ^1$-diffeomorphism from $I$ to $\R$ of the form $g_0 : x\in I \mapsto z_0+\int_{x_0}^x {\dd r} / \lambda(r) \in \R $ (understood as a limit when $z_0=\pm\infty$). Let $(D_t)_{0\leq t\leq T}$ be a continuous process with strictly increasing quadratic variation, taking values in $\overline \R = \R\cup\{\pm\infty\}$ (defined up to time-change) and verifying the following two conditions.

\medskip

\noindent
\textnormal{(i) Well-posedness of the flow.}
For every $x\in I$, the integral equation
$$g_t(x)=g_0(x)+\int_0^t\1_{(z_0,g_s(x))}(D_s)\dd[D]_s$$
admits a unique solution until time $T(x):=\inf\{t\geq 0, g_t(x)=\pm\infty\}$, and the map
$(t,x)\mapsto g_t(x)$
is continuous on its domain $\{(t,x), x\in I, 0\le t < T(x)\}$. 

\medskip

\noindent
\textnormal{(ii) Jointly continuous local times along the flow.}
For $x\in I$, assume that the family of processes $(R_t^x)_{0\leq t <T(x)} :=(D_t-g_t(x))_{0\leq t <T(x)} $ admits jointly continuous local
times: namely, assume that there exists a nonnegative field
$(L_t^x(a))_{x\in I,a\in\R,\, 0\leq t<T(x)}$, jointly continuous (at least in a neighborhood of $a=0$)
in $(t,x,a)$, such that for every $x\in I$, every $0\leq t<T(x)$,
and every bounded Borel function $f$,
$$\int_0^t f(R_s^x)\dd[R^x]_s=\int_{\mathbb R}f(a)L_t^x(a)\dd a.
$$

\ms

Write   
$L_t(x):=L_t^x(0).$ For $0\leq t \leq T$, let $I_t := \{ x \in I,\, T(x) > t\}$, and finally let us define for such a process $D$ its final time $T(D) := \inf\{s\leq T,\, \mathring I_s=\emptyset\}\wedge T $.
Then the following properties hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $0 \leq t < T(D)$, the map $x\mapsto g_t(x)$ is an increasing $C^1$-diffeomorphism from the open interval $I_t := \{ x \in I,\, T(x) > t\}$ to $\R$, with
$$\partial_x g_t(x)=({\exp(L_t(x))}) / {\lambda(x)}.$$

\item  The process $X$ defined for $0\leq t< T(D)$ by
$X_t:=g_t^{-1}(D_t)\in \overline I_t$
is continuous and admits a bicontinuous local time $(\Lambda_t(x))_{0\leq t <T(D),\,x\in I}$, where
$\Lambda_t(x)=\lambda(x)\left(1-\exp\bigl(-L_t(x)\bigr)\right)$, i.e.\ for every bounded Borel function $f$, 
$$\int_0^t f(X_s)\dd[X]_s=\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)\Lambda_t(x)\dd x.
$$
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T06:02:34.824843+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fcb3169320cd7400e6048b3ca5b434de404a9ce45cab668add20c31fa69ae15f","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 30 (Lyapunov drift for the forward and adjoint chains) of arXiv:2607.19752, 'Weak Equilibrium Measures and Capacity--Hitting Identities\\ for the Hypoelliptic Third-Or'] Assume Assumptions~\ref{ass:U} and~\ref{ass:whole-space-growth}.  Write
$\calL_\eps^{(+)}=\calL_\eps$ and
$\calL_\eps^{(-)}=\calL_\eps^*$.  Equivalently,
\[
    \calL_\eps^{(\sigma)} f
    =
    \sigma p\cdot\nabla_\theta f
    +\left(-\sigma L^{-1}\nabla U(\theta)+\sigma\gamma r\right)
        \cdot\nabla_p f
    +(-\sigma\gamma p-\gamma r)\cdot\nabla_r f
    +\frac{\gamma\eps}{L}\Delta_r f,
    \qquad \sigma\in\{+1,-1\}.
\]
There exist constants $\kappa,\alpha,\eta,C_V,c,C>0$, with
$\eta=\kappa\alpha$, such that the functions
\[
    V_\sigma(\theta,p,r)
    =
    C_V+H(\theta,p,r)+\eta H(\theta,p,r)^2
    +\alpha K_\sigma(\theta,p,r),
    \qquad \sigma\in\{+1,-1\},
\]
where
\[
    K_\sigma
    =
    \sigma\theta\cdot p+\theta\cdot r
    +\frac{2\sigma}{\gamma}p\cdot r
    +\frac{\gamma}{2}|\theta|^2,
\]
are nonnegative, have compact sublevel sets, and satisfy
\begin{equation}
    \calL_\eps^{(\sigma)}V_\sigma
    \le
    -c\left(U(\theta)+|p|^2+|r|^2+H(\theta,p,r)|r|^2\right)+C,
    \qquad \sigma\in\{+1,-1\}.
\end{equation}
In particular, for every
\[
    R\ge \frac{C+1}{c},
\]

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T10:42:55.336658+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fcb65a10590ee834330a07c918b367accedcf96958ab8de0266d0ecaefb6f848","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 25 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] The fixed-domain perturbation formulas used later are collected here.

\textup{(i)} Assume the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:simplicitycore}, so that the principal eigenvalue is simple in the positive cone. Let $h\in C_c(\R)$ satisfy $h\ge0$ and $h\not\equiv0$. Then $\Lp(\cA_\R+h)<\Lp(\cA_\R)$.

\textup{(ii)} Let $b\in C_c(\R)$ satisfy $b\ge0$ and $b\not\equiv0$, and assume that the Lyapunov hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:simplicitycore} hold for every operator $\cA_\R+rb$ under consideration. Then $r\longmapsto\Lp(\cA_\R+rb)$
is strictly decreasing and locally Lipschitz. If there exist $r_-<r_+$ such that the two values have opposite signs, there is a unique $r_*$ with $\Lp(\cA_\R+r_*b)=0$.

\textup{(iii)} Let $\Omega=(\alpha,\beta)$ be fixed. Let
\[
\cA_\tau u=d\int_\Omega\big(J(x-y)+\tau H(x,y)\big)u(y)\,dy+\big(q(x)+\tau r(x)\big)u'(x)+\big(b(x)+\tau h(x)\big)u(x),
\]
where $q,r\in C^1(\overline \Omega)$, $b,h\in C(\overline \Omega)$ and $H\in C(\overline \Omega^2)$.  We restrict $\tau$ to a real interval on which the drift is bounded away from zero and the kernels $J(x-y)+\tau H(x,y)$ are nonnegative and satisfy a common positivity condition in a neighborhood of the diagonal. Let $\lambda(\tau)=\Lp(\cA_\tau)$. Then the principal eigenvalue and the normalized principal eigenfunction are real analytic in $\tau$ on that interval. If $\phi,\phi^*>0$ are the direct and adjoint principal eigenfunctions at $\tau=0$, normalized by $\int_\Omega\phi\phi^*\,dx=1$,
then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\lambda'(0)={}&-d\int_\Omega\int_\Omega\phi^*(x)H(x,y)\phi(y)\,dy\,dx\\
&-\int_\Omega r(x)\phi'(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx
-\int_\Omega h(x)\phi(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx.
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, for a potential perturbation alone,
\[
\lambda'(0)=-\int_\Omega h(x)\phi(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx.
\]

\textup{(iv)} On a fixed bounded interval let
\[
\cA_{d,c}u=d\left(\int_\Omega J(x-y)u(y)\,dy-u(x)\right)+c\,r(x)u'(x)+a(x)u(x),
\]
where $d>0$, $c$ ranges in an interval on which $cr(x)$ has a fixed sign bounded away from zero, and $r\in C^1(\overline \Omega)$. Normalize the direct and adjoint eigenfunctions by $\int_\Omega\phi\phi^*=1$. Then the principal eigenvalue and the normalized eigenfunction are real analytic in $(d,c)$ on every connected parameter region on which $d>0$ and $cr$ keeps a fixed sign bounded away from zero, and
\[
\partial_d\Lp=-\int_\Omega\phi^*(x)\left(\int_\Omega J(x-y)\phi(y)\,dy-\phi(x)\right)dx,
\]
\[
\partial_c\Lp=-\int_\Omega r(x)\phi'(x)\phi^*(x)\,dx.
\]
No sign is asserted for these derivatives in general.

\textup{(v)} For the scaled operator
\[
\cA_{\sigma,m,L}u=\frac1{\sigma^m}\left(\int_{-L}^{L}J_\sigma(x-y)u(y)\,dy-u(x)\right)+q(x)u'(x)+a(x)u(x),
\]
put $\rho=\sigma/L$ and $v(\xi)=u(L\xi)$. Then
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})=\Lp\left(L^{-m}\rho^{-m}(\mathcal J_\rho-I)+L^{-1}q(L\cdot)\partial_\xi+a(L\cdot),(-1,1)\right),
\]
where
\[
\mathcal J_\rho v(\xi)=\int_{-1}^{1}J_\rho(\xi-\eta)v(\eta)\,d\eta.
\]","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":["γ is a closed piecewise C^1 curve (or a cycle) in C","the point a does not lie on the trace of γ"],"created_at":"2026-09-12T09:49:42.483563+00:00","domain":"complex analysis","id":"claim_fcf7242c6dd1f3172a2cc112bfa1af26bdbbd80032c909e06e994d0138efa1ef","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"Let γ : [α,β] → C be a closed piecewise C^1 curve and let a be a point not on the trace of γ. The winding number (index) of γ about a is n(γ,a) = (1/2πi) ∫_γ dz/(z - a). It is always an integer; as a function of a it is constant on each connected component of the complement of the trace of γ, and it is 0 on the unbounded component. The definition extends additively to cycles (finite formal integer combinations of closed curves) and, via continuous branches of the argument, to merely continuous closed curves. A cycle γ lying in an open set U is called null-homologous in U (homologous to zero) if n(γ,w) = 0 for every w in C minus U. An open connected U ⊂ C is simply connected if and only if every cycle in U is null-homologous in U, if and only if the complement of U in the Riemann sphere is connected. The homology form of Cauchy's theorem reads: if f is holomorphic on U and γ is a cycle null-homologous in U, then ∫_γ f(z) dz = 0 and n(γ,z) f(z) = (1/2πi) ∫_γ f(ζ)/(ζ - z) dζ for every z in U off the trace of γ.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T17:38:58.691190+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fd3f33f91cf25ba014d416e2eece172c26b2356fd641a601b008ae507258cf22","kind":"theorem","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition prop:two_r of arXiv:2510.21186, 'Weingarten Calculus with Virtual Isometries'] Let $m$, $l$ be nonnegative integers, and consider four sequences
\[
\bm{i}=(i_1,\dots, i_m), \qquad \bm{j} =(j_1,\dots, j_m), \qquad
\bm{i}'=(i_1',\dots, i_l'), \qquad \bm{j}' =(j_1',\dots, j_l')
\]
 of positive integers in $\{1,2,\dots,n\}.$
Then, for each $1 \le s \le n$, the moment
\[
\mathbb{E} \bigl[p_{i_1 j_1} \cdots p_{i_m j_m} \overline{p_{i_1' j_1'} \cdots p_{i_l' j_l'}} |r_{ss}|^2 \bigr]
\]
 vanishes unless $\bm{i} \sqcup \bm{j}'$ is a permutation of $\bm{j} \sqcup \bm{i}'$.
In this case, the moment is equal to
\begin{align*}
&\alpha_1 ! \cdots \alpha_{n-1}! \frac{n^{\uparrow \alpha_n}}{n^{\uparrow (m+1)} n^{\uparrow (l+1)}} \\
& \qquad \times
\begin{cases}
 ( (n+m)(n+l) -(\alpha_s+1)(2n+m+l) +(\alpha_s+1)(\alpha_s+2) ) & \text{if $s<n$},
\\
 ( n +(m-\alpha_n)(l-\alpha_n) + \alpha_n ) & \text{if $s=n$},
\end{cases}
\end{align*}
where $\alpha_k:=\mathsf{m}_{k}(\bm{i}\sqcup \bm{j}') = \mathsf{m}_{k}(\bm{j}\sqcup\bm{i}')$
for all $k=1,2,\dots, n$.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-26T19:45:38.358633+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fd527c5e182f142023c6cc0fa4257a99e1fbd74c4494cfe38b91ed170dfe1321","kind":"concept","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Proposition 6 (Aldous' criterion for tightness {\cite[Theorem~16.10) of arXiv:2604.21143, 'Quantitative homogenization for the critical long-range random conductance model'] {Billingsley1999}}]

Then there exist constants $C>0,c>0$ depending only on the random variable $\zeta$ and the constants $\kappa,\Delta$ such that for any $\delta_1,\delta_2\geq 0$, we have the following singular value estimate jointly at $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$:

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T09:38:13.643698+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fd6ff510501e8fffde2302a15f6c21d928dfdae69dd1ad6e5729b2866bd95456","kind":"definition","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Definition 3 (Viscosity solutions of the obstacle problem) of arXiv:2609.00703, 'Ellipsoidal Positivity Sets for Fractional Obstacle Problems with Quadratic Forcing'] Let \(f\in C(\mathbb R^n)\).

A function \(u\in C_b(\mathbb R^n)\) is a viscosity subsolution of \eqref{eq:obstacle}
if, whenever \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(r>0\), and
\(\phi\in C^2(B_r(x_0))\cap C(\overline{B_r(x_0)})\) are such that
\[
u(x_0)=\phi(x_0),
\qquad
u\le\phi
\quad\text{in }B_r(x_0),
\]
one has \(u(x_0)\le0\) or
\[
\mathcal L_r[\phi,u](x_0)-f(x_0)\le0.
\]

A function \(u\in C_b(\mathbb R^n)\) is a viscosity supersolution of \eqref{eq:obstacle}
if \(u\ge0\) in \(\mathbb R^n\) and, whenever \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(r>0\), and
\(\phi\in C^2(B_r(x_0))\cap C(\overline{B_r(x_0)})\) are such that
\[
u(x_0)=\phi(x_0),
\qquad
u\ge\phi
\quad\text{in }B_r(x_0),
\]
one has
\[
\mathcal L_r[\phi,u](x_0)-f(x_0)\ge0.
\]

A function \(u\in C_b(\mathbb R^n)\) is a viscosity solution of \eqref{eq:obstacle}
if it is both a viscosity subsolution and a viscosity supersolution.","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-28T02:56:14.237827+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fda39fb63d5bb25b7c8a8bff90c5e20b44a62f742cbaa054b6cfe8a8bb83ae5d","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma generalMDP of arXiv:2412.09471, 'On the moderate deviation principles in the sparse multi-type Erd\H{o}s R\'enyi random gra'] Let $a_n$ be a sequence such that $1\ll a_n\ll\sqrt{n}$. Let $(\xi^{n,k})_{k\in{\mathbb N}}$ be a sequence of  $i.i.d.$ random vectors in  ${\mathbb R}^d$. Suppose that their moments satisfy:
  $${\mathbb E} \xi^{n,1}=m+O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}),$$
  and $${\mathbb E}(\xi^{n,1}_i-m_i)(\xi^{n,1}_j-m_j)=\sigma_{ij}+O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}),$$
  for some $m\in{\mathbb R}^d$ and some covariance matrix $C=(\sigma_{ij})_{d\times d}$. Let $b_n\in{\mathbb R}^d$ be a sequence such that $|b_{n}|=O\left(\sqrt{n}+a_n^2\right)$.
  Suppose that there exists $R>0$ such that for all $\eta\in{\mathbb R}^d$ and $|\eta|<R$, $\sup_n\log {\mathbb E}\exp(\eta\cdot \xi^n)<\infty$. 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item   Let $N(\lambda_n n)$ be an independent Poisson process with $\lambda_n=\lambda+O(\frac{1}{n})$. The sequence of random variables 
    $$\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{N(\lambda_n n)}\xi^{n,k}-\lambda m n+b_n}{a_n\sqrt{n}}$$
    satisfies the moderate deviation principle in ${\mathbb R}^d$ with speed $a_n^2$ and the rate function 
    \[
    \sup_{l\in{\mathbb R}^d}\left\{\langle l,x\rangle-\frac\lambda{2}\langle l, (C+mm^T)l\rangle\right\}.
    \]
    Moreover, when the matrix $C+mm^T$ is positive-definite, the rate function equals  
    $${\frac{1}{2\lambda}\<x,(C+mm^T)^{-1}x\>.}$$
    \item For any $\lambda>0$ and $u\in{\mathbb R}$, the sequence of random variables 
    $$\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor\lambda n+ua_n\sqrt{n}\rfloor}\xi^{n,k}-(\lambda n+ua_n\sqrt{n})m+b_n}{a_n\sqrt{n}}$$
    satisfies the moderate deviation principle in ${\mathbb R}^d$ with speed $a_n^2$ and the rate function
    \[
    \sup_{l\in{\mathbb R}^d}\left\{\langle l,x\rangle-\frac\lambda{2}\langle l, C l\rangle\right\}.
    \]
    Moreover, when the matrix $C$ is positive-definite, the rate function equals
    $${\frac{1}{2\lambda}\<x,C^{-1}x\>.}$$
\end{enumerate}","status":"unverified"}

{"assumptions":[],"created_at":"2026-10-27T07:25:06.117137+00:00","domain":"probability theory","id":"claim_fdae6c4ee554ca6248c37797498bbb0db64e8ad2eff50bd7246bfb5234f83696","kind":"lemma","schema_version":1,"statement":"[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2608.22342, 'Completely Positive Entropy and Fourier Central Limit Theorems for Stationary Random Measu'] Let $A,B\subset\bR^d$ be bounded Borel sets with
$\lambda_d(\partial A)=\lambda_d(\partial B)=0$. Then
\begin{equation}

    \Cov_\eta\bigl(\mathbb S\ind_A,\mathbb S\ind_B\bigr)
    =\int_{\bR^d}\widehat{\ind}_A(\xi)
       \overline{\widehat{\ind}_B(\xi)}\,d\sigma_\eta(\xi).
\end{equation}
In particular, $\Var_\eta(\mathbb S\ind_A)$ is obtained by taking $A=B$.
For every $g\in\mathcal S(\bR^d)$, one also has the mixed identity
\begin{equation}

    \Cov_\eta\bigl(\mathbb S\ind_A,\mathbb S g\bigr)
    =\int_{\bR^d}\widehat{\ind}_A(\xi)
      \overline{\hat g(\xi)}\,d\sigma_\eta(\xi).
\end{equation}
Consequently, the Bartlett covariance identity holds on the linear span of
Schwartz functions and indicators of bounded Borel sets with boundary of
Lebesgue measure zero. Moreover, for every $\xi\in\bR^d$, the centered statistic
$M(\ind_A\chi_\xi)$ has Koopman spectral measure
\begin{equation}

    d\varsigma_{M(\ind_A\chi_\xi)}(\lambda)
    =\bigl|\widehat{\ind}_A(\lambda-\xi)\bigr|^2
      \,d\sigma_\eta(\lambda).
\end{equation}","status":"unverified"}
